Justus enim septies in die cadit; sed ministerio angelorum, et inspiratione eorum purgatur ac pœnitet; mutatoriisque vestitur, id est donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti. Sed et cidaris ponitur super caput ejus, id est dignitas Ordinis sacerdotalis dispositive ab angelis, a quibus electi diriguntur, secundum præordinationem divinam ad sacerdotii Christi susceptionem: sicque induitur vestimentis virtutum, et gratia sacramentali quæ in susceptione Ordinis sacerdotalis confertur.
paras.en: Moreover this man is [[3:3|clothed with filthy garments|indutus vestibus sordidis]]. For [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|Justus enim septies in die cadit]] a day [Denis quotes Prov 24:16 in its common form, "seven times a day"]; but by the ministry of the angels and by their inspiration he is cleansed and does penance, and is clothed with [[3:4|change of garments|mutatoriisque vestitur]], that is, with the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost. And the [[3:5|mitre|cidaris]] too is put [[3:5|upon his head|super caput ejus]], that is, the dignity of the priestly Order, dispositively [that is, the angels prepare and dispose him, while God gives the Order itself] by the angels, by whom the elect are directed, according to the divine preordination, to the receiving of the priesthood of Christ: and so he is clothed with the garments of the virtues, and with the sacramental grace that is conferred in receiving the priestly Order.

paras.t: Denique hujuscemodi sacerdotem sive pontificem Dominus contestatur: Si in viis meis ambulaveris, tu quoque judicabis domum meam, id est, congregationem fidelium tibi commissam sapienter discuties, discernes ac reges, atque in sacerdotii tui officio salubriter permanebis. Datque ei Deus omnipotens angelorum subsidium, qui sibi in subditorum custodia et salute fideliter cooperentur. Hinc insuper Dominus ait: Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem, id est, Christum tibi adesse faciam in Sacramento, et in medio loquentium de ipso ex caritate. Sed et Pater et Filius ad fideles veniendo, mansionem in ipsis efficiunt gratiosam.
paras.en: Lastly, the Lord solemnly charges such a priest or bishop: [[3:7|If thou wilt walk in my ways|Si in viis meis ambulaveris]], [[3:7|thou also shalt judge my house|tu quoque judicabis domum meam]], that is, thou shalt wisely examine, discern and govern the congregation of the faithful committed to thee, and shalt abide to good effect in the office of thy priesthood. And almighty God gives him the help of the angels, to work faithfully with him in the guarding and the salvation of those under him. Hence the Lord says moreover: [[3:8|behold, I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT|Ecce adducam servum meum Orientem]], that is, I will make Christ present to thee in the Sacrament, and in the midst of those who speak of him out of charity[[Matt 18:20||]]. And indeed the Father and the Son, coming to the faithful, make a gracious abode in them[[John 14:23||]].

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: And the angel that spoke in me came again.

paras.t: Capitulo præcedenti facta est ad pontificem Judæorum divina promissio, quod in sacerdotii sui ministerio esset divinitus stabiliendus, dummodo divinis pareret mandatis. Nunc ad ducem seu principem eorumdem divina fit sponsio consolativa de templi perfectione.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter the divine promise was made to the high priest of the Jews, that he would be established by God in the ministry of his priesthood, provided he obeyed the divine commandments[[Zach 3:7||]]. Now a consoling divine pledge is made to the leader or prince of the same people concerning the completion of the temple.

paras.t: Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me, id est, per quem mihi specialius prophetice revelationes fiebant: de quo jam supra secundo capitulo dixerat, Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur. Ad horam namque disparuit. Et suscitavit me, id est, ad intellectualem considerationem mentisque elevationem excitavit me, a stupore animi quem ex præscriptæ visionis inspectione incurri, quasi virum qui suscitatur de somno suo. Unde ad Ezechielem loquitur angelus: Fili hominis, pone cor tuum in omnia quæ dicam tibi.
paras.en: [[4:1|And the angel that spoke in me came again|Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me]], that is, the one through whom prophetic revelations were made to me in a more special way; of whom he had already said above, in the second chapter, [[Zach 2:3|the angel that spoke in me went forth|Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur]]. For he had vanished for a time. [[4:1|and he waked me|Et suscitavit me]], that is, he roused me to understanding consideration and to the lifting up of the mind, out of the stupor of soul into which I had fallen from beholding the vision described before, [[4:1|as a man that is wakened out of his sleep|quasi virum qui suscitatur de somno suo]]. Hence the angel says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 40:4|Son of man|Fili hominis]], [[Ezech 40:4|set thy heart upon all|pone cor tuum in omnia]] that I shall say to thee [Denis has *quæ dicam tibi*, "that I shall say to thee", where the Vulgate has "that I shall shew thee"].

paras.t: Et dixit ad me: Quid tu vides? Et dixi: Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius, id est, in summitate candelabri fuit; et septem lucernæ ejus, puta candelabri, super illud, id est, in calamis candelabri pendere videbantur; et septem infusoria lucernis, id est vasa aurea deservientia usui lucernarum, quia ex eis oleum infundebatur lucernis, quæ erant super caput illius, quia in vertice candelabri apparebant; et duæ olivæ super illud, una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus, id est, duo rami olivarum circa candelabrum apparuerunt, formam spicarum habentes, et eminebant candelabro, inter quas media fuit lampas in summitate candelabri lucens. Hæc omnia vidit Propheta imaginaria visione, et quid significarent, ignorabat. Ideo subditur:
paras.en: [[4:2|And he said to me: What seest thou? And I said|Et dixit ad me: Quid tu vides? Et dixi]]: [[4:2|I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, and its lamp upon the top of it|Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius]], that is, it was at the summit of the candlestick; [[4:2|and the seven lights thereof|et septem lucernæ ejus]], namely of the candlestick, [[4:2|upon it|super illud]], that is, they were seen hanging on the branches of the candlestick; [[4:2|and seven funnels for the lights|et septem infusoria lucernis]], that is, golden vessels serving the use of the lights, since oil was poured from them into the lights, [[4:2|that were upon the top thereof|quæ erant super caput illius]], since they appeared at the top of the candlestick; [[4:3|And two olive trees over it: one upon the right side of the lamp, and the other upon the left side thereof|et duæ olivæ super illud, una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus]], that is, two olive branches appeared around the candlestick, having the form of ears [*spicæ*, the word the Douay-Rheims renders "branches" at v. 12], and they rose above the candlestick, and between them, in the middle, was the lamp shining at the summit of the candlestick. All these things the Prophet saw in an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination, as distinct from a bodily or a purely intellectual vision], and he did not know what they signified. Therefore it follows:

paras.t: Et respondi, et aio ad angelum qui loquebatur in me, dicens: Quid sunt hæc, domine mi? id est, quid similitudines istæ rerum significant? Et respondit angelus qui loquebatur in me, et dixit ad me: Numquid nescis quid sunt hæc? Et dixi: Non, domine mi. Et respondit, et ait ad me, dicens: Hoc est verbum Domini ad Zorobabel, id est, sermo Domini qui ad Zorobabel factus est, prædictæ visionis interpretatio est. Et quis sit sermo ille, subjungitur, dicens: Non in exercitu, nec in robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, non in multitudine pugnatorum, nec virtute humana, sed in Dei spiritu, seu inspiratione divina, ex qua Cyrus ac Darius annuerunt petitionibus Judæorum, ipsos Judæos de Babylonica captivitate esse reductos, pleniusque reducendos, adversarios quoque vastandos, et templum in brevi perficiendum. Nempe quum candelabrum aureum cum ceteris prænominatis, fuerit de specialibus templi ornamentis, nec ponebatur in eo nisi jam consummato, idcirco per visionem candelabri, et ceterorum ad illud pertinentium, significabatur quod templi ædificium esset per Zorobabel mox complendum, ob cujus completionem divina inspiratione atque potentia fuerunt Judæi reducti.
paras.en: [[4:4|And I answered, and said to the angel that spoke in me, saying: What are these things, my lord?|Et respondi, et aio ad angelum qui loquebatur in me, dicens: Quid sunt hæc, domine mi?]] That is, what do these likenesses of things signify? [[4:5|And the angel that spoke in me answered, and said to me: Knowest thou not what these things are? And I said: No, my lord.|Et respondit angelus qui loquebatur in me, et dixit ad me: Numquid nescis quid sunt hæc? Et dixi: Non, domine mi.]] [[4:6|And he answered, and spoke to me, saying: This is the word of the Lord to Zorobabel|Et respondit, et ait ad me, dicens: Hoc est verbum Domini ad Zorobabel]], that is, the word of the Lord which came to Zorobabel is the interpretation of the vision described. And what that word is, follows: [[4:6|saying: Not with an army, nor by might, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts|dicens: Non in exercitu, nec in robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, not in a multitude of fighting men, nor by human strength, but in the spirit of God, or divine inspiration, by which Cyrus and Darius granted the petitions of the Jews[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 6:1||]]: meaning that the Jews themselves had been brought back from the Babylonian captivity and were to be brought back more fully, that their adversaries too were to be laid waste, and that the temple was soon to be finished. For since the golden candlestick, with the other things named before, was among the special ornaments of the temple, and was not set in it until the temple was already completed, therefore the vision of the candlestick, and of the other things belonging to it, signified that the building of the temple was soon to be completed by Zorobabel; and it was for its completion that the Jews had been brought back by divine inspiration and power.

paras.t: Præterea, sicut refert Hieronymus, Hebræi, a quibus ipse in veteri Testamento se asserit eruditum, per candelabrum aureum intelligunt solidam legem per Moysen divinitus datam; per lampadem autem, id est flammam in vertice candelabri lucentem atque fulgentem, Christum, qui caput est legis et omnium hominum illuminator; per septem lucernas, septem dona Spiritus Sancti; per septem infusoria intelligunt, quod dona ista de cœlo ad homines per legem descendunt; per duas vero olivas, legem et Prophetas.
paras.en: Moreover, as Jerome relates, the Hebrews, by whom he says he was taught in the Old Testament, understand by the golden candlestick the solid law [*solidam*, answering to the candlestick "all of gold"] given by God through Moses; by the lamp, that is, the flame shining and glowing at the top of the candlestick, Christ, who is the head of the law and the enlightener of all men; by the seven lights, the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost; by the seven funnels they understand that these gifts come down from heaven to men through the law; and by the two olive trees, the Law and the Prophets.

paras.t: Quis tu, mons magne, id est, diabole, per superbiam intumescens, et sublimis naturæ, quamvis vitiatæ, coram Zorobabel in planum, id est divina virtute in terram dejectus, atque in planum coram duce Judæorum jacens prostratus ac victus? tanquam dicat: Tu, dæmon, qui stetisti ad dexteram Jesu sacerdotis, ut ei insidiareris, frustra te erexisti contra Zorobabel, ut eum a templi ædificio impedires. Et educet lapidem primarium, id est, Deus Christum Filium suum mittet in mundum: de quo Christo dictum est præcedenti capitulo, Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt; fuitque semper auxilio populo Judæorum. Et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus, id est, gratia subventionis quam fecit Deus patribus Judæorum ab antiquo, et nunc post reditum de Chaldæa, similis est gratiæ quam faciet Christus quum venerit, quamvis non sit omnino æqualis. Vel sic, secundum Hieronymum: Gratia ejus, utpote lapidis hujus, in eos quos de Babylone reduxit, exæquavit gratiam quam in patres eorum semper exercuit. Quidam exponunt sic: Et educet ipse Zorobabel lapidem primarium, id est, super lapidem fundamenti ante jam positum, educet structuram templi in altum; et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus, id est, Zorobabel impetrabit a Dario rege gratiam consummandi templum, quemadmodum Cyrus rex dedit gratiam ædificandi. Unde subjungitur:
paras.en: [[4:7|Who art thou, O great mountain|Quis tu, mons magne]], that is, O devil, swelling with pride, and of a lofty nature, though a corrupted one, [[4:7|before Zorobabel|coram Zorobabel]]? [[4:7|thou shalt become a plain|in planum]], that is, cast down to the earth by divine power, and lying on the plain before the leader of the Jews, prostrate and conquered. As if he said: Thou, demon, who stoodest at the right hand of Jesus the priest to lie in wait for him[[Zach 3:1||]], hast raised thyself up in vain against Zorobabel, to hinder him from building the temple. [[4:7|and he shall bring out the chief stone|Et educet lapidem primarium]], that is, God will send Christ his Son into the world: of which Christ it was said in the preceding chapter, [[Zach 3:9|upon one stone there are seven eyes|Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt]]; and he was always a help to the people of the Jews. [[4:7|and shall give equal grace to the grace thereof|Et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus]], that is, the grace of succour which God showed the fathers of the Jews of old, and now after the return from Chaldæa, is like the grace which Christ will show when he comes, though it is not altogether equal. Or thus, according to Jerome: His grace, that is, the grace of this stone, towards those whom he brought back from Babylon, has equalled the grace which he always showed towards their fathers. Some explain it thus: [[4:7|and he shall bring out|Et educet]], Zorobabel himself, [[4:7|the chief stone|lapidem primarium]], that is, upon the foundation stone already laid before, he will carry the structure of the temple up on high; [[4:7|and shall give equal grace to the grace thereof|et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus]], that is, Zorobabel will obtain from king Darius the grace [*gratia*, here a favour or grant] of completing the temple[[1 Esd 6:1||]], just as king Cyrus gave the grace of building it[[1 Esd 1:1||]]. Hence it follows:

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens: Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam, scilicet templum tempore Cyri, et manus ejus perficient eam, Dario regnante, sicut in libro Esdræ clarius recitatur. Opus quippe adscribitur principi, tanquam principali agenti. Et scietis, templi consummatione perspecta, quia Dominus exercituum misit me Zachariam prophetam ad vos de templo construendo monendos. Impletio enim vaticinii, signum est veritatis et destinationis divinæ, secundum quod in Jeremia habetur: Propheta qui vaticinatus est, quum venerit verbum ejus, scietur Propheta quem miserit Dominus in veritate.
paras.en: [[4:8|And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:|Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens:]] [[4:9|The hands of Zorobabel have laid the foundations of this house|Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam]], namely the temple, in the time of Cyrus, [[4:9|and his hands shall finish it|et manus ejus perficient eam]], in the reign of Darius, as is told more clearly in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 6:15||]]. For the work is ascribed to the prince, as to the principal agent. [[4:9|and you shall know|Et scietis]], when you see the temple completed, [[4:9|that the Lord of hosts hath sent me|quia Dominus exercituum misit me]], Zacharias the prophet, [[4:9|to you|ad vos]], to exhort you to build the temple. For the fulfilment of a prophecy is a sign of its truth and of its being sent by God, according to what is found in Jeremias: [[Jer 28:9|The prophet that prophesied|Propheta qui vaticinatus est]], [[Jer 28:9|when his word shall come to pass, the prophet shall be known, whom the hath sent in truth|quum venerit verbum ejus, scietur Propheta quem miserit Dominus in veritate]].

paras.t: Quis enim despexit dies parvos? Hoc dupliciter declaratur. Primo sic: Quis contempsit brevem ac fragilem potestatem eorum qui nisi sunt templi instaurationem impedire? quasi dicat: Pauci fuerunt, videlicet constantes, qui non obstante adversariorum furore, templum cum Zorobabel construxerunt. Secundo sic: Quis despexit dies parvos, id est statum Judæorum a Babylonia reversorum? qui primo modicus fuit, et ab adversariis valde contemptus, juxta illud Esdræ: Dixerunt: Ædificent; si ascenderint vulpes, transilient murum eorum. Et lætabuntur Judæi qui dies parvos hostium despexerunt, atque ab adversariis Samaritanis ac ceteris despecti fuerunt, et videbunt lapidem stanneum in manu Zorobabel, id est fortem materiam atque idoneam facultatem ad templi erectionem. Gavisi sunt ergo Judæi, ex divini subsidii experientia, et templi eminentia. Quidam per lapidem stanneum intelligunt Christum, quem illuminati Judæi viderunt per fidem de stirpe Zorobabel nasciturum. Septem isti oculi sunt Domini, id est, septem oculi de quibus supra dictum est quod erant super lapidem unum, sunt septem gratiæ intellectuales, omnium corda illuminantes. Propter quod subditur: qui discurrunt in universam terram, id est ad omnes habitantes in terra fideles. Vel per septem oculos, juxta sensum præhabitum, intelligitur universitas angelorum qui ad explenda divinæ majestatis obsequia emittuntur, præsertim ad homines.
paras.en: [[4:10|For who hath despised little days?|Quis enim despexit dies parvos?]] This is explained in two ways. First thus: Who has scorned the brief and frail power of those who strove to hinder the restoration of the temple? As if he said: Few they were, namely the steadfast, who in spite of the fury of their adversaries built the temple with Zorobabel. Second thus: [[4:10|who hath despised little days|Quis despexit dies parvos]], that is, the state of the Jews returned from Babylonia, which at first was small, and much despised by their adversaries, according to that of Esdras: They said: [[2 Esd 4:3|Let them build: if a fox go up, he will leap over their|Ædificent; si ascenderint vulpes, transilient murum eorum]] wall [Denis has the plural: "if foxes go up, they will leap over their wall"]. [[4:10|and they shall rejoice|Et lætabuntur]], namely the Jews who despised the little days of their enemies, and were themselves despised by their adversaries, the Samaritans and the rest, [[4:10|and shall see the tin plummet in the hand of Zorobabel|et videbunt lapidem stanneum in manu Zorobabel]], that is, strong material and fit means for raising the temple. So the Jews rejoiced, from their experience of the divine help and from the excellence of the temple. Some understand by the tin stone [*lapis stanneus*, the Douay-Rheims' "tin plummet"] Christ, whom the enlightened Jews saw by faith as one to be born of the stock of Zorobabel. [[4:10|These are the seven eyes of the Lord|Septem isti oculi sunt Domini]], that is, the seven eyes of which it was said above that they were upon one stone[[Zach 3:9||]] are seven intellectual graces, enlightening the hearts of all. Wherefore it is added: [[4:10|that run to and fro through the whole earth|qui discurrunt in universam terram]], that is, to all the faithful dwelling on the earth. Or by the seven eyes, according to the sense given before, is understood the whole company of the angels, who are sent forth to fulfil the services of the divine majesty, especially to men.

paras.t: Consequenter sciscitatur Propheta quid duæ olivæ superius positæ ac descriptæ significent. Et respondi, et dixi ad eum, id est angelum in me loquentem: Quid sunt duæ olivæ istæ ad dexteram candelabri, et ad sinistram ejus? Sic enim in visione imaginaria situatæ videbantur. Et respondi secundo, et dixi ad eum. Primæ enim interrogationi angelus non statim respondit, ut desiderium agnoscendi veritatem accenderetur in corde Prophetæ, sicque divinæ illustrationis capacior redderetur. Quid sunt duæ spicæ olivarum, quæ sunt juxta duo rostra aurea, in quibus sunt suffusoria ex auro? Rostra ista fuerunt duæ recurvationes in candelabro factæ, in quibus infusoria aurea dependebant. Denique, primo quæsivit Propheta quid essent duæ olivæ; nunc quærit quid sint duæ spicæ olivarum, quasi parcius quærens. Sed quia redit in idem, angelus ei respondit. Et ait ad me, dicens: Numquid nescis quid sunt hæc, id est, quid designent? Et dixi: Non, domine mi. Interrogatio angeli ex ignorantia non procedit; sed quæritur, ut responsionis dilatio augeat in Propheta audiendæ veritatis amorem: desideria siquidem dilatione crescunt.
paras.en: Next the Prophet asks what the two olive trees placed and described above[[4:3||]] signify. [[4:11|And I answered, and said to him|Et respondi, et dixi ad eum]], that is, to the angel speaking in me: [[4:11|What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick, and upon the left side thereof?|Quid sunt duæ olivæ istæ ad dexteram candelabri, et ad sinistram ejus?]] For so they appeared to be placed in the imaginary vision. [[4:12|And I answered again, and said to him|Et respondi secundo, et dixi ad eum]]. For the angel did not answer the first question at once, so that the desire of knowing the truth might be kindled in the Prophet's heart, and he might thus be made more capable of divine enlightenment. [[4:12|What are the two olive branches, that are by the two golden beaks, in which are the funnels of gold?|Quid sunt duæ spicæ olivarum, quæ sunt juxta duo rostra aurea, in quibus sunt suffusoria ex auro?]] These beaks were two bends made in the candlestick, from which the golden funnels hung. So then, first the Prophet asked what the two olive trees were; now he asks what the two olive branches are, as though asking about less. But because it comes to the same thing, the angel answered him. [[4:13|And he spoke to me, saying: Knowest thou not what these are?|Et ait ad me, dicens: Numquid nescis quid sunt hæc]] That is, what do they signify? [[4:13|And I said: No, my lord|Et dixi: Non, domine mi]]. The angel's question does not proceed from ignorance; but it is asked so that the delay of the answer may increase in the Prophet the love of hearing the truth: for desires grow by delay.

paras.t: Et dixit: Isti sunt duo filii olei, id est, designati per duas olivas, sunt duo filii olei, scilicet Jesus pontifex filius Josedec, atque Zorobabel dux populi. Primus enim erat de tribu sacerdotali, alter de stirpe regali, quarum utraque in veteri Testamento ungebatur, quantum ad regem et pontificem, quamvis unctio illa in transmigratione Babylonis cessasse, nec post fuisse dicatur. Vel dicuntur filii olei propter gratiam et pietatem quam circa populi gubernationem habebant. Unde Aquila transtulit: Filii splendoris, id est divinæ illustrationis. Qui adsistunt Dominatori universæ terræ, id est, Deo omnipotenti omnibus imperanti, in ejus obsequio ac templi instauratione, et populi administratione fideliter efficaciterque intenti. Sic quippe Elias et Eliseus Deo adstantes, dixerunt: Vivit Dominus, in cujus conspectu sto.
paras.en: [[4:14|And he said: These are two sons of oil|Et dixit: Isti sunt duo filii olei]], that is, those signified by the two olive trees are two sons of oil, namely Jesus the high priest, the son of Josedec, and Zorobabel the leader of the people. For the first was of the priestly tribe, the other of the royal stock, and in the Old Testament both were anointed, as regards the king and the high priest, although that anointing is said to have ceased at the transmigration of Babylon and not to have existed afterwards. Or they are called sons of oil because of the grace and kindness they showed in governing the people. Hence Aquila translated: Sons of splendour, that is, of divine enlightenment. [[4:14|who stand before the Lord of the whole earth|Qui adsistunt Dominatori universæ terræ]], that is, before God almighty, who commands all things, being intent faithfully and effectually upon his service, the restoration of the temple, and the governing of the people. For so Elias and Eliseus, standing before God, said: [[3 Kings 17:1|As the Lord liveth|Vivit Dominus]], [[3 Kings 17:1|in whose sight I stand|in cujus conspectu sto]][[4 Kings 3:14||]].

4.title: De spirituali et mystico ejusdem capituli quarti intellectu.
4.title_en: On the spiritual and mystical understanding of the same fourth chapter.

paras.t: Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me. Per Zachariam, qui interpretatur memoria Domini, designatur quicumque fidelis divinorum speculationi semper intentus. Ad talem ergo angelus ejus, qui animæ suæ illuminator et custos est, frequenter revertitur, atque cum eo libenter moratur. Et suscitavit me, quasi virum qui suscitatur de somno. Quotiescumque humana fragilitas suæ relinquitur imbecillitati, Dei et angelorum auxilium ab ea recedit. Dum ergo mens contemplativi incipit evagari, inaniter affici, acediæ torpore pulsari, tentatione gravari, adversitatibus dejici, passione aut vitio aliquo obrui, indiget ab angelo visitari, et velut de somno negligentiæ suscitari, confortari et consolari.
paras.en: [[4:1|And the angel that spoke in me came again|Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me]]. By Zacharias, which is interpreted *memory of the Lord*, is signified every faithful soul always intent on the contemplation of divine things. To such a one, then, his angel, who is the enlightener and guardian of his soul, often returns, and gladly stays with him. [[4:1|and he waked me|Et suscitavit me]], [[4:1|as a man that is wakened out of his sleep|quasi virum qui suscitatur de somno]]. Whenever human frailty is left to its own weakness, the help of God and of the angels withdraws from it. When, therefore, the mind of the contemplative begins to wander, to be stirred by vain affections, to be struck by the torpor of acedia [that is, spiritual sloth, a weariness of divine things], to be weighed down by temptation, cast down by adversities, or overwhelmed by some passion or vice, it needs to be visited by the angel, and as it were roused from the sleep of negligence, strengthened and consoled.

paras.t: Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius, etc. Per candelabrum aureum Prophetæ monstratum, allegorice intelligitur ipsa Ecclesia, quoad electos præ cunctis mundi hominibus, rutilantissimis gratiarum ornamentis fulcita, quæ in sacra Scriptura sensum et mentem magis quam verba attendit. Unde in Apocalypsi vidit Joannes similem Filio hominis, ambulantem in medio candelabrorum aureorum. In hujus Ecclesiæ capite est lampas, videlicet Christus, qui ait: Ego sum lux mundi, quæ illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum. Insuper per septem lucernas, ut dictum est, intelliguntur septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quæ descendunt super electos. Et septem infusoria lucernis, quæ erant super caput illius. Ista septem infusoria, quæ sunt super caput Ecclesiæ, et in nutrimentum lucernarum præstantur, intelligi possunt septem sacramenta Ecclesiæ, quæ sunt vasa medicinalia, gratiæ contentiva, significativa, et effectiva. Efficiunt enim quod repræsentant. Et oleum pietatis in eis est, scilicet gratia sacramentalis, per quam dona Spiritus Sancti conservantur, aluntur, ac perficiuntur: siquidem gratiæ et virtutes ac dona, se invicem muniunt, juvant, perficiunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, and its lamp upon the top of it|Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius]], etc. By the golden candlestick shown to the Prophet is understood, allegorically, the Church herself, which, as regards the elect, is furnished beyond all the men of the world with the most brilliant ornaments of graces, and which in holy Scripture attends to the sense and meaning more than to the words. Hence in the Apocalypse John saw [[Apoc 1:13|one like to the Son of man|similem Filio hominis]], walking [[Apoc 1:13|in the midst of the|in medio]] [[Apoc 1:13|golden candlesticks|candelabrorum aureorum]]. At the head of this Church is the lamp, namely Christ, who says: [[John 8:12|I am the light of the world|Ego sum lux mundi]], [[John 1:9|which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world|quæ illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum]]. Moreover, by the seven lights, as has been said, are understood the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, which come down upon the elect. [[4:2|and seven funnels for the lights that were upon the top thereof|Et septem infusoria lucernis, quæ erant super caput illius]]. These seven funnels, which are upon the head of the Church and are supplied for the nourishment of the lights, may be understood as the seven sacraments of the Church, which are medicinal vessels, containing, signifying and effecting grace. For they effect what they represent. And the oil of piety is in them, namely sacramental grace, by which the gifts of the Holy Ghost are preserved, nourished and perfected: for graces and virtues and gifts strengthen, help and perfect one another.

paras.t: Et duæ olivæ super illud, una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus. Per duas istas olivas super Ecclesiam, id est aliorum directioni prælatos ac præsidentes, quidam intelligunt Moysen et Eliam, qui cum Christo loquebantur in monte in hora transfigurationis; alii, Petrum et Paulum; alii, vitam contemplativam, quasi a dextris, et activam, quasi a sinistris; alii, vetus et novum Testamentum, illud a sinistris, istud a dextris. Sed quoniam nomine olivæ, pietas compassionis exprimi solet: per illam quæ fuit a dextris, intelligi potest qui opera misericordiæ spiritualia explet; per aliam, qui operibus misericordiæ corporalibus vacat.
paras.en: [[4:3|And two olive trees over it: one upon the right side of the lamp, and the other upon the left side thereof|Et duæ olivæ super illud, una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus]]. By these two olive trees over the Church, that is, set over others to direct them and presiding over them, some understand Moses and Elias, who were speaking with Christ on the mountain in the hour of the transfiguration[[Matt 17:3||]]; others, Peter and Paul; others, the contemplative life, as on the right, and the active, as on the left; others, the Old and the New Testament, the former on the left, the latter on the right. But since the name of the olive commonly expresses the tenderness of compassion, by the one that was on the right may be understood the man who fulfils the spiritual works of mercy, and by the other, the man who gives himself to the corporal works of mercy.

paras.t: Hoc est verbum Domini ad Zorobabel, id est Christum populi christiani ducem ac principem: Non in exercitu, nec in robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Dominus. Hoc quippe Christus in Evangelio docet, quod salus, virtus, sufficientia, et profectus animæ nostræ non est in multitudine aut robore creaturarum, sed ex Spiritu Sancto: et hoc Deus Trinitas docuit Christum, quantum ad naturam assumptam: nam animæ ejus hoc revelavit. Denique et ipse de se ipso testatur: Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam. Et iterum ait: A me ipso facio nihil, sed sicut docuit me Pater, hæc loquor.
paras.en: [[4:6|This is the word of the Lord to Zorobabel|Hoc est verbum Domini ad Zorobabel]], that is, to Christ, the leader and prince of the Christian people: [[4:6|Not with an army, nor by might, but by my spirit, saith the Lord|Non in exercitu, nec in robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Dominus]]. For Christ teaches this in the Gospel, that the salvation, strength, sufficiency and progress of our soul is not in the multitude or strength of creatures, but from the Holy Ghost; and this God the Trinity taught Christ, as regards the nature he assumed: for he revealed it to his soul. And indeed he himself bears witness of himself: [[John 5:19|the Son cannot do any thing of himself|Non potest Filius a se facere quidquam]]. And again he says: [[John 8:28|I do nothing of myself. But as the Father hath taught me, these things I speak|A me ipso facio nihil, sed sicut docuit me Pater, hæc loquor]].

paras.t: Quis tu, mons magne, id est, diabole tumide, coram Zorobabel, id est Christo, contra quem te erigens, dicere præsumpsisti, Hæc omnia mundi regna tibi dabo, si cadens adoraveris me; sed coram eo ab eo in planum dejectus et victus es. Et educet Dominus exercituum lapidem primarium, utpote Christum: quem secundum carnem eduxit de semine Patriarcharum. Deinde eduxit eum de sæculo isto ad regnum æternum, et per Apostolorum doctrinam eduxit eum de occulto ignorantiæ ad lucem salutaris notitiæ in cordibus electorum. De quo scriptum est: Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, electum, angularem, pretiosum; et omnis qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur. Apud Matthæum quoque Christus loquitur de se ipso: Qui ceciderit super lapidem istum, confringetur; super quem vero ceciderit, conteret ipsum. Et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus, id est, gratiam evangelicæ legis æquabit Deus gratiæ veteris Testamenti, ut non minor sit perfectio patrum novi Testamenti quam veteris: imo Prophetis ac Patriarchis præferuntur Apostoli. Propter quod a Joanne asseritur: De plenitudine ejus, videlicet Christi, nos omnes accepimus, gratiam pro gratia.
paras.en: [[4:7|Who art thou, O great mountain|Quis tu, mons magne]], that is, O swollen devil, [[4:7|before Zorobabel|coram Zorobabel]], that is, before Christ, against whom thou didst raise thyself up and presume to say: [[Matt 4:9|All these|Hæc omnia]] kingdoms of the world [[Matt 4:9|will I give thee, if falling down thou wilt adore me|tibi dabo, si cadens adoraveris me]]; but before him, and by him, thou art cast down and conquered: [[4:7|thou shalt become a plain|in planum]]. [[4:7|and he shall bring out|Et educet]], namely the Lord of hosts, [[4:7|the chief stone|lapidem primarium]], that is, Christ: whom he brought forth according to the flesh from the seed of the Patriarchs. Then he brought him forth from this world to the eternal kingdom; and through the teaching of the Apostles he brought him forth from the hiding-place of ignorance into the light of saving knowledge in the hearts of the elect. Of him it is written: [[1 Pet 2:6|Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious. And he that shall believe in him shall not be confounded|Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, electum, angularem, pretiosum; et omnis qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur]][[Is 28:16||]] [Denis's wording is close to 1 Pet 2:6, where St Peter quotes Isaias 28:16]. In Matthew also Christ speaks of himself: [[Matt 21:44|whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder|Qui ceciderit super lapidem istum, confringetur; super quem vero ceciderit, conteret ipsum]]. [[4:7|and shall give equal grace to the grace thereof|Et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus]], that is, God will make the grace of the law of the Gospel equal to the grace of the Old Testament, so that the perfection of the fathers of the New Testament is not less than that of the Old: indeed, the Apostles are preferred to the Prophets and Patriarchs. Wherefore John declares: [[John 1:16|of his fulness|De plenitudine ejus]], namely of Christ's, [[John 1:16|we all have received|nos omnes accepimus]], [[John 1:16|grace for grace|gratiam pro gratia]].

paras.t: Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam, et manus ejus perficient eam: id est, virtus et gratia Christi initiavit Ecclesiam, et perficiet eam, præsertim in resurrectione futura; et a tempore Apostolorum quotidie eam, quantum ad quosdam electos, perfecit, augendo in eis spiritualem profectum. Ipse equidem ait: Super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam. Et in Psalmo cantamus eidem: Infirmata est, tu vero perfecisti eam.
paras.en: [[4:9|The hands of Zorobabel have laid the foundations of this house, and his hands shall finish it|Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam, et manus ejus perficient eam]]: that is, the power and grace of Christ began the Church, and will perfect it, especially in the resurrection to come; and from the time of the Apostles it has been perfecting it daily, as regards certain of the elect, by increasing their spiritual progress. He himself indeed says: [[Matt 16:18|upon this rock I will build my church|Super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]. And in the Psalm we sing to him: [[Ps 67:10|it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect|Infirmata est, tu vero perfecisti eam]].

paras.t: Quis enim despexit dies parvos? id est, utique ipse Christus mundi hujus statum, vanitatem, dominium, ac brevissimam vitam contempsit, idcirco construxit Ecclesiam, instruendo fideles ad terrenorum contemptum, cœlestiumque amorem. Sic et ceteri fecerunt electi. Unde et beatissimus patriarcha Jacob profitetur: Dies peregrinationis vitæ meæ super terram, centum triginta anni sunt, parvi et mali. Et lætabuntur gaudio spirituali fideles, qui temporalia vilipenderunt, et videbunt lapidem stanneum, id est virtutem discretivam, in manu Zorobabel, id est in potestate atque judicio Christi. Sicut enim, teste Hieronymo, stannum alia metalla ab ignis læsione defendit, mixta quoque et adulterata inter se metalla per ignem dissociat; sic Christus per judiciariam potestatem triticum a paleis, hoc est electos a reprobis, separabit, quemadmodum de ipso in Evangelio legitur: Cujus ventilabrum in manu ejus, et purgabit aream suam; et congregabit triticum in horreum suum, paleas autem comburet igni inexstinguibili.
paras.en: [[4:10|For who hath despised little days?|Quis enim despexit dies parvos?]] That is: Christ himself, assuredly, despised the state of this world, its vanity, its dominion and its very brief life, and therefore he built the Church, instructing the faithful in contempt of earthly things and love of heavenly ones. So too did the rest of the elect. Hence also the most blessed patriarch Jacob professes: [[Gen 47:9|The days of my pilgrimage|Dies peregrinationis]] in this life upon earth [[Gen 47:9|are a hundred and thirty years, few, and evil|centum triginta anni sunt, parvi et mali]]. [[4:10|and they shall rejoice|Et lætabuntur]] with spiritual joy, namely the faithful who have held temporal things cheap, [[4:10|and shall see the tin plummet|et videbunt lapidem stanneum]], that is, the power of discernment, [[4:10|in the hand of Zorobabel|in manu Zorobabel]], that is, in the power and judgment of Christ. For as, on the testimony of Jerome, tin protects other metals from injury by fire, and also by fire separates metals mixed and adulterated together, so Christ by his judicial power will separate the wheat from the chaff, that is, the elect from the reprobate, as is read of him in the Gospel: [[Luke 3:17|Whose fan is in his hand: and he will purge his floor and will gather the wheat into his barn: but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire|Cujus ventilabrum in manu ejus, et purgabit aream suam; et congregabit triticum in horreum suum, paleas autem comburet igni inexstinguibili]][[Matt 3:12||]] [Denis's wording is that of Luke 3:17].

paras.t: Duo rostra aurea, in quibus sunt suffusoria ex auro. Jam dictum est quemadmodum per septem infusoria aurea, intelliguntur septem Ecclesiæ sacramenta. Et ista esse dicuntur in aureis rostris, id est in manibus et membris ministrorum Ecclesiæ consecratis, per quos conficiuntur, tractantur, ac dispensantur. Cetera ex præinductis clarissime innotescunt.
paras.en: [[4:12|the two golden beaks, in which are the funnels of gold?|Duo rostra aurea, in quibus sunt suffusoria ex auro]] It has already been said how by the seven golden funnels are understood the seven sacraments of the Church. And these are said to be in golden beaks, that is, in the consecrated hands and members of the ministers of the Church, by whom they are confected, handled and dispensed. The rest is made most clear by what has been set out before.

5.title: Expositio literalis capituli quinti: Et conversus sum.
5.title_en: Literal explanation of the fifth chapter: And I turned.

paras.t: POSTQUAM divinitus ostensa sunt Prophetæ jucunda de Judæorum liberatione a Babylone, et Judææ ac templi reparatione, nunc ostenduntur eidem adversa ac tristia. Et conversus sum ego Zacharias interiore conversione ab una visione prophetali ad aliam, et levavi oculos meos, præsertim intellectuales, et vidi visione imaginaria ac mentali, et ecce volumen volans mihi apparuit.
paras.en: After the joyful things concerning the deliverance of the Jews from Babylon, and the restoration of Judæa and of the temple, have been divinely shown to the Prophet, now adverse and sad things are shown to him. [[5:1|And I turned|Et conversus sum]], I Zacharias, by an inward turning from one prophetic vision to another, [[5:1|and lifted up my eyes|et levavi oculos meos]], above all the eyes of the intellect, [[5:1|and I saw|et vidi]] by an imaginary and mental vision [that is, a vision formed in the imagination and the mind, not seen with the bodily eyes], [[5:1|and behold a volume flying|et ecce volumen volans]] appeared to me.

paras.t: Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me, de quo jam dictum est sæpe : Quid tu vides? Et dixi : Ecce ego video volumen volans. Cujus quantitas subditur : longitudo ejus viginti cubitorum, et latitudo ejus decem cubitorum. Cujus rationem quidam assignant, quia volumen istud videbatur de civitate Jerusalem et templo exire. Ideo, sicut longitudo porticus erat viginti cubitorum, et latitudo ejus decem cubitorum ante faciem templi, ita et de mensura voluminis fuit. Porro, secundum Hieronymum, per numerum vicesimum, qui ex duabus decadibus fit, austera ac tristia nuntiantur; per decem, id est una decade, meliora et prospera. Quoniam ergo flagella et pœnæ præsentis vitæ a Deo infliguntur, ut corrigamur et emendemur (pœnæ namque hujusmodi sunt medicinales, ut castigati erudiamur), hinc longitudo hujus voluminis recte fuisse describitur cubitorum viginti, latitudoque decem.
paras.en: [[5:2|And he said to me|Et dixit ad me]] the angel that spoke in me, of whom much has already been said: [[5:2|What seest thou?|Quid tu vides?]] [[5:2|And I said|Et dixi]]: Behold, [[5:2|I see a volume flying|ego video volumen volans]]. Its size is then given: [[5:2|the length thereof is twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof ten cubits|longitudo ejus viginti cubitorum, et latitudo ejus decem cubitorum]]. Some give the reason for this: that this volume seemed to come out of the city of Jerusalem and the temple. Therefore, as the length of the porch was twenty cubits, and its breadth ten cubits, before the face of the temple[[3 Kings 6:3||]], so it was too with the measure of the volume. Further, according to Jerome, by the number twenty, which is made of two tens, harsh and sad things are announced; by ten, that is, by a single ten, better and prosperous things. Since, then, the scourges and punishments of the present life are inflicted by God so that we may be corrected and amended[[Jdt 8:27||]] (for punishments of this kind are medicinal, so that being chastised we may be taught), the length of this volume is rightly described as twenty cubits, and its breadth as ten.

paras.t: Et dixit ad me : Hæc est maledictio, id est, in volumine isto scripta sunt et significata peccata atque supplicia Judæorum, quæ egreditur super faciem omnis terræ, id est, simul cum Judæis de terra promissionis expellitur ad diversas mundi provincias in quibus captivi abducti fuerunt Judæi tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis et ante. Nunc enim est sermo de expulsione multiplicium iniquitatum a terra populoque Judæ. Quia omnis fur, sicut ibi scriptum est, scilicet in præfato volumine, judicabitur judicio condemnationis, et omnis jurans, ex hoc volumine similiter judicabitur, si vitiose, false, inordinateque juret.
paras.en: [[5:3|And he said to me: This is the curse|Et dixit ad me : Hæc est maledictio]], that is, in this volume are written and signified the sins and the punishments of the Jews, [[5:3|that goeth forth over the face of the earth|quæ egreditur super faciem omnis terræ]], that is, it is driven out of the land of promise together with the Jews into the various provinces of the world into which the Jews were led away captive at the time of the Babylonian captivity and before. For the discourse here is of the expulsion of manifold iniquities from the land and people of Juda. [[5:3|For every thief|Quia omnis fur]], [[5:3|as is there written|sicut ibi scriptum est]], namely in the aforesaid volume, [[5:3|shall be judged|judicabitur]] with the judgment of condemnation, [[5:3|and every one that sweareth in like manner shall be judged by it|et omnis jurans, ex hoc volumine similiter judicabitur]], that is, by this volume, if he swear viciously, falsely and inordinately.

paras.t: Simile est quod in Daniele legitur : Throni positi sunt, judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt. Per quæ omnia designatur, quod homines judicantur a Deo secundum infallibilem sapientiam atque notitiam ejus, itemque secundum quod in libris conscientiarum contentum est.
paras.en: Like this is what we read in Daniel: [[Dan 7:9|thrones were placed|Throni positi sunt]], [[Dan 7:10|the judgment sat, and the books were opened|judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt]]. By all which it is signified that men are judged by God according to His infallible wisdom and knowledge, and likewise according to what is contained in the books of their consciences.

paras.t: Educam illud volumen egrediens, dicit Dominus exercituum; et veniet ad domum furis, et ad domum jurantis in nomine meo mendaciter : id est, punitio per istud volumen figurata, inducetur et infligetur furibus ac perjuris : quod ad Judæos præsertim refertur, in quibus vitia ista plurimum abundabant ante Babylonicam captivitatem. Et ita loquitur Propheta de præterito, tanquam futuro, sicut frequenter fit in libris propheticis. Et commorabitur, id est, punitio ista manebit, in medio domus ejus, id est in ipso fure seu perjuro et cunctis ad ipsum spectantibus, suæque pravitatis consortibus, et consumet eam et ligna ejus et lapides ejus, id est totam ejus congeriem sive familiam peccatricem, vel etiam habitacula ejus, dum comburuntur aut destruuntur.
paras.en: [[5:4|I will bring it forth|Educam illud]], the volume going forth, [[5:4|saith the Lord of hosts: and it shall come to the house of the thief, and to the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name|dicit Dominus exercituum; et veniet ad domum furis, et ad domum jurantis in nomine meo mendaciter]]: that is, the punishment figured by this volume shall be brought upon and inflicted on thieves and perjurers. This refers above all to the Jews, among whom these vices abounded greatly before the Babylonian captivity; and so the Prophet speaks of the past as though it were future, as is often done in the prophetic books. [[5:4|And it shall remain|Et commorabitur]], that is, this punishment shall abide, [[5:4|in the midst of his house|in medio domus ejus]], that is, in the thief or perjurer himself and in all that belong to him and share in his wickedness, [[5:4|and shall consume it, with the timber thereof, and the stones thereof|et consumet eam et ligna ejus et lapides ejus]], that is, his whole heap, or sinful household, or even his dwellings, when they are burned or destroyed.

paras.t: Denique ei quod nunc dictum est hic de volumine volante, simile est quod Ezechiel scribit de libro in quo continebantur lamentationes et væ. Ex his quoque secundum Hieronymum elucescit, quanta sit gravitas furti atque perjurii. Quod si in his (ut idem ait) quæ minora putantur peccata, videlicet furto ac perjurio, tanta pœnarum est comminatio : quid dicemus de fornicatione, adulterio, homicidio, sacrilegio, cunctisque criminibus quæ ab Apostolo inter carnis opera numerantur?
paras.en: Lastly, like what has now been said here of the flying volume is what Ezechiel writes of the book in which were contained lamentations and woe[[Ezech 2:9||]]. From these things too, according to Jerome, it shines out how grave are theft and perjury. And if (as he says) in these, which are thought the lesser sins, namely theft and perjury, so great a punishment is threatened, what shall we say of fornication, adultery, murder, sacrilege, and all the crimes which the Apostle numbers among the works of the flesh[[Gal 5:19||]][[Gal 5:21||]]?

paras.t: Consequenter inducitur alia visio, idololatriam præsertim concernens. Et egressus est angelus qui loquebatur in me, et stetit quasi coram me, et dixit ad me : Leva oculos tuos, et vide visione imaginaria, quid est hoc quod egreditur de templo et urbe Jerusalem et Judæa.
paras.en: Next another vision is brought in, concerning idolatry above all. [[5:5|And the angel went forth that spoke in me|Et egressus est angelus qui loquebatur in me]], and stood as it were before me [these words are not in the Vulgate text of the verse], [[5:5|and he said to me: Lift up thy eyes, and see|et dixit ad me : Leva oculos tuos, et vide]] by an imaginary vision [[5:5|what this is, that goeth forth|quid est hoc quod egreditur]] from the temple, the city of Jerusalem and Judæa.

paras.t: Et dixi : Quidnam est? Et ait : Hæc est amphora egrediens. Et dixit : Hæc est oculus eorum in universa terra, id est, amphora ista designat multiplicationem et collectionem iniquitatum Judæorum : per quam multiplicationem ipsi Judæi manifestati sunt cunctis gentibus, quales inter se fuerunt. Dum enim propter facinora sua hinc inde captivi translati sunt, innotuit omnibus qualia in terra propria egerunt peccata : sicque amphora ista fuit eorum oculus, id est causa præfatæ manifestationis eorum.
paras.en: [[5:6|And I said: What is it?|Et dixi : Quidnam est?]] [[5:6|And he said: This is a vessel going forth|Et ait : Hæc est amphora egrediens]]. [[5:6|And he said: This is their eye in all the earth|Et dixit : Hæc est oculus eorum in universa terra]], that is, this vessel [amphora, a large jar] signifies the multiplying and heaping up of the iniquities of the Jews: by which multiplying the Jews themselves were shown to all the nations for what they had been among themselves. For when, for their crimes, they were carried away captive hither and thither, it became known to all what sins they had committed in their own land; and so this vessel was their eye, that is, the cause of their being thus shown.

paras.t: Et ecce talentum plumbi portabatur, id est, plumbea massa ferebatur, vel jussione divina, vel ab angelo. Et ecce mulier una sedens in medio amphoræ.
paras.en: [[5:7|And behold a talent of lead was carried|Et ecce talentum plumbi portabatur]], that is, a mass of lead was borne, either at God's command or by the angel. [[5:7|and behold a woman sitting in the midst of the vessel|Et ecce mulier una sedens in medio amphoræ]].

paras.t: Et dixit angelus ad me : Hæc est impietas, id est idololatria : quæ antonomastice impietas nuncupatur, quum sit maxime contra Deum, sicut de ea ait beatus Job : Quæ est impietas maxima, et negatio contra Deum omnipotentem. Et projecit eam in medio amphoræ, id est, infra amphoram eam depressit, ita quod amplius foras non eminebat, nec apparebat ut ante, nec egredi poterat : id est, hanc impietatem aliis suis criminibus superposuerunt Judæi ante Babylonicam captivitatem. Et misit massam plumbeam in os ejus, scilicet amphoræ, eam superius claudens ob causas prætactas. Hæc massa significavit enormitatem et gravitatem vitiorum populi hujus.
paras.en: [[5:8|And he said|Et dixit]], the angel, to me: [[5:8|This is wickedness|Hæc est impietas]], that is, idolatry, which is called wickedness by antonomasia [that is, given the general name as the thing that most deserves it; impietas is properly ungodliness], since it is most of all against God, as blessed Job says of it: [[Job 31:28|Which is a very great iniquity, and a denial against the most high God|Quæ est impietas maxima, et negatio contra Deum omnipotentem]] [Denis reads impietas, "ungodliness", where the Vulgate has iniquitas, and "almighty God" for "the most high God"; Job is speaking of worshipping the sun and moon]. [[5:8|And he cast her into the midst of the vessel|Et projecit eam in medio amphoræ]], that is, he pressed her down within the vessel, so that she no longer stood out above it, nor appeared as before, nor could come out: that is, the Jews before the Babylonian captivity piled this wickedness on top of their other crimes. [[5:8|and cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof|Et misit massam plumbeam in os ejus]], namely of the vessel, closing it from above for the reasons touched on. This mass signified the enormity and heaviness of the vices of this people.

paras.t: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi : et ecce duæ mulieres egredientes de terra Israel, et spiritus, id est potestas diaboli, in aliis earum, id est, in processu et actu, vanitate, flatu, atque impulsu earum fuit; et habebant alas quasi alas milvi, id est, rapacissimæ erant et insidiosæ, quemadmodum milvus avis est rapax, semperque domesticis avibus insidians. Hæ duæ mulieres significabant, secundum Hieronymum, plebem decem tribuum ab Assyriis captam, et plebem duarum tribuum, scilicet Juda ac Benjamin, a Chaldæis vastatam. Alii per duas mulieres intelligunt duas has tribus. Et levaverunt amphoram inter cœlum et terram, id est, peccatorum suorum mensuram secum ferebant, quocumque ducebantur.
paras.en: [[5:9|And I lifted up my eyes and looked: and behold there came out two women|Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi : et ecce duæ mulieres egredientes]] from the land of Israel, [[5:9|and wind|et spiritus]], that is, the power of the devil, [[5:9|was in their wings|in aliis earum]] [the print has aliis, a slip for alis, "wings"], that is, was in their going and acting, their vanity, breath and impulse; [[5:9|and they had wings like the wings of a kite|et habebant alas quasi alas milvi]], that is, they were most rapacious and treacherous, as the kite is a bird of prey, always lying in wait for farmyard birds. These two women signified, according to Jerome, the people of the ten tribes taken captive by the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]], and the people of the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin, laid waste by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:1||]]. Others understand by the two women these two tribes. [[5:9|and they lifted up the vessel between the earth and the heaven|Et levaverunt amphoram inter cœlum et terram]], that is, they carried with them the measure of their sins wherever they were led.

paras.t: Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me: Quo istæ deferent amphoram? Et dixit ad me: Ut ædificetur ei domus in terra Sennaar, id est in terra Babylonis. Sennaar quippe est campus in quo filii Adam ædificaverunt turrim, ubi postea constructa est Babylon, sicuti in Genesi scribitur. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : In terra Babylonis. Et stabiliatur et ponatur ibi super basim suam. Per ista insinuatur, quod Judæi simul cum idololatria sua transferebantur in Babylonem, et illic domum seu mansionem sumpserunt; ipsaque idololatria horum taliter ibi super basim suam locata est, quod in terram Judææ ultra non rediit, saltem tam copiose et frequenter ut ante. Non enim Judæi post reversionem a Babylone idola coluerunt, nisi quidam, comparative pauci, sub rege Antiocho, secundum quod in libro Machabæorum describitur.
paras.en: [[5:10|And I said to the angel that spoke in me: Whither do these carry the vessel?|Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me: Quo istæ deferent amphoram?]] [[5:11|And he said to me: That a house may be built for it in the land of Sennaar|Et dixit ad me: Ut ædificetur ei domus in terra Sennaar]], that is, in the land of Babylon. For Sennaar is the plain in which the sons of Adam built the tower, where Babylon was afterwards built, as is written in Genesis[[Gen 10:10||]][[Gen 11:2||]][[Gen 11:4||]]. Hence the Septuagint translated: In the land of Babylon. [[5:11|and that it may be established, and set there upon its own basis|Et stabiliatur et ponatur ibi super basim suam]]. By these words it is intimated that the Jews were carried over into Babylon together with their idolatry, and there took up a house or dwelling; and their idolatry was so set there upon its own basis that it did not return any more into the land of Judæa, at least not so abundantly and so often as before. For after their return from Babylon the Jews did not worship idols, except some, comparatively few, under king Antiochus, as is described in the book of Machabees[[1 Mach 1:55||]][[1 Mach 2:16||]].

paras.t: PRÆTEREA, secundum spiritualem ac mysticum intellectum, non est difficile, ea quæ ad populum Judæorum relata sunt, generaliter omnibus gentibus applicare. Sicque per volumen volans, intelligi potest sacra Scriptura, quantum ad comminationes et increpationes quæ peccatoribus fiunt in ea. Idcirco vocatur maledictio, quia in ipsa omnium reproborum peccata atque tormenta conscripta sunt; egrediturque super faciem universæ terræ, quia ubique Scriptura ista vulgata est. Omnis quoque fur et perjurus et omnis transgressor, secundum quod ibi scriptum est, judicabitur atque damnabitur.
paras.en: MOREOVER, according to the spiritual and mystical sense, it is not hard to apply to all nations generally the things that have been related of the people of the Jews. And so by the flying volume can be understood Holy Scripture, as to the threats and rebukes made in it to sinners. It is called the curse because in it are written down the sins and the torments of all the reprobate; and it goes forth over the face of the whole earth because this Scripture has been spread abroad everywhere. Every thief, too, and perjurer, and every transgressor shall be judged and condemned according to what is written there.

paras.t: Insuper, per amphoram egredientem, intelligitur totius plebis iniquitas congregata, atque in tanta mensura multiplicata, ut divina exigente justitia, oporteat eam mox vindicari, ac per hoc omnibus declarari, quales exstiterint, qui tanta commiserunt flagitia, quum tamen vicissim boni fuerint reputati. Frequenter enim contingit, quosdam tanto interius gravioribus criminibus deformari, quanto exterius compositiores ac meliores videntur. In hujus amphoræ medio sedet mulier, quæ appellatur impietas, utpote sui ipsius amor privatus ac improbus, vel gloriatio in peccatis, vel propriæ culpæ defensio seu impœnitentia : quæ infra amphoram talento plumbi deprimitur atque includitur, quoniam vitiositatis suæ gravissimo pondere amplius ad loca inferni pœnalia mox trudetur.
paras.en: Further, by the vessel going forth is understood the iniquity of the whole people, gathered together and multiplied to so great a measure that, as divine justice demands, it must soon be punished, and thereby it be made known to all what sort of men they were who committed such great crimes, though they had in their turn been reputed good. For it often happens that some are disfigured within by graver crimes the more composed and better they seem without. In the midst of this vessel sits a woman who is called wickedness: that is, private and wicked love of oneself, or glorying in sins, or the defence of one's own fault, or impenitence; who is pressed down and shut in within the vessel by the talent of lead, since by the most heavy weight of her viciousness she will soon be thrust down further into the places of punishment in hell.

paras.t: At vero duæ mulieres de electorum Ecclesia egredientes, quæ amphoram istam ad terram Sennaar, id est Babyloniæ, portant, sunt collectio hæreticorum et inobedientium Christianorum, qui peccata sua quotidie deferunt ad Babylonem, id est ad terram confusionis et totius inordinationis, puta ad sortem et societatem reproborum, ad ecclesiam malignantium, vel certe ad locum tartareum, qui est terra miseriæ ac tenebrarum, ubi nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat. Prævaricatores namque dum in vitia prolabuntur, nec pœnitent, a mystico Christi corpore separantur, ac dæmoni incorporantur, ejusque damnando consortio connectuntur. Vel duæ mulieres amphoram deferentes, sunt amor voluptatis et timor adversitatis, quia hæc duo sunt omnium pene vitiorum origines. Hæc breviter tacta sint, ut detur lectori occasio subtilius cogitandi.
paras.en: But the two women going out of the Church of the elect, who carry this vessel to the land of Sennaar, that is, of Babylonia, are the gathering of heretics and of disobedient Christians, who daily carry their sins to Babylon, that is, to the land of confusion and of all disorder: to the lot and fellowship of the reprobate, for instance, to the church of the malignant, or indeed to the place of hell, which is [[Job 10:22|a land of misery and darkness|terra miseriæ ac tenebrarum]], where there is [[Job 10:22|no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth|nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat]]. For transgressors, when they slip into vices and do not repent, are cut off from the mystical body of Christ, and are made members of the devil, and are bound to his fellowship, which brings damnation. Or the two women carrying the vessel are the love of pleasure and the fear of adversity, because these two are the origins of almost all vices. Let these things be touched on briefly, so as to give the reader occasion to think more deeply.

6.title: Expositio litteralis capituli sexti: Et conversus sum, et levavi oculos meos.
6.title_en: Literal explanation of the sixth chapter: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes.

paras.t: In præsenti capitulo describit Propheta quadripartiti regni distinctionem ac successionem, Christi quoque adventum, et Ecclesiæ ab eo ædificationem.
paras.en: In the present chapter the Prophet describes the distinction and succession of the fourfold kingdom, and also the coming of Christ, and the building of the Church by him.

paras.t: Et conversus sum, et levavi oculos meos, et vidi. Hoc totum in exordio capituli præcedentis expositum recolo. Et ecce quatuor quadrigæ, id est quatuor regna, erant secundum imaginariam visionem seu propheticam repræsentationem, egredientes de medio duorum montium, id est secundum oracula Prophetarum, quoniam regnaverunt, atque in regnando sibi invicem successerunt, secundum modum et ordinem a Prophetis descriptum; et montes, montes ærei, id est, Prophetæ isti similes erant montibus æreis, propter stabilitatem mentis in Deo, constantiamque virtutum et inflexibilitatem animi a via justitiæ. Dicuntur autem Prophetæ montes, propter vitæ eminentiam, contemplationisque apicem, et gratiarum sublimitatem. Duo quoque vocantur : vel propter duo regna, de quibus fuerunt. Nam quidam de regno duarum tribuum, alii de regno decem tribuum exstiterunt. Vel per duos montes, specialiter intelliguntur Propheta hic Zacharias et Daniel, qui de præsenti materia evidentius prophetasse videntur.
paras.en: [[6:1|And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw|Et conversus sum, et levavi oculos meos, et vidi]]. All this I recall as having been explained at the beginning of the preceding chapter. [[6:1|and behold four chariots|Et ecce quatuor quadrigæ]], that is, four kingdoms, according to an imaginary vision [that is, a vision formed in the imagination, as distinct from a bodily and an intellectual vision] or prophetic representation, [[6:1|came out from the midst of two mountains|egredientes de medio duorum montium]], that is, according to the oracles of the Prophets: since they reigned, and in reigning succeeded one another, in the manner and order described by the Prophets; [[6:1|and the mountains were mountains of brass|et montes, montes ærei]], that is, these Prophets were like mountains of brass, because of the steadfastness of their mind in God, the constancy of their virtues, and the unbending firmness of their soul in the way of justice. Now the Prophets are called mountains because of the eminence of their life, the height of their contemplation, and the sublimity of their graces. And they are called two, either because of the two kingdoms they came from: for some arose from the kingdom of the two tribes, others from the kingdom of the ten tribes. Or by the two mountains are meant in particular the Prophet Zacharias here and Daniel[[Dan 2:1||]][[Dan 7:1||]], who seem to have prophesied of the present matter more plainly [the margin gives Dan. ii, vii: the statue of the four kingdoms and the four beasts].

paras.t: In quadriga prima equi rufi : id est, in regno atque exercitu Chaldæorum fuerunt reges sanguinarii et cruenti. Chaldæi namque sanguinem plurimum effuderunt, multos Judæorum occiderunt, et nimia crudelitate omnibus erant terribiles. Porro reges per equos congrue designantur, quoniam post se trahebant exercitum, ut equi quadrigas. In quadriga secunda equi nigri : id est, regno Persarum ac Medorum erant præsidentes, qui populo Judæorum summum horrorem ac tristitiam incusserunt, præsertim dum ad suggestionem Aman, Assuerus rex jussit universos Judæos in omni suo imperio simul interfici. Cambyses quoque rex filius Cyri contristavit Judæos, dum templum reædificari prohibuit. In quadriga tertia equi albi : id est, in regno Græcorum fuerunt reges Judæis valde faventes, videlicet Alexander rex Magnus, et Seleucus Asiæ rex. Quamvis enim Alexander adveniret Jerusalem ut eam destrueret, tamen obviante sibi in via summo Judæorum pontifice in pontificalibus cum ceteris sacerdotibus, magnam ei reverentiam fecit, asserens quod Deus Judæorum sibi in tali habitu apparuisset, sicque pacatus a Judæa discessit, quemadmodum in Scholastica historia plenius continetur. Et in quadriga quarta equi varii et fortes : id est, in imperio Romanorum fuerunt reges diversi ac præpotentes : quorum nonnulli fuerunt Judæis clementes, ut Octavianus atque Tiberius ; alii autem crudeles, ut Nero, Vespasianus et Adrianus.
paras.en: [[6:2|In the first chariot were red horses|In quadriga prima equi rufi]]: that is, in the kingdom and army of the Chaldeans there were bloodthirsty and cruel kings. For the Chaldeans shed very much blood, killed many of the Jews, and by their excessive cruelty were a terror to all. Kings are fittingly signified by horses, since they drew the army after them, as horses draw chariots. [[6:2|in the second chariot black horses|In quadriga secunda equi nigri]]: that is, those who presided over the kingdom of the Persians and Medes, who struck the Jewish people with the utmost horror and sorrow, above all when, at the suggestion of Aman, king Assuerus ordered all the Jews throughout his empire to be killed at once[[Esth 3:8||]]. Cambyses too, the king, the son of Cyrus, saddened the Jews when he forbade the temple to be rebuilt[[1 Esd 4:17||]] [in 1 Esdras 4 the king is called Artaxerxes; Denis follows those who take him to be Cambyses]. [[6:3|And in the third chariot white horses|In quadriga tertia equi albi]]: that is, in the kingdom of the Greeks there were kings very favourable to the Jews, namely king Alexander the Great, and Seleucus, king of Asia[[2 Mach 3:3||]]. For although Alexander came to Jerusalem to destroy it, yet when the high priest of the Jews met him on the way in his pontifical vestments with the other priests, he showed him great reverence, declaring that the God of the Jews had appeared to him in such a garb; and so, appeased, he departed from Judea, as is told more fully in the Scholastic History. [[6:3|and in the fourth chariot grisled horses, and strong ones|Et in quadriga quarta equi varii et fortes]]: that is, in the empire of the Romans there were diverse and very mighty kings [*varii*, "grisled", that is, of mixed colour, also means "diverse"]: some of whom were mild towards the Jews, as Octavian and Tiberius; others cruel, as Nero, Vespasian and Adrian.

paras.t: Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me : Quid sunt hæc, domine mi? id est, quid currus isti et equi significant? Et respondit angelus, et ait ad me : Isti sunt quatuor venti cœli, id est quatuor plagæ seu plagatores mundi, qui egrediuntur ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ, id est, divinæ pareant voluntati, in quantum divina justitia punivit peccatores per eos. Ita exponit Hieronymus. Vel, secundum alios : Isti sunt quatuor venti cœli, id est quatuor regna instar ventorum velociter per mundum currentia, atque in quatuor mundi partibus, in quibus oriuntur venti, exorta ; qui egrediuntur ad regnandum, ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ, id est, in potestate dominioque perdurent secundum tempus eis a Deo præfixum, de quo scriptum est in Daniele : Ipse mutat tempora et ætates, transfert regna atque constituit. Vel dicuntur venti cœli, id est ventilatores Synagogæ, quæ eis successive servivit : et ipsi divino præsentabuntur judicio.
paras.en: And I [[6:4|said to the angel that spoke in me|dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me]]: [[6:4|What are these, my lord?|Quid sunt hæc, domine mi?]] that is, what do these chariots and horses signify? [[6:5|And the angel answered, and said to me|Et respondit angelus, et ait ad me]]: [[6:5|These are the four winds of the heaven|Isti sunt quatuor venti cœli]], that is, the four strokes, or smiters, of the world [*plaga* means both a stroke and a region of the world, and the four winds blow from the four regions], [[6:5|which go forth to stand before the Lord of all the earth|qui egrediuntur ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ]], that is, they obey the divine will, inasmuch as divine justice punished sinners through them. So Jerome explains it. Or, according to others: [[6:5|These are the four winds of the heaven|Isti sunt quatuor venti cœli]], that is, four kingdoms running swiftly through the world like winds, and arisen in the four parts of the world in which the winds arise; [[6:5|which go forth|qui egrediuntur]] to reign, [[6:5|to stand before the Lord of all the earth|ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ]], that is, to last in power and dominion for the time fixed for them by God, of which it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 2:21|he changeth times and ages: taketh away kingdoms, and establisheth them|Ipse mutat tempora et ætates, transfert regna atque constituit]]. Or they are called winds of heaven, that is, winnowers [*ventilatores*, from *ventus*, "wind": those who fan and winnow] of the Synagogue, which served them in turn: and they themselves will be brought before the divine judgment.

paras.t: In qua erant equi nigri, id est Persæ ac Medi, egrediebantur de terra sua in terram aquilonis, id est versus Chaldæos ac Babylonem. Cyrus enim rex Persarum, et Darius rex Medorum, regnum Chaldæorum sunt demoliti. Et albi egressi sunt post eos, id est, Græci sive Macedones postea eamdem terram vastaverunt, scilicet Alexander Magnus, qui regnum Persarum ac Medorum in terra Chaldæa sibi subjugata regnantium, superavit. Et varii egressi sunt ad terram austri, id est, Romani imperium suum in plaga australi pugnando auxerunt. Qui autem erant robustissimi, id est præfati Romani, qui supra designati sunt per equos fortes ac varios, quorum regnum potentissimum fuit : propter quod a Daniele ferreum nuncupatur; exierunt de Italia, et quærebant ire et discurrere per omnem terram, quoniam totum sibi mundum subjecerunt. Et dixit eis angelus, vel Deus per angelum : Ite, perambulate terram, omnia regna vestro subjugantes imperio. Et perambulaverunt terram. Deo enim volente, Romani cetera regna propter eorum peccata impugnaverunt, atque vicerunt : non tamen a peccato excusantur, quia non recta intentione egerunt hoc.
paras.en: [[6:6|That in which were the black horses|In qua erant equi nigri]], that is, the Persians and Medes, [[6:6|went forth|egrediebantur]] from their own land [[6:6|into the land of the north|in terram aquilonis]], that is, towards the Chaldeans and Babylon. For Cyrus king of the Persians and Darius king of the Medes overthrew the kingdom of the Chaldeans[[Dan 5:30||]][[Dan 5:31||]]. [[6:6|and the white went forth after them|Et albi egressi sunt post eos]], that is, the Greeks or Macedonians afterwards laid waste the same land, namely Alexander the Great, who overcame the kingdom of the Persians and Medes, who were reigning in the land of Chaldea which they had subdued. [[6:6|and the grisled went forth to the land the south|Et varii egressi sunt ad terram austri]], that is, the Romans enlarged their empire by fighting in the southern region. [[6:7|And they that were most strong|Qui autem erant robustissimi]], that is, the aforesaid Romans, who were signified above by the strong and grisled horses, whose kingdom was the mightiest: for which reason Daniel calls it iron[[Dan 2:40||]]; [[6:7|went out|exierunt]] of Italy, [[6:7|and sought to go, and to run to and fro through all the earth|et quærebant ire et discurrere per omnem terram]], since they subjected the whole world to themselves. [[6:7|And he said|Et dixit]] to them, the angel, or God through the angel: [[6:7|Go, walk throughout the earth|Ite, perambulate terram]], subjugating all kingdoms to your empire. [[6:7|and they walked throughout the earth|Et perambulaverunt terram]]. For by God's will the Romans attacked the other kingdoms for their sins, and conquered them: yet they are not excused from sin, since they did not do this with a right intention.

paras.t: Et vocavit me angelus, mihi ista demonstrans, atque interpretans, et locutus est ad me, dicens : Ecce qui egrediuntur in terram aquilonis, id est Persæ ac Medi Babyloniam impugnantes, vel ut alii dicunt, Græci per albos equos designati, qui post Persas introierunt Chaldæam, requiescere fecerunt spiritum meum in terra aquilonis, id est, indignationem vel iram seu zelum justitiæ meæ contra Chaldæos impleverunt, ipsis Chaldæis oppressis. Deus namque crudelitatem Chaldæorum per prædictos punivit. Hoc in persona Dei loquitur angelus. Vel, secundum Hieronymum, Græci fecerunt requiescere spiritum prophetalem, quando Alexander rex in terra aquilonis dejecit regnum Persarum atque Medorum propter eorum peccata, sicut prædixit spiritus prophetalis.
paras.en: [[6:8|And he called me|Et vocavit me]], the angel, showing me these things and interpreting them, [[6:8|and spoke to me, saying|et locutus est ad me, dicens]]: [[6:8|Behold they that go forth into the land of the north|Ecce qui egrediuntur in terram aquilonis]], that is, the Persians and Medes attacking Babylonia, or, as others say, the Greeks, signified by the white horses, who entered Chaldea after the Persians, [[6:8|have quieted my spirit in the land of the north|requiescere fecerunt spiritum meum in terra aquilonis]] [literally "have made my spirit to rest"], that is, they have fulfilled the indignation, or anger, or zeal of my justice against the Chaldeans, the Chaldeans themselves being crushed. For God punished the cruelty of the Chaldeans through those just named. The angel says this in the person of God. Or, according to Jerome, the Greeks made the prophetic spirit rest, when king Alexander overthrew, in the land of the north, the kingdom of the Persians and Medes for their sins, as the prophetic spirit had foretold.

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens per angelum in me loquentem : Sume a transmigratione, id est Judæis in Babylonem ductis et inde reversis, vel quia iidem numero, vel iidem specie erant, videlicet transmigrantibus a Judæa in Babylonem. Et subduntur nomina eorum a quibus sumere debeat : ab Holdai, et a Tobia, et ab Idaia. Et venies tu in die illa, et intrabis in domum Josiæ filii Sophoniæ, qui venerunt de Babylone. Et sumes aurum et argentum, et facies ex eis coronas auri et argenti varietate distinctas in domo Josiæ, et pones unam in capite Jesu filii Josedec sacerdotis magni, et loqueris ad eum, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus. Hoc Hebræi de isto Jesu Judæorum summo sacerdote accipiunt, vel de ipso Zorobabel duce ipsorum : quorum uterque dictus sit Oriens, quia in similitudine germinis in bonis succrevit, profecit, et sub eis ortum sive constructum est templum. Propter quod subditur : Et subter eum orietur, id est, sub Jesu isto sive Zorobabel crescet ac perficietur ædificium templi, et ædificabit templum Domino : ambo enim principales fuerunt in templi reparatione.
paras.en: [[6:9|And the word of the Lord came to me, saying|Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens]] through the angel speaking in me: [[6:10|Take of them of the captivity|Sume a transmigratione]], that is, of the Jews led into Babylon and returned from there, called so either because they were the same in number, or the same in kind, as those who were carried from Judea into Babylon [that is, either the very persons who had been carried off, or men of the same people]. And the names are added of those from whom he is to take: [[6:10|of Holdai, and of Tobias, and of Idaias|ab Holdai, et a Tobia, et ab Idaia]]. [[6:10|thou shalt come in that day, and shalt go into the house of Josias, the son of Sophonias, who came out of Babylon|Et venies tu in die illa, et intrabis in domum Josiæ filii Sophoniæ, qui venerunt de Babylone]]. [[6:11|And thou shalt take gold and silver|Et sumes aurum et argentum]], [[6:11|and shalt make|et facies]] of them [[6:11|crowns|coronas]] distinguished by the variety of gold and silver, in the house of Josias, [[6:11|and thou shalt set|et pones]] one [[6:11|on the head of Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest|in capite Jesu filii Josedec sacerdotis magni]], [[6:12|And thou shalt speak to him, saying|et loqueris ad eum, dicens]]: [[6:12|Thus saith the Lord of hosts|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum]]: [[6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]]. The Hebrews take this of this Jesus, the high priest of the Jews, or of Zorobabel himself, their leader: either of whom may have been called the Orient [*Oriens* means "the one rising" or "springing up"; hence *orietur*, "shall spring up", and the likeness of a growing shoot], because like a shoot he grew up in good things and went forward, and under them the temple rose, or was built. Hence it is added: [[6:12|and under him shall he spring up|Et subter eum orietur]], that is, under this Jesus or Zorobabel the building of the temple will grow and be completed, [[6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]]: for both were the chief men in the restoring of the temple.

paras.t: Et ipse exstruet templum Domino. Et ipse portabit gloriam : id est, Zorobabel alteram feret coronam, vel Jesus filius Josedec portabit pontificatus honorem atque decorem ; et ipse sedebit et dominabitur super solio suo : alter quippe præfuit in regimine spirituali, alter in temporali. Et erit sacerdos super solio suo : id est, Jesus iste sedebit ut pontifex in pontificali throno. Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos : id est, Jesus iste et Zorobabel in populi gubernatione unanimes erunt.
paras.en: [[6:13|Yea, he shall build a temple to the Lord|Et ipse exstruet templum Domino]]. [[6:13|and he shall bear the glory|Et ipse portabit gloriam]]: that is, Zorobabel will wear the other crown, or Jesus the son of Josedec will bear the honour and dignity of the high priesthood; [[6:13|and shall sit, and rule upon his throne|et ipse sedebit et dominabitur super solio suo]]: for the one presided in spiritual government, the other in temporal. [[6:13|and he shall be a priest upon his throne|Et erit sacerdos super solio suo]]: that is, this Jesus will sit as high priest on the pontifical throne. [[6:13|and the counsel of peace shall be between them both|Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]]: that is, this Jesus and Zorobabel will be of one mind in governing the people.
