paras.t: Et coronæ erunt Helem, et Tobiæ, et Idaiæ, et Hen filio Sophoniæ, memoriale in templo Domini : id est, coronæ prædictæ postquam in capitibus summi sacerdotis principisque fuerint, tollentur et consecrabuntur in templo ad ornatum ac reverentiam ejus, in memoriam prædictorum virorum, de quorum argento et auro factæ fuerunt.
paras.en: [[6:14|And the crowns shall be to Helem, and Tobias, and Idaias, and to Hem, the son of Sophonias, a memorial in the temple of the Lord|Et coronæ erunt Helem, et Tobiæ, et Idaiæ, et Hen filio Sophoniæ, memoriale in templo Domini]]: that is, the aforesaid crowns, after they have been on the heads of the high priest and of the prince, will be taken off and consecrated in the temple, for its adornment and honour, in memory of the aforesaid men, of whose silver and gold they were made.

paras.t: Et qui procul sunt a vobis, puta gentiles, vel Judæi qui hucusque in terris gentilium remanserunt, venient in Jerusalem, et ædificabunt in templo Domini, illud ordinando, ditando, seu perficiendo : sicut in libro Machabæorum scriptum est, quod reges et principes locum summo honore dignum duxerunt, et templum maximis muneribus illustraverunt. Et scietis per prophetiæ meæ evidentem impletionem, quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad vos ad prænuntiandum et faciendum hæc omnia. Etenim per impositionem coronæ super caput pontificis, figurabatur prosperatio sacerdotii sui et consummatio templi.
paras.en: [[6:15|And they that are far off|Et qui procul sunt]] from you, such as the gentiles, or the Jews who till now have remained in the lands of the gentiles, [[6:15|shall come|venient]] to Jerusalem, [[6:15|and shall build in the temple of the Lord|et ædificabunt in templo Domini]], by ordering it, enriching it, or completing it: as it is written in the book of the Machabees that [[2 Mach 3:2|the kings themselves and the princes esteemed the place worthy of the highest honour, and glorified the temple with very great gifts|reges et principes locum summo honore dignum duxerunt, et templum maximis muneribus illustraverunt]]. [[6:15|and you shall know|Et scietis]], through the evident fulfilment of my prophecy, [[6:15|that the Lord of hosts sent me to you|quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad vos]] to foretell and to do all these things. For by the placing of the crown upon the high priest's head was figured the prospering of his priesthood and the completion of the temple.

paras.t: Præterea, teste Hieronymo, Hebræi affirmant Ananiam, Azariam et Misael de Babylone redisse, et aurum ac argentum in oblationem templi et pro faciendis coronis summi sacerdotis ac ducis, secum tulisse, Danielem quoque venisse cum donis.
paras.en: Moreover, as Jerome testifies, the Hebrews affirm that Ananias, Azarias and Misael returned from Babylon and brought with them gold and silver as an offering for the temple and for making the crowns of the high priest and of the leader, and that Daniel too came with gifts.

paras.t: Erit autem hoc, id est, prædicta implebuntur, si auditu audieritis vocem Domini Dei vestri, id est, auribus mentis verba Prophetarum adverteritis, credendo eis ac obediendo. Et bene ait Propheta, Erit hoc, si, etc., quoniam promissiones divinæ, similiter comminationes, quæ fiunt in sacra Scriptura, frequenter intelligendæ sunt sub conditione, videlicet si illi quibus fit promissio, non demereantur, sed in bono persistant, illi quoque quibus fit comminatio, in vitiis perseverent. Propterea per Jeremiam Dominus ait : Repente loquar adversus gentem et regnum, ut eradicem et destruam illud; si pœnitentiam egerit gens illa, agam et ego pœnitentiam super malo quod cogitavi ut facerem ei. Et repente loquar de gente et regno, ut ædificem et plantem illud; si fecerit malum in oculis meis, pœnitentiam agam super bono quod locutus sum ut facerem ei.
paras.en: [[6:15|But this shall come to pass|Erit autem hoc]], that is, the foregoing will be fulfilled, [[6:15|if hearing you will hear the voice of the Lord your God|si auditu audieritis vocem Domini Dei vestri]], that is, if with the ears of the mind you heed the words of the Prophets, believing and obeying them. And the Prophet says well, [[6:15|this shall come to pass|Erit hoc]], if, etc., since the divine promises, and likewise the threats, made in holy Scripture are often to be understood under a condition: namely, the promise, if those to whom it is made do not forfeit it by their deserts but persevere in good; the threat likewise, if those to whom it is made persevere in their vices. Therefore the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 18:7|I will suddenly speak against a nation, and against a kingdom, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy it.|Repente loquar adversus gentem et regnum, ut eradicem et destruam illud]]; [[Jer 18:8|If that nation against which I have spoken, shall repent of their evil, I also will repent of the evil that I have thought to do to them.|si pœnitentiam egerit gens illa, agam et ego pœnitentiam super malo quod cogitavi ut facerem ei]]. [[Jer 18:9|And I will suddenly speak of a nation and of a kingdom, to build up and plant it.|Et repente loquar de gente et regno, ut ædificem et plantem illud]]; [[Jer 18:10|If it shall do evil in my sight, that it obey not my voice: I will repent of the good that I have spoken to do unto it.|si fecerit malum in oculis meis, pœnitentiam agam super bono quod locutus sum ut facerem ei]].

paras.t: Denique, ut quidam catholice dicunt, ubi nostra translatio continet, Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, translatio Chaldaica, quæ apud Judæos authentica fertur, sic habet : Ecce vir, Messias nomen ejus. Sicque locus iste ad litteram intelligendus est de Domino Jesu Christo : qui est vir de quo in Jeremia habetur, Mulier circumdabit virum ; et Oriens appellatur, tanquam splendor lucis æternæ, et quia in diebus ejus orta est justitia et abundantia pacis, sicut Psalmista prædixit. Et subter eum orietur, id est, se ipsum exinaniet, formam servilem assumens : ita quod secundum naturam humanam, qua temporaliter orietur ex Virgine, erit se ipso inferior quoad naturam divinam, qua æternaliter oritur a Patre. Et ædificabit templum Domino, id est Ecclesiam Deo Patri, vel Deo omnipotenti, trino ac simplici, ex electis tanquam ex vivis lapidibus. De qua ædificatione dicit Apostolus ad Ephesios : In Christo omnis ædificatio constructa crescit in templum sanctum in Domino, in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto. Hæc est ædificatio spiritualis, qua corda humana per fidem, caritatem et spem, ceterasque virtutes junguntur, et templum Divinitatis efficiuntur, I Petr. ii, secundum quod Petrus inducit : Ad Christum accedentes lapidem vivum, et ipsi tanquam lapides vivi superædificamini in domos spirituales.
paras.en: Lastly, as some say in a catholic sense, where our translation has [[6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]], the Chaldee translation, which is held authoritative among the Jews, reads thus: Behold a man, Messias is his name. And so this passage is to be understood literally of the Lord Jesus Christ: who is the man of whom it is said in Jeremias, [[Jer 31:22|A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Mulier circumdabit virum]]; and he is called the Orient, as the brightness of eternal light, and because, as the Psalmist foretold, [[Ps 71:7|In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace|in diebus ejus orta est justitia et abundantia pacis]] [Denis says *orta est*, "has sprung up", where the Psalm has *orietur*, "shall spring up"]. [[6:12|and under him shall he spring up|Et subter eum orietur]], that is, he will empty himself, taking the form of a servant[[Phil 2:7||]]: so that according to the human nature, in which he will spring up in time from the Virgin, he will be lower than himself as to the divine nature, in which he springs eternally from the Father. [[6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|Et ædificabit templum Domino]], that is, the Church, to God the Father, or to God almighty, three and simple, out of the elect as out of living stones. Of this building the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:21|In whom all the building, being framed together, groweth up into an holy temple in the Lord|In Christo omnis ædificatio constructa crescit in templum sanctum in Domino]], [[Eph 2:22|In whom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the Spirit|in quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto]]. This is the spiritual building by which human hearts are joined together through faith, charity and hope, and the other virtues, and are made a temple of the Godhead (1 Pet. 2), according to what Peter brings in: [[1 Pet 2:4|Unto whom coming, as to a living stone|Ad Christum accedentes lapidem vivum]], [[1 Pet 2:5|Be you also as living stones built up, a spiritual house|et ipsi tanquam lapides vivi superædificamini in domos spirituales]].

paras.t: Et ipse portabit gloriam, id est, principatum universorum, et corporis glorificationem accepit in resurrectione, juxta illud ad Hebræos : Eum, qui modico quam angeli minoratus est, videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis gloria et honore coronatum. De quo ait Psalmista : Magna gloria ejus in salutari tuo; gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum. Et sedebit ad dexteram Patris in die ascensionis, et dominabitur in omni creatura super solio suo : de quo ait in Apocalypsi, Qui vicerit, dabo ei sedere mecum in throno meo; Apostolus quoque ad Hebræos, Adeamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus. Assumptus est enim in cœlum, et sedet ad dexteram Patris, secundum Marcum. Vel solium Christi, est judiciaria ejus potestas, vel ipsa Ecclesia.
paras.en: [[6:13|and he shall bear the glory|Et ipse portabit gloriam]], that is, the sovereignty over all things; and he received the glorification of his body in the resurrection, according to that saying to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:9|But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour|Eum, qui modico quam angeli minoratus est, videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis gloria et honore coronatum]]. Of him the Psalmist says: [[Ps 20:6|His glory is great in thy salvation: glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.|Magna gloria ejus in salutari tuo; gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum]]. [[6:13|and shall sit|Et sedebit]] at the right hand of the Father on the day of the ascension, [[6:13|and rule|et dominabitur]] in all creation [[6:13|upon his throne|super solio suo]]: of which he says in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 3:21|To him that shall overcome, I will give to sit with me in my throne|Qui vicerit, dabo ei sedere mecum in throno meo]]; and the Apostle too, to the Hebrews, [[Heb 4:16|Let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace|Adeamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus]]. For he [[Mark 16:19|was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|Assumptus est enim in cœlum, et sedet ad dexteram Patris]], according to Mark. Or the throne of Christ is his power as judge, or the Church itself.

paras.t: Et erit sacerdos super solio suo. Est enim sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Et ut ait Apostolus ad Hebræos, Christus eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium. Ipse namque est princeps pastorum, mediator Dei et hominum, semper vivens ad interpellandum pro nobis. De quo ait princeps Apostolorum : Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum. Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos, id est populum Judæorum, atque gentilium in Christum credentium, ex quibus constructa est una Ecclesia, uno Dei Spiritu congregata.
paras.en: [[6:13|and he shall be a priest upon his throne|Et erit sacerdos super solio suo]]. For he is [[Ps 109:4|a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech|sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech]]. And, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews, Christ, [[Heb 7:24|for that he continueth for ever, hath an everlasting priesthood|eo quod maneat in æternum, sempiternum habet sacerdotium]]. For he is the prince of pastors, the mediator of God and men, [[Heb 7:25|always living to make intercession for us|semper vivens ad interpellandum pro nobis]]. Of him the prince of the Apostles says: [[1 Pet 2:25|you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls|Conversi estis ad pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum]] [the margin gives 1 Pet. v, 25; the words are at 1 Pet 2:25]. [[6:13|and the counsel of peace shall be between them both|Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]], that is, the people of the Jews and that of the gentiles believing in Christ, of whom the one Church has been built, gathered together by the one Spirit of God.

paras.t: Postremo, quum Jesus filius Josedec summus sacerdos fuerit Christi figura re et appellatione, convenienter Propheta quum locutus fuisset de illo, qui fuit figura, inseruit prophetiam de figurato, quemadmodum alibi sæpius in Scripturis de figurato transitur ad figuram sub eodem contextu, propter similitudinem eorum ad invicem, sicut in Isaia et Ezechiele de rege Babylonis et principe Tyri atque diabolo fit sermo permixtum.
paras.en: Lastly, since Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest, was a figure of Christ both in fact and in name [he bore the same name, *Jesus*], the Prophet, having spoken of him who was the figure, fittingly inserted a prophecy of the one figured; just as elsewhere in the Scriptures there is often a passing from the thing figured to the figure within the same context, because of their likeness to each other: as in Isaias and Ezechiel the discourse is mixed, about the king of Babylon[[Is 14:1||]] and the prince of Tyre[[Ezech 28:1||]] and about the devil [the margin gives Is. xiv and Ezech. xxviii; the passages begin at Is 14:4 and Ezech 28:2].

paras.t: At vero juxta mysticum intellectum, spiritualis Zacharias, id est contemplativus, Dei jugiter reminiscens, ait : Et conversus sum a multis ad unum (unum enim est necessarium), ab exterioribus et terrenis ad interiora atque divina. Et levavi oculos mentales ab infimis ad superna. Levantur nempe, dum contemplantur cœlestia; deprimuntur, dum sensibilibus immerguntur. Et vidi, et ecce quatuor quadrigæ, id est quatuor libri Evangelistarum, seu quatuor Evangelia, quibus homines vehuntur de terra ad cœlum : quæ licet sint unum ex parte objecti, videlicet Christi, de quo loquuntur, quatuor tamen sunt ex parte describentium ea; egredientes de medio duorum montium, id est a Christo, cujus verba in Evangelio principalissime recitantur, et a Moyse seu veteri Testamento, cujus scripta in libris evangelicis sæpius allegantur. Hi montes sunt æræi, id est in virtutibus valde robusti.
paras.en: But according to the mystical sense, the spiritual Zacharias, that is, the contemplative, who continually remembers God [the name *Zacharias* is interpreted "remembrance of the Lord"], says: [[6:1|And I turned|Et conversus sum]] from many things to one (for [[Luke 10:42|one thing is necessary|unum enim est necessarium]]), from outward and earthly things to inward and divine ones. And I [[6:1|lifted up my eyes|levavi oculos]], the eyes of my mind, from the lowest things to those on high. For they are lifted up when they contemplate heavenly things, and weighed down when they are sunk in the things of sense. [[6:1|and saw: and behold four chariots|Et vidi, et ecce quatuor quadrigæ]], that is, the four books of the Evangelists, or the four Gospels, by which men are carried from earth to heaven: which, though they are one on the side of their object, namely Christ, of whom they speak, are yet four on the side of those who wrote them; [[6:1|came out from the midst of two mountains|egredientes de medio duorum montium]], that is, from Christ, whose words are above all recounted in the Gospel, and from Moses, or the old Testament, whose writings are very often cited in the books of the Gospel. These mountains are [[6:1|mountains of brass|montes sunt æræi]], that is, very strong in the virtues.

paras.t: In quadriga prima equi rufi : id est, in evangelio S. Matthæi sunt, qui pro Christo sanguinem fuderunt, sicut ipse Matthæus et similes ei, qui istam quadrigam post se traxerunt, verba evangelica semper secum ferentes : qui martyrio rufi sunt. In quadriga secunda equi nigri : id est, in evangelio Marci sunt, qui maximis in hoc sæculo tribulationibus obscurantur, sicut et Marcus etiam ante suam pro Christo occisionem, eique similes, quorum tota vita adversitatibus singulariter plena est. In quadriga tertia equi albi : id est, in evangelio Lucæ sunt, virgineæ munditiæ observatores, quemadmodum Lucas, qui etiam de beatissima Virgine et Christi innocentissima pueritia plenius scripsit, et similes ejus, qui hujus evangelii documenta specialiter secum deportant. Et in quadriga quarta equi varii et fortes : id est, in evangelio Joannis sunt, viri perfecti, activi, simul et contemplativi, variisque gratiarum charismatibus singulariter adornati, quales fuerunt præsertim Apostoli, deinde apostolicæ perfectionis viri.
paras.en: [[6:2|In the first chariot were red horses|In quadriga prima equi rufi]]: that is, in the gospel of St. Matthew are those who shed their blood for Christ, as did Matthew himself and those like him, who drew this chariot after them, ever carrying the words of the gospel with them: these are red with martyrdom. [[6:2|in the second chariot black horses|In quadriga secunda equi nigri]]: that is, in the gospel of Mark are those who are darkened by the greatest tribulations in this world, as Mark was too, even before his death for Christ, and those like him, whose whole life is singularly full of adversities. [[6:3|And in the third chariot white horses|In quadriga tertia equi albi]]: that is, in the gospel of Luke are the keepers of virginal cleanness, like Luke, who also wrote more fully of the most blessed Virgin and of the most innocent childhood of Christ, and those like him, who carry the teachings of this gospel with them in a special way. [[6:3|and in the fourth chariot grisled horses, and strong ones|Et in quadriga quarta equi varii et fortes]]: that is, in the gospel of John are perfect men, active and at the same time contemplative, and singularly adorned with the various gifts of graces, such as were above all the Apostles, and after them the men of apostolic perfection.

paras.t: Isti libri sunt quatuor venti cœli: quoniam omnium in quatuor mundi partibus demorantium corda dulciter atque celeriter perflaverunt, quemadmodum scriptum est: Velociter currit sermo ejus; qui egrediuntur ex ore Evangelistarum, ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ, id est, a Christo approbantur et confirmantur, juxta illud Marci: Prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis.
paras.en: [[6:5|These|Isti]] books [[6:5|are the four winds of the heaven|sunt quatuor venti cœli]]: since they have breathed sweetly and swiftly upon the hearts of all who dwell in the four parts of the world, as it is written: [[Ps 147:4|his word runneth swiftly|Velociter currit sermo ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 15, the Hebrew numbering]; [[6:5|which go forth|qui egrediuntur]] from the mouth of the Evangelists, [[6:5|to stand before the Lord of all the earth|ut stent coram Dominatore universæ terræ]], that is, they are approved and confirmed by Christ, according to that saying of Mark: they [[Mark 16:20|preached every where: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed|Prædicaverunt ubique, Domino cooperante, et sermonem confirmante sequentibus signis]].

paras.t: In qua erant equi nigri, egrediebantur in terram aquilonis, id est ad eos qui in frigore vitiorum morantur, a quibus et adversa multa perpessi sunt; et albi egressi sunt post eos, quia virginalis puritatis candore fulgentes, prædicaverunt eisdem. Qui autem erant robustissimi, quærebant discurrere per omnem terram, puta Apostoli, qui ceteris latius prædicaverunt, ita quod in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum : quibus et Christus, Eritis (inquit) mihi testes usque ad ultimum terræ. Denique qui egressi sunt in terram aquilonis, requiescere fecerunt spiritum Dei in terra aquilonis : quia quos converterunt ad fidem, inhabitari fecerunt a Spiritu Sancto.
paras.en: [[6:6|That in which were the black horses went forth into the land of the north|In qua erant equi nigri, egrediebantur in terram aquilonis]], that is, to those who dwell in the cold of vices, from whom they also suffered many adversities; [[6:6|and the white went forth after them|et albi egressi sunt post eos]], because, shining with the whiteness of virginal purity, they preached to the same. [[6:7|And they that were most strong|Qui autem erant robustissimi]] [[6:7|sought|quærebant]] [[6:7|to run to and fro through all the earth|discurrere per omnem terram]], namely the Apostles, who preached more widely than the rest, so that [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]: to whom Christ too said, [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses|Eritis]] (he says) [[Acts 1:8|unto me|mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|even to the uttermost part of the earth|usque ad ultimum terræ]]. Lastly, [[6:8|they that go forth into the land of the north|qui egressi sunt in terram aquilonis]] [[6:8|have quieted|requiescere fecerunt]] the [[6:8|spirit|spiritum]] of God [[6:8|in the land of the north|in terra aquilonis]] [literally "have made the spirit of God to rest"]: because those whom they converted to the faith they caused to be indwelt by the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Porro a transmigratione, hoc est ab his qui de vitiis redeunt ad virtutes, et de via ad patriam properant, considerantes se hic non habere manentem civitatem, sumitur aurum et argentum, id est vita caritate fulcita atque scientia clara. Ex quibus fiunt coronæ quæ ponuntur in capite Jesu, id est animarum varia ornamenta ac divina præconia, quæ omnia Christo principaliter adscribuntur. Per Jesum quoque intelligi potest quicumque efficax pastor, idoneusque sacerdos, cui virtutes et merita gregis sibi commissi non immerito, tanquam dispositivo principio, attribuuntur: et ipse eisdem ornatur, sicut quosdam discipulorum suorum Paulus apostolus asserit suam esse coronam in Christi adventu. Et Joannes in tertia sua Canonica: Majorem, inquit, horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes. Talis quippe audiet a Christo: Euge, serve bone et fidelis, quia super pauca fuisti fidelis, supra multa te constituam. Insuper talis meretur audire atque laudari his verbis:
paras.en: Furthermore, [[6:10|of them of the captivity|a transmigratione]], that is, of those who return from vices to virtues, and hasten from the way to the fatherland, considering that they [[Heb 13:14|have not here a lasting city|hic non habere manentem civitatem]], is taken [[6:11|gold and silver|aurum et argentum]], that is, a life upheld by charity and bright with knowledge. Of these are made [[6:11|crowns|coronæ]] which are set [[6:11|on the head of Jesus|in capite Jesu]], that is, the various adornments and divine praises of souls, all of which are ascribed principally to Christ. By Jesus can also be understood any effective pastor and fit priest, to whom the virtues and merits of the flock committed to him are not undeservedly attributed, as to their disposing principle [that is, the one who prepares and disposes them for grace, God being their principal cause]: and he himself is adorned with them; as the apostle Paul declares certain of his disciples to be his crown at the coming of Christ[[1 Thess 2:19||]]. And John in his third canonical epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace|Majorem]], he says, [[3 John 1:4|than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes]]. For such a one will hear from Christ: [[Matt 25:21|Well done, good and faithful servant, because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things|Euge, serve bone et fidelis, quia super pauca fuisti fidelis, supra multa te constituam]][[Matt 25:23||]]. Moreover such a one deserves to hear, and to be praised in, these words:

paras.t: Ecce vir, a vigore virtutum animique virore ex gratiæ innovatione, Oriens nomen ejus. Quum enim quotidie oriatur in eo Christus per gratiam pleniorem, et ipse renovetur in Spiritu Sancto, fiatque fecundus in sanctis operibus, recte Oriens nuncupatur. Et subter eum orietur, id est, sub ipso prosperatur in spiritualibus plebs sive Ecclesia sibi commissa; et ædificabit templum Domino, id est, Christo parabit plebem fidelem, et in cordibus gregis sui construet Deo conscientiæ domum; facietque congregationem cui præsidet, esse habitaculum Spiritus Sancti, non dæmonum, expellendo ab eis dominium vitiorum atque insidias diabolorum. Hoc utique pertinet ad omnem prælatum.
paras.en: [[6:12|BEHOLD A MAN|Ecce vir]], from the vigour of his virtues and the freshness of his soul through the renewal of grace [Denis derives *vir*, "man", from *vigor*, "vigour", and *viror*, "greenness"], [[6:12|THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Oriens nomen ejus]]. For since Christ daily rises in him by fuller grace, and he himself is renewed in the Holy Ghost and becomes fruitful in holy works, he is rightly named the Orient. [[6:12|and under him shall he spring up|Et subter eum orietur]], that is, under him the people, or the Church, committed to him prospers in spiritual things; [[6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]], that is, he will prepare a faithful people for Christ, and in the hearts of his flock will build for God a house of conscience; and he will make the congregation over which he presides a dwelling of the Holy Ghost, not of demons, by driving out from them the dominion of vices and the snares of the devils. This indeed belongs to every prelate.

paras.t: Et ipse portabit gloriam, quia cooperator atque vicarius Christi est, et prælationis sacerdotiique honorem digne possidet. Maximum quoque a Deo præmium sortietur. Unde ad Timotheum ait Apostolus: Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni habeantur. Imo, secundum divinum Dionysium, divinissimum est Deo cooperari in animarum reductione ad Deum. Et dominabitur sibi commissis spirituali regimine cum omni humilitate, sollicitudine, ac timore. Et erit sacerdos re et nomine, sacra subditis administrando, eorumque preces et vota Deo fideliter offerendo. Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos, id est inter quoscumque subditorum suorum prius aliquando discordantes: quoniam quantum in se est, debet omnis prælatus indesinenter conari, ut subditi inter se pacifice conversentur. Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Simili ratione, infelices discordes, quoniam filii dæmonis probabuntur. Ideo ad Hebræos dicitur : Pacem sequimini cum omnibus, sine qua nemo Deum videbit.
paras.en: [[6:13|and he shall bear the glory|Et ipse portabit gloriam]], because he is the fellow worker and vicar of Christ, and worthily possesses the honour of prelacy and of the priesthood. He will also obtain the greatest reward from God. Hence the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 5:17|Let the priests that rule well be esteemed worthy of double honour|Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, duplici honore digni habeantur]]. Indeed, according to the divine Dionysius, the most divine of all things is to be God's fellow worker in leading souls back to God [Dionysius, *Celestial Hierarchy*, ch. 3]. [[6:13|and rule|Et dominabitur]] over those committed to him by spiritual government, with all humility, solicitude and fear. [[6:13|and he shall be a priest|Et erit sacerdos]] in fact and in name, administering sacred things to his subjects and faithfully offering their prayers and vows to God. [[6:13|and the counsel of peace shall be between them both|Et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]], that is, between any of his subjects who were before at some time at odds: since, as far as in him lies, every prelate ought to strive unceasingly that his subjects live peaceably among themselves. For [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.|Beati enim pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur]]. By the same reasoning, unhappy are the quarrelsome, for they will be shown to be children of the devil. Therefore it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace with all men|Pacem sequimini cum omnibus]], [[Heb 12:14|without which no man shall see God|sine qua nemo Deum videbit]].

paras.t: Et qui procul sunt, id est, per dissimilitudinem vitiorum longe distant a Deo et a conversatione electorum ipsius, venient per pœnitentiam salutarem, et ædificabunt in templo Domini, id est, in Ecclesia Christi virtuose operabuntur, et proximos bonis exemplis roborare curabunt. Boni enim prælati tales frequenter convertunt, ita ut ubi abundavit iniquitas, abundet et gratia. Hinc in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea.
paras.en: [[6:15|And they that are far off|Et qui procul sunt]], that is, those who through the unlikeness of their vices stand far from God and from the company of his elect, [[6:15|shall come|venient]] by saving penance, [[6:15|and shall build in the temple of the Lord|et ædificabunt in templo Domini]], that is, they will work virtuously in the Church of Christ, and take care to strengthen their neighbours by good example. For good prelates often convert such men, so that [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|ubi abundavit iniquitas, abundet et gratia]]. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein.|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]].

paras.t: Postremo coronæ erunt Helem, et Tobiæ, et Idaiæ, etc., id est, quamvis ornamenta ista virtutum atque donorum exsistentium in mentibus subditorum eorum, prælatis, et maxime Christo, attribuantur, nihilo minus remanent eis et decorantur eisdem; suntque eis memoriale in templo Domini, id est, in Ecclesia militanti merentur per ea perpetuam, honorabilem, ac felicem habere memoriam. Deus enim glorificantes se glorificat. Et Salomon ait : Memoria justi cum laudibus; nomen autem impiorum putrescet. Videmus namque ad oculum, quam præclare atque magnifice Deus sanctos suos in tota Ecclesia mirificet et exaltet : tanto plane sublimius, quo illi gloriam et honorem Dei sincerius intenderunt et acquisierunt.
paras.en: Lastly, [[6:14|the crowns shall be to Helem, and Tobias, and Idaias|coronæ erunt Helem, et Tobiæ, et Idaiæ]], etc., that is, although these adornments of the virtues and gifts that exist in the minds of their subjects are attributed to the prelates, and above all to Christ, they nonetheless remain the subjects' own, and the subjects are adorned with them; and they are to them [[6:14|a memorial in the temple of the Lord|memoriale in templo Domini]], that is, in the Church militant they merit by them a perpetual, honourable and happy memory. For God glorifies those who glorify him[[1 Kings 2:30||]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 10:7|The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot.|Memoria justi cum laudibus; nomen autem impiorum putrescet]]. For we see with our own eyes how splendidly and magnificently God makes his saints wonderful and exalts them throughout the Church: the more sublimely, plainly, the more sincerely they aimed at and won the glory and honour of God.

7.title: Expositio capituli septimi: Et factum est in anno quarto Darii regis.
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius.

paras.t: Et factum est in anno quarto Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam, in quarta mensis noni, id est die quarto mensis noni, qui est Casleu, id est, in lingua Hebræa ita vocatur. Et miserunt ad domum Dei quidam adhuc in Babylonia demorantes, videlicet Sarasar et Rogomelech, et viri qui erant cum eis. Isti miserunt nuntios ad templum, ad deprecandum faciem Domini, quatenus ministri templi, et prophetæ ac ceteri justi, ac ipsi quoque eorum nuntii, orarent Deum verum pro ipsis, qui in templo illo specialiter se esse, habitare, et exaudire asseruit. Itaque Sarasar iste non fuit unus de nuntiis, ut quidam affirmant. Multi insuper dicunt, viros præfatos fuisse Judæos. Hieronymus vero refert, quod Hebræi dicunt eos fuisse Persas et duces Darii regis, Deum timentes.
paras.en: [[7:1|And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius, that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah|Et factum est in anno quarto Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam]], [[7:1|in the fourth day of the ninth month|in quarta mensis noni]], that is, on the fourth day of the ninth month [the Latin says only *in quarta*, "on the fourth", leaving "day" to be understood], [[7:1|which is Casleu|qui est Casleu]], that is, it is so called in the Hebrew tongue. And certain men still dwelling in Babylonia [[7:2|sent to the house of God|Et miserunt ad domum Dei]], namely [[7:2|Sarasar|Sarasar]] and Rogomelech, [[7:2|and the men that were with him|et viri qui erant cum eis]] [Denis reads *cum eis*, "with them"]. These sent messengers to the temple, [[7:2|to entreat the face of the Lord|ad deprecandum faciem Domini]], so that the ministers of the temple, and the prophets and the other just men, and also their own messengers, might pray for them to the true God, who declared that he was present, dwelt and gave ear in a special way in that temple. So this Sarasar was not one of the messengers, as some maintain. Many say, moreover, that the men named were Jews. But Jerome relates that the Hebrews say they were Persians and captains of king Darius, men who feared God.

paras.t: Ut dicerent nuntii isti ex parte mittentium, sacerdotibus domus Domini exercituum et prophetis, loquentes: Numquid flendum est mihi populo Dei in Babylonia remanenti, in quinto mense, vel sanctificare me debeo, id est per jejunium emundare, sicut feci multis jam annis, videlicet septuaginta, quibus vastitas templi duravit? Judæi quippe in Babylone annuatim planxerunt et jejunaverunt, die quo urbs Jerusalem et templum eversa fuerunt a Chaldæis mense quinto. Simili modo fecerunt septimo mense, propter occisionem Godoliæ et dispersionem Judæorum qui erant cum ipso. Quoniam ergo nunc isti in Babylone audierunt urbem et templum pene instaurata, dubitabant an juxta pristinum morem flere ac jejunare deberent, an potius inde cessare atque lætari, quia mutata causa, mutatur effectus.
paras.en: [[7:3|To speak|Ut dicerent]], that is, these messengers on behalf of those who sent them, [[7:3|to the priests of the house of the Lord of hosts, and to the prophets, saying|sacerdotibus domus Domini exercituum et prophetis, loquentes]]: [[7:3|Must I weep|Numquid flendum est mihi]], I, the people of God remaining in Babylonia, [[7:3|in the fifth month, or must I sanctify myself|in quinto mense, vel sanctificare me debeo]], that is, cleanse myself by fasting, [[7:3|as I have now done for many years|sicut feci multis jam annis]], namely seventy, during which the desolation of the temple lasted? For the Jews in Babylon mourned and fasted every year on the day on which the city of Jerusalem and the temple were overthrown by the Chaldeans, in the fifth month[[4 Kings 25:8||]]. They did likewise in the seventh month, because of the slaying of Godolias[[4 Kings 25:25||]] and the scattering of the Jews who were with him. Since, then, these men in Babylon had now heard that the city and the temple were almost restored, they were in doubt whether they ought to weep and fast according to their former custom, or rather leave off from it and rejoice: for when the cause is changed, the effect is changed.

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini exercituum ad me, dicens: Loquere ad omnem populum terræ, et ad sacerdotes, id est ad universos qui de Judæa ad templum concurrunt, et per eos ad alios non præsentes, dicens: Quum jejunaretis et plangeretis in quinto et septimo mense pro causis jam tactis, per hos septuaginta annos, quibus Babylonica duravit captivitas, numquid jejunium jejunastis mihi? id est, abstinentia vestra mihi non placuit, nec erat actus virtutis debito modo exhibitus, quoniam abstinendo a cibis, non abstinuistis a divinorum præceptorum transgressionibus.
paras.en: [[7:4|And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying:|Et factum est verbum Domini exercituum ad me, dicens]] [[7:5|Speak to all the people of the land, and to the priests|Loquere ad omnem populum terræ, et ad sacerdotes]], that is, to all who flock to the temple from Judæa, and through them to others not present, [[7:5|saying|dicens]]: [[7:5|When you fasted, and mourned in the fifth and the seventh month|Quum jejunaretis et plangeretis in quinto et septimo mense]] for the reasons already touched on, [[7:5|for these seventy years|per hos septuaginta annos]] during which the Babylonian captivity lasted, [[7:5|did you keep a fast unto me|numquid jejunium jejunastis mihi]]? that is, your abstinence did not please me, nor was it an act of virtue performed in due manner, because in abstaining from food you did not abstain from transgressing the divine commandments.

paras.t: Et quum comedistis et bibistis immoderanter et cum sensuali affectu seu delicate, numquid non vobis comedistis, et vobismetipsis bibistis? id est, ad vestram voluptatem et carnalitatem, non ad meum honorem, illa fecistis.
paras.en: [[7:6|And when you did eat and drink|Et quum comedistis et bibistis]] immoderately and with sensual affection, or daintily, [[7:6|did you not eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?|numquid non vobis comedistis, et vobismetipsis bibistis?]] that is, you did those things for your own pleasure and carnality, not for my honour.

paras.t: Numquid non hæc sunt verba quæ locutus est vobis Dominus? id est, imo sunt verba Dei, de modo jejunandi virtuose, et etiam vitiose, quæ dixit Dominus, in manu Prophetarum priorum, id est per ministerium Prophetarum qui ante Babylonicam captivitatem fuerunt, quum adhuc Jerusalem habitaretur a Judæis, et esset opulenta; et ipsa, et urbes ejus, quarum ipsa metropolis fuit, in circuitu ejus habitarentur, et ad austrum, et in campestribus, id est ad omnem situs differentiam, habitaretur, quantum ad urbes ad ipsam pertinentes.
paras.en: [[7:7|Are not these the words which the Lord spoke|Numquid non hæc sunt verba quæ locutus est vobis Dominus?]] to you? that is, yes indeed, they are words of God, about the manner of fasting virtuously and also viciously, which the Lord spoke [[7:7|by the hand of the former prophets|in manu Prophetarum priorum]], that is, through the ministry of the prophets who lived before the Babylonian captivity, [[7:7|when Jerusalem as yet was inhabited|quum adhuc Jerusalem habitaretur]] by the Jews, [[7:7|and was wealthy|et esset opulenta]]; and when [[7:7|both itself and the cities|et ipsa, et urbes ejus]], of which it was the mother city, [[7:7|round about it|in circuitu ejus]] were inhabited, and [[7:7|towards the south, and in the plain|et ad austrum, et in campestribus]], that is, in every kind of situation, [[7:7|there were inhabitants|habitaretur]], as regards the cities belonging to it.

paras.t: Denique Isaias aliique Prophetæ sufficienter instruxerunt Judæos, quale jejunium Deo placeret, et quale non. Quum enim interrogarent inordinate jejunantes, Quare jejunavimus, et non adspexisti? respondit Dominus: Ecce in die jejunii vestri invenitur voluntas vestra, ecce ad lites et contentiones jejunatis. Nolite jejunare sicut usque ad hanc diem, ut audiatur in excelso clamor vester. Deinde de virtuoso jejunio subditur: Nonne hoc est magis jejunium quod elegi? Dissolve colligationes impietatis; frange esurienti panem tuum, et egenos vagosque induc in domum tuam; quum videris nudum, operi eum. Hinc quoque Joel disseruit: Sanctificate jejunium, hoc est, aliarum virtutum actibus ipsum perficite.
paras.en: Indeed, Isaias and the other prophets sufficiently instructed the Jews what kind of fast pleased God and what kind did not. For when those who fasted in a disordered way asked, [[Is 58:3|Why have we fasted, and thou hast not regarded|Quare jejunavimus, et non adspexisti?]]? the Lord answered: [[Is 58:3|Behold in the day of your fast your own will is found|Ecce in die jejunii vestri invenitur voluntas vestra]], [[Is 58:4|Behold you fast for debates and strife|ecce ad lites et contentiones jejunatis]]. [[Is 58:4|Do not fast as you have done until this day, to make your cry to be heard on high|Nolite jejunare sicut usque ad hanc diem, ut audiatur in excelso clamor vester]]. Then, of the virtuous fast, it is added: [[Is 58:6|Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? loose the bands of wickedness|Nonne hoc est magis jejunium quod elegi? Dissolve colligationes impietatis]]; [[Is 58:7|Deal thy bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house: when thou shalt see one naked, cover him|frange esurienti panem tuum, et egenos vagosque induc in domum tuam; quum videris nudum, operi eum]]. Hence Joel too taught: [[Joel 1:14|Sanctify ye a fast|Sanctificate jejunium]], that is, perfect it by the acts of the other virtues.

paras.t: Idcirco jam subditur: Et factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam, dicens: Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens: Judicium verum judicate, id est, ex virtute justitiæ secundum directionem prudentiæ, sententiam et proprios actus discutite, dijudicate, punite, ne amore vel odio a recto tramite recedatis, nec alicujus personam accipiatis, nec munera diligatis. Hoc demum et Christus in Evangelio ait: Nolite, inquiens, secundum faciem judicare, sed justum judicium judicate. Porro quod alibi dicit, Nolite judicare ut non judicemini, dictum est de judicio temerario, usurpato, inordinato. Unde Moyses scribit: Juste judicabis, nec consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis; et alibi, Sic parvum audietis ut magnum, quia judicium Dei est. Væ itaque eis, præsertim judicibus ac prælatis, qui secundum affectionem potius judicant, quam secundum rationem. Propter quod secundo libro Paralipomenon Josaphat ait judicibus suis: Videte quid faciatis: non enim hominum exercetis judicium, sed Domini; et quidquid judicaveritis, in vos redundabit. Sit timor Domini Dei vestri vobiscum, et cum diligentia cuncta facite. Insuper judicando non palpemus, nec vane justificemus nos ipsos, sed fortiter arguamus: quia ut ait Apostolus, Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur.
paras.en: Therefore it is now added: [[7:8|And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:|Et factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam, dicens]] [[7:9|Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying|Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens]]: [[7:9|Judge ye true judgment|Judicium verum judicate]], that is, by the virtue of justice, under the direction of prudence, examine, weigh and punish both the case before you and your own acts, so that you do not leave the right path through love or hatred, nor respect anyone's person, nor love gifts. This too Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 7:24|Judge not|Nolite]], he says, [[John 7:24|according to the appearance: but judge just judgment|secundum faciem judicare, sed justum judicium judicate]]. But what he says elsewhere, [[Matt 7:1|Judge not, that you may not be judged|Nolite judicare ut non judicemini]], is said of rash, usurped and disordered judgment. Hence Moses writes: Thou shalt judge justly [Lev 19:15 has *Juste judica*, "judge … according to justice", at the end of the verse], [[Lev 19:15|Respect not the person of the poor: nor honour the countenance of the mighty|nec consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis]]; and elsewhere, [[Deut 1:17|you shall hear the little as well as the great|Sic parvum audietis ut magnum]], [[Deut 1:17|because it is the judgment of God|quia judicium Dei est]]. Woe, therefore, to those, especially judges and prelates, who judge according to their feelings rather than according to reason. For this reason, in the second book of Paralipomenon, Josaphat says to his judges: [[2 Par 19:6|Take heed what you do: for you exercise not the judgment of man, but of the Lord: and whatsoever you judge, it shall redound to you|Videte quid faciatis: non enim hominum exercetis judicium, sed Domini; et quidquid judicaveritis, in vos redundabit]]. [[2 Par 19:7|Let the fear of the Lord be with you, and do all things with diligence|Sit timor Domini Dei vestri vobiscum, et cum diligentia cuncta facite]]. Moreover, in judging, let us not flatter ourselves nor vainly justify ourselves, but rebuke ourselves sternly: for, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur]].

paras.t: Et misericordiam, quantum ad interiorem compassionis affectum, et miserationes, quantum ad opera pietatis, facite, unusquisque cum fratre suo, id est proximis, primo cognatis atque fidelibus, si indigeant, secundum ordinem caritatis, spirituali, non carnali, amore. Beati enim misericordes, quoniam misericordiam consequentur. Et judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam.
paras.en: And [[7:9|mercy|Et misericordiam]], as regards the inward affection of compassion, [[7:9|and compassion|et miserationes]], as regards works of kindness, [[7:9|shew ye|facite]], [[7:9|every man to his brother|unusquisque cum fratre suo]], that is, to their neighbours, first to kinsfolk and to the faithful, if they are in need, according to the order of charity [that is, the order in which charity owes its help, nearest first], with a spiritual, not a carnal, love. For [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati enim misericordes, quoniam misericordiam consequentur]]. And [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]].

paras.t: Et viduam, et pupillum, et advenam, et pauperem nolite calumniari. Hæ namque personæ sunt magis destitutæ humano solatio, et magis miserabiles sunt: ideo major eis est pietas impendenda, non calumnia inferenda, secundum quod ait Psalmista: Judicate egeno et pupillo, humilem et pauperem justificate. Moyses quoque protestatur: Deus facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum. Et malum, id est nocumentum, vir fratri, id est proximo, suo non cogitet in corde suo cum consensu et mora. Ex quo patet error dicentium cogitationem non esse peccatum, quoadusque procedat in opus.
paras.en: [[7:10|And oppress not the widow, and the fatherless, and the stranger, and the poor|Et viduam, et pupillum, et advenam, et pauperem nolite calumniari]]. For these persons are more destitute of human comfort, and are more to be pitied: therefore greater kindness is to be shown them, and no oppression inflicted on them, according to what the Psalmist says: [[Ps 81:3|Judge for the needy and fatherless: do justice to the humble and the poor|Judicate egeno et pupillo, humilem et pauperem justificate]]. Moses also declares: [[Deut 10:18|He doth judgment to the fatherless and the widow, loveth the stranger|Deus facit judicium pupillo et viduæ, amatque peregrinum]]. [[7:10|and let not a man devise evil|Et malum]], that is, harm, [[7:10|against his brother|vir fratri]], that is, his neighbour, [[7:10|in his heart|suo non cogitet in corde suo]], with consent and lingering [*mora*: dwelling on an evil thought with deliberate pleasure, which the schoolmen call *delectatio morosa*]. From this is plain the error of those who say that a thought is not a sin until it goes forth into a deed.

paras.t: Et noluerunt attendere verba ista patres vestri ante destructionem Jerusalem, et averterunt scapulam recedentes, id est, cor suum ex malitia averterunt a me, sicut is qui hortantem contemnit, et ex contemptu dorsum sibi in faciem vertit. Unde in Jeremia Dominus ait de istis: Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem. Et aures suas aggravaverunt, id est, aures cordis impleverunt peccatis, quæ sunt gravissima animæ onera usque in infernum eam prementia, sicut fertur in Psalmo: Quoniam iniquitates meæ supergressæ sunt caput meum, et sicut onus grave gravatæ sunt super me; ne audirent verba salutis.
paras.en: [[7:11|But they would not hearken|Et noluerunt attendere]] to these words, your fathers before the destruction of Jerusalem, [[7:11|and they turned away the shoulder to depart|et averterunt scapulam recedentes]], that is, they turned their heart away from me out of malice, like one who despises him that exhorts him and out of contempt turns his back to his face. Hence in Jeremias the Lord says of them: [[Jer 2:27|they have turned their back to me, and not their face|Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem]]. [[7:11|and they stopped their ears|Et aures suas aggravaverunt]] [*aggravaverunt*, literally "made heavy": hence the burdens of sin that follow], that is, they filled the ears of the heart with sins, which are the heaviest burdens of the soul, pressing it down even to hell, as is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 37:5|For my iniquities are gone over my head: and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me|Quoniam iniquitates meæ supergressæ sunt caput meum, et sicut onus grave gravatæ sunt super me]]; [[7:11|not to hear|ne audirent]] the words of salvation.

paras.t: Et cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem, id est, obstinatum atque durissimum exhibuerunt, ne audirent legem, observando divina præcepta, et verba exhortatoria, saluberrima atque prophetica, quæ misit Dominus exercituum in spiritu suo sancto, id est in Spiritu Sancto, et ex revelatione ipsius, per manum, id est subministrationem, Prophetarum priorum, Jeremiæ, Isaiæ, et aliorum qui Babylonicam captivitatem præcesserunt. Simile huic est illud Isaiæ: Incrassatum est cor populi hujus, et auribus graviter audiverunt. Hinc Jeremias asserit: Induraverunt facies suas super petram, et noluerunt reverti. Et iterum: Non audierunt, inquit, nec inclinaverunt aurem suam, sed induraverunt aures suas, ne audirent, et ne reciperent disciplinam. Porro, secundum Hieronymum, adamas lapis durissimus est, ita ut omnia metalla confringat, et a nullo confringatur. Et facta est indignatio magna, id est, grandis et rigorosa punitio Judæis inflicta est, a Domino exercituum.
paras.en: [[7:12|And they made their heart as the adamant stone|Et cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem]], that is, they showed it obstinate and most hard, [[7:12|lest they should hear the law|ne audirent legem]] by keeping the divine commandments, [[7:12|and the words|et verba]] of exhortation, most wholesome and prophetic, [[7:12|which the Lord of hosts sent in his spirit|quæ misit Dominus exercituum in spiritu suo]], his holy one, that is, in the Holy Spirit and by his revelation, [[7:12|by the hand|per manum]], that is, the ministry, [[7:12|of the former prophets|Prophetarum priorum]], Jeremias, Isaias and the others who came before the Babylonian captivity. Like this is that saying of Isaias[[Is 6:10||]]: [[Matt 13:15|the heart of this people is grown gross, and with their ears they have been dull of hearing|Incrassatum est cor populi hujus, et auribus graviter audiverunt]] [the margin gives Is. vi, 10 and Matt. xiii, 15; Denis's wording is that of St Matthew, who quotes Isaias]. Hence Jeremias declares: [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt facies suas super petram, et noluerunt reverti]]. And again: [[Jer 17:23|they did not hear|Non audierunt]], he says, [[Jer 17:23|nor incline their ear: but hardened their neck, that they might not hear me, and might not receive instruction|nec inclinaverunt aurem suam, sed induraverunt aures suas, ne audirent, et ne reciperent disciplinam]] [Denis reads *aures*, "ears", where the Vulgate has *cervicem*, "neck"]. Further, according to Jerome, the adamant is a stone so very hard that it breaks all metals and is broken by none. And [[7:12|a great indignation came|Et facta est indignatio magna]], that is, a great and rigorous punishment was inflicted on the Jews, from the [[7:12|Lord of hosts|Domino exercituum]].

paras.t: Et factum est sicut locutus est: quia per Chaldæos vastati sunt, sicut Prophetæ divinitus prænunciaverunt. Et sicut non audierunt verba mea, sic clamabunt, et non exaudiam eos in tempore necessitatis: vel quia ex timore servili precati sunt, et necessitate compulsi, non caritate inducti; vel quia in præsenti sæculo volui eos corrigere, ne in æternum perirent. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait: Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos; et quum multiplicaveritis preces, non exaudiam.
paras.en: [[7:13|And it came to pass that as he spoke|Et factum est sicut locutus est]]: for they were laid waste by the Chaldeans, as the prophets had foretold by God's inspiration. And as [[7:13|they heard not|non audierunt]] my words, [[7:13|so shall they cry, and I will not hear|sic clamabunt, et non exaudiam]] them in the time of need [Denis's reading of the verse differs here from the Vulgate]: either because they prayed out of servile fear and driven by necessity, not moved by charity; or because I willed to correct them in the present age, so that they might not perish for ever. Hence the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 1:15|when you stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes|Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos]]; [[Is 1:15|and when you multiply prayer, I will not hear|et quum multiplicaveritis preces, non exaudiam]].

paras.t: Et dispersi eos per omnia regna quæ nescierunt, id est per diversa ac plurima regna, in quæ translati fuerunt, et eis incognita erant, puta per regna Assyriorum, Chaldæorum, Persarum, Medorum, et regiones illis subjectas. Et terra desolata est ab eis, eorum incolatu privata, eo quod non esset transiens et revertens per eam de populo Judæorum. Et posuerunt terram desiderabilem, id est terram promissionis uberrimam, lacte et melle manantem (de qua cantatur in Psalmo, Pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem; et Moyses asserit eam inter omnes terras egregiam), in desertum: id est, suis peccatis id meruerunt, quod per Chaldæos in solitudinem est redacta, habitatoribus ejus sublatis.
paras.en: [[7:14|And I dispersed them throughout all kingdoms, which they know not|Et dispersi eos per omnia regna quæ nescierunt]], that is, through divers and very many kingdoms, into which they were carried away and which were unknown to them, for instance through the kingdoms of the Assyrians, Chaldeans, Persians and Medes, and the regions subject to them. [[7:14|and the land was left desolate behind them|Et terra desolata est ab eis]], deprived of their dwelling in it, [[7:14|so that no man passed through or returned|eo quod non esset transiens et revertens]] through it, of the people of the Jews. [[7:14|and they changed the delightful land|Et posuerunt terram desiderabilem]], that is, the most fruitful land of promise, flowing with milk and honey (of which it is sung in the Psalm, [[Ps 105:24|they set at nought the desirable land|Pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem]]; and Moses declares it goodly[[Deut 4:22||]] above all lands[[Deut 8:7||]] [the margin gives Deut. iv, 22; viii, 7-10]), [[7:14|into a wilderness|in desertum]]: that is, by their sins they deserved that it should be reduced to a solitude by the Chaldeans, its inhabitants being taken away.

paras.t: Denique, quod in hujus capituli principio dictum est contra Judæos indiscrete abstinentes, mystice applicandum est omnibus Christianis non internis, sed rudibus, qui pietatis actus et interiorem profectum ac virium animæ reformationem non satis curantes, sed negligentes, corporalem exercitationem et exteriores observantias habent pro magno, faciuntque scrupulositatem non parvam in minus principalibus, et principalia non advertunt, caritatem, humilitatem, patientiam, mititatem. Istis, si jejunia sua et cetera exteriora sua exercitia cupiunt Deo placere, inculcandum est ut juxta sensum præinductum, verum judicium judicent, suisque proximis compassivi, benigni, ac liberales exsistant, mentem suam semper in Deo stabiliant, omnem cordis duritiam prorsus abjiciant, sintque molles ac patuli ad suscipiendum in se verbum Dei. Alioqui terra eorum erit desolata, id est Spiritus Sancti inhabitatione privata, et per varia vitia dispergentur.
paras.en: Lastly, what was said at the beginning of this chapter against the Jews who fasted without discernment is to be applied mystically to all Christians who are not inward but unformed [*rudes*: beginners, untaught in the inner life], who, caring too little for the acts of piety, for inward progress and the reforming of the powers of the soul, and rather neglecting them, make much of bodily exercise and outward observances, and are not a little scrupulous in things of less account, while they pay no heed to the chief things: charity, humility, patience, meekness. If such men wish their fasts and their other outward exercises to please God, it must be impressed on them that, in the sense set out above, they judge [[7:9|true judgment|verum judicium]], be compassionate, kind and generous to their neighbours, keep their mind ever fixed in God, cast off all hardness of heart entirely, and be soft and open to receive the word of God into themselves. Otherwise their land will be desolate, that is, deprived of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, and they will be scattered through various vices.

8.title: Expositio litteralis capituli octavi: Et factum est verbum Domini exercituum ad me.
8.title_en: Literal exposition of the eighth chapter: And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me.

paras.t: Postquam præcedenti capitulo Dominus populum Judæorum multipliciter increpavit, nunc variis promissionibus consolatur eumdem, more optimi medici, post potionem amaram adhibens remedium dulce ac lenitivum : sic enim Samaritanus ille piissimus infudit vinum et oleum.
paras.en: After the Lord rebuked the people of the Jews in many ways in the preceding chapter, he now consoles them with various promises, after the manner of a very good physician who, after a bitter draught, applies a sweet and soothing remedy: for so that most loving Samaritan poured in wine and oil[[Luke 10:34||]].

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini exercituum ad me, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Zelatus sum Sion zelo magno. Hoc idem scriptum est atque expositum primo capitulo. Synagogam quippe sive Israeliticum populum, qui hic nomine Sion designatur, desponsavit sibi Deus, et quasi in conjugem sibi assumpsit, dum ei in deserto tradidit legem, ne de cetero mente fornicaretur cum idolis gentium, sicut de hoc in Ezechiele multa mystice conscribuntur. Propter quod in Jeremia Dominus loquitur : Recordatus sum tui, miserans adolescentiam tuam et caritatem desponsationis, quando secuta es me in deserto. Itaque singulari quodam amore Deus Sion dilexit, quemadmodum et in Deuteronomio Moyses contestatur : Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus Deus tuus, et amavit eos, elegitque semen eorum post eos. Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam, id est, contra transgressiones ipsius ex zelo meo ad eam indignatus sum valde : non motum passionis vel tranquillitatis habendo, sed rigorosam punitionem infligendo, sicut vir uxorem peccantem dire redarguit. Ista indignatio fuit, quod tradidit eam manibus adversariorum, Assyriis atque Chaldæis, ut patet in libro Regum.
paras.en: [[8:1|And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying|Et factum est verbum Domini exercituum ad me, dicens]]: [[8:2|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I have been jealous for Sion with a great jealousy|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Zelatus sum Sion zelo magno]]. This same thing was written and explained in the first chapter[[Zach 1:14||]]. For God espoused to himself the Synagogue, or the people of Israel, which is here designated by the name of Sion, and took her as it were for his wife, when he gave her the law in the desert, so that she should no more commit fornication in mind with the idols of the Gentiles; and many things are written of this mystically in Ezechiel[[Ezech 16:1||]]. For which reason the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:2|I have remembered thee, pitying thy youth, and the love of thy espousals, when thou followedst me in the desert|Recordatus sum tui, miserans adolescentiam tuam et caritatem desponsationis, quando secuta es me in deserto]]. And so God loved Sion with a certain singular love, as Moses also testifies in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:15|the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers, and loved them and chose their seed after them|Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus Deus tuus, et amavit eos, elegitque semen eorum post eos]]. [[8:2|and with a great indignation have I been jealous for her|Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam]], that is, out of my jealousy for her I was greatly indignant against her transgressions: not by having any movement of passion or [loss of] tranquillity, but by inflicting a rigorous punishment, as a husband sternly rebukes a wife who sins. This indignation was that he delivered her into the hands of her adversaries, the Assyrians and the Chaldeans, as is plain in the book of Kings[[4 Kings 15:19||]][[4 Kings 15:29||]][[4 Kings 17:3||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]][[4 Kings 25:1||]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Reversus sum ad Sion, id est, ab effectu justitiæ ad misericordiæ dulcorem, ad populum istum sine mea mutatione conversus sum, et pœnitenti indulsi, ac gratiam præstiti ; et habitabo in medio Jerusalem, id est in templo ac populo, corda bonorum per caritatem ac gratiam inhabitando. Christus quoque verus Deus et homo, Deus deorum, in Sion visibiliter conversatus ac visus est. Et vocabitur Jerusalem, civitas veritatis, id est veri Dei, vel veritatis vitæ, doctrinæ atque justitiæ, eo quod post reditum a Chaldæa, fuerint in Jerusalem viri perfecti ac virtuosi, veritatem in omnibus colentes, loquentes, ac diligentes. Istud tamen præcipue verificatum est per Christi adventum, qui in Jerusalem pluries prædicavit : in quem et urbs postea credidit. Et mons Domini exercituum, id est mons Sion in quo constructum est templum, vocabitur mons sanctificatus, id est ab idololatria expurgatus, divinoque cultui deputatus : de quo fertur in Psalmo, Induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ. Hinc in Isaia Dominus ait : Post hæc vocaberis civitas Justi, urbs fidelis.
paras.en: [[8:3|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I am returned to Sion|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Reversus sum ad Sion]], that is, from the working of justice to the sweetness of mercy: without change in myself I have turned to this people, and have pardoned them in their repentance, and shown them grace; [[8:3|and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem|et habitabo in medio Jerusalem]], that is, in the temple and among the people, dwelling in the hearts of the good by charity and grace. Christ too, true God and man, [[Ps 83:8|the God of gods|Deus deorum]], lived visibly in Sion and was seen there. [[8:3|and Jerusalem shall be called The city of truth|Et vocabitur Jerusalem, civitas veritatis]], that is, of the true God, or of truth of life, of doctrine and of justice, because after the return from Chaldea there were in Jerusalem perfect and virtuous men, who cherished, spoke and loved the truth in all things. Yet this was chiefly made true by the coming of Christ, who preached many times in Jerusalem, and in whom the city afterwards believed. [[8:3|and the mountain of the Lord of hosts|Et mons Domini exercituum]], that is, Mount Sion, on which the temple was built, shall be called [[8:3|The sanctified mountain|mons sanctificatus]], that is, cleansed of idolatry and set apart for the worship of God: of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 77:54|he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary|Induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ]] [Latin *sanctificationis*, "of his sanctification", the same word as the *sanctified* mountain]. Hence the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 1:26|After this thou shalt be called the city of the just, a faithful city|Post hæc vocaberis civitas Justi, urbs fidelis]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus in plateis Jerusalem, id est, viri et feminæ non interficientur nunc ut ante, tempore Babylonicæ vastitatis, sed naturalis periodi cursum implebunt ; et viri baculus in manu ejus præ multitudine dierum, id est, viri adeo erunt antiqui, quod deficientia atque trementia membra baculo sustentabunt. Et plateæ civitatis Jerusalem complebuntur infantibus et puellis ludentibus in plateis ejus, id est, ingens erit securitas, pax, et propagatio hominum in Jerusalem, ita ut adolescentior ætas, juxta consuetudinem suam, lusibus vacet. Hinc per Jeremiam loquitur Dominus : Adhuc audietur in loco isto vox gaudii et vox lætitiæ, vox sponsi et vox sponsæ, vox dicentium : Confitemini Domino exercituum, quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus.
paras.en: [[8:4|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus in plateis Jerusalem]], that is, men and women will not now be slain as before, in the time of the Babylonian devastation, but will complete the course of their natural span; [[8:4|and every man with his staff in his hand through multitude of days|et viri baculus in manu ejus præ multitudine dierum]], that is, the men will be so old that they will hold up their failing and trembling limbs with a staff. [[8:5|And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls, playing in the streets thereof|Et plateæ civitatis Jerusalem complebuntur infantibus et puellis ludentibus in plateis ejus]], that is, there will be great security, peace and increase of men in Jerusalem, so that the younger age will give itself to play according to its custom. Hence the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 33:10|There shall be heard again in this place|Adhuc audietur in loco isto]] [[Jer 33:11|The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say: Give ye glory to the Lord of hosts, for the Lord is good, for his mercy endureth for ever|vox gaudii et vox lætitiæ, vox sponsi et vox sponsæ, vox dicentium : Confitemini Domino exercituum, quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus, id est, si et quamvis vobis, qui de Babylonica captivitate superstites estis atque reversi, videatur difficile, ut Jerusalem ad tantam (sicut jam dixi) hominum multitudinem, reparationem et prosperitatem pertingat, in diebus illis, id est tempore isto quo hoc futurum dixi (istud enim videbatur multis incredibile, eo quod tempore prophetiæ hujus, adhuc pauci essent ibidem Judæi) ; numquid in oculis meis, id est in luce sapientiæ et virtute omnipotentiæ meæ, difficile erit istud implere? dicit Dominus exercituum. Non utique. Ideo in Evangelio ait Salvator : Quæ apud homines impossibilia sunt, possibilia sunt apud Deum. In Jeremia quoque habetur : Domine Deus, non erit tibi difficile omne verbum.
paras.en: [[8:6|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: If it seem hard in the eyes of the remnant of this people|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus]], that is, if, and although, it seems hard to you who have survived the Babylonian captivity and returned, that Jerusalem should attain to so great a multitude of men (as I have just said), to such restoration and prosperity, [[8:6|in those days|in diebus illis]], that is, at the time at which I have said this will be (for this seemed incredible to many, because at the time of this prophecy there were still few Jews there): [[8:6|shall it be hard in my eyes|numquid in oculis meis]], that is, in the light of my wisdom and the power of my omnipotence, [shall it be hard] to fulfil this? [[8:6|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]. By no means. Therefore the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 18:27|The things that are impossible with men are possible with God|Quæ apud homines impossibilia sunt, possibilia sunt apud Deum]]. In Jeremias too we have: [[Jer 32:17|O Lord God|Domine Deus]], [[Jer 32:17|no word shall be hard to thee|non erit tibi difficile omne verbum]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis, id est, de captivitate seu dispersione qua dispersi ac capti fuerunt in diversis partibus mundi, scilicet in oriente et occidente, eruam eos ; et adducam eos ad Judæam, et habitabunt in medio Jerusalem ; et erunt mihi in populum per specialem gratiam, quam eis præstabo, et ego ero eis in Deum per præcipuam devotionem eorum ad me, in veritate, id est vera fide, et sana doctrina, et in justitia, qua reddent unicuique quod ei debetur, videlicet Deo et sibi ac proximo. Ut autem refert Hieronymus, quidam Hebræi asserunt hæc impleta post ipsum Zorobabel usque Herodis alienigenæ tempus, quoniam interim templo reparato et urbe, multi Judæorum de multis mundi partibus ad Jerusalem habitandi gratia confluxerunt. Verius tamen pleniusque impletum est post Christi adventum, quando per Apostolorum prædicationem multi ubique Judæi et gentiles a Deo electi, conversi sunt ; spiritualiter quoque per fidem et caritatem adducti, habitaverunt in ipsa Ecclesia. De quibus et Christus prædixit : Multi ab oriente et occidente venient, etc. Quidquid hic breviter dicitur, in Jeremia et Ezechiele, imo et in Isaia diffusius scribitur ; sed brevitati studens, allegationes dimitto.
paras.en: [[8:7|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Behold I will save my people from the land of the east, and from the land of the going down of the sun|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis]], that is, I will rescue them from the captivity or dispersion in which they were scattered and held captive in various parts of the world, namely in the east and the west; [[8:8|And I will bring them|et adducam eos]] to Judea, [[8:8|and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem|et habitabunt in medio Jerusalem]]: [[8:8|and they shall be my people|et erunt mihi in populum]] through the special grace which I will bestow on them, [[8:8|and I will be their God|et ego ero eis in Deum]] through their particular devotion to me, [[8:8|in truth|in veritate]], that is, in true faith and sound doctrine, [[8:8|and in justice|et in justitia]], by which they will render to each what is due to him, namely to God, to themselves and to their neighbour. Now, as Jerome reports, certain Hebrews maintain that these things were fulfilled after Zorobabel himself, up to the time of Herod the foreigner, since in the meantime, when the temple and the city had been restored, many of the Jews flocked together to Jerusalem from many parts of the world to dwell there. Yet it was more truly and more fully fulfilled after the coming of Christ, when through the preaching of the Apostles many Jews and Gentiles everywhere, chosen by God, were converted; and being brought spiritually through faith and charity, they dwelt in the Church itself. Of these Christ also foretold: [[Matt 8:11|many shall come from the east and the west|Multi ab oriente et occidente venient]], etc. Whatever is said here briefly is written more at length in Jeremias and Ezechiel, and indeed in Isaias; but in my concern for brevity I leave out the citations.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Confortentur manus vestræ, o Judæi, et viriliter agite, confidentes in Domino, qui auditis in his diebus quibus templum quotidie prosperatur, sermones istos per os Prophetarum, videlicet Aggæi et Zachariæ, loquentium vobis in die qua fundata est domus Domini, de qua die supra dictum est, ut templum ædificaretur. Ad hoc enim domus Dei seu templum fuit fundata, ut ædificaretur perfecte.
paras.en: [[8:9|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Let your hands be strengthened|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Confortentur manus vestræ]], O Jews, and act manfully, trusting in the Lord, [[8:9|you that hear in these days|qui auditis in his diebus]], in which the temple daily goes forward, [[8:9|these words by the mouth of the prophets|sermones istos per os Prophetarum]], namely of Aggeus and Zacharias, speaking to you [[8:9|in the day that the house of the Lord of hosts was founded|in die qua fundata est domus Domini]] (of which day mention was made above), [[8:9|that the temple might be built|ut templum ædificaretur]]. For the house of God, or temple, was founded for this, that it might be built to completion.

paras.t: Siquidem ante dies illos, id est antequam templum ædificaretur, merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum erat, id est, homines et jumenta in agricultura, in mercimoniis aliisque diversis operibus infructuose et frustra laboraverunt, ita ut vix necessaria victui obtinerent. De hac terræ sterilitate propter negligentiam populi circa ædificationem templi inducta, dictum est plenius in Aggæo propheta. Neque introeunti, neque exeunti propria loca, id est habitatoribus terræ, erat pax præ tribulatione, id est adversariorum persecutione atque multiplici adversitate. Hoc clarius patet in libro Esdræ, ubi inter cetera dicitur in principio libri Nehemiæ : Qui remanserunt in provincia, in tribulatione magna sunt et in opprobrio ; et murus Jerusalem dissipatus est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni. Et dimisi omnes homines, puta Judæos a captivitate reversos, unumquemque contra proximum suum, id est, domesticas insidias inter se, permittente me, habuerunt. Ista tamen distributio est accommoda. De hoc quoque in Esdra habetur, quemadmodum quidam Judæorum fratres suos vendebant, superiores quoque gravabant populum, et subditos oppresserunt.
paras.en: [[8:10|For before those days|Siquidem ante dies illos]], that is, before the temple was built, [[8:10|there was no hire for men, neither was there hire for beasts|merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum erat]], that is, men and beasts laboured fruitlessly and in vain in farming, in trade and in various other works, so that they scarcely got the necessaries of life. Of this barrenness of the land, brought on because of the people's neglect in building the temple, more has been said in the prophet Aggeus[[Agg 1:10||]][[Agg 1:11||]]. [[8:10|neither was there peace to him that came in, nor to him that went out|Neque introeunti, neque exeunti]] their own places, that is, to the inhabitants of the land, [[8:10|because of the tribulation|erat pax præ tribulatione]], that is, through the persecution of their adversaries and adversity of many kinds. This is plainer in the book of Esdras, where among other things it is said at the beginning of the book of Nehemias: [[2 Esd 1:3|They that have remained|Qui remanserunt]] in the province [[2 Esd 1:3|are in great affliction, and reproach: and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and the gates thereof are burnt with fire|in tribulatione magna sunt et in opprobrio ; et murus Jerusalem dissipatus est, et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni]]. [[8:10|and I let all men go|Et dimisi omnes homines]], namely the Jews returned from captivity, [[8:10|every one against his neighbour|unumquemque contra proximum suum]], that is, by my permission they had plots at home against one another. This application, however, is an accommodated one [that is, a sense adapted to the words rather than their strict literal meaning]. Of this too we read in Esdras, how some of the Jews sold their brethren[[2 Esd 5:4||]][[2 Esd 5:5||]][[2 Esd 5:8||]], and the rulers too burdened the people and oppressed their subjects[[2 Esd 5:15||]].

paras.t: Nunc autem, dum ædificationi templi fortiter insudatis, non juxta dies priores ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, populum istum, qui de multis paucus remansit, non ita affligam, sicut prædictis afflixi diebus ; sed semen pacis erit, id est, filii pacis erunt, me eis pacem donante. Vel, Semen pacis erit, id est, semen eorum in terram projectum, pacifice excoletur et germinabit. Ideo subditur : Vinea dabit fructum suum, et terra dabit germen suum, et cœli aerii dabunt rorem suum : quia ex nubibus in aere motis, humor ad terræ fecundationem descendit ; et possidere faciam reliquias populi hujus universa hæc terræ nascentia, ita quod hostes terram non occupabunt.
paras.en: [[8:11|But now|Nunc autem]], while you toil hard at the building of the temple, [[8:11|I will not deal with the remnant of this people according to the former days|non juxta dies priores ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus]], [[8:11|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, I will not afflict this people, which has remained few out of many, as I afflicted them in the days spoken of; [[8:12|But there shall be the seed of peace|sed semen pacis erit]], that is, they will be children of peace, since I will give them peace. Or: the seed of peace shall be, that is, their seed cast into the ground will be tilled in peace and will spring up. Therefore it is added: [[8:12|the vine shall yield her fruit, and the earth shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew|Vinea dabit fructum suum, et terra dabit germen suum, et cœli aerii dabunt rorem suum]] [Denis reads *cœli aerii*, "the heavens of the air"]: because from the clouds moving in the air moisture comes down to make the earth fruitful; [[8:12|and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things|et possidere faciam reliquias populi hujus universa hæc]] that the earth brings forth, so that enemies shall not seize the land.

paras.t: Et erit, id est, fiet quod dicam : Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel, id est, quemadmodum vos, o duæ tribus, per domum Juda significatæ, et vos, decem tribus, per domum Israel designatæ, a gentibus maledicebamini tanquam infelices, egeni et miseri : juxta illud in Jeremia, Dabo eos in vexationem et maledictionem et in stuporem et sibilum gentibus ; sic salvabo vos de tribulationibus præinductis, et eritis benedictio, id est, felices vos reputabunt. Nolite timere carnali seu mundano timore ; confortentur manus vestræ.
paras.en: [[8:13|And it shall come to pass|Et erit]], that is, what I shall say will be done: [[8:13|that as you were a curse among the Gentiles, O house of Juda, and house of Israel|Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel]], that is, just as you, O two tribes, signified by the house of Juda, and you, ten tribes, designated by the house of Israel, were cursed by the Gentiles as unhappy, needy and wretched, according to that in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo eos in vexationem]], [[Jer 29:18|a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing|et maledictionem et in stuporem et sibilum]] to the nations: [[8:13|so will I save you|sic salvabo vos]] from the tribulations brought on before, [[8:13|and you shall be a blessing|et eritis benedictio]], that is, they will count you happy. [[8:13|fear not|Nolite timere]] with a carnal or worldly fear; [[8:13|let your hands be strengthened|confortentur manus vestræ]].

paras.t: Quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Sicut cogitavi ut affligerem vos, quum ad iracundiam me provocassent patres vestri, Babylonica scilicet captivitate instante, quando patres vestri idololatriæ dediti erant, et etiam postea, dicit Dominus, et non sum misertus ; sic conversus, cogitavi in diebus istis quibus circa templum efficaciter laboratis, ut benefaciam Jerusalem et domui Juda, id est duarum tribuum populo a Chaldæa reverso. Loquitur autem Deus affectu et more humano, ut melius capiatur, quanquam in ipso imperturbabili atque invariabili Deo nulla provocatio sit ad iram, neque conversio mutationem ponens in ipso.
