Qualiter vero ista sibi conveniant, dictum est sæpe. Hinc demum in Jeremia habetur : Ego scio cogitationes quas cogito super vos, ait Dominus, cogitationes pacis, et non afflictionis, ut dem vobis finem et patientiam. Nolite timere.
paras.en: [[8:14|For thus saith the Lord of hosts: As I purposed to afflict you, when your fathers had provoked me to wrath|Quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Sicut cogitavi ut affligerem vos, quum ad iracundiam me provocassent patres vestri]], namely when the Babylonian captivity was at hand, when your fathers were given to idolatry, and afterwards too, [[8:14|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]], [[8:15|And I had no mercy|et non sum misertus]]: [[8:15|so turning again I have thought in these days|sic conversus, cogitavi in diebus istis]], in which you labour effectively at the temple, [[8:15|to do good to the house of Juda, and Jerusalem|ut benefaciam Jerusalem et domui Juda]], that is, to the people of the two tribes returned from Chaldea. Now God speaks with a human feeling and in a human way, that he may be the better understood, though in God himself, who cannot be disturbed or changed, there is no provoking to anger, nor any turning that implies change in him. How these things agree with each other has often been said. Hence, lastly, we have in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:11|I know the thoughts that I think towards you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of affliction, to give you an end and patience|Ego scio cogitationes quas cogito super vos, ait Dominus, cogitationes pacis, et non afflictionis, ut dem vobis finem et patientiam]]. [[8:15|fear not|Nolite timere]].

paras.t: Hæc sunt ergo verba quæ facietis : id est, subscripta præcepta servabitis, ut mereamini beneficia repromissa semper tenere. Loquimini veritatem, unusquisque cum proximo suo : id est, nullus alteri mentiatur, sed veritatem simplici proferat corde, secundum exigentiam causæ, loci ac temporis, observando circumstantias ad operationem virtutum requisitas. Veritatem, et judicium pacis, id est, quo pax reparetur ac conservetur, judicate, id est judicando perfecte, in portis vestris, o judices populi. Siquidem olim apud Judæos judices residebant in portis, sicut et Moyses jussit, Judices constitues in portis tuis : ut ab omnibus facilius invenirentur, et ne rusticani atque agricolæ compellerentur ingredi urbes, et rerum suarum pati dispendium.
paras.en: [[8:16|These then are the things, which you shall do|Hæc sunt ergo verba quæ facietis]] [Latin *verba*, "words"]: that is, you shall keep the commandments written below, that you may deserve to hold the promised benefits for ever. [[8:16|Speak ye truth every one to his neighbour|Loquimini veritatem, unusquisque cum proximo suo]]: that is, let no one lie to another, but let each speak the truth with a simple heart, according to what the matter, the place and the time require, observing the circumstances required for the exercise of the virtues. [[8:16|truth and judgment of peace|Veritatem, et judicium pacis]], that is, the judgment by which peace is restored and preserved, [[8:16|judge ye|judicate]], that is, by judging perfectly, [[8:16|in your gates|in portis vestris]], O judges of the people. For formerly among the Jews the judges sat in the gates, as Moses also commanded: [[Deut 16:18|Thou shalt appoint judges and magistrates in all thy gates|Judices constitues in portis tuis]]: so that they might be found more easily by all, and that country people and farmers might not be forced to enter the cities and suffer loss in their affairs.

paras.t: Et unusquisque malum contra amicum suum ne cogitetis in cordibus vestris, et verbum mendax ne diligatis : imo ut colubrum incessabiliter abhorreatis. Omnia enim hæc sunt quæ odi, dicit Dominus, qui detestatur, odit et reprobat omne peccatum. De quo scriptum est in libro Judith : Deus odit iniquitatem. Et Moyses ait : Aversatur Dominus omnem injustitiam.
paras.en: [[8:17|And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his friend|Et unusquisque malum contra amicum suum ne cogitetis in cordibus vestris]], [[8:17|and love not a false oath|et verbum mendax ne diligatis]] [Denis's text reads *verbum mendax*, "a lying word"; the margin gives the Vulgate reading *juramentum*, "oath"]: nay, shun it unceasingly as a serpent[[Ecclus 21:2||]]. [[8:17|for all these are the things that I hate, saith the Lord|Omnia enim hæc sunt quæ odi, dicit Dominus]], who detests, hates and condemns every sin. Of which it is written in the book of Judith: [[Jdt 5:21|God hateth iniquity|Deus odit iniquitatem]]. And Moses says: The Lord [[Deut 25:16|hateth all injustice|Aversatur Dominus omnem injustitiam]].

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens : Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Jejunium quarti mensis, quo dirupta et capta est Jerusalem a Chaldæis, ut patet quarto Regum : quo etiam mense secundum Hebræos, Moyses tabulas testamenti confregit ; et jejunium quinti mensis, quo incensum est templum urbsque Jerusalem a Chaldæis : quo et Judæi in deserto jussi sunt in eremum regredi, eo quod propter verba exploratorum contra Dominum graviter murmurassent ; et jejunium septimi mensis, quo occisus est Godolias, et qui secum erant Judæi, dispersi sunt ; et jejunium decimi mensis, quo propheta Ezechiel, et secum consistentes in Babylone Judæi, primo audierunt templum esse combustum, Jerusalemque destructam ; erit domui Juda, id est populo Synagogæ, in gaudium et lætitiam mentis et corporis, juxta illud : Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum. Delectatio siquidem cordis redundat in corpus, atque in facie lucet, juxta illud Proverbiorum : Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit ; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa. Et in solennitates præclaras : id est, sicut hucusque habuerunt ista jejunia in luctu et gemitu propter adversa quæ temporibus prænominatis contigerunt, ita deinceps habebunt ea cum gaudio et festivitatibus magnis, propter bona eis a me nunc promissa. His verbis solvitur quæstio, quæ præcedenti movebatur capitulo, de observatione jejunii quinti ac septimi mensis.
paras.en: [[8:18|And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying|Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens]]: [[8:19|Thus saith the Lord of hosts|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum]]: [[8:19|The fast of the fourth|Jejunium quarti mensis]] month, in which Jerusalem was broken into and taken by the Chaldeans, as is plain in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 25:4||]][[Jer 39:2||]]; in which month too, according to the Hebrews, Moses broke the tables of the testament[[Ex 32:19||]]; [[8:19|and the fast of the fifth|et jejunium quinti]] month, in which the temple and the city of Jerusalem were burned by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:8||]][[4 Kings 25:9||]]; in which also the Jews in the desert were commanded to go back into the wilderness, because they had murmured grievously against the Lord on account of the words of the spies[[Num 14:25||]] [the margin gives Num. xiii, xiv]; [[8:19|and the fast of the seventh|et jejunium septimi]] month, in which Godolias was slain, and the Jews who were with him were scattered[[4 Kings 25:25||]]; [[8:19|and the fast of the tenth|et jejunium decimi]] month, in which the prophet Ezechiel and the Jews living with him in Babylon first heard that the temple was burned and Jerusalem destroyed: [[8:19|shall be to the house of Juda|erit domui Juda]], that is, to the people of the Synagogue, [[8:19|joy, and gladness|in gaudium et lætitiam]] of mind and body, according to that saying: [[Ps 83:3|My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God|Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum]]. For the delight of the heart overflows into the body and shines in the face, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 17:22|A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones.|Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit ; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]] [[8:19|and great solemnities|Et in solennitates præclaras]]: that is, as until now they have kept these fasts in mourning and groaning for the adversities that befell them at the times named, so from now on they will keep them with joy and great festivities, for the good things I now promise them. By these words the question raised in the preceding chapter, about keeping the fast of the fifth and of the seventh month, is resolved[[Zach 7:3||]][[Zach 7:5||]].

paras.t: Veritatem tantum et pacem diligite, veritatem videlicet triplicem, et triplicem pacem, videlicet : veritatem doctrinæ, vitæ, justitiæ ; pacem pectoris, temporis, æternitatis. Hæc igitur tantum amanda sunt, non ut alia non amentur, sed ut ista principalius quam corporalia exercitia diligantur, nec aliquid his contrarium admittatur. Ecce his verbis jubemur vere, juste, atque pacifice invicem conversari. Unde et Christus ait : Pacem habete inter vos ; et, Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Apud Joannem quoque : Si manseritis, inquit, in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis, et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos.
paras.en: [[8:19|only love ye truth and peace|Veritatem tantum et pacem diligite]]: that is, a threefold truth and a threefold peace, namely the truth of doctrine, of life and of justice, and peace of the heart, of time and of eternity. These, then, alone are to be loved: not that other things are not to be loved, but that these are to be loved more chiefly than bodily exercises, and nothing contrary to them admitted. See, by these words we are commanded to live with one another truly, justly and peaceably. Hence Christ also says: [[Mark 9:49|have peace among you|Pacem habete inter vos]]; and: [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.|Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur]] And in John: [[John 8:31|If you continue|Si manseritis]], he says, [[John 8:31|in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed|in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis]]. [[John 8:32|And you shall know the truth: and the truth shall make you free.|et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos]]

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Usquequo veniant populi, prædicta jejunia erunt Judæis in gaudium et solennitates præclaras. Veritatem etiam et pacem diligendas eis præcipio, quousque veniant populi, et habitent in civitatibus multis, id est, Judæi in urbibus suis hucusque destructis multiplicentur, et vadant habitatores urbium harum, unus ad alterum, dicentes : Eamus Jerusalem, et deprecemur faciem Domini in templo jam reparato, et quæramus Dominum exercituum, id est, ei placere, uniri, obedire, eumque perfectius noscere studeamus per opera bona. Judæi etenim certis temporibus anni tenebantur venire ad templum. Vadam etiam ego. Istud, si ordinem litteræ rite pensemus, est verbum in persona Domini exercituum, et de ipso dictum, ut sit sensus : Vadam etiam ego Dominus exercituum cum aliis ad templum : quod utique in Domino nostro Jesu Christo, vero Deo et homine, impletum esse Evangelistæ testantur. Unde his verbis implicite insinuatur incarnatio unigeniti Filii Dei.
paras.en: [[8:20|Thus saith the Lord of hosts, until people come|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Usquequo veniant populi]]: the fasts spoken of will be to the Jews joy and great solemnities; and I command them to love truth and peace, until people come [[8:20|and dwell in many cities|et habitent in civitatibus multis]], that is, until the Jews multiply in their cities, hitherto destroyed, [[8:21|And the inhabitants go|et vadant habitatores]] of these cities [[8:21|one to another, saying|unus ad alterum, dicentes]]: [[8:21|Let us go|Eamus]] to Jerusalem, [[8:21|and entreat the face of the Lord|et deprecemur faciem Domini]] in the temple now restored, [[8:21|and let us seek the Lord of hosts|et quæramus Dominum exercituum]], that is, let us strive by good works to please him, to be united to him, to obey him and to know him more perfectly. For the Jews were bound to come to the temple at certain times of the year[[Deut 16:16||]]. [[8:21|I also will go|Vadam etiam ego]]. This, if we weigh the order of the letter rightly, is a word in the person of the Lord of hosts, and said of himself, so that the sense is: I also, the Lord of hosts, will go with the others to the temple. And the Evangelists testify that this was fulfilled in our Lord Jesus Christ, true God and man. Hence by these words the incarnation of the only-begotten Son of God is implicitly suggested.

paras.t: Hinc alii præcedentia verba pro tempore Christi exponunt, ut sit sensus : Usquequo veniant populi ad fidem Christi, nempe usque ad id temporis cæremonialia legis duraverunt, et habitent in civitatibus multis, non in Judæa dumtaxat, sed in omni orbe terrarum, et vadant habitatores, dicentes : Eamus, et deprecemur faciem Domini, in Ecclesia Christi orantes Patrem in spiritu et veritate, in omni loco puras manus ad Deum levantes.
paras.en: Hence others explain the preceding words of the time of Christ, so that the sense is: [[8:20|until people come|Usquequo veniant populi]] to the faith of Christ (for until that time the ceremonial precepts of the law lasted), [[8:20|and dwell in many cities|et habitent in civitatibus multis]], not in Judea only but in all the world, [[8:21|And the inhabitants go|et vadant habitatores]], [[8:21|saying: Let us go, and entreat the face of the Lord|dicentes : Eamus, et deprecemur faciem Domini]], in the Church of Christ, praying to [[John 4:23|the Father in spirit and in truth|Patrem in spiritu et veritate]], [[1 Tim 2:8|in every place, lifting up pure hands|in omni loco puras manus ad Deum levantes]] to God.

paras.t: Et venient populi multi, et gentes robustæ ad quærendum Dominum exercituum in Jerusalem, et deprecandam faciem Domini : quia ad templum illud non solum Judæi, sed multi quoque gentilium orandi gratia confluxerunt, quemadmodum ex evangelio Joannis comprobatur. Huic insuper expositioni sequentia amplius consonant.
paras.en: [[8:22|And many peoples, and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord.|Et venient populi multi, et gentes robustæ ad quærendum Dominum exercituum in Jerusalem, et deprecandam faciem Domini]] For not only Jews but also many of the Gentiles flocked to that temple to pray, as is proved from the Gospel of John. And what follows agrees further with this explanation.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : In diebus illis, videlicet tempore promulgationis evangelicæ legis, seu apostolicæ prædicationis, in quibus apprehendent decem homines ex omnibus linguis gentium, et apprehendent fimbriam viri Judæi, id est vestimentum Christianorum ex Judaismo in Christum credentium, præsertim Apostolorum, dicentes : Ibimus vobiscum, id est, Deum colemus, et in Ecclesiam colligemur, sicut et vos, credendo in Christum. Audivimus enim ex fama miraculorum et documentorum vestrorum ex lege et Prophetis, quoniam Deus, verus, unus ac trinus, seu Christus, vobiscum est per gratiam præeminentem et singularem.
paras.en: [[8:23|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: In those days|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : In diebus illis]], namely in the time of the promulgation of the law of the Gospel, or of the preaching of the Apostles, [[8:23|wherein ten men of all languages of the Gentiles|in quibus apprehendent decem homines ex omnibus linguis gentium]] [[8:23|shall take hold, and shall hold fast the skirt of one that is a Jew|et apprehendent fimbriam viri Judæi]], that is, the garment of the Christians from Judaism who believe in Christ, above all of the Apostles, [[8:23|saying: We will go with you|dicentes : Ibimus vobiscum]], that is, we will worship God and be gathered into the Church, as you are, by believing in Christ. [[8:23|for we have heard|Audivimus enim]] by the fame of your miracles and of your teachings from the Law and the Prophets, [[8:23|that God|quoniam Deus]], the true God, one and three, or Christ, [[8:23|is with you|vobiscum est]] by a pre-eminent and singular grace.

paras.t: Porro per decem, qui est numerorum terminus, numerusque perfectus, multitudo seu universitas gentilium Apostolis cohærentium, atque in Christum credentium, designatur. Innumerabiles enim adhæserunt eisdem. Postremo quod ait, Decem homines ex omnibus linguis, dupliciter accipi potest : primo, quod ex qualibet lingua decem homines istud acturi sint ; secundo, quod ex omnibus simul : sed utroque modo tempore Apostolorum exstat impletum.
paras.en: Further, by *ten*, which is the limit of the numbers and a perfect number, is designated the multitude or whole body of the Gentiles who cleave to the Apostles and believe in Christ; for countless people joined themselves to them. Lastly, when he says [[8:23|ten men of all languages|Decem homines ex omnibus linguis]], it can be taken in two ways: first, that from each language ten men will do this; second, that ten will do it from all languages together. But in either way it was fulfilled in the time of the Apostles.

8.title: De spirituali ejusdem capituli octavi intellectu.
8.title_en: On the spiritual understanding of the same eighth chapter.

paras.t: Quod in præsentis capituli exordio ad litteram dictum est de Synagoga, spiritualiter de Christi Ecclesia et qualibet anima christiana accipi potest. Itaque Dominus ait: Zelatus sum Sion, id est Ecclesiam, seu animam christifidelem, zelo magno. Ipsa enim est sponsa Christi, qui ex amore suo ad eam factus est homo pro ea, et proprio ipsam sanguine liberavit: ad quam ait in Canticis, Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa. Propter quod ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret. Sed et ipsemet Christus in Joanne protestatur: Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos. Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam, quoniam quo eam plus diligo, eo peccata illius amplius odio, et statim castigationem adhibeo: juxta illud Apocalypsis, Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo.
paras.en: What was said literally at the opening of the present chapter about the Synagogue can be taken spiritually of the Church of Christ and of every Christian soul. Thus the Lord says: [[8:2|I have been jealous for Sion|Zelatus sum Sion]], that is, for the Church, or for the soul faithful to Christ, [[8:2|with a great jealousy|zelo magno]]. For she is the spouse of Christ, who out of his love for her was made man for her sake, and set her free with his own blood; to whom he says in the Canticles: [[Cant 4:9|Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse|Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa]]. On which account the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it|ut illam sanctificaret]]. And Christ himself also declares in John: [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]. [[8:2|and with a great indignation have I been jealous for her|Et indignatione magna zelatus sum eam]], because the more I love her, the more I hate her sins, and at once I apply chastisement: according to that word of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Reversus sum ad Sion, quoniam pœnitentem clementer recipio, gratiamque refundo. Imo nondum pœnitentem Christus frequenter piissime prævenit, ad bona instigat, ad gratiam aptat, spiritualiter visitat, et operi manuum suarum in vitiorum cœno jacenti, adjutricem porrigit manum, de lacu miseriæ et de luto fæcis ipsam educens. Et habitabo in medio Jerusalem, id est in pectore animæ seu Ecclesiæ, divinæ pacis visioni fideliter inhiantis. Ideo orat Apostolus: Det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ, virtutem corroborari in interiori homine per Spiritum Sanctum, habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris. Et vocabitur Jerusalem, id est Ecclesia, civitas veritatis, videlicet Christi, qui ait: Ego sum via, veritas, et vita. De qua fertur in Psalmo: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei. In Ecclesia nempe est unio civium: quibus scribit Apostolus, Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei. Anima quoque justi, civitas Christi censetur: quia in ea est cogitationum et affectionum, tanquam civium, sub rationis imperio ordinata consensio; et mons sanctificatus, propter contemplationis sublimitatem, vitæ eminentiam, gratiæ apicem. De quibus civitate ac monte ad Hebræos legitur: Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem.
paras.en: [[8:3|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:3|I am returned to Sion|Reversus sum ad Sion]], because I mercifully receive the penitent, and pour grace back into him. Nay more, Christ often most lovingly goes before the soul not yet penitent, urges it to good, fits it for grace, visits it spiritually, and to the work of his hands lying in the mire of vices he reaches out a helping hand[[Job 14:15||]], leading it out [[Ps 39:3|of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs|de lacu miseriæ et de luto fæcis]]. [[8:3|and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem|Et habitabo in medio Jerusalem]], that is, in the breast of the soul or of the Church, faithfully longing for the vision of divine peace [Jerusalem being interpreted *vision of peace*]. Therefore the Apostle prays: [[Eph 3:16|That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened by his Spirit with might unto the inward man|Det vobis secundum divitias gloriæ suæ, virtutem corroborari in interiori homine per Spiritum Sanctum]], [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris]]. [[8:3|and Jerusalem shall be called|Et vocabitur Jerusalem]], that is, the Church, [[8:3|The city of truth|civitas veritatis]], namely of Christ, who says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita]]. Of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 86:3|Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei]]. For in the Church there is the union of citizens, to whom the Apostle writes: [[Eph 2:19|you are no more strangers and foreigners: but you are fellow citizens with the saints and the domestics of God|Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei]]. The soul of the just man, too, is reckoned a city of Christ, because in it there is an ordered agreement of thoughts and affections, as of citizens, under the rule of reason; and [[8:3|The sanctified mountain|mons sanctificatus]], because of the sublimity of its contemplation, the eminence of its life, the summit of its grace. Of which city and mountain we read in the Epistle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus, id est in virtutum perfectione maturi, animo graves, in virtutibus exercitati: quibus lacte opus non est, sed solidum queunt capere cibum; qui tentationibus probati sunt atque experti. Unde in Sapientiæ libro habetur: Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata; cani autem sunt sensus hominis, et ætas senectutis, vita immaculata. Verum, ut Isaias asserit: Puer centum annorum morietur. De hujuscemodi senibus scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Non te prætereat narratio seniorum. Hi moriuntur in senectute bona, senes et pleni dierum. Anus quoque sunt simili modo accipiendæ: quæ et aliorum matres digne possunt vocari. De qualibus dicit Apostolus: Viduas honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt. Hi itaque habitabunt, id est, stabiliter vivent ac permanebunt, in plateis Jerusalem, in divinis præceptis atque consiliis, in virtutibus cunctis, præsertim in caritate Dei ac proximi. Per has plateas ad æternam illam supercœlestem Jerusalem itur et pervenitur. Unde et scriptum est in Psalmo: Statuisti in loco spatioso pedes meos; et, Latum mandatum tuum nimis. Sponsa quoque in Canticis per vicos et plateas quærit quem diligit. Nec obstat, quod arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam: arcta est equidem, quia difficulter in ea persistitur; et lata, quia ut regia via omnes capere potest, et per caritatem ad universos, etiam ad adversarios, se extendit.
paras.en: [[8:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:4|There shall yet old men and old women dwell|Adhuc habitabunt senes et anus]], that is, those ripe in the perfection of the virtues, grave of mind, practised in the virtues: who have no need of milk, but can take solid food[[Heb 5:12||]]; who have been proved and tried by temptations. Hence it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 4:8|venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs|Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata; cani autem sunt sensus hominis]], [[Wis 4:9|And a spotless life is old age|et ætas senectutis, vita immaculata]]. Indeed, as Isaias asserts: [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old|Puer centum annorum morietur]]. Of old men of this kind it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 8:11|Let not the discourse of the ancients escape thee|Non te prætereat narratio seniorum]]. These die in a good old age, old and full of days [printed as Scripture, with no margin reference; not from Ecclesiasticus 8: compare Gen 25:8 and 1 Par 29:28]. The old women are to be taken in like manner: who may also worthily be called the mothers of others. Of such the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 5:3|Honour widows that are widows indeed|Viduas honora, quæ vere viduæ sunt]]. These, then, shall dwell, that is, shall steadfastly live and remain, [[8:4|in the streets of Jerusalem|in plateis Jerusalem]]: in the divine precepts and counsels, in all the virtues, above all in the charity of God and of the neighbour. By these streets [*plateæ*, broad streets or open squares] one goes to that eternal Jerusalem above the heavens, and arrives there. Hence it is also written in the Psalm: [[Ps 30:9|thou hast set my feet in a spacious place|Statuisti in loco spatioso pedes meos]]; and: [[Ps 118:96|thy commandment is exceeding broad|Latum mandatum tuum nimis]]. The spouse too, in the Canticles, seeks him whom she loves through [[Cant 3:2|the streets and the broad ways|vicos et plateas]]. Nor does it stand in the way that [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life|arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam]]: strait it is indeed, because it is hard to persevere in it; and broad, because like a royal road it can take in all, and through charity it reaches out to all men, even to adversaries.

paras.t: Et viri baculus in manu ejus, id est, in horum seniorum manu seu potestate erit virga directionis, paterna correptio, auctoritas prælationis, consolatio et sustentatio infirmorum: idque conveniet eis præ multitudine dierum, id est merito sanctæ conversationis quam tempore longo duxerunt. Unde Apostolus non vult neophytum ordinari episcopum. Propter quod Moyses dixit: Date ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes. Et de reprobo populo Dominus in Isaia loquitur: Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis.
paras.en: [[8:4|and every man with his staff in his hand|Et viri baculus in manu ejus]], that is, in the hand or power of these elders there shall be the rod of direction, fatherly correction, the authority of prelacy, the consolation and support of the weak: and this shall befit them [[8:4|through multitude of days|præ multitudine dierum]], that is, by the merit of the holy life which they have led for a long time. Hence the Apostle does not want a neophyte to be ordained bishop[[1 Tim 3:6||]]. For which reason Moses said: [[Deut 1:13|Let me have from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers|Date ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes]]. And of the reprobate people the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 3:4|I will give children to be their princes, and the effeminate shall rule over them|Dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis]].

paras.t: Et plateæ civitatis, id est mandata Ecclesiæ, complebuntur infantibus et puellis, id est innocentibus simplicibus, qui juxta Christi doctrinam conversi sunt, et facti ut parvuli: quibus dicit et Paulus, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote; et Petrus in prima sua Canonica, Deponentes omnem malitiam et omnem dolum, et simulationes et invidias, quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite; ludentibus in plateis ejus, id est in divinorum præceptorum observantiis cordialiter gloriantibus, atque internam lætitiam gestu corporali monstrantibus: sicut et David testatur, Ludam, et ero humilis in oculis meis. Denique et Sapientia ait in Proverbiorum libro: Delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram Domino omni tempore, ludens in orbe terrarum. Insuper spiritualis recreatio et ludus ad eutrapeliam pertinens, competit istis pro causa, loco, et tempore.
paras.en: [[8:5|And the streets of the city|Et plateæ civitatis]], that is, the commandments of the Church, [[8:5|shall be full of boys and girls|complebuntur infantibus et puellis]], that is, of the innocent and simple, who according to the teaching of Christ have been converted and become as little children[[Matt 18:3||]]: to whom Paul too says: [[1 Cor 14:20|do not become children in sense. But in malice be children|Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote]]; and Peter in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice and all guile and dissimulations and envies|Deponentes omnem malitiam et omnem dolum, et simulationes et invidias]], [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire the rational milk|quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite]] [Denis's text reads *rationabiles*, so that it is the babes, not the milk, that are rational]; [[8:5|playing in the streets thereof|ludentibus in plateis ejus]], that is, glorying from the heart in the keeping of the divine precepts, and showing their inward gladness by bodily gesture: as David too bears witness: [[2 Kings 6:22|I will both play|Ludam]], [[2 Kings 6:22|and I will be little in my own eyes|et ero humilis in oculis meis]]. Lastly, Wisdom too says in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 8:30|was delighted every day, playing before him at all times|Delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram Domino omni tempore]], [[Prov 8:31|Playing in the world|ludens in orbe terrarum]]. Moreover, spiritual recreation and play belonging to eutrapelia [that is, the virtue of seemly mirth and pleasantry in recreation] befit these, as cause, place and time allow.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus, id est, licet reformatio Ecclesiæ, et multiplicatio fidelium videatur impossibilis, aut multum difficilis bonis Christianis perpaucis, propter nimium lapsum fidelium; numquid in oculis meis difficile erit? Non plane, quia non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum. Non ergo de reformatione Ecclesiæ desperemus, sed quo major est ejus indigentia ac ruina, eo instantius atque ferventius divinæ pietatis imploremus suffragia.
paras.en: [[8:6|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:6|If it seem hard in the eyes of the remnant of this people|Si difficile videbitur in oculis reliquiarum populi hujus]], that is, although the reform of the Church and the multiplying of the faithful may seem impossible, or very hard, to the very few good Christians, because of the excessive falling away of the faithful: [[8:6|shall it be hard in my eyes|numquid in oculis meis difficile erit]]? Plainly not, because [[Luke 1:37|no word shall be impossible with God|non erit impossibile apud Deum omne verbum]]. Let us not, then, despair of the reform of the Church; but the greater her need and her ruin, the more urgently and fervently let us implore the help of the divine mercy.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis. Ubique novit Dominus qui sunt ejus; et salvantur quicumque præordinati sunt ad vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[8:7|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[8:7|Behold I will save my people from the land of the east, and from the land of the going down of the sun|Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis, et de terra occasus solis]]. Everywhere [[2 Tim 2:19|the Lord knoweth who are his|novit Dominus qui sunt ejus]]; and saved are [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting|quicumque præordinati sunt ad vitam æternam]].

paras.t: Confortentur manus vestræ, et indefessi in operibus bonis estote, qui auditis in his diebus sermones istos de reformatione Ecclesiæ promissionibusque divinis, et animarum profectu, per os Prophetarum, id est a prædicatoribus atque doctoribus, ceterisque devotis, futurum Dei judicium, ac omnium venturam finalem remunerationem jugiter vobis narrantibus (de quibus ad Corinthios scribit Apostolus: Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant, et ceteri dijudicent), in die qua fundata est domus Domini, id est, animæ vestræ esse cœperunt domus, templum ac thalamus Sponsi cœlestis, per fidem formatam et gratiæ infusionem, ut templum ædificaretur, id est, per opera virtuosa continuata vos ipsi consecraremini in templum Spiritus Sancti: sicut ait Apostolus, Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
paras.en: [[8:9|Let your hands be strengthened|Confortentur manus vestræ]], and be unwearied in good works, [[8:9|you that hear in these days these words|qui auditis in his diebus sermones istos]] about the reform of the Church, the divine promises and the progress of souls, [[8:9|by the mouth of the prophets|per os Prophetarum]], that is, from preachers and doctors and other devout persons, who continually tell you of the judgment of God to come and of the final reward that awaits all (of whom the Apostle writes to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 14:29|let the prophets speak, two or three: and let the rest judge|Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant, et ceteri dijudicent]]), [[8:9|in the day that the house of the Lord of hosts was founded|in die qua fundata est domus Domini]], that is, your souls began to be the house, the temple and the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, through formed faith [that is, faith given its form, its life, by charity] and the infusion of grace, [[8:9|that the temple might be built|ut templum ædificaretur]], that is, that by virtuous works kept up without a break you yourselves might be consecrated into a temple of the Holy Ghost: as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]].

paras.t: Siquidem ante dies illos, id est, antequam domus Dei modo præfato initiaretur in vobis, merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum, id est, nec litterati, nec idiotæ aliquid meritorie operabantur, quoniam caritate infusa (quæ est animæ vita) carebant, et sine gratia nihil futuræ beatitudinis promeretur natura; neque introeunti, neque exeunti erat pax, id est vera mentis tranquillitas in Deo, præ tribulatione, id est vitiorum inordinatione et confusione. Animus quippe inordinatus, sibi ipsi pœnosus est: sicut et vir eruditus, in Deo tranquillus, suavis est animæ suæ. Et dimisi omnes homines, unumquemque contra proximum suum. Quum enim caritas et gratia deest, mox oriuntur ex amore privati lites, contentiones, discordiæ, et cetera opera carnis.
paras.en: [[8:10|For before those days|Siquidem ante dies illos]], that is, before the house of God was begun in you in the manner just described, [[8:10|there was no hire for men, neither was there hire for beasts|merces hominum non erat, nec merces jumentorum]], that is, neither the learned nor the unlettered did anything meritoriously, because they lacked infused charity (which is the life of the soul), and without grace nature merits nothing of the beatitude to come; [[8:10|neither was there peace to him that came in, nor to him that went out|neque introeunti, neque exeunti erat pax]], that is, true tranquillity of mind in God, [[8:10|because of the tribulation|præ tribulatione]], that is, the disorder and confusion of the vices. For a disordered mind is a torment to itself: as, on the other hand, the learned man, tranquil in God, [[Ecclus 37:22|is sweet to his own soul|suavis est animæ suæ]]. [[8:10|and I let all men go every one against his neighbour|Et dimisi omnes homines, unumquemque contra proximum suum]]. For when charity and grace are lacking, there soon arise from private love quarrels, [[Gal 5:20|contentions|contentiones]], discords, and the other [[Gal 5:19|works of the flesh|opera carnis]].

paras.t: Nunc autem, quum domum conscientiæ mihi præparaverunt, non juxta dies priores, quibus sine gratia exsistentes, sine mercede fuerunt, ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus, id est residuis Christianis; sed semen pacis erit, id est filii pacis atque pacifice mutuo conversantes. Vinea, id est Ecclesia: de qua ait in Evangelio Christus, Homo quidam plantavit vineam: de qua scriptum est in Canticis, Vinea fuit Pacifico; dabit fructum suum, id est, in bonis operibus fructuosa erit, ut dicere queat: Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera. Vel vinea ista est Christus, qui ait, Ego sum vitis vera: qui dedit et dat fructum, spirituales filios generando, et de plenitudine suæ gratiæ ceteris influendo, suumque meritum nobis per sacramenta applicando et communicando.
paras.en: [[8:11|But now|Nunc autem]], when they have prepared for me the house of their conscience, [[8:11|I will not deal with the remnant of this people|ego faciam reliquiis populi hujus]], that is, with the Christians that remain, [[8:11|according to the former days|non juxta dies priores]], in which, being without grace, they were without hire; [[8:12|But there shall be the seed of peace|sed semen pacis erit]], that is, sons of peace, living peaceably with one another. [[8:12|the vine|Vinea]], that is, the Church, of which Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 20:9|A certain man planted a vineyard|Homo quidam plantavit vineam]]; of which it is written in the Canticles: [[Cant 8:11|The peaceable had a vineyard|Vinea fuit Pacifico]]; [[8:12|shall yield her fruit|dabit fructum suum]], that is, she shall be fruitful in good works, so that she may say: [[Ps 51:10|But I, as a fruitful olive tree|Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera]]. Or this vine is Christ, who says: [[John 15:1|I am the true vine|Ego sum vitis vera]]; who has given and gives fruit, by begetting spiritual sons, by pouring of the fullness of his grace into others, and by applying and imparting his merit to us through the sacraments.

paras.t: Et terra dabit germen suum. Terra ista sunt, de quibus ait Salvator: Quod autem in terram bonam cecidit, hi sunt qui audientes verbum Dei, corde bono et optimo retinent, et afferunt fructum in patientia. Quum ergo Dominus benignitatem dat gratiæ suæ, terra nostra dat fructum suum. Et cæli dabunt rorem suum: id est, viri spirituales et contemplativi, prædicatores verbi Dei, verba eruditionis et consolationis auditoribus suis infundent, et corda eorum irrigabunt, ac fecundabunt.
paras.en: [[8:12|and the earth shall give her increase|Et terra dabit germen suum]]. This earth is those of whom the Saviour says: [[Luke 8:15|that on the good ground are they who in a good and perfect heart, hearing the word, keep it and bring forth fruit in patience|Quod autem in terram bonam cecidit, hi sunt qui audientes verbum Dei, corde bono et optimo retinent, et afferunt fructum in patientia]]. When, therefore, the Lord gives the goodness of his grace, [[Ps 84:13|our earth shall yield her fruit|terra nostra dat fructum suum]]. [[8:12|and the heavens shall give their dew|Et cæli dabunt rorem suum]]: that is, spiritual and contemplative men, preachers of the word of God, will pour words of instruction and consolation into their hearers, and will water their hearts and make them fruitful.

paras.t: Et erit: Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel, sic salvabo vos, et eritis benedictio. Frequenter contingit, ut aliqui Christiani, sive sæculares, sive religiosi, et præsertim religiosi et clerici, qui ad perfectiorem vitam tenentur, suis exigentibus vitiis, gratia Dei priventur, et deinceps valde reprehensibiliter conversentur, atque ob id ab aliis contemnantur et maledicantur. Quumque clementia Dei ad virtuosam vitam reduxerit eos, eatenus se emendant, ut alii ædificentur et benedicant eisdem. Ideo Petrus inducit: Abstinete a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam, conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis, tanquam de malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum. Et rursus: Hæc est, inquit, voluntas Dei, ut obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam.
paras.en: [[8:13|And it shall come to pass, that as you were a curse among the Gentiles, O house of Juda, and house of Israel: so will I save you, and you shall be a blessing|Et erit: Sicut eratis maledictio in gentibus, domus Juda et domus Israel, sic salvabo vos, et eritis benedictio]]. It often happens that some Christians, whether seculars or religious, and especially religious and clerics, who are bound to a more perfect life, are deprived of the grace of God as their vices deserve, and afterwards live in a very blameworthy way, and for this are despised and cursed by others. And when the mercy of God has brought them back to a virtuous life, they amend themselves so far that others are edified and bless them. Therefore Peter urges you [[1 Pet 2:11|to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|Abstinete a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]], [[1 Pet 2:12|Having your conversation good among the Gentiles: that whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by the good works which they shall behold in you, glorify God|conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis, tanquam de malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum]]. And again: This, he says, is [[1 Pet 2:15|the will of God|voluntas Dei]], that [[1 Pet 2:15|you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men|obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam]].

paras.t: Cetera ex præcedenti articulo adeo lucide patent, ut hic nihil reiterare oporteat. Verumtamen huic quod nunc ait Propheta, Jejunium quarti, et jejunium quinti, etc., erit domui Juda in gaudium, consonat quod in Matthæo loquitur Christus: Quum jejunatis, nolite fieri sicut hypocritæ, tristes; tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava, ne videaris hominibus jejunans, sed Patri tuo qui est in abscondito. Docemur quoque ex his, jejunia temporalia, et alia ab Ecclesia instituta atque præcepta, diligenter servare. Non enim sine mortali peccato omittuntur, nisi adsit vere rationabilis causa. Siquidem Deo et Ecclesiæ rectæque rationi pariformiter obedire debemus. Postremo, sic jejunare debet Christianus, ut vitia universa pro viribus vitet. Scriptum est enim: Homo qui jejunat in peccatis suis, et iterum facit ea, quid proficit humiliando se?
paras.en: The rest is so clear from the preceding article that there is no need to repeat anything here. Yet with what the Prophet now says, [[8:19|The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth|Jejunium quarti, et jejunium quinti]], etc., [[8:19|shall be to the house of Juda, joy|erit domui Juda in gaudium]], there agrees what Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 6:16|when you fast, be not as the hypocrites, sad|Quum jejunatis, nolite fieri sicut hypocritæ, tristes]]; [[Matt 6:17|But thou, when thou fastest anoint thy head, and wash thy face|tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava]], [[Matt 6:18|That thou appear not to men to fast, but to thy Father who is in secret|ne videaris hominibus jejunans, sed Patri tuo qui est in abscondito]]. We are taught also by these words to keep diligently the fasts of the seasons [that is, the Ember Days, the fasts of the four seasons of the year], and the other fasts instituted and commanded by the Church. For they are not omitted without mortal sin, unless a truly reasonable cause be present; since we ought to obey God, the Church and right reason alike. Lastly, a Christian ought so to fast that he shuns all vices as far as he can. For it is written: [[Ecclus 34:31|a man that fasteth for his sins, and doth the same again, what doth his humbling himself profit him?|Homo qui jejunat in peccatis suis, et iterum facit ea, quid proficit humiliando se?]]

paras.t: Iterum, quum aliquem justum sensatum et laudabiliter in omnibus se habentem conspicimus, apprehendamus vestem ipsius, dicentes: Ibimus tecum: audivimus enim quoniam Dominus tecum est. Hocque dicendo, sequamur vestigia ejus, seu virtutum exempla. Ideo enim in Ecclesiastico dicitur: Quum videris sensatum, statim evigila ad illum; et, Cum viro sancto assiduus esto.
paras.en: Again, when we see some just man, of good understanding and bearing himself praiseworthily in all things, let us take hold of his garment, saying: [[8:23|We will go with you|Ibimus tecum]]: [[8:23|for we have heard that God is with you|audivimus enim quoniam Dominus tecum est]] [Denis has *with thee* and *the Lord*, fitting the words to one man]. And saying this, let us follow his footsteps, that is, the examples of his virtues. For this is why it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 6:36|if thou see a man of understanding, go to him early in the morning|Quum videris sensatum, statim evigila ad illum]]; and: [[Ecclus 37:15|be continually with a holy man|Cum viro sancto assiduus esto]].

9.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli noni: Onus verbi Domini.
9.title_en: Literal explanation of the ninth chapter: The burden of the word of the Lord.

paras.t: CAPITULUM nunc elucidandum, obscuritatibus plenum est, atque ob id a diversis diversimode explanatur. Porro divus Hieronymus in exordio expositionis ejus affirmat: Omnis hæc visio, ad vocationem gentium et exstructionem Ecclesiæ pertinet. Verumtamen expositio ista S. Hieronymi, videtur aliis potius spiritualis et mystica, quam litteralis: idcirco quidam exponunt ad litteram de triumphis Judæorum tempore Machabæorum, alii de victoriis Alexandri Magni. Judæi vero putant hæc corporaliter adimplenda in adventu regis Messiæ, quem inaniter præstolantur venturum, et in hoc mundo temporaliter regnaturum; civitates quoque et regna hic expressa, imo totum orbem Judæis subjecturum, non obstante quod in hoc ipso capitulo primus Christi adventus in omnimoda paupertate describatur. Primo igitur breviter introducenda est expositio B. Hieronymi.
paras.en: The chapter now to be explained is full of obscurities, and for that reason it is explained in different ways by different men. Now St. Jerome, at the opening of his exposition of it, affirms: This whole vision belongs to the calling of the Gentiles and the building up of the Church. Yet this exposition of St. Jerome seems to others to be spiritual and mystical rather than literal; and so some expound it literally of the triumphs of the Jews in the time of the Machabees, others of the victories of Alexander the Great. The Jews, however, think that these things are to be fulfilled bodily at the coming of the king Messias, whom they vainly await as one who is to come and to reign temporally in this world; and that the cities and kingdoms named here, nay the whole world, will be made subject to the Jews: notwithstanding that in this very chapter the first coming of Christ is described in utter poverty. First, then, the exposition of blessed Jerome is to be set out briefly.

paras.t: Onus verbi Domini, id est afflictio prophetico Dei eloquio designata, in terra Adrach; Adrach, secundum Hieronymum, est dictio ex duobus integris composita, scilicet ab AD, quod est acutum, et DRACH, quod est molle. Itaque, Onus verbi Domini Adrach, id est acutum in peccatores, et molle in justos, in terra, id est, hominibus imminet. Istudque onus verbi Domini, et Damasci requiei ejus, id est super Damascum, quæ est requies ejus, scilicet oneris hujus, vel requies Domini, cujus onus super eam incubuit. Unde Adrach quidam referunt ad populum Judæorum (in quos Dominus austeritatem clementiamque suam exercuit: in eos quidem qui crediderunt, clementiam; in alios, æquitatis rigorem), Damascum autem, ad vocationem gentilium. Quia Domini est oculus hominis, id est, oculus cujuscumque de gentibus in Deum fide respiciens, ad Dominum pertinet, et omnium tribuum Israel, id est, oculus omnium Israelitarum in Deum respicientium, similiter Dei est.
paras.en: [[9:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the affliction signified by God's prophetic utterance, [[9:1|in the land of Hadrach|in terra Adrach]]. Adrach, according to Jerome, is a word compounded of two whole words, namely of AD, which means sharp, and DRACH, which means soft. And so, [[9:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]] Adrach, that is, sharp against sinners and soft towards the just, hangs over the land, that is, over men. And this burden of the word of the Lord, [[9:1|and of Damascus the rest thereof|et Damasci requiei ejus]], that is, upon Damascus, which is its rest, namely the rest of this burden; or the rest of the Lord, whose burden lay upon it. Hence some refer Adrach to the people of the Jews (on whom the Lord exercised both his severity and his clemency: clemency on those who believed, on the others the rigour of equity), and Damascus to the calling of the Gentiles. [[9:1|for the eye of man|Quia Domini est oculus hominis]] is the Lord's, that is, the eye of anyone from among the Gentiles who looks to God by faith belongs to the Lord, [[9:1|and of all the tribes of Israel|et omnium tribuum Israel]], that is, the eye of all the Israelites who look to God is likewise God's.

paras.t: Emath quoque, id est urbs illa quæ alio nomine Antiochia appellatur, in terminis ejus, et Tyrus et Sidon: id est, civitates istæ erunt in terminis Damasci vel terræ Adrach, credendo in Dominum Salvatorem, cui Pater ait in Psalmo: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam. Et rursus de Tyro cantat Psalmista: Audi, filia, et vide, et concupiscet rex decorem tuum, quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabunt eum; et filiæ Tyri in muneribus, etc. Assumpserunt sibi quippe sapientiam valde: nam ante conversionem ad fidem, in sapientia sæculi abundare conatæ sunt, deinceps fide suscepta, in sapientia christiana.
paras.en: [[9:2|Emath also|Emath quoque]], that is, the city which by another name is called Antioch, [[9:2|in the borders thereof, and Tyre, and Sidon|in terminis ejus, et Tyrus et Sidon]]: that is, these cities will be within the borders of Damascus, or of the land of Adrach, by believing in the Lord the Saviour, to whom the Father says in the Psalm: [[Ps 2:8|Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance|Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam]]. And again the Psalmist sings of Tyre: [[Ps 44:11|Hearken, O daughter, and see|Audi, filia, et vide]], [[Ps 44:12|And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore|et concupiscet rex decorem tuum, quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabunt eum]]; [[Ps 44:13|And the daughters of Tyre with gifts|et filiæ Tyri in muneribus]], etc. [[9:2|for they have taken to themselves to be exceeding wise|Assumpserunt sibi quippe sapientiam valde]]: for before their conversion to the faith they strove to abound in the wisdom of the world, and afterwards, having received the faith, in Christian wisdom.

paras.t: Et ædificavit Tyrus munitionem suam, id est sophismata sua et dialecticæ retia, contra fidei veritatem, antequam fidei obediret; et coacervavit argentum, id est eloquentiæ nitorem, quasi humum, id est copiose, et aurum, id est sensuum calliditatem, ut lutum platearum. Sed istæ munitiones, per spiritualia arma sapientiæ atque virtutum Apostolorum dejectæ sunt, quemadmodum ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus: Arma militiæ nostræ non carnalia sunt, sed potentia Deo ad destructionem munitionum, consilia destruentes et omnem altitudinem extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei, et in captivitatem redigentes omnem intellectum in obsequium Christi.
paras.en: [[9:3|And Tyre hath built herself a strong hold|Et ædificavit Tyrus munitionem suam]], that is, her sophisms and the nets of dialectic, against the truth of the faith, before she obeyed the faith; [[9:3|and heaped together silver|et coacervavit argentum]], that is, the brilliance of eloquence, [[9:3|as earth|quasi humum]], that is, in abundance, [[9:3|and gold|et aurum]], that is, the cunning of her thoughts, [[9:3|as the mire of the streets|ut lutum platearum]]. But these strongholds were cast down by the spiritual arms of the wisdom and virtues of the Apostles, as the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 10:4|For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but mighty to God, unto the pulling down of fortifications, destroying counsels|Arma militiæ nostræ non carnalia sunt, sed potentia Deo ad destructionem munitionum, consilia destruentes]] [[2 Cor 10:5|And every height that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God: and bringing into captivity every understanding unto the obedience of Christ|et omnem altitudinem extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei, et in captivitatem redigentes omnem intellectum in obsequium Christi]].

paras.t: Ecce Dominus possidebit eam, convertendo eam ad fidem; et percutiet in mari fortitudinem ejus: id est, in mundo isto, qui est mare magnum amaritudine vitiorum, inquietudine negotiorum, multitudine periclitantium, conteret per apostolicam prædicationem præfatas Tyri munitiones, ne quid pristinæ sapientiæ in ea permaneat, sed eloquentiam suam atque scientiam in Dei convertat honorem; et hæc igne devorabitur, id est, quidquid vitiorum in ea est, igne illo purgabitur et tolletur, de quo Salvator: Ignem, inquit, veni mittere in terram. De quo in Matthæo loquitur Joannes Baptista, Ipse baptizabit vos in Spiritu Sancto et igni.
paras.en: [[9:4|Behold the Lord shall possess her|Ecce Dominus possidebit eam]], by converting her to the faith; [[9:4|and shall strike her strength in the sea|et percutiet in mari fortitudinem ejus]]: that is, in this world, which is a great sea for the bitterness of its vices, the restlessness of its business and the multitude of those in peril, he will crush the aforesaid strongholds of Tyre by the apostolic preaching, so that nothing of her former wisdom may remain in her, but she may turn her eloquence and knowledge to the honour of God; [[9:4|and she shall be devoured with fire|et hæc igne devorabitur]], that is, whatever of vice is in her shall be purged and taken away by that fire of which the Saviour says: [[Luke 12:49|I am come to cast fire|Ignem]], he says, [[Luke 12:49|on the earth|veni mittere in terram]]. Of which John the Baptist speaks in Matthew: [[Matt 3:11|he shall baptize you in the Holy Ghost and fire|Ipse baptizabit vos in Spiritu Sancto et igni]].

paras.t: Videbit Ascalon, id est, urbs illa Palæstinæ considerabit conversionem Emath, Sidonis et Tyri, et timebit divinum judicium; et Gaza, et dolebit nimis, id est, etiam civitas illa, visis prædictis, sua vehementer lugebit peccata; et Accaron simili modo dolebit, quoniam confusa est spes ejus, id est, spes ejus pristina vana fuit, reprobataque est. Et peribit rex de Gaza, id est, princeps mundi hujus amplius in ea dominium non habebit, sed Christus; et Ascalon non habitabitur a talibus, quales ante demorabantur in ea, sed a fidelibus: nam et conversi, non fuerunt quod ante, eo sensu quod Salomon ait in Proverbiis: Verte impios, et non erunt.
paras.en: [[9:5|Ascalon shall see|Videbit Ascalon]], that is, that city of Palestine shall consider the conversion of Emath, Sidon and Tyre, [[9:5|and shall fear|et timebit]] the divine judgement; [[9:5|and Gaza, and shall be very sorrowful|et Gaza, et dolebit nimis]], that is, that city too, having seen the things aforesaid, will mourn its sins vehemently; [[9:5|and Accaron|et Accaron]] will likewise grieve, [[9:5|because her hope is confounded|quoniam confusa est spes ejus]], that is, her former hope was vain and has been rejected. [[9:5|and the king shall perish from Gaza|Et peribit rex de Gaza]], that is, the prince of this world shall no longer have dominion in her, but Christ; [[9:5|and Ascalon shall not be inhabited|et Ascalon non habitabitur]] by such as dwelt in her before, but by the faithful: for once converted they were not what they had been, in the sense in which Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]].

paras.t: Et sedebit separator in Azoto, id est, Christus, qui triticum a palea, id est electos a reprobis, segregat, in populo urbis istius converso regnabit. Et disperdam superbiam Philistinorum, id est, elationem eorum tollam ab ipsis, ut discant a Salvatore, quoniam mitis est et humilis corde. Et auferam sanguinem ejus, id est verba crudelitatis atque blasphemiæ, de ore ejus, et abominationes ejus, id est idololatriam et esum idolothytorum, de medio dentium ejus, ita quod ultra idola non colet, nec idolis immolata manducabit. Et relinquetur etiam ipse Deo nostro, id est, populus urbium harum Deo Israel adhærebit et attinebit, et erit quasi dux in Juda, id est ductor aliorum virtuosus in populo Christum confitente. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Relinquentur et ipsi Deo nostro. Et Accaron, id est hujus civitatis plebs conversa, quasi Jebusæus, id est, similis erit Jerosolymitanis credentibus. Jerusalem quippe alio nomine dicta est Jebus.
paras.en: [[9:6|And the divider shall sit in Azotus|Et sedebit separator in Azoto]], that is, Christ, who separates the wheat from the chaff, that is, the elect from the reprobate, will reign among the converted people of that city. [[9:6|and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines|Et disperdam superbiam Philistinorum]], that is, I will take their haughtiness from them, so that they may learn of the Saviour, because he is meek and humble of heart. [[9:7|And I will take away his blood|Et auferam sanguinem ejus]], that is, words of cruelty and blasphemy, [[9:7|out of his mouth|de ore ejus]], [[9:7|and his abominations|et abominationes ejus]], that is, idolatry and the eating of things offered to idols, [[9:7|from between his teeth|de medio dentium ejus]], so that he will no longer worship idols nor eat what has been sacrificed to them. [[9:7|and even he shall be left to our God|Et relinquetur etiam ipse Deo nostro]], that is, the people of these cities will cleave and belong to the God of Israel, [[9:7|and he shall be as a governor in Juda|et erit quasi dux in Juda]], that is, a virtuous leader of others among the people that confesses Christ. Hence the Septuagint translated: And they too shall be left to our God. [[9:7|and Accaron|Et Accaron]], that is, the converted populace of this city, [[9:7|as a Jebusite|quasi Jebusæus]], that is, will be like the believers of Jerusalem: for Jerusalem was called by another name Jebus.

paras.t: Et circumdabo domum meam, id est Ecclesiam militantem, ex his qui militant mihi, id est prædictis ad fidem conversis, vel prædicatoribus sanctis, qui muniunt alios, circumdant ac protegunt. Ideo subditur: euntes et revertentes, id est, hinc inde ad imperium Dei discurrentes, ad confirmandum credentes vel militantes. Isti sunt angeli sancti de cœlo ad terram euntes ac revertentes, quorum præsidio circumdat Deus Ecclesiam. Et non transibit super eos ultra exactor, id est diabolus pro culpa pœnam infligere exigens, insatiabilis homicida, persecutorque pessimus. Is namque Christifidelibus prædestinatis prævalere in finem nequaquam permittitur. Quia nunc vidi in oculis meis, id est, ista omnia implebuntur, quoniam ego Dominus nunc et in momento æternitatis vidi ista futura, et ea facere decrevi in oculo pietatis ac sapientiæ meæ.
paras.en: [[9:8|And I will encompass my house|Et circumdabo domum meam]], that is, the Church militant, [[9:8|with them that serve me in war|ex his qui militant mihi]], that is, with those aforesaid who were converted to the faith, or with the holy preachers, who fortify, surround and protect others. Therefore it is added: [[9:8|going and returning|euntes et revertentes]], that is, running to and fro at God's command, to strengthen the believers or those who fight. These are the holy angels going from heaven to earth and returning, by whose protection God surrounds the Church. [[9:8|and the oppressor shall no more pass through them|Et non transibit super eos ultra exactor]] [exactor: literally the one who exacts payment, hence Denis's gloss], that is, the devil, who demands to inflict punishment for guilt, the insatiable murderer and most wicked persecutor: for he is in no way permitted to prevail in the end over the predestined faithful of Christ. [[9:8|for now I have seen with my eyes|Quia nunc vidi in oculis meis]], that is, all these things will be fulfilled, because I the Lord have now, in the moment of eternity, seen them to come, and have decreed to do them, in the eye of my mercy and wisdom.

paras.t: Hæc est Hieronymi super hunc passum expositio, quæ si litteralis censenda sit, diligentis judicio derelinquo. Alii demum exponunt pro tempore Alexandri Magni; eritque sensus: Onus verbi Domini, id est punitio prophetice prænuntiata et superventura, in terra Adrach, id est Syriæ, et Damasci requiei ejus, id est in terra Damasci: quæ fuit civitas metropolitana in Syria, ita quod Syria in ea tanquam in capitanea urbe quievit, juxta illud Isaiæ, Caput Syriæ Damascus; quia Domini est oculus, id est inspectio, hominis et omnium tribuum Israel: id est, Deus inspicit et disponit actus humanos, præsertim populi Israel, quem peculiariter præelegit, et de quo incarnari decrevit. Quoniam ergo Deus omnia regit, ejus est mala punire, et bona remunerare. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Quia Dominus respicit homines, et omnes tribus Israel.
paras.en: This is Jerome's exposition of this passage; whether it is to be held literal I leave to the judgement of the careful reader. Others, again, expound it of the time of Alexander the Great, and the sense will be: [[9:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the punishment foretold by prophecy and about to come, [[9:1|in the land of Hadrach|in terra Adrach]], that is, of Syria, [[9:1|and of Damascus the rest thereof|et Damasci requiei ejus]], that is, in the land of Damascus, which was the metropolitan city in Syria, so that Syria rested in it as in its chief city, according to that saying of Isaias, [[Is 7:8|the head of Syria is Damascus|Caput Syriæ Damascus]]; [[9:1|for the eye|quia Domini est oculus]], that is, the regard, [[9:1|of man, and of all the tribes of Israel is the Lord's|hominis et omnium tribuum Israel]]: that is, God beholds and disposes human acts, above all those of the people of Israel, which he chose for his own, and of which he decreed to become incarnate. Since, then, God rules all things, it is his to punish evil and to reward good. Hence the Septuagint translated: For the Lord looketh upon men, and upon all the tribes of Israel.

paras.t: Emath quoque et Tyrus et Sidon in terminis ejus, id est, ad Syriam pertinent: sicut tertio Regum innuitur. Assumpserunt sibi quippe sapientiam valde, id est terrenam illam prudentiam, per quam temporalia colliguntur, ut vita præsens in deliciis, divitiis atque honoribus deducatur. De qua testatur Apostolus: Prudentia carnis mors est. De qua item apud Jacobum fertur: Non est sapientia ista de cœlo descendens, sed terrena, animalis, et diabolica. Et Baruch: Filii Agar, qui exquirunt prudentiam quæ de terra est, viam sapientiæ nescierunt.
paras.en: [[9:2|Emath also in the borders thereof, and Tyre, and Sidon|Emath quoque in terminis ejus]], that is, they belong to Syria, as is implied in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 8:65||]][[4 Kings 14:28||]]. [[9:2|for they have taken to themselves to be exceeding wise|Assumpserunt sibi quippe sapientiam valde]], that is, with that earthly prudence by which temporal goods are gathered, so that the present life may be spent in delights, riches and honours. Of which the Apostle testifies: [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the flesh is death|Prudentia carnis mors est]]. Of which, again, it is said in James: [[Jas 3:15|this is not wisdom, descending from above: but earthly, sensual, devilish|Non est sapientia ista de cœlo descendens, sed terrena, animalis, et diabolica]]. And Baruch: [[Bar 3:23|The children of Agar also, that search after the wisdom that is of the earth|Filii Agar, qui exquirunt prudentiam quæ de terra est]], [[Bar 3:23|but the way of wisdom they have not known|viam sapientiæ nescierunt]].

paras.t: Et ædificavit Tyrus munitionem contra hostes, et coacervavit argentum et aurum, etc. Erat nempe opulentissima civitas, et sita in corde maris, sicut in Ezechiele plenissime legitur. Ecce Dominus possidebit eam, et percutiet in mari fortitudinem ejus, et igne devorabitur. Hoc dicitur, quoniam Alexander rex divina virtute istam urbem devicit atque combussit: nam terra, lignis et saxis aquam maris a littore usque ad mœnia Tyri implevit, sicque eam accessit.
paras.en: [[9:3|And Tyre hath built herself a strong hold|Et ædificavit Tyrus munitionem]] against her enemies, [[9:3|and heaped together silver|et coacervavit argentum]] [[9:3|and gold|et aurum]], etc. For it was a most opulent city, and situated in the heart of the sea, as is read most fully in Ezechiel[[Ezech 27:4||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxvi–xxviii, the prophecy against Tyre; the words "in the heart of the sea" are from Ezech 27:4]. [[9:4|Behold the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be devoured with fire|Ecce Dominus possidebit eam, et percutiet in mari fortitudinem ejus, et igne devorabitur]]. This is said because King Alexander by divine power conquered this city and burned it: for he filled up the water of the sea from the shore to the walls of Tyre with earth, timber and stones, and so came at it.

paras.t: Videbit Ascalon, etc., id est, præscriptæ urbes Philistinorum, cognita Tyri destructione (quæ erat fortissima civitas: unde Nabuchodonosor eam obtinere non potuit modo præfato), vehementer timebunt, ne et ipsis similiter accidat. Timebit et civitas Accaron, quoniam confusa est spes ejus, id est, fiducia qua in auxilio Tyri confisa est, evacuata consistit. Et peribit rex de Gaza. Regulos enim Philistiim Alexander dejecit.
paras.en: [[9:5|Ascalon shall see|Videbit Ascalon]], etc., that is, the aforesaid cities of the Philistines, learning of the destruction of Tyre (which was a very strong city, so that Nabuchodonosor could not take it in the way just described), will fear vehemently lest the same befall them also. And the city of Accaron too [[9:5|shall fear|Timebit]], [[9:5|because her hope is confounded|quoniam confusa est spes ejus]], that is, the trust with which she relied on the help of Tyre has come to nothing. [[9:5|and the king shall perish from Gaza|Et peribit rex de Gaza]]: for Alexander cast down the petty kings of the Philistines.

paras.t: Et sedebit separator, id est Alexander, qui terras separavit et suis divisit, ut dicitur primo libro Machabæorum, in Azoto. Secundum Hieronymum, in Hebræo dicitur, Sedebit manzer. Et alius quidam affirmat, quod in Hebræo dicatur, Sedebit spurius: idque huic expositioni alludit, quoniam Alexander de adulterio natus fuit ex Olympiade uxore Philippi, de Nectanabi profugo rege Ægypti.
paras.en: [[9:6|And the divider shall sit|Et sedebit separator]], that is, Alexander, who divided lands and parcelled them out to his own men, as is said in the first book of Machabees[[1 Mach 1:7||]], [[9:6|in Azotus|in Azoto]]. According to Jerome, the Hebrew reads: There shall sit a manzer [that is, mamzer, one of unlawful birth]. And a certain other writer affirms that the Hebrew says: There shall sit a bastard; and this suits this exposition, since Alexander was born of adultery, of Olympias, the wife of Philip, by Nectanabus, the fugitive king of Egypt.

paras.t: Et auferam sanguinem ejus de ore ejus, id est, non permittam Alexandrum effundere sanguinem Judæorum, quorum se sanguinem dixit fusurum: quia ut dictum est sexto capitulo, quum contra Judæam veniret, Deo disponente, in mansuetudinem versus fuit; et abominationes ejus, id est, blasphemias ejus contra Deum Israel auferam. Et relinquetur etiam ipse Deo nostro. Nam Alexander tandem Deum verum Judæorum cognovit, et ei in templo sacrificavit, secundum Josephum. Et erit quasi dux in Juda: quia Judæis favorabilis fuit, præsertim quia ex Daniele ostenderant sibi, quod Deus prænuntiasset, ei subjicienda esse plurima regna mundi, imo Medorum atque Persarum, sicut in Scholastica habetur historia. Et Accaron quasi Jebusæus: id est, urbem Accaron nomine, subjugabit Judæis, quemadmodum per manum David fuerat Jebusæus Judæorum plebi subjectus, ut legitur secundo libro Regum.
paras.en: [[9:7|And I will take away his blood out of his mouth|Et auferam sanguinem ejus de ore ejus]], that is, I will not allow Alexander to shed the blood of the Jews, whose blood he had said he would shed: for, as was said on the sixth chapter[[Zach 6:3||]] [the margin refers to Denis's own commentary on Zach 6:3], when he came against Judea he was, by God's disposing, turned to gentleness; [[9:7|and his abominations|et abominationes ejus]], that is, I will take away his blasphemies against the God of Israel. [[9:7|and even he shall be left to our God|Et relinquetur etiam ipse Deo nostro]]: for Alexander at last came to know the true God of the Jews, and offered sacrifice to him in the temple, according to Josephus. [[9:7|and he shall be as a governor in Juda|Et erit quasi dux in Juda]]: for he was favourable to the Jews, above all because they had shown him from Daniel that God had foretold that very many kingdoms of the world were to be made subject to him, namely those of the Medes and Persians, as is related in the Scholastic History [the Historia Scholastica of Peter Comestor]. [[9:7|and Accaron as a Jebusite|Et Accaron quasi Jebusæus]]: that is, he will subject to the Jews the city named Accaron, as the Jebusite had been subjected to the people of the Jews by the hand of David, as we read in the second book of Kings[[2 Kings 5:6||]][[2 Kings 5:7||]].

paras.t: Præterea quæ sequuntur, de Machabæis exponunt. Et circumdabo domum meam, id est Synagogam et templum, ex his qui militant mihi, id est Juda Machabæo, fratribus et adjutoribus ejus, qui præliabantur prælia Israel cum lætitia, templumque Domini recuperaverunt ac mundaverunt, ut scribitur primo et secundo libro Machabæorum. Et non transibit super eos ultra exactor, id est tributi quæsitor. Unde primo libro Machabæorum legitur: Defecit impugnans eos super terram; reges contriti sunt in illis diebus.
paras.en: Further, what follows they expound of the Machabees. [[9:8|And I will encompass my house|Et circumdabo domum meam]], that is, the Synagogue and the temple, [[9:8|with them that serve me in war|ex his qui militant mihi]], that is, with Judas Machabeus, his brothers and his helpers, who [[1 Mach 3:2|fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel|præliabantur prælia Israel cum lætitia]], and recovered and cleansed the temple of the Lord, as is written in the first and second books of Machabees[[1 Mach 4:36||]][[2 Mach 10:1||]]. [[9:8|and the oppressor shall no more pass through them|Et non transibit super eos ultra exactor]], that is, the exactor of tribute. Hence we read in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 14:13|There was none left in the land to fight against them: kings were discomfited in those days|Defecit impugnans eos super terram; reges contriti sunt in illis diebus]].

paras.t: Postremo, si innumerabiles atque magnificæ illæ victoriæ [considerantur], quas primo Machabæorum in diversis capitulis leguntur Judas Machabæus et fratres ejus habuisse contra gentes vicinas, et præcipue contra Philistæos ac Syros, arbitror litteram istam satis congruenter posse applicari ad Machabæorum triumphos: cujus prosecutionem brevitati studens pertranseo, quia et unicuique diligenter legenti innotescere potest.
paras.en: Lastly, if one considers those countless and magnificent victories which, as we read in various chapters of the first book of Machabees, Judas Machabeus and his brothers won against the neighbouring nations, and especially against the Philistines and the Syrians, I think that this letter [that is, the literal sense of the passage] can be applied quite fittingly to the triumphs of the Machabees. Aiming at brevity, I pass over working it out, since it can be plain to anyone who reads carefully.

paras.t: ET quoniam sanctus Dei propheta hic Zacharias, Spiritu Sancto revelante agnovit, statim post eorum quæ dicta sunt expletionem, esse venturum regem Messiam, mox gratulabundus adjungit: Exsulta satis, filia Sion; jubila, filia Jerusalem, id est, plebs Juda in Jerusalem habitans, in qua fuit mons Sion, ubi fuerat templum: ita quod idem populus designatur per filiam Sion, filiamque Jerusalem: qui populus dicitur filia Sion, juxta modum loquendi propheticum sæpe jam explanatum.
paras.en: And since this holy prophet of God, Zacharias, knew by the revelation of the Holy Ghost that immediately after the fulfilment of the things that have been said the king Messias would come, he at once adds, rejoicing: [[9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exsulta satis, filia Sion]]; [[9:9|shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem|jubila, filia Jerusalem]], that is, the people of Juda dwelling in Jerusalem, in which was Mount Sion, where the temple had been: so that the same people is designated by the daughter of Sion and the daughter of Jerusalem. This people is called the daughter of Sion according to the prophetic manner of speaking, already often explained.

paras.t: Ecce Rex tuus, Christus Dominus: de quo in Jeremia inducitur, Regnabit rex et sapiens erit; et in Luca, Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis; veniet tibi, id est ad tuam operandam salutem, justus: quia secundum divinam naturam, totius sanctitatis atque justitiæ fons est. De quo in Sapientiæ libro legitur: Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis; virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est. Secundum naturam quoque assumptam justissimus utique fuit, quoniam Patris gloriam semper quæsivit, et peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus. Per viam quoque justitiæ pro hominibus satisfecit, pro illorum culpa se ipsum tradens caritative in pœnam acerbissimæ mortis, ut divinæ majestatis honori satisfieret, nec peccatum remaneret inultum. Hinc de se ipso loquitur in Joanne: Qui quærit gloriam ejus qui misit illum, hic verax est, et injustitia in illo non est. De quo et Stephanus ait Judæis: Patres vestri occiderunt eos qui annuntiaverunt de adventu Justi, cujus vos nunc proditores et homicidæ fuistis. Et salvator. De quo angelus dixit ad Joseph: Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum, ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. Nempe ut Deus, est salvator creative, efficienter et principaliter, peccata auctoritative dimittendo, gratiam per creationem infundendo, gloriam tribuendo; sed ut homo, Dei et hominum mediator, ipse quoque salvator est ut causa instrumentalis, dispositiva ac meritoria, quoniam sua sanctissima conversatione ac morte omnibus meruit indulgentiam, gratiam et gloriam. De quo ait Apostolus: Apparuit gratia Salvatoris nostri. In cujus typo Joseph appellatus est Salvator mundi.
paras.en: [[9:9|BEHOLD THY KING|Ecce Rex tuus]], Christ the Lord: of whom it is brought in in Jeremias, [[Jer 23:5|a king shall reign, and shall be wise|Regnabit rex et sapiens erit]]; and in Luke, [[Luke 1:32|he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]], [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]]; [[9:9|will come to thee|veniet tibi]], that is, to work thy salvation, [[9:9|the just|justus]]: for according to his divine nature he is the fountain of all holiness and justice. Of whom we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 12:15|as thou art just, thou orderest all things justly|Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis]]; [[Wis 12:16|For thy power is the beginning of justice|virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est]]. According to the nature he assumed, too, he was most just indeed, for he always sought his Father's glory, and [[1 Pet 2:22|did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth|peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]]. By the way of justice also he made satisfaction for men, handing himself over in charity, for their guilt, to the penalty of a most bitter death, that satisfaction might be made to the honour of the divine majesty and sin might not remain unpunished. Hence he speaks of himself in John: [[John 7:18|he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him, he is true and there is no injustice in him|Qui quærit gloriam ejus qui misit illum, hic verax est, et injustitia in illo non est]]. Of whom Stephen too says to the Jews: [[Acts 7:52|your fathers|Patres vestri]] [[Acts 7:52|have slain them who foretold of the coming of the Just One: of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers|occiderunt eos qui annuntiaverunt de adventu Justi, cujus vos nunc proditores et homicidæ fuistis]]. [[9:9|and saviour|Et salvator]]. Of whom the angel said to Joseph: [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus. For he shall save his people from their sins|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum, ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]. For as God he is Saviour creatively, efficiently and principally, forgiving sins by his own authority, infusing grace by creating it, bestowing glory; but as man, the mediator of God and men, he too is Saviour, as instrumental, dispositive and meritorious cause, since by his most holy life and death he merited pardon, grace and glory for all. Of whom the Apostle says: [[Tit 2:11|the grace of God our Saviour hath appeared|Apparuit gratia Salvatoris nostri]]. In type of him Joseph was called [[Gen 41:45|the saviour of the world|Salvator mundi]].

paras.t: Ipse pauper, secundum humanitatem, quantum ad usum. Siquidem, etiam ut homo, fuit Dominus universæ creaturæ, secundum quod dicitur in Joanne: Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus. Sed nil in hoc sæculo voluit possidere per usum, ut perfectissimæ paupertatis et contemptus omnium terrenorum temporaliumque bonorum nobis exhiberet exemplum. Unde de se ipso in Evangelio contestatur: Volucres cœli nidos habent, et vulpes terræ foveas; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet. Quum enim dives esset, propter nos egenus factus est, ut inopia ejus divites essemus. Hanc regis Messiæ paupertatem in primo suo adventu Jeremias admirans, ait: Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum? Et ascendens super asinam et super pullum filium asinæ. Hoc in Christo Domino nostro fuisse impletum in die Palmarum, sacrosancti Evangelistæ concorditer profitentur. Scriptum est enim in Luca: Quum autem appropinquaret jam ad descensum montis Oliveti, cœperunt omnes turbæ descendentium gaudentes laudare Deum voce magna, super omnibus quas viderant virtutibus, dicentes: Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, pax in cœlo, et gloria in excelsis. Credendum est quoque, quod Christus successive super utrumque animal sedit, quemadmodum super Matthæum plenius comprobavi. Porro, secundum Hieronymum, per asinam designabatur populus Judæorum, qui jugum legis diu portavit; per pullum, gentiles, qui populus frenorum legis divinæ ignarus, lascivus fuit atque indomitus.
