Christus ergo utrique animali insedit, ad figurandum quod in militanti Ecclesia electis ex utroque populo præsideret.
paras.en: [[9:9|he is poor|Ipse pauper]], according to his humanity, as regards use. For even as man he was Lord of all creation, according to what is said in John: [[John 3:35|The Father loveth the Son: and he hath given all things into his hand.|Pater diligit Filium et omnia dedit in manu ejus.]] But he willed to possess nothing in this world by use, that he might show us an example of the most perfect poverty and of contempt of all earthly and temporal goods. Hence he testifies of himself in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:20|The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests|Volucres cœli nidos habent, et vulpes terræ foveas]]; [[Matt 8:20|but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet]]. For [[2 Cor 8:9|being rich he became poor for your sakes: that through his poverty you might be rich|Quum enim dives esset, propter nos egenus factus est, ut inopia ejus divites essemus]]. Jeremias, marvelling at this poverty of the king Messias in his first coming, says: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum?]] [[9:9|and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt, the foal of an ass|Et ascendens super asinam et super pullum filium asinæ]]. That this was fulfilled in Christ our Lord on Palm Sunday the holy Evangelists declare with one accord[[Matt 21:1||]][[Luke 19:29||]]. For it is written in Luke: [[Luke 19:37|when he was now coming near the descent of Mount Olivet, the whole multitude of his disciples began with joy to praise God with a loud voice, for all the mighty works they had seen|Quum autem appropinquaret jam ad descensum montis Oliveti, cœperunt omnes turbæ descendentium gaudentes laudare Deum voce magna, super omnibus quas viderant virtutibus]] [Denis reads "of them that came down" where the Vulgate has "of his disciples"], [[Luke 19:38|Saying: Blessed be the king who cometh in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory on high!|dicentes: Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, pax in cœlo, et gloria in excelsis]] It is to be believed, too, that Christ sat upon each animal in turn, as I have shown more fully on Matthew[[Matt 21:7||]] [the margin refers to Denis's commentary on Matt 21:7]. Further, according to Jerome, by the she-ass was signified the people of the Jews, which had long borne the yoke of the Law; by the colt, the Gentiles, a people that knew nothing of the bridle of the divine law, and was wanton and untamed. Christ therefore sat upon both animals, to figure that in the Church militant he would rule over the elect of both peoples.

paras.t: Et disperdam quadrigam ex Ephraim, et equum de Jerusalem: id est, equi et currus non erunt causa pugnandi in tribubus Israel, sed [erit] pax atque concordia: ideo subditur, et dissipabitur arcus belli. Unde in Isaia habetur: Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium; et in Jeremia, In diebus illis Israel habitabit confidenter. In Christi enim adventu fuit pax inaudita, longa et magna, toto orbe Romanis subjecto. Ex his confunditur Judæorum figmentum, dicentium quod Christus in primo suo adventu omnibus mundi regnis temporaliter præsidebit, multosque gentilium occidet. Unde jam subditur: Et loquetur pacem gentibus: quia Apostolis jussit prædicare gentibus Evangelium pacis; imo per se ipsum aliquibus gentilium in Evangelio legitur prædicasse. Hinc de Christo loquitur Pater in Isaia: Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus; et item, Dedi te (inquit) in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Christus namque pacem docuit et præcepit; suisque Apostolis dixit: In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui. Et potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare, id est per omnem terram, a brachiis maris magni, inter se vehementer distantibus, et a flumine Jordanis, seu alio quolibet, usque ad fines terræ: quia ubique diffusa fuit prædicatio novæ legis. Propter quod prædixit Psalmista: Dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terræ.
paras.en: [[9:10|And I will destroy the chariot out of Ephraim, and the horse out of Jerusalem|Et disperdam quadrigam ex Ephraim, et equum de Jerusalem]]: that is, horses and chariots shall not be a cause of fighting in the tribes of Israel, but there shall be peace and concord; therefore it is added, [[9:10|and the bow for war shall be broken|et dissipabitur arcus belli]]. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 2:4|nation shall not lift up sword against nation|Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium]]; and in Jeremias, [[Jer 23:6|In those days|In diebus illis]] [[Jer 23:6|Israel shall dwell confidently|Israel habitabit confidenter]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 6; Denis's words, with "Israel", are those of Jer 23:6; Jer 33:16 has "Jerusalem"]. For at the coming of Christ there was a peace unheard of, long and great, the whole world being subject to the Romans. By this the fiction of the Jews is confounded, who say that Christ at his first coming will rule temporally over all the kingdoms of the world and slay many of the Gentiles. Hence it is now added: [[9:10|and he shall speak peace to the Gentiles|Et loquetur pacem gentibus]]: for he commanded the Apostles to preach the Gospel of peace to the Gentiles[[Mark 16:15||]]; nay, he himself is read in the Gospel to have preached to some of the Gentiles[[John 12:20||]]. Hence the Father speaks of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 55:4|Behold I have given him for a witness to the people, for a leader and a master to the Gentiles|Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus]]; and again, [[Is 49:6|I have given thee|Dedi te]] (he says) [[Is 49:6|to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. For Christ taught and commanded peace, and said to his Apostles: [[Luke 10:5|Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house|In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui]]. [[9:10|and his power shall be from sea to sea|Et potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare]], that is, through all the earth, from the arms of the great sea that lie far apart from one another, [[9:10|and from the rivers|et a flumine]] of the Jordan, or any other, [[9:10|even to the end of the earth|usque ad fines terræ]]: for the preaching of the new law was spread abroad everywhere. Wherefore the Psalmist foretold: [[Ps 71:8|he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth|Dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terræ]].

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta, vel Deus Pater omnipotens per Prophetam, alloquitur Christum. Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui, id est merito tuæ benedictæ passionis, et sanguinis tui effusione qua confirmatum est novum Testamentum: secundum quod Christus hora Cœnæ dixit Apostolis, Hic est calix novi Testamenti in meo sanguine; emisisti vinctos tuos, id est sanctos patres, et eos qui solo originalis peccati reatu differebantur a gloria, de lacu in quo non est aqua, id est de limbo inferni, in quo consolatio defuit seu refrigerium vitæ æternæ. Christus equidem in die resurrectionis hoc fecit, illos de inferno secum ducendo, sicut per Osee loquitur: Ero morsus tuus, inferne. Unde et hoc loco nomine laci, intelligit Hieronymus infernum, in quo nulla est refrigeratio. Verum de hoc inferno, quantum ad partem ejus in qua nulla est spes futuræ liberationis, sancti patres non fuerunt.
paras.en: Next the Prophet, or God the Father almighty through the Prophet, addresses Christ. [[9:11|Thou also by the blood of thy testament|Tu quoque in sanguine testamenti tui]], that is, by the merit of thy blessed passion and the shedding of thy blood, by which the New Testament was confirmed: according to what Christ said to the Apostles at the hour of the Supper, [[Luke 22:20|This is the chalice, the new testament in my blood|Hic est calix novi Testamenti in meo sanguine]]; [[9:11|hast sent forth thy prisoners|emisisti vinctos tuos]], that is, the holy fathers, and those who were kept back from glory by the guilt of original sin alone, [[9:11|out of the pit, wherein is no water|de lacu in quo non est aqua]], that is, out of the limbo of hell, in which there was no consolation or refreshment of eternal life. Christ indeed did this on the day of the resurrection, leading them with him out of hell, as he says by Osee: [[Osee 13:14|O hell, I will be thy bite|Ero morsus tuus, inferne]]. Hence in this place too Jerome understands by the name of pit [lacus, a pit or cistern] hell, in which there is no refreshment. Yet the holy fathers were not in that part of hell in which there is no hope of future deliverance.

paras.t: Denique quæ sequuntur, intricata sunt valde, et a diversis multiformiter intelliguntur. Itaque ait: Convertimini ad munitionem, id est, ad tutum locum redite, vincti spei, id est, qui captivi fuistis cum spe evadendi. Hoc S. Hieronymus bene atque catholice refert ad præfatos electos, qui cum Christo ascenderunt paradisum cœlestem, qui est munitissimus locus. Quidam exponunt de vocatione gentium ad evangelicam legem, quæ est firma munitio; alii, de reditu Judæorum a Babylone ad Jerusalem reædificatam; alii, de reversione Judæorum a facie Antiochi regis fugientium, qui auditis victoriis Judæ Machabæi fratrumque ejus contra duces Antiochi, ad Judam de diversis locis reversi sunt. Sed quoniam tædiosum atque prolixum esset omnes expositiones has prosequi, unam quæ rationabilior apparet, deducam.
paras.en: Then what follows is very involved, and is understood in many ways by different men. So he says: [[9:12|Return to the strong hold|Convertimini ad munitionem]], that is, go back to a safe place, [[9:12|ye prisoners of hope|vincti spei]], that is, you who were captives with the hope of escaping. This St. Jerome refers, well and in a Catholic sense, to the aforesaid elect, who ascended with Christ to the heavenly paradise, which is the most strongly fortified of places. Some expound it of the calling of the Gentiles to the law of the Gospel, which is a firm stronghold; others, of the return of the Jews from Babylon to Jerusalem rebuilt; others, of the return of the Jews who had fled from the face of King Antiochus, and who, hearing of the victories of Judas Machabeus and his brothers over the generals of Antiochus, came back to Judas from various places. But since it would be tedious and lengthy to pursue all these expositions, I shall follow out one, which appears the more reasonable.

paras.t: Sequitur ergo: Hodie quoque annuntians, id est, jam nunc per Zachariam prophetam ista prædicens atque insinuans, duplicia reddam tibi, id est præmium copiosum ac superabundans pro labore temporali et persecutione terrena, scilicet duplicem stolam, quæ est gloria corporis et animæ. Propter quod ait Apostolus ad Corinthios: Id quod est in præsenti modicum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum in sublimitate æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis. Christus quoque in Evangelio: Mensuram, inquit, bonam et confertam et coagitatam et supereffluentem dabunt in sinus vestros.
paras.en: It follows, then: [[9:12|as I declare today|Hodie quoque annuntians]], that is, even now foretelling and intimating these things by the prophet Zacharias, [[9:12|I will render thee double|duplicia reddam tibi]], that is, a plentiful and superabundant reward for temporal labour and earthly persecution, namely the double stole, which is the glory of body and of soul. Wherefore the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 4:17|that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation worketh for us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory|Id quod est in præsenti modicum et leve tribulationis nostræ, supra modum in sublimitate æternum gloriæ pondus operatur in nobis]]. Christ too in the Gospel: [[Luke 6:38|good measure|Mensuram]], he says, [[Luke 6:38|and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom|bonam et confertam et coagitatam et supereffluentem dabunt in sinus vestros]].

paras.t: Quoniam extendi mihi Judam, quasi arcum, id est, electos Judæos in Christum credentes mihi assumpsi: ut sicut per arcum adversarii compelluntur et sagittantur, sic per eos gentiles, qui fuerant Deo inimici, convertantur et Christo subdantur. De his enim in Isaia Dominus loquitur: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes longe, tenentes sagittam. De quorum sagittis ait Psalmista: Sagittæ tuæ acutæ, populi sub te cadent, in corda inimicorum regis. Implevi Ephraim, id est filios Israel ex decem tribuum plebe in Christum credentes, Spiritu Sancto. Nomine equidem Ephraim, regnum ac populus decem tribuum in Scripturis sæpius designatur. Apostoli autem pro majori parte, multique credentium ex Judaismo in primitiva Ecclesia, ex decem tribubus erant: de quibus cantamus in Psalmo, Principes Juda duces eorum, principes Zabulon, principes Nephthali. Et suscitabo filios tuos, Sion, id est Apostolos atque ex Synagoga Christifideles, super filios tuos, Græcia, id est super plebem Græcorum, cui multi Apostolorum prædicasse noscuntur; et ponam te quasi gladium fortium: id est, mea virtute infidelibus, o fidelis Synagoga, seu primitiva Ecclesia, prævalebis, convertendo eos ad fidem per hoc quod efficaciter ingeres eis verbum Dei: quod est gladius spiritus, sicut ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus. Unde et in Isaia habetur: Dominus posuit os meum quasi gladium acutum.
paras.en: [[9:13|Because I have bent Juda for me as a bow|Quoniam extendi mihi Judam, quasi arcum]], that is, I have taken to myself the chosen Jews who believe in Christ: so that, as adversaries are driven back and shot at with a bow, so through them the Gentiles, who had been God's enemies, may be converted and made subject to Christ. For of these the Lord speaks in Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes]] [[Is 66:19|afar off|longe]], [[Is 66:19|them that draw the bow|tenentes sagittam]]. Of whose arrows the Psalmist says: [[Ps 44:6|Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, into the hearts of the king's enemies.|Sagittæ tuæ acutæ: populi sub te cadent, in corda inimicorum regis.]] [[9:13|I have filled Ephraim|Implevi Ephraim]], that is, the children of Israel of the people of the ten tribes who believe in Christ, with the Holy Ghost. For by the name of Ephraim the kingdom and people of the ten tribes is often designated in the Scriptures. Now the Apostles for the greater part, and many of the believers from Judaism in the primitive Church, were of the ten tribes: of whom we sing in the Psalm, [[Ps 67:28|The princes of Juda are their leaders: the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali|Principes Juda duces eorum, principes Zabulon, principes Nephthali]]. [[9:13|and I will raise up thy sons, O Sion|Et suscitabo filios tuos, Sion]], that is, the Apostles and the faithful of Christ from the Synagogue, [[9:13|above thy sons, O Greece|super filios tuos, Græcia]], that is, above the people of the Greeks, to whom many of the Apostles are known to have preached; [[9:13|and I will make thee as the sword of the mighty|et ponam te quasi gladium fortium]]: that is, by my power, O faithful Synagogue, or primitive Church, thou shalt prevail over the unbelievers, converting them to the faith by thrusting upon them with effect the word of God, which is [[Eph 6:17|the sword of the Spirit|gladius spiritus]], as the Apostle says to the Ephesians [the margin gives Eph. vi, 16; the words are in Eph 6:17]. Hence it is said also in Isaias: [[Is 49:2|he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword|Dominus posuit os meum quasi gladium acutum]].

paras.t: Et Dominus Deus super eos videbitur: id est, gratia atque potentia ejus in illorum conversione splendebit ac innotescet; et exibit ut fulgur jaculum ejus: id est, sermo divinus (qui est sagitta spiritualis, de qua in Isaia asseritur, Posuit me Dominus quasi sagittam electam) splendide atque velociter ab Apostolorum ore ad corda illorum procedet. Et Dominus Deus in tuba canet, id est, per evangelicam Apostolorum prædicationem tubalem illis, quæ salutaris sunt, insonabit. Unde et Isaias: Quasi tuba, ait, exalta vocem tuam. Hinc Christus in Evangelio Joannem et Jacobum appellat filios tonitrui. Et vadet in turbine austri, id est, per Apostolos aliosque credentes, etiam australibus vitiorum turbine inquietis verbum Dei inferet gratiose.
paras.en: [[9:14|And the Lord God shall be seen over them|Et Dominus Deus super eos videbitur]]: that is, his grace and power will shine forth and be made known in their conversion; [[9:14|and his dart shall go forth as lightning|et exibit ut fulgur jaculum ejus]]: that is, the divine word (which is a spiritual arrow, of which it is asserted in Isaias, [[Is 49:2|hath made me as a chosen arrow|Posuit me Dominus quasi sagittam electam]]) will go forth splendidly and swiftly from the mouth of the Apostles to their hearts. [[9:14|and the Lord God will sound the trumpet|Et Dominus Deus in tuba canet]], that is, by the evangelical preaching of the Apostles he will sound, as with a trumpet, the things that are for their salvation. Hence Isaias too: [[Is 58:1|like a trumpet|Quasi tuba]], he says, [[Is 58:1|lift up thy voice|exalta vocem tuam]]. Hence Christ in the Gospel calls John and James [[Mark 3:17|The sons of thunder|filios tonitrui]]. [[9:14|and go in the whirlwind of the south|Et vadet in turbine austri]], that is, through the Apostles and other believers he will graciously bring the word of God even to those who are troubled by the southern whirlwind of vices.

paras.t: Dominus exercituum proteget eos, videlicet prædicatores et milites suos præfatos, ne frangantur adversis; et devorabunt et subjicient lapidibus fundæ, id est, prædicationibus et comminationibus Scripturarum infideles totaliter superabunt, eorumque vitia consument, et ipsos evangelicæ legi prorsus subjicient. Prophetæ autem frequenter metaphorice et obscure loquuntur. Et jam mox in fine hujus capituli elucescet, quod Zacharias metaphorice nunc loquitur. Et bibentes, id est prædicatores prædicti de aliorum conversione se ipsos spiritualiter reficientes, inebriabuntur quasi a vino, id est, exuberanter omnino delectabuntur in Domino, sicut et Paulus scribit discipulis suis: Nunc vivimus si vos statis in Domino; et replebuntur ut phialæ, id est, charismatibus Spiritus Sancti mirabiliter redundabunt: unde Paulus profatur, Repletus sum consolatione, superabundo gaudio in omni tribulatione nostra; et quasi cornua altaris, quæ sacrificiorum sanguine replebantur in lege. Juxta hunc modum fertur in Psalmo: Inebriabuntur ab ubertate domus tuæ; et, Justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei. Atque in Canticis: Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi.
paras.en: [[9:15|The Lord of hosts will protect them|Dominus exercituum proteget eos]], namely his aforesaid preachers and soldiers, lest they be broken by adversities; [[9:15|and they shall devour, and subdue with the stones of the sling|et devorabunt et subjicient lapidibus fundæ]], that is, by the preachings and threatenings of the Scriptures they will wholly overcome the unbelievers, consume their vices, and subject them entirely to the law of the Gospel. Now the prophets often speak metaphorically and obscurely; and presently, at the end of this chapter, it will become clear that Zacharias is here speaking metaphorically. [[9:15|and drinking|Et bibentes]], that is, the said preachers, refreshing themselves spiritually on the conversion of others, [[9:15|they shall be inebriated as it were with wine|inebriabuntur quasi a vino]], that is, they will delight in the Lord most abundantly, as Paul too writes to his disciples: [[1 Thess 3:8|now we live, if you stand in the Lord|Nunc vivimus si vos statis in Domino]]; [[9:15|and they shall be filled as bowls|et replebuntur ut phialæ]], that is, they will overflow wonderfully with the gifts of the Holy Ghost: whence Paul declares, [[2 Cor 7:4|I am filled with comfort: I exceedingly abound with joy in all our tribulation|Repletus sum consolatione, superabundo gaudio in omni tribulatione nostra]]; [[9:15|and as the horns of the altar|et quasi cornua altaris]], which in the Law were filled with the blood of the sacrifices. In this manner it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 35:9|They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house|Inebriabuntur ab ubertate domus tuæ]]; and, [[Ps 67:4|let the just feast, and rejoice before God|Justi epulentur et exsultent in conspectu Dei]]. And in the Canticles: [[Cant 5:1|eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved|Comedite, amici, et bibite; et inebriamini, carissimi]].

paras.t: Et salvabit eos Dominus Deus eorum in die illa, id est, in evangelicæ legis prædicatione sanctos suos prædicatores de omnium persecutorum manu eripiet, æternaliterque salvabit, ut gregem populi sui, id est sicut oves suas electas: quibus ait, Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri dare vobis regnum. Unde et Paulus ad Timotheum scribit: Dominus mihi adstitit et confortavit me, ut per me prædicatio impleatur; liberavit me autem Dominus ab omni opere malo, et salvum faciet in regnum suum cœleste. Quia lapides sancti, id est præfati Apostoli et viri perfecti a Deo electi, elevabuntur super terram, id est, per dona gratiæ meritaque præclara magni erunt in Ecclesia militanti, deinde per dona gloriæ et præmium consummatum in Ecclesia triumphanti et regione vivorum, quæ est terra ac patria Beatorum. De eis namque fertur in Psalmo: Constitues eos principes super omnem terram.
paras.en: [[9:16|And the Lord their God will save them in that day|Et salvabit eos Dominus Deus eorum in die illa]], that is, in the preaching of the law of the Gospel he will rescue his holy preachers from the hand of all their persecutors, and will save them eternally, [[9:16|as the flock of his people|ut gregem populi sui]], that is, as his chosen sheep, to whom he says: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri dare vobis regnum]] Hence Paul too writes to Timothy: [[2 Tim 4:17|the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, that by me the preaching may be accomplished|Dominus mihi adstitit et confortavit me, ut per me prædicatio impleatur]]; [[2 Tim 4:18|The Lord hath delivered me from every evil work and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom|liberavit me autem Dominus ab omni opere malo, et salvum faciet in regnum suum cœleste]]. [[9:16|for holy stones|Quia lapides sancti]], that is, the aforesaid Apostles and perfect men chosen by God, [[9:16|shall be lifted up over his land|elevabuntur super terram]], that is, they will be great in the Church militant through the gifts of grace and their excellent merits, and afterwards, through the gifts of glory and the consummated reward, in the Church triumphant and the region of the living, which is the land and fatherland of the Blessed. For of them it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:17|thou shalt make them princes over all the earth|Constitues eos principes super omnem terram]].

paras.t: Ecce ex isto ostenditur, quod Propheta hic metaphorice loquitur, præsertim quum subdat: Quid enim bonum ejus est, et quid pulchrum ejus? id est, quid Deo omnipotenti decorum, gratum et placitum est? nisi frumentum electorum, id est corpus Christi, ex pane frumenti consecratum, seu ipsemet Christus, qui ait: Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram, mortuum fuerit, ipsum solum manet; et alibi, Ego sum panis vivus; et, Caro mea vere est cibus. De quo et in Psalmo cantamus, Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium: ubi pro firmamento, alia translatio continet, Frumentum; et alia, Memoriale triticum. Et vinum germinans virgines, id est sanguis Christi sub vini specie, ad virgineam vitam sua gratia conferens ac perducens. Certum est autem, hæc de consueto materiali frumento et vino non posse intelligi: corporalia namque non sunt Dei præcipua bona. Quidam vero per frumentum electorum, intelligunt legem divinam, quæ est spiritualis fidelium cibus; per vinum vero, eruditionem sacræ Scripturæ, quæ gignit credentes.
paras.en: See, from this it is shown that the Prophet is speaking metaphorically here, especially as he adds: [[9:17|For what is the good thing of him, and what is his beautiful thing|Quid enim bonum ejus est, et quid pulchrum ejus?]]? that is, what is seemly, pleasing and acceptable to almighty God? [[9:17|but the corn of the elect|nisi frumentum electorum]] [corn: that is, grain, wheat], that is, the body of Christ, consecrated from wheaten bread, or Christ himself, who says: [[John 12:24|unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die|Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram, mortuum fuerit]], [[John 12:25|Itself remaineth alone|ipsum solum manet]]; and elsewhere, [[John 6:51|I am the living bread|Ego sum panis vivus]]; and, [[John 6:56|my flesh is meat indeed|Caro mea vere est cibus]]. Of which we sing in the Psalm too, [[Ps 71:16|there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains|Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium]]: where for firmament another translation has Corn, and another, A memorial of wheat. [[9:17|and wine springing forth virgins|Et vinum germinans virgines]], that is, the blood of Christ under the species of wine, which by its grace brings and leads men to the virginal life. Now it is certain that these things cannot be understood of ordinary material corn and wine: for bodily things are not the chief goods of God. Some, however, understand by the corn of the elect the divine law, which is the spiritual food of the faithful; and by the wine, the learning of sacred Scripture, which begets believers.

10.title: Expositio litteralis capituli decimi: Petite a Domino pluviam.
10.title_en: Literal explanation of the tenth chapter: Ask ye of the Lord rain.

paras.t: Quemadmodum præcedens capitulum, præsertim ab illo loco, Exsulta satis, filia Sion, a quibusdam ad litteram exponitur pro tempore Christi, ita et præsens capitulum. Verumtamen aliqui ipsum exponunt de multiplicatione fructuum terræ, et magnitudine victoriarum tempore Machabæorum. Tanta demum est capituli hujus difficultas, ut S. Hieronymus dicat : Omnis hic locus obscurus et dubius est. Itaque primam expositionem, quæ spiritualior est atque utilior, diffusius prosequar, deinde aliam tangam.
paras.en: As the preceding chapter, especially from the place [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exsulta satis, filia Sion]], is expounded by some literally of the time of Christ, so also is the present chapter. Some, however, expound it of the multiplying of the fruits of the earth and of the greatness of the victories in the time of the Machabees. So great, indeed, is the difficulty of this chapter that St Jerome says: This whole passage is obscure and doubtful. I shall therefore follow out the first exposition, which is the more spiritual and the more useful, at greater length, and afterwards touch on the other.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo in præcedenti capitulo annuntiavit Propheta de Christi adventu et gentium conversione ad ipsum, nunc admonet : Petite, o omnes qui Christi optatis adventum, pluviam, id est cœlestis gratiæ et evangelicæ prædicationis irrigationem, a Domino, ut Deus Pater Filium suum mittat in mundum. De quo canit Psalmista : Descendet sicut pluvia in vellus, et sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram. Doctrina quippe pluviæ comparatur, juxta illud Deuteronomii : Concrescat ut pluvia doctrina mea. In tempore serotino, id est in ultima mundi ætate et novi tempore Testamenti, de quo ait in prima sua epistola Joannes : Novissima hora est. Et Dominus faciet nives, id est documenta et gratiæ dona, vitiorum ardorem et concupiscentiæ æstum exstinguentia, et pluviam imbris (de qua jam dictum est), quæ animæ infecunditatem siccitatemque tollit. Et dabit eis singulis herbam, id est incrementum spiritualis fecunditatis, in agro cordis, vel in ipsa Ecclesia, quæ est ager dominicus. Hæc ergo ad veri Dei cultum pertinentia, sunt petenda.
paras.en: Since, then, in the preceding chapter the Prophet foretold the coming of Christ and the conversion of the Gentiles to him, he now admonishes: [[10:1|Ask ye|Petite]], O all you who long for the coming of Christ, [[10:1|rain|pluviam]], that is, the watering of heavenly grace and of the preaching of the Gospel, [[10:1|of the Lord|a Domino]], that God the Father may send his Son into the world. Of him the Psalmist sings: [[Ps 71:6|He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; and as showers falling gently upon the earth|Descendet sicut pluvia in vellus, et sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram]]. For doctrine is compared to rain, according to that of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:2|Let my doctrine gather as the rain|Concrescat ut pluvia doctrina mea]]. [[10:1|in the latter season|In tempore serotino]], that is, in the last age of the world and the time of the New Testament, of which John says in his first epistle: [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]. [[10:1|and the Lord will make snows|Et Dominus faciet nives]], that is, teachings and gifts of grace, which quench the heat of the vices and the burning of concupiscence, and [[10:1|showers of rain|pluviam imbris]] (of which we have already spoken), which take away the barrenness and dryness of the soul. [[10:1|and will give them|Et dabit eis]] [[10:1|to every one grass|singulis herbam]], that is, an increase of spiritual fruitfulness, [[10:1|in the field|in agro]] of the heart, or in the Church herself, which is the Lord's field. These things, then, which belong to the worship of the true God, are to be asked for.

paras.t: Quia simulacra locuta sunt inutile : id est, idola, quæ gentiles et aliquando Judæi coluerunt, inutiliter suis cultoribus sunt locuta, imo dæmones per illas imagines : non enim statuæ illæ, sed dæmones per eas, responsa dederunt; et divini, id est futurorum conjectores, viderunt mendacium, id est, falsum prædixerunt; et somniatores, id est, qui ex somniis suis phantasticis de rebus ferre sententiam præsumpserunt, frustra locuti sunt aliis, et vane consolabantur desolatos. Idololatriæ namque divinationibus, somniis atque auguriis intendebant gentiles, et frequenter Judæi. Quocontra scriptum est in Levitico : Non augurabimini, nec observabitis somnia. In Ecclesiastico quoque : Somnia extollunt imprudentes. Quasi qui apprehendit umbram, et persequitur ventum, secundum hoc visio somniorum. Multos errare fecerunt somnia, et exciderunt sperantes in illis. Divinatio erroris et auguria vanitas est; ne dederis cor tuum in illis.
paras.en: [[10:2|For the idols have spoken what was unprofitable|Quia simulacra locuta sunt inutile]]: that is, the idols which the Gentiles, and at times the Jews, worshipped spoke unprofitably to their worshippers; or rather the demons spoke through those images, for it was not those statues but the demons through them that gave answers. [[10:2|and the diviners|et divini]], that is, those who guess at things to come, [[10:2|have seen a lie|viderunt mendacium]], that is, foretold what was false; [[10:2|and the dreamers|et somniatores]], that is, those who presumed to pass judgment on things from their own fanciful dreams, [[10:2|have spoken vanity|frustra locuti sunt]] to others, [[10:2|they comforted in vain|et vane consolabantur]] the desolate. For the Gentiles, and often the Jews, gave themselves to idolatry, divinations, dreams and auguries. Against this it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:26|You shall not divine nor observe dreams|Non augurabimini, nec observabitis somnia]]. And in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 34:1|dreams lift up fools|Somnia extollunt imprudentes]]. [[Ecclus 34:2|like to him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind|Quasi qui apprehendit umbram, et persequitur ventum]], so is [[Ecclus 34:3|the vision of dreams|secundum hoc visio somniorum]] [Denis joins the words *secundum hoc visio somniorum*, "according to this is the vision of dreams", from verse 3 to the end of verse 2]. [[Ecclus 34:7|dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them|Multos errare fecerunt somnia, et exciderunt sperantes in illis]]. [[Ecclus 34:5|Deceitful divinations and lying omens and the dreams of evildoers, are vanity|Divinatio erroris et auguria vanitas est]]; [[Ecclus 34:6|set not thy heart upon them|ne dederis cor tuum in illis]].

paras.t: Idcirco abducti sunt quasi grex : id est, prædicta vanitatibus intenti, per errores a via veritatis atque justitiæ erraverunt; vel, in captivitatem translati sunt. Propter quod in Isaia legitur : Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus; unusquisque in viam suam declinavit. Affligentur adversis et debitis pœnis, nisi pœniteant, quia non est eis pastor, id est fidelis atque idoneus doctor, prælatus seu princeps. Ideo Moyses oravit ad Dominum : Ne sit populus tuus sicut oves absque pastore. Et in Proverbiis Salomon scribit : Ubi non est gubernator, populus corruet.
paras.en: [[10:2|therefore they were led away as a flock|Idcirco abducti sunt quasi grex]]: that is, being intent on the vanities just named, they strayed through errors from the way of truth and justice; or, they were carried away into captivity. Wherefore we read in Isaias: [[Is 53:6|All we like sheep have gone astray, every one hath turned aside into his own way|Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus; unusquisque in viam suam declinavit]]. [[10:2|they shall be afflicted|Affligentur]] with adversities and deserved punishments, unless they repent, [[10:2|because they have no shepherd|quia non est eis pastor]], that is, no faithful and fit teacher, prelate or prince. Therefore Moses prayed to the Lord: [[Num 27:17|lest the people of the Lord be as sheep without a shepherd|Ne sit populus tuus sicut oves absque pastore]] [Denis has *populus tuus*, "thy people"]. And Solomon writes in Proverbs: [[Prov 11:14|Where there is no governor, the people shall fall|Ubi non est gubernator, populus corruet]].

paras.t: Super pastores iratus est furor meus. Istud de indignis et falsis pastoribus tam Judæorum quam aliorum intelligi potest, qui sua negligentia atque malitia se ipsos et alios perdiderunt. Hinc per Ezechielem Dominus protestatur : Væ pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos. His non tantum ira, sed et furor imminet Dei, quia judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet. Et Jeremias ait : Ululate, pastores, et clamate; et adspergite vos cinere, optimates gregis : quia impleti sunt dies vestri, ut interficiamini, et cadetis quasi vasa pretiosa. Et super hircos visitabo, id est, pastorum illorum discipulos, in vitiis consentientes suis pastoribus, puniam.
paras.en: [[10:3|My wrath is kindled against the shepherds|Super pastores iratus est furor meus]]. This may be understood of the unworthy and false shepherds, of the Jews as well as of others, who by their negligence and malice destroyed themselves and others. Hence the Lord declares by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:2|Woe to the shepherds of Israel, that fed themselves|Væ pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos]]. Over these hangs not only the anger but also the fury of God [*furor*, the word the Douay-Rheims here renders "wrath"], because [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]. And Jeremias says: [[Jer 25:34|Howl, ye shepherds, and cry: and sprinkle yourselves with ashes, ye leaders of the flock: for the days of your slaughter and your dispersion are accomplished|Ululate, pastores, et clamate; et adspergite vos cinere, optimates gregis : quia impleti sunt dies vestri, ut interficiamini]], [[Jer 25:34|and you shall fall like precious vessels|et cadetis quasi vasa pretiosa]]. [[10:3|and I will visit upon the buck goats|Et super hircos visitabo]], that is, I will punish the disciples of those shepherds, who consent to their shepherds in their vices.

paras.t: Hujus autem causam vel signum subjungit Propheta. Quia visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum, id est oves, electos videlicet, domum Juda, puta Judæos in Christum credentes, et ceteros ei fideliter confitentes confessione laudis divinæ ac propriæ culpæ. Hæc visitatio in bono accipitur. Et posuit eos quasi equum gloriæ suæ in bello, id est, in bonis fecit eos fortes, victoriosos ac agiles contra humanæ hostes salutis, instar equorum prævalidorum.
paras.en: Of this the Prophet adds the cause or the sign: [[10:3|for the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock|Quia visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum]], that is, the sheep, namely the elect, [[10:3|the house of Juda|domum Juda]], that is, the Jews who believe in Christ, and the others who faithfully confess him with the confession of the divine praise and of their own guilt [Denis plays on the name Juda, which is interpreted "confession" or "praise"]. This visitation is taken in a good sense. [[10:3|and hath made them as the horse of his glory in the battle|Et posuit eos quasi equum gloriæ suæ in bello]], that is, he made them strong in what is good, victorious and nimble against the enemies of man's salvation, like very powerful horses.

paras.t: Ex ipso angulus, id est, ex præfato Dei grege processit regia dignitas, quæ continet populos, et copulat eos; et ex ipso paxillus, id est potestas seu ordo sacerdotalis, in quo alii pendent, quemadmodum in paxillo alia suspenduntur. Propterea in Isaia Dominus ait : Figam illum, puta Eliacim sacerdotem, quasi paxillum. Et Petrus : Vos, inquit, genus electum, regale sacerdotium. Denique in domino Papa utriusque potestatis residet plenitudo. Et sicut per angulum Imperator, ita per paxillum summus posset accipi Pontifex. Imo per utrumque illorum intelligi potest Christus rex pontifex noster, qui secundum naturam assumptam est de grege Ecclesiæ : sic enim caput Christi Deus. Et ipsemet : Narrabo, inquit, nomen tuum fratribus meis.
paras.en: [[10:4|Out of him shall come forth the corner|Ex ipso angulus]], that is, out of the aforesaid flock of God came forth the royal dignity, which holds the peoples together and joins them; and [[10:4|out of him the pin|ex ipso paxillus]], that is, the priestly power or order, on which the others hang, as other things are hung on a pin [*paxillus*, a peg]. Therefore the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 22:23|I will fasten him|Figam illum]], namely Eliacim the priest, [[Is 22:23|as a peg|quasi paxillum]] [the same word *paxillus*]. And Peter: [[1 Pet 2:9|you|Vos]], he says, [[1 Pet 2:9|are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood|genus electum, regale sacerdotium]]. Lastly, in the lord Pope resides the fulness of both powers. And as by the corner the Emperor, so by the pin the supreme Pontiff might be understood. Nay, by both of them may be understood Christ, our king and pontiff, who according to the nature he assumed is of the flock of the Church: for so [[1 Cor 11:3|the head of Christ is God|caput Christi Deus]]. And he himself: [[Ps 21:23|I will declare|Narrabo]], he says, [[Ps 21:23|thy name to my brethren|nomen tuum fratribus meis]].

paras.t: Et ex ipso arcus prælii, id est efficacia impugnandi adversarios veritatis, videlicet sapientia, virtus et eloquentia. De quibus testatus est Christus : Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non potuerunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri. Ex ipso egredietur omnis exactor simul : id est, a grege Dei electo separabitur et recedet omnis indignus ac reprobus dominator sive oppressor, juxta illud in prima Joannis Canonica : Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis : nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum.
paras.en: And [[10:4|out of him the bow of battle|ex ipso arcus prælii]], that is, power to fight against the adversaries of the truth, namely wisdom, strength and eloquence; to which Christ bore witness: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non potuerunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]]. [[10:4|out of him every exacter together|Ex ipso egredietur omnis exactor simul]]: that is, every unworthy and reprobate lord or oppressor shall be separated from God's chosen flock and shall go out from it [Denis takes *egredietur*, "shall come forth", as going out from the flock], according to that in the first Canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis : nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum]].

paras.t: Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio : id est, omnibus adversariis suis, mundo, carni, diabolo, victoriosissime Deo auxiliante prævaluerunt, quemadmodum ait Apostolus ad Romanos : Certus sum quia neque angeli, neque principatus, nec vita, nec mors, neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei. Et bellabunt, quia Dominus cum eis est. Nonne sancti in primitiva Ecclesia fortissime contra hoc sæculum nequam, contra diabolum et proprium corpus pugnaverunt? quum dicat Apostolus : Non coronabitur, nisi qui legitime certaverit; et item, Si (secundum hominem) ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi. Fuit autem Christus cum eis per gratiam singularem, qui ait : Sine me nihil potestis facere. Unde hac Dei gratia Petrus destitutus, mox ad vocem ancillæ succubuit : qui postea in verbo oris sui contra principes sacerdotum triumphanter pugnavit.
paras.en: [[10:5|And they shall be as mighty men, treading under foot the mire of the ways in battle|Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio]]: that is, with God's help they prevailed most victoriously over all their adversaries, the world, the flesh and the devil, as the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 8:38|I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities|Certus sum quia neque angeli, neque principatus, nec vita, nec mors]], [[Rom 8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God|neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei]]. [[10:5|and they shall fight, because the Lord is with them|Et bellabunt, quia Dominus cum eis est]]. Did not the saints in the primitive Church fight most bravely against this wicked world, against the devil and their own body? since the Apostle says that a man [[2 Tim 2:5|is not crowned, except he strive lawfully|Non coronabitur, nisi qui legitime certaverit]]; and again: [[1 Cor 15:32|If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus|Si (secundum hominem) ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi]]. And Christ was with them by a singular grace, who says: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]. Hence Peter, left without this grace of God, gave way at once at the voice of a maidservant[[Matt 26:69||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxvi, 69–74]; who afterwards fought triumphantly by the word of his mouth against the princes of the priests[[Acts 4:8||]] [the margin gives Acts iv, 8 and following].

paras.t: Et confundentur ascensores equorum, id est filii hujus sæculi in propria fortitudine confidentes. Quidam enim eorum bene confusi sunt, ad pœnitentiam redeuntes; alii in malitia persistentes, æternam confusionem illapsi sunt. Est nempe duplex confusio, scilicet bona et mala, secundum illud Ecclesiastici : Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam.
paras.en: [[10:5|and the riders of horses shall be confounded|Et confundentur ascensores equorum]], that is, the children of this world who trust in their own strength. For some of them were confounded to their good, returning to penance; others, persisting in malice, fell into everlasting confusion. For confusion is twofold, good and bad, according to that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 4:25|there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame that bringeth glory and grace|Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam]] [*confusio*, "confusion", the word the Douay-Rheims here renders "shame"].

paras.t: Et confortabo per dona Spiritus Sancti, per virtutes et gratiam multiformem, domum Juda, id est ex Judaismo credentes in Christum de regno duarum tribuum; et domum Joseph salvabo, eos videlicet qui ex decem tribubus crediderunt : qui nomine Joseph designantur, eo quod primus eorum rex fuit Jeroboam de tribu Ephraim filii Joseph. Et convertam eos ad fidem catholicam, quia miserebor eorum. Bonitas enim et pietas Dei, non meritum nostrum, est totius salutis et gratiæ nostræ prima principalisque causa. Ideo ait Psalmista : Brachium eorum non salvavit eos; sed dextera tua et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui, quoniam complacuisti in eis.
paras.en: [[10:6|And I will strengthen|Et confortabo]], through the gifts of the Holy Ghost, through the virtues and manifold grace, [[10:6|the house of Juda|domum Juda]], that is, those of the kingdom of the two tribes who believe in Christ out of Judaism; [[10:6|and save the house of Joseph|et domum Joseph salvabo]], namely those of the ten tribes who believed: who are designated by the name of Joseph because their first king was Jeroboam, of the tribe of Ephraim the son of Joseph. [[10:6|and I will bring them back again|Et convertam eos]] to the Catholic faith [*convertam*, "I will turn back", also "I will convert"], [[10:6|because I will have mercy on them|quia miserebor eorum]]. For the goodness and loving-kindness of God, not our merit, is the first and principal cause of all our salvation and grace. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 43:4|neither did their own arm save them. But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: because thou wast pleased with them|Brachium eorum non salvavit eos; sed dextera tua et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui, quoniam complacuisti in eis]].

paras.t: Et erunt sicut fuerunt, quando non projeceram eos, id est, donis gratiæ abundabunt, quemadmodum ipsi seu patres eorum, quando peccatis a me aversi non fuerant. Sicut autem tempore David fuit magna valde in Synagoga devotio, sic multoque plus, quando post resurrectionem Christi missus est filiis præelectis Israel Spiritus Sanctus. Ego enim Dominus Deus eorum, et exaudiam eos. Ideo Joannes in prima fatetur sua Canonica : Fiduciam habemus ad Deum, et quidquid petierimus, accipiemus. Christus quoque in Evangelio : Si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, hoc faciam. Porro in quam supernaturalibus et miraculosis operibus Deus exaudierit eos, in Actibus Apostolorum, legendis chronicisque Sanctorum relucet.
paras.en: [[10:6|and they shall be as they were when I had not cast them off|Et erunt sicut fuerunt, quando non projeceram eos]], that is, they shall abound in the gifts of grace, as they themselves or their fathers did when they had not yet turned away from me by sins. And as in the time of David there was very great devotion in the Synagogue, so there was, and much more, when after the resurrection of Christ the Holy Ghost was sent to the chosen children of Israel. [[10:6|for I am the Lord their God, and will hear them|Ego enim Dominus Deus eorum, et exaudiam eos]]. Therefore John declares in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 3:21|we have confidence towards God|Fiduciam habemus ad Deum]], [[1 John 3:22|And whatsoever we shall ask, we shall receive|et quidquid petierimus, accipiemus]]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[John 16:23|if you ask the Father any thing in my name|Si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo]], [[John 14:13|that will I do|hoc faciam]] [Denis joins the beginning of John 16:23 to the end of John 14:13]. Moreover, with what supernatural and miraculous works God heard them shines out in the Acts of the Apostles and in the legends and chronicles of the Saints.

paras.t: Et erunt quasi fortes Ephraim, id est sicut Josue ac ceteri justi de tribu Ephraim nati, qui ab æquitatis semita non discesserunt : prout de ipso in Josue legitur, quod non præterivit de universis mandatis Domini, ne unum quidem verbum. Et lætabitur cor eorum quasi a vino, id est, spiritualibus delectationibus exuberabunt in Deo. Quibus et Christus locutus est : Gaudete, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis; et rursus, Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quando videlicet omnem adversitatem et persecutionem patimini. Et filii eorum, id est discipuli per eos in Christo renati per prædicationem atque Baptismum, videbunt, id est, gratiam patrum suorum cognoscent, et lætabuntur, considerando beneficia Dei; et exsultabit cor eorum in Domino, sicut in principali objecto, omnis boni datore primo, summo, dignissimo, ad quem referenda est omnis lætitia ex creatis bonis concepta : ut omnino qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur, in quo solo delectari debet rationalis creatura.
paras.en: [[10:7|And they shall be as the valiant men of Ephraim|Et erunt quasi fortes Ephraim]], that is, like Josue and the other just men born of the tribe of Ephraim, who did not depart from the path of equity: as we read of him in the book of Josue, that [[Jos 11:15|he left not one thing undone of all the commandments|non præterivit de universis mandatis Domini, ne unum quidem verbum]]. [[10:7|and their heart shall rejoice as through wine|Et lætabitur cor eorum quasi a vino]], that is, they shall overflow with spiritual delights in God. To them also Christ said: [[Luke 10:20|rejoice in this, that your names are written in heaven|Gaudete, quia nomina vestra scripta sunt in cœlis]]; and again: [[Luke 6:23|Be glad in that day and rejoice|Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate]] [Denis has *in illa hora*, "in that hour"], namely when you suffer every adversity and persecution. [[10:7|and their children|Et filii eorum]], that is, the disciples reborn in Christ through them by preaching and Baptism, [[10:7|shall see|videbunt]], that is, shall know the grace of their fathers, [[10:7|and shall rejoice|et lætabuntur]], considering the benefits of God; [[10:7|and their heart shall be joyful in the Lord|et exsultabit cor eorum in Domino]], as in the principal object, the first, highest and most worthy giver of all good, to whom all joy conceived from created goods is to be referred: so that by all means [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]], in whom alone the rational creature ought to delight.

paras.t: Sibilabo eis, id est, verbum evangelicæ legis eis annuntiabo, et congregabo illos spirituali unione per fidem, spem et caritatem, quia redemi eos. Christus enim quantum in se est, universos redemit. Et multiplicabo eos, sicut ante fuerant multiplicati. Apostoli enim, aliique ex Judaismo conversi, plures spirituales filios habuerunt, videlicet universos quos genuerunt in Christo, quam unquam carnales filios habuit Synagoga.
paras.en: [[10:8|I will whistle for them|Sibilabo eis]], that is, I will proclaim to them the word of the law of the Gospel, [[10:8|and I will gather them together|et congregabo illos]] by a spiritual union through faith, hope and charity, [[10:8|because I have redeemed them|quia redemi eos]]. For Christ, as far as lies in him, redeemed all. [[10:8|and I will multiply them as they were multiplied before|Et multiplicabo eos, sicut ante fuerant multiplicati]]. For the Apostles and the others converted from Judaism had more spiritual children, namely all whom they begot in Christ, than the Synagogue ever had children according to the flesh.

paras.t: Et seminabo eos in populis, id est, per diversas gentium nationes et terras dispergam et mittam Apostolos et primos ex Judæis credentes : de quibus scriptum est in Isaia, Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt. Quibus et Christus ait : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Et de longe recordabuntur nominis mei, id est, de omnibus finibus mundi me collaudabunt, per se ipsos et eos quos converterint. Propter quod cecinit Isaias : A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi. Et vivent vita gratiæ in via, et vita gloriæ in patria, cum filiis suis spiritualibus ac devotis; et revertentur per mentis recollectionem atque affectuum adunationem ac simplificationem in Deum, ut unum illud quod solum necessarium est, ultimate intendant.
paras.en: [[10:9|And I will sow them among peoples|Et seminabo eos in populis]], that is, I will scatter and send the Apostles and the first believers from among the Jews through the various nations and lands of the Gentiles: of whom it is written in Isaias: [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt]]. To them Christ also says: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. [[10:9|and from afar they shall remember me|Et de longe recordabuntur nominis mei]] [Denis reads *nominis mei*, "my name", where the Vulgate has *mei*, "me"], that is, from all the ends of the world they shall praise me, by themselves and by those whom they convert. Wherefore Isaias sang: [[Is 24:16|From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi]]. [[10:9|and they shall live|Et vivent]] the life of grace on the way and the life of glory in the fatherland, [[10:9|with their children|cum filiis suis]], spiritual and devout; [[10:9|and shall return|et revertentur]] to God by recollection of the mind and by the gathering together and simplifying of the affections, so that they may aim finally at that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]].

paras.t: Et reducam eos de terra Ægypti, et de Assyriis congregabo eos, id est, de terris dispersionis eorum eripiam eos; et ad terram Galaad et Libani adducam eos. Plurimi quippe Judæi in mundi partibus conversi, ad terram promissionis rediisse ex devotione leguntur. Et non invenietur eis locus. Hoc accipi potest, quia tot converterunt, quod solita locorum angustia contineri non poterant, juxta illud in Isaia : Angustus est mihi locus; fac spatium, ut habitem.
paras.en: [[10:10|And I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt, and I will gather them from among the Assyrians|Et reducam eos de terra Ægypti, et de Assyriis congregabo eos]], that is, I will rescue them from the lands of their dispersion; [[10:10|and will bring them to the land of Galaad, and Libanus|et ad terram Galaad et Libani adducam eos]]. For very many Jews converted in the various parts of the world are read to have returned out of devotion to the land of promise. [[10:10|and place shall not be found for them|Et non invenietur eis locus]]. This may be taken to mean that so many were converted that they could not be held within the usual narrow bounds of the places, according to that in Isaias: [[Is 49:20|The place is too strait for me, make me room to dwell in|Angustus est mihi locus; fac spatium, ut habitem]].

paras.t: Et transibunt in maris freto, per loca aquosa redeundo ad terram optatam navigio aut pari adminiculo; et percutiet in mari fluctus, id est, fluctus marinos cessare Dominus faciet, ut secure procedant. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait : Me insulæ exspectant, et naves maris in principio, ut adducam filios tuos de longe. Et confundentur omnia profunda fluminis, id est, per modum erubescentis se habebunt, dum jussione divina a naturali desinunt fluctuatione turbulenta. Et humiliabitur superbia Assur, id est, Assyriorum elatio dejicietur, quia conversi ex eis, facti sunt humiles, increduli vero, in tartarum sunt projecti; et sceptrum Ægypti recedet a pristina idolorum cultura, vel in parte magna deficiet, quia Octavianus, sub quo natus est Christus, regnum Ægypti sibi subjecit, atque in diversas partes divisit, ut esset de cetero regnum humile et non rebelle.
paras.en: [[10:11|And he shall pass over the strait of the sea|Et transibunt in maris freto]] [Denis reads *transibunt*, "they shall pass", where the Vulgate has *transibit*], returning by watery places to the longed-for land by ship or some like help; [[10:11|and shall strike the waves in the sea|et percutiet in mari fluctus]], that is, the Lord will make the waves of the sea cease, so that they may go forward safely. Whence the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 60:9|the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the beginning: that I may bring thy sons from afar|Me insulæ exspectant, et naves maris in principio, ut adducam filios tuos de longe]]. [[10:11|and all the depths of the river shall be confounded|Et confundentur omnia profunda fluminis]], that is, they shall behave like one who blushes, when at the divine command they cease from their natural, turbulent surging. [[10:11|and the pride of Assyria shall be humbled|Et humiliabitur superbia Assur]], that is, the haughtiness of the Assyrians shall be cast down, because those of them who were converted became humble, while the unbelievers were cast into hell; [[10:11|and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart|et sceptrum Ægypti recedet]] from its former worship of idols, or shall in great part fail, because Octavian, under whom Christ was born, subjected the kingdom of Egypt to himself and divided it into several parts, so that it should thenceforth be a humble kingdom and not a rebellious one.

paras.t: Confortabo eos, videlicet primitivæ Ecclesiæ filios, in Domino, et in nomine ejus ambulabunt, id est in ipso, secundum voluntatem ipsius, atque in gratia ejus ac spe divina in omnibus conversari, prædicare, et facere satagent, dicit Dominus. Ecce in isto versiculo rursus loquitur Deus Dominus de Deo Domino, quasi de alio : per quod in divinis pluralitas Personarum innuitur.
paras.en: [[10:12|I will strengthen them|Confortabo eos]], namely the children of the primitive Church, [[10:12|in the Lord, and they shall walk in his name|in Domino, et in nomine ejus ambulabunt]], that is, in him, according to his will, and in his grace and in divine hope they will take care to live, to preach and to act in all things, [[10:12|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. Behold, in this little verse God the Lord again speaks of God the Lord as of another: by which a plurality of Persons in the Godhead is intimated.

paras.t: Nunc breviter tangam quomodo præsens capitulum pro tempore Machabæorum possit exponi. Itaque, quod in ejus exordio dicitur, Petite pluviam a Domino, etc., accipiendum est de pluviis quibus terra Israel fecundabatur, et quæ ad fructificandum necessariæ erant.
paras.en: Now I shall touch briefly on how the present chapter may be expounded of the time of the Machabees. So what is said at its beginning, [[10:1|Ask ye of the Lord rain|Petite pluviam a Domino]], etc., is to be taken of the rains by which the land of Israel was made fruitful, and which were necessary for its bearing fruit.

paras.t: Visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum, domum Juda, id est fideles atque constantes illos qui sub persecutione Antiochi permanserunt in lege, quibus præfecit Judam Machabæum et fratres ipsius. Ex quo grege fuit angulus, scilicet regia dignitas, et paxillus, id est sacerdotium, et arcus prælii, id est viri fortissimi ad pugnandum. Unde ait Hieronymus : Judas Machabæus, et quotquot de genere ejus principes fuerunt in populo, et angulus erat, quia regia potestate populum continebant; et paxillus, quia fuerunt sacerdotes; et arcus prælii, quia viri fortissimi, ut non solum aciem exercitumque disponerent, sed primi ad prælium prosilirent.
paras.en: [[10:3|the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock, the house of Juda|Visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum, domum Juda]], that is, those faithful and steadfast men who under the persecution of Antiochus remained in the law, over whom he set Judas Machabeus and his brothers. Out of this flock came [[10:4|the corner|angulus]], namely the royal dignity, and [[10:4|the pin|paxillus]], that is, the priesthood, and [[10:4|the bow of battle|arcus prælii]], that is, men most valiant in fighting. Whence Jerome says: Judas Machabeus, and as many of his family as were princes among the people, were both the corner, because they held the people together with royal power; and the pin, because they were priests; and the bow of battle, because they were most valiant men, so that they not only drew up the battle line and the army, but were the first to leap forward into the fight.

paras.t: Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio. Longo siquidem tempore oppresserunt Macedones. Et confundentur ascensores equorum, videlicet duces regum Græciæ, contra quos Machabæus cum suis pugnavit atque præliavit, sicut primo Machabæorum copiose describitur.
paras.en: [[10:5|And they shall be as mighty men, treading under foot the mire of the ways in battle|Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio]]. For over a long time they crushed the Macedonians [the Latin can also mean "the Macedonians had long oppressed them"]. [[10:5|and the riders of horses shall be confounded|Et confundentur ascensores equorum]], namely the generals of the kings of Greece, against whom Machabeus with his men fought and waged war, as is described at length in the first book of Machabees.

paras.t: Et confortabo domum Juda, id est eos qui de genere Judæ Machabæi fuerunt, vel ex duarum tribuum populo Machabæum juverunt; et domum Joseph salvabo, id est, illos qui ex decem tribubus sibi adsistebant, de manu adversariorum eripiam. Et convertam eos de locis ad quæ confugerunt, in quibus et latuerunt ad tempus, scilicet in deserto, juxta illud secundi libri Machabæorum : Judas Machabæus secesserat in desertum locum, ibique inter feras vitam in montibus cum suis agebat, et fœni cibo vescentes demorabantur. Ego Dominus Deus exaudiam eos. Quam mirabiliter Deus exaudierit Judam et commilitones ejus, primo et secundo Machabæorum libris satis describitur.
paras.en: [[10:6|And I will strengthen the house of Juda|Et confortabo domum Juda]], that is, those who were of the family of Judas Machabeus, or who from the people of the two tribes helped Machabeus; [[10:6|and save the house of Joseph|et domum Joseph salvabo]], that is, I will rescue from the hand of their adversaries those of the ten tribes who stood by him. [[10:6|and I will bring them back again|Et convertam eos]] from the places to which they had fled, in which they also lay hidden for a time, namely in the desert, according to that of the second book of Machabees: [[2 Mach 5:27|Judas Machabeus|Judas Machabæus]] [[2 Mach 5:27|had withdrawn himself into a desert place, and there lived amongst wild beasts in the mountains with his company: and they continued feeding on herbs|secesserat in desertum locum, ibique inter feras vitam in montibus cum suis agebat, et fœni cibo vescentes demorabantur]]. [[10:6|I am the Lord their God, and will hear them|Ego Dominus Deus exaudiam eos]]. How wonderfully God heard Judas and his fellow soldiers is described fully enough in the first and second books of Machabees.

paras.t: Et lætabitur cor eorum quasi a vino. Præliabantur enim prælia Israel cum lætitia, et post victorias quasdam valde supernaturales, maximas Deo gratias referebant, juxta illud secundi Machabæorum : In hymnis et confessionibus benedicebant Domino, qui magna fecit in Israel, et victoriam dedit eis. Et filii eorum videbunt patrum suorum triumphos, et lætabuntur.
paras.en: [[10:7|and their heart shall rejoice as through wine|Et lætabitur cor eorum quasi a vino]]. For [[1 Mach 3:2|they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel|Præliabantur enim prælia Israel cum lætitia]], and after certain victories quite above nature they gave the greatest thanks to God, according to that of the second book of Machabees: [[2 Mach 10:38|they blessed the Lord with hymns and thanksgiving, who had done great things in Israel, and given them the victory|In hymnis et confessionibus benedicebant Domino, qui magna fecit in Israel, et victoriam dedit eis]]. [[10:7|and their children shall see|Et filii eorum videbunt]] the triumphs of their fathers, [[10:7|and shall rejoice|et lætabuntur]].

paras.t: Sibilabo eis, id est, sono aliquo, ut revertantur, eis insinuabo, et congregabo illos, quia redemi eos de adversantium manibus; et multiplicabo eos, sicut ante fuerant multiplicati, antequam scilicet Babylonica fuit captivitas.
paras.en: [[10:8|I will whistle for them|Sibilabo eis]], that is, by some sound I will make known to them that they should return, [[10:8|and I will gather them together, because I have redeemed them|et congregabo illos, quia redemi eos]] from the hands of their adversaries; [[10:8|and I will multiply them as they were multiplied before|et multiplicabo eos, sicut ante fuerant multiplicati]], that is, before the Babylonian captivity took place.

paras.t: Et seminabo eos in populis. Judas namque cum suis diversas gentilium terras intravit atque vastavit, videlicet terram Philistiim, Idumæ, filiorum Ammon et Syriæ. Et de longe recordabuntur mei : in omni enim loco Deo gratias referebant.
paras.en: [[10:9|And I will sow them among peoples|Et seminabo eos in populis]]. For Judas with his men entered and laid waste various lands of the Gentiles, namely the land of the Philistines, of Idumea, of the children of Ammon and of Syria[[1 Mach 5:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. v, the whole chapter]. [[10:9|and from afar they shall remember me|Et de longe recordabuntur mei]]: for in every place they gave thanks to God.

paras.t: Et reducam eos de terra Ægypti et de Assyriis. Judæi namque hinc inde dispersi, audita eorum qui in terra Israel habitabant prosperatione, redierunt illuc quamplurimi. Et non invenietur eis locus, id est, terra Israel capere eos non poterit. Hoc per hyperbolen dictum esse intelligi potest, eo quod ultra spem plures valde reversi sunt. Cetera ex præinducta expositione utcumque clarescunt.
paras.en: [[10:10|And I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt|Et reducam eos de terra Ægypti]] [[10:10|and I will gather them from among the Assyrians|et de Assyriis]]. For the Jews scattered here and there, hearing of the prosperity of those who dwelt in the land of Israel, returned thither in very great numbers. [[10:10|and place shall not be found for them|Et non invenietur eis locus]], that is, the land of Israel will not be able to hold them. This may be understood as said by hyperbole, because very many more returned than could have been hoped. The rest becomes clear enough from the exposition given above.

10.title: De spirituali et mystica ejusdem capituli decimi elucidatione.
10.title_en: Of the spiritual and mystical explanation of the same tenth chapter.

paras.t: Universis autem fidelibus, id quod ait scriptura ista, implendum est: Petite pluviam a Domino, id est divinorum stillicidiorum instillationem a Deo in mentem, uberrimam quoque a Spiritu Sancto fecundationem, refrigerationem, et salutaris sapientiæ aquam. Unde apud Joannem dicitur: Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum. Et Dominus faciet nives, id est dona gratiæ, desideriorum malorum ardorem delentia; et pluviam optatam jam dictam infundet, secundum illud Apocalypsis: Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, bibat aquam vitæ gratis. Hinc in Joanne legitur: Clamabat Jesus: Si quis sitit, veniat ad me et bibat. Et dabit eis singulis herbam, id est bonæ famæ odorem, virtutum virorem, spirituale germen, in agro cordis atque Ecclesiæ. Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit.
paras.en: Now by all the faithful must be fulfilled what this scripture says: [[10:1|Ask ye of the Lord rain|Petite pluviam a Domino]], that is, the distilling of divine droplets from God into the mind, and also the most abundant fruitfulness, refreshment and water of saving wisdom from the Holy Ghost. Hence it is said in John: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum]]. [[10:1|And the Lord will make snows|Et Dominus faciet nives]], that is, gifts of grace, which put out the heat of evil desires; and He will pour in the longed-for [[10:1|rain|pluviam]] already spoken of, according to that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:17|he that thirsteth, let him come. And he that will, let him take the water of life, freely|Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, bibat aquam vitæ gratis]] [Denis reads *bibat*, let him drink, where the Vulgate has *accipiat*, let him take]. Hence we read in John: Jesus cried: [[John 7:37|If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink|Si quis sitit, veniat ad me et bibat]]. And He will give them [[10:1|to every one grass|singulis herbam]], that is, the fragrance of good repute, the greenness of the virtues, a spiritual shoot, [[10:1|in the field|in agro]] of the heart and of the Church. [[Matt 7:8|For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth|Omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit]].

paras.t: Quia simulacra, id est vana phantasmata, feminarum imagines cordi impressæ, peccata, præsertim avaritia, quæ idolorum est servitus, hæreticorum et schismaticorum figmenta et dogmata, hypocrisis, et cetera vitia specie virtutum velata, locuta sunt inutile, quia ad inanissima verba faciunt hominem prosilire; et divini, qui sibi quod Dei est usurpantes, de futuris prænosticant inordinate, et longam sibi vitam promittunt, viderunt mendacium, quia decepti; et somniatores frustra locuti sunt. Ecce his verbis docemur somnia vana contemnere, nec somniatorum verbis intendere. Circa quod multi imprudenter se habent, et tales sæpe a dæmonibus ad magnas illusiones trahuntur. Angelus quippe Satanæ se transfigurat in angelum lucis. Unde subjungitur: Abducti sunt a Deo et veritate doctrinæ per vitia et errores, affligentur ultione divina, quia non est eis pastor. Christum enim, qui ait, Ego sum pastor bonus, non imitantur: ideo devorantur ab infernalibus lupis, de quibus cantamus in Psalmo, Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi.
paras.en: [[10:2|For the idols|Quia simulacra]], that is, empty phantasms, images of women imprinted on the heart, sins, and above all [[Col 3:5|covetousness, which is the service of idols|avaritia, quæ idolorum est servitus]], the inventions and doctrines of heretics and schismatics, hypocrisy, and the other vices veiled under the appearance of virtues, [[10:2|have spoken what was unprofitable|locuta sunt inutile]], because they make a man break out into the emptiest words; [[10:2|and the diviners|et divini]], who, usurping for themselves what belongs to God, foretell the future inordinately and promise themselves a long life, [[10:2|have seen a lie|viderunt mendacium]], because they are deceived; [[10:2|and the dreamers have spoken vanity|et somniatores frustra locuti sunt]]. See, by these words we are taught to despise vain dreams and not to heed the words of dreamers. In this matter many behave imprudently, and such men are often drawn by the demons into great delusions. For the angel of Satan [[2 Cor 11:14|transformeth himself into an angel of light|se transfigurat in angelum lucis]]. Hence it is added: [[10:2|they were led away|Abducti sunt]] from God and from the truth of doctrine through vices and errors; [[10:2|they shall be afflicted|affligentur]] by divine vengeance, [[10:2|because they have no shepherd|quia non est eis pastor]]. For they do not imitate Christ, who says, [[John 10:11|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]][[John 10:14||]]: therefore they are devoured by the wolves of hell, of whom we sing in the Psalm, [[Ps 73:19|Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee|Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi]] [Denis has the singular, *animam confitentem*, the soul that confesseth].

paras.t: Super pastores iratus est furor meus. Sicut dicit S. Bernardus: A nullis sustinet Christus tantam jacturam atque injuriam, ut a sacerdotibus, prælatis, pastoribusque indignis, qui gregem sibi creditum negligunt, et animas pro quibus sanguinem suum Christus effudit, perire permittunt, imo sæpe et faciunt, subditos scandalizando, insufficientes vicarios substituendo, sæculariter carnaliterque vivendo. His ergo justissime iratus est furor impassionabilis Dei. Quocontra beatissimus archiapostolus Petrus in prima sua hortatur Canonica: Seniores, obsecro, pascite qui in vobis est gregem, providentes secundum Deum, non turpis lucri gratia, neque ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis effecti, et ex animo. Et super hircos visitabo, id est carnales et reprobos: de quibus in Evangelio fertur, quod Christus statuet oves a dextris, hœdos autem a sinistris. Visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum, domum Juda, id est veros Christi confessores, et electorum Ecclesiam. Tales enim Dominus Deus per gratiam Spiritus Sancti, angelorum præsidia et alia media, dirigit, custodit et salvat, quamvis pastores negligenter et vitiose se habeant, quemadmodum apud Ezechielem testatur: Ecce ego ipse requiram gregem meum, et pascam oves meas, salvabo gregem meum.
paras.en: [[10:3|My wrath is kindled against the shepherds|Super pastores iratus est furor meus]]. As St. Bernard says: From none does Christ suffer so great loss and injury as from unworthy priests, prelates and pastors, who neglect the flock entrusted to them and let perish the souls for which Christ shed His blood, nay often even cause them to perish, by giving scandal to their subjects, by putting inadequate vicars in their place, and by living in a worldly and carnal way. Against these, then, is the impassible wrath [that is, wrath without passion: God is angry without being moved or disturbed] of God most justly kindled. Against this the most blessed chief apostle Peter exhorts in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 5:1|The ancients|Seniores]], [[1 Pet 5:1|I beseech|obsecro]]: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|pascite qui in vobis est gregem]], [[1 Pet 5:2|taking care of it|providentes]] [[1 Pet 5:2|according to God|secundum Deum]], [[1 Pet 5:2|not for filthy lucre's sake|non turpis lucri gratia]], [[1 Pet 5:3|Neither as lording it over the clergy but being made a pattern of the flock from the heart|neque ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis effecti, et ex animo]]. [[10:3|and I will visit upon the buck goats|Et super hircos visitabo]], that is, the carnal and the reprobate: of whom it is told in the Gospel that Christ [[Matt 25:33|shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left|statuet oves a dextris, hœdos autem a sinistris]]. [[10:3|the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock, the house of Juda|Visitavit Dominus exercituum gregem suum, domum Juda]], that is, the true confessors of Christ, and the Church of the elect. For such as these the Lord God directs, guards and saves through the grace of the Holy Ghost, the protection of the angels and other means, however negligently and wickedly the shepherds behave, as He testifies in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:11|Behold I myself|Ecce ego ipse]] [[Ezech 34:10|will require my flock|requiram gregem meum]], and [[Ezech 34:15|I will feed my sheep|pascam oves meas]], [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|salvabo gregem meum]].

paras.t: Ex ipso angulus, id est, Deus ex grege suo præficiet principem virtuosum, qui contineat alios et conservet; et ex ipso paxillus, id est prælatus idoneus: propter quod in Jeremia, Dabo, inquit, vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina; et ex ipso arcus prælii, id est arma spiritualis militiæ, virtutes et dona Spiritus Sancti, quibus victorialiter contra omnia tentamenta pugnatur.
paras.en: [[10:4|Out of him shall come forth the corner|Ex ipso angulus]], that is, God will set over His flock, out of the flock itself, a virtuous prince, to hold the others together and preserve them; and [[10:4|out of him the pin|ex ipso paxillus]] [*paxillus*, a peg or stake that holds a thing fast], that is, a fit prelate: for which reason, in Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give|Dabo]], He says, [[Jer 3:15|you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]; and [[10:4|out of him the bow of battle|ex ipso arcus prælii]], that is, the arms of the spiritual warfare, the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost, with which the fight is waged victoriously against all temptations.

paras.t: Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio. Electi nempe ac virtuosi, divino suffulti auxilio, miserabilem istam ac lutosam carnem castigant, refrenant, sicque Satanam cum mundo suppeditant, cum Paulo dicentes: Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat; et cum Psalmista, Qui tribulant me inimici mei, ipsi infirmati sunt et ceciderunt. Et bellabunt contra concupiscentias, passiones et vitia, quibus impii vincuntur et obsequuntur, quia Dominus cum eis est per gratiam adjuvantem: aliter enim et ipsi fœdus inirent cum morte, et adversariis suæ salutis manum porrigerent. Ideo illud Jeremiæ dicere cum gratiarum actione humilitateque possunt: Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis: idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt. Et confundentur ascensores equorum, id est inaniter gloriosi in sæculo isto: de quibus cantatur in Psalmo, Ab increpatione tua, Deus Jacob, dormitaverunt qui ascenderunt equos.
paras.en: [[10:5|And they shall be as mighty men, treading under foot the mire of the ways in battle|Et erunt quasi fortes conculcantes lutum viarum in prælio]]. For the elect and the virtuous, upheld by divine help, chastise and rein in this wretched and miry flesh, and so trample Satan and the world under foot, saying with Paul: [[Phil 4:13|I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me|Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat]]; and with the Psalmist, [[Ps 26:2|My enemies that trouble me, have themselves been weakened, and have fallen|Qui tribulant me inimici mei, ipsi infirmati sunt et ceciderunt]]. [[10:5|and they shall fight|Et bellabunt]] against the concupiscences, passions and vices by which the wicked are overcome and which they obey, [[10:5|because the Lord is with them|quia Dominus cum eis]] by His helping grace: for otherwise they too would make a covenant with death and hold out their hand to the enemies of their salvation. Therefore they can say, with thanksgiving and humility, that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall, and shall be weak|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis: idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt]]. [[10:5|and the riders of horses shall be confounded|Et confundentur ascensores equorum]], that is, those who are vainly glorious in this world: of whom it is sung in the Psalm, [[Ps 75:7|At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback|Ab increpatione tua, Deus Jacob, dormitaverunt qui ascenderunt equos]].

paras.t: Et confortabo domum Juda, eos videlicet qui in verbis et actibus Dominum laudant; et domum Joseph, id est eos qui in virtutibus crescunt, salvabo. Joseph autem incrementum vel crescens interpretatur. Qui vero in virtutibus non crescit, decrescit. Ideo dicit Apostolus ad Colossenses: Ambuletis digne Deo, per omnia crescentes in scientia Dei.
paras.en: [[10:6|And I will strengthen the house of Juda|Et confortabo domum Juda]], namely those who praise the Lord in words and deeds; and [[10:6|the house of Joseph|domum Joseph]], that is, those who grow in the virtues, will I [[10:6|save|salvabo]]. For *Joseph* is interpreted increase, or growing. But he who does not grow in the virtues, goes back. Therefore the Apostle says to the Colossians: That [[Col 1:10|you may walk worthy of God, in all things|Ambuletis digne Deo, per omnia]] [[Col 1:10|increasing in the knowledge of God|crescentes in scientia Dei]].

paras.t: Et erunt quasi fortes Ephraim, id est, spirituali ubertate implebuntur. Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit.
