Merita quoque de meritis oriuntur, atque ad majora merita pertrahunt, sicut mala de malis, et mala minora ad graviora disponunt: idcirco qui modica negligit, cito deficiet. Ephraim autem interpretatur ubertas.
paras.en: [[10:7|And they shall be as the valiant men of Ephraim|Et erunt quasi fortes Ephraim]], that is, they shall be filled with spiritual abundance. For [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound|Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit]]. Merits also spring from merits and draw a man on to greater merits, just as evils spring from evils, and lesser evils dispose to graver ones: therefore [[Ecclus 19:1|he that contemneth small things|qui modica negligit]] shall soon fail [the Vulgate has *paulatim decidet*, shall fall by little and little; Denis has *cito deficiet*]. And *Ephraim* is interpreted abundance.

paras.t: Sibilabo eis, per instinctum angelicum ac divinum. Spiritus enim ubi vult spirat; et vocem ejus audis, sed nescis unde veniat aut quo vadat. Et congregabo illos, ut vinculo caritatis maneant jugiter adunati, uniusque moris habitent simul in domo: et multiplicabo eos numero et merito: quemadmodum ad Thessalonicenses orat Apostolus: Vos autem Deus multiplicet, et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes.
paras.en: [[10:8|I will whistle for them|Sibilabo eis]], by angelic and divine prompting. For [[John 3:8|The Spirit breatheth where he will and thou hearest his voice: but thou knowest not whence he cometh and whither he goeth|Spiritus enim ubi vult spirat; et vocem ejus audis, sed nescis unde veniat aut quo vadat]]. [[10:8|and I will gather them together|Et congregabo illos]], that they may abide ever united in the bond of charity, and dwell together in the house [[Ps 67:7|of one manner|uniusque moris]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxvii, 7; the words are from Ps 67:7]: [[10:8|and I will multiply them|et multiplicabo eos]] in number and in merit: as the Apostle prays for the Thessalonians: [[1 Thess 3:12|And may the Lord multiply you and make you abound in charity towards one another and towards all men|Vos autem Deus multiplicet, et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem et in omnes]] [Denis has *Deus*, God, for *Dominus*].

paras.t: Reducam eos de terra Ægypti et de Assyriis, id est de tenebris hujus mundi et potestate diaboli. Ægyptus namque, quæ interpretatur caligo, figura est mundi. Assyrius vero, qui secundum Hieronymum interpretatur arguens vel convincens, est diabolus, fratrum infatigabilis accusator. Et ad terram Galaad et Libani, id est ad societatem ac vitam spiritualem virtute splendentium, adducam eos, ut de vitiis ad virtutes transmigrent, virtutibusque dealbati nitescant. Galaad enim, transmigrationis testimonium; Libanus vero, dealbatio interpretatur.
paras.en: [[10:10|I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt|Reducam eos de terra Ægypti]] and [[10:10|from among the Assyrians|de Assyriis]], that is, out of the darkness of this world and the power of the devil. For *Egypt*, which is interpreted darkness, is a figure of the world. And the *Assyrian*, who according to Jerome is interpreted one who reproves or convicts, is the devil, the unwearied accuser of the brethren[[Apoc 12:10||]]. And [[10:10|to the land of Galaad, and Libanus|ad terram Galaad et Libani]], that is, to the fellowship and spiritual life of those who shine with virtue, [[10:10|will bring them|adducam eos]], so that they may pass over from vices to virtues, and, made white by the virtues, may shine. For *Galaad* is interpreted the witness of passing over, and *Libanus* whitening.

paras.t: Et transibunt in maris freto, id est, sæculum istud mari comparatum, sine submersione peccati perambulabunt; et percutiet in mari fluctus, id est, inquietudines mundi eis sedabit. Post tempestatem enim dat Deus tranquillitatem: qui non sinit nos tentari supra possibilitatem, et tribulationis tempore specialius adest. Et humiliabitur superbia Assur: id est, dæmonum tentatorum nostrorum præsumptio dejicietur, dum Christi virtute ab electis vincuntur, atque sub pedibus fortium conteruntur; et sceptrum Ægypti recedet: id est, mundanæ conversationis imperium cadet, nec electis fidelibus prævalebit. Cetera ex præinductis patent.
paras.en: [[10:11|And he shall pass over the strait of the sea|Et transibunt in maris freto]] [Denis reads *transibunt*, they shall pass over], that is, they shall walk through this world, which is likened to the sea, without being drowned by sin; [[10:11|and shall strike the waves in the sea|et percutiet in mari fluctus]], that is, He will calm for them the unrest of the world. For [[Tob 3:22|after a storm|Post tempestatem]] God gives [[Tob 3:22|a calm|tranquillitatem]]: He who does not suffer us to be tempted beyond what we can bear[[1 Cor 10:13||]], and is present more especially in the time of tribulation[[Ps 90:15||]]. [[10:11|and the pride of Assyria shall be humbled|Et humiliabitur superbia Assur]]: that is, the presumption of the demons who tempt us shall be cast down, when by the power of Christ they are overcome by the elect and crushed under the feet of the strong; [[10:11|and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart|et sceptrum Ægypti recedet]]: that is, the rule of worldly ways of life shall fall, and shall not prevail against the elect faithful. The rest is clear from what has been said before.

11.title: Expositio capituli undecimi: Aperi, Libane, portas tuas.
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: Open thy gates, O Libanus.

paras.t: Postquam de prosperatione Judæorum post reditum de Babylone, multa prædixit Propheta, jam de eorum calamitate non parva prænuntiat, ne prosperis extollantur, sed in die bonorum memores sint malorum.
paras.en: After the Prophet has foretold many things about the prosperity of the Jews after their return from Babylon, he now foretells their calamity, which was not small, so that they may not be lifted up by prosperity, but [[Ecclus 11:27|In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils|in die bonorum memores sint malorum]].

paras.t: Aperi, Libane, portas tuas. Secundum Hieronymum et universos expositores, hic prænuntiatur destructio templi, civitatum et populi Judæorum a Romanis : ita quod nomine Libani, templum tempore Zachariæ ædificatum notatur, ob suam altitudinem et decorem. Nihil enim monte Libano in terra promissionis excelsius est, nemorosius, sive condensius, secundum Hieronymum. Libanus ergo portas suas aperuit permissive, quando per eas ingressi sunt templum Romani sub Tito ac Vespasiano. Et comedet ignis cedros tuas. Romani enim templum incenderunt, et omnia ligna ex quibus fuit constructum.
paras.en: [[11:1|Open thy gates, O Libanus|Aperi, Libane, portas tuas]]. According to Jerome and all the expositors, here is foretold the destruction of the temple, of the cities and of the people of the Jews by the Romans: so that by the name of Libanus is signified the temple built in the time of Zacharias, because of its height and beauty. For nothing in the land of promise is loftier than Mount Libanus, more wooded or more dense, according to Jerome. Libanus therefore opened its gates permissively [that is, by God's permission, not by his will], when the Romans under Titus and Vespasian entered the temple through them. [[11:1|and let fire devour thy cedars|Et comedet ignis cedros tuas]]. For the Romans burned the temple, and all the timbers of which it had been built.

paras.t: Ulula, abies, quia cecidit cedrus. Per abietem principes, per cedrum sacerdotes Judæorum signantur. Monet igitur eos Propheta ut mutuo se deplorent. Quid enim per abietem cedrumque significaverit, subdit : quoniam magnifici, id est superiores in Synagoga, vastati sunt a Romanis.
paras.en: [[11:2|Howl, thou fir tree, for the cedar is fallen|Ulula, abies, quia cecidit cedrus]]. By the fir tree the princes, by the cedar the priests of the Jews are signified. The Prophet therefore admonishes them to bewail one another. For what he meant by the fir tree and the cedar he adds: [[11:2|for the mighty|quoniam magnifici]], that is, those higher in the Synagogue, [[11:2|are laid waste|vastati sunt]] by the Romans.

paras.t: Ululate, quercus Basan, quoniam succisus est saltus munitus. Si per quercus Basan et saltum munitum seu nemorosum, intelliguntur ligna illa et arbores in regione Basan trans Jordanem, ubi olim tribus Ruben et Gad ac media tribus Manasse habitaverunt; tunc quercus jubentur ululare materialiter et metaphorice, propter succisionem saltus illius : Romani enim ligna succiderunt. Si vero per quercus Basan intelliguntur Judæi ibidem manentes ; tunc per saltum succisum accipitur ipsa Jerusalem urbs Judææ fortissima, vel templum ejus firmissimum, cujus destructio fuit omnibus Judæis ratio ululandi.
paras.en: [[11:2|howl, ye oaks of Basan, because the fenced forest is cut down|Ululate, quercus Basan, quoniam succisus est saltus munitus]]. If by the oaks of Basan and the fenced or wooded forest are understood those timbers and trees in the region of Basan beyond the Jordan, where of old the tribes of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses dwelt[[Num 32:33||]], then the oaks are bidden to howl, both literally and figuratively, because of the cutting down of that forest: for the Romans cut down the timber. But if by the oaks of Basan are understood the Jews dwelling there, then by the forest cut down is meant Jerusalem itself, the strongest city of Judea, or its most firm temple, whose destruction was for all the Jews a reason for howling.

paras.t: Vox ululatus pastorum, id est, sonus et clamor maximi fletus sacerdotum atque doctorum Judaicæ plebis, dire insonuit, quia vastata est magnificentia eorum, scilicet famosum illud ac prænominatum templum ipsorum. Vox rugitus leonum, id est principum populi hujus, quoniam vastata est superbia Jordanis, id est terræ seu populi Judæorum circa Jordanem, qui est maximus fluvius in Judæa, secundum Hieronymum : unde et de fluvio illo tremebant.
paras.en: [[11:3|The voice of the howling of the shepherds|Vox ululatus pastorum]], that is, the sound and outcry of the very great weeping of the priests and teachers of the Jewish people, rang out dreadfully, [[11:3|because their glory is laid waste|quia vastata est magnificentia eorum]], namely that famous and renowned temple of theirs. [[11:3|the voice of the roaring of the lions|Vox rugitus leonum]], that is, of the princes of this people, [[11:3|because the pride of the Jordan is spoiled|quoniam vastata est superbia Jordanis]], that is, of the land or people of the Jews about the Jordan, which is the greatest river in Judea, according to Jerome: hence also they trembled for that river [so the Latin; the sense of this clause is obscure].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus meus : Pasce pecora occisionis : id est, tu, Zacharia propheta, populum istum instar brutorum occidendum tempore Titi, nunc instrue, prædicendo jam eorum calamitatem futuram, quatenus ipsi tempore suo, illam ex tuo vaticinio perpendentes sibi mox imminere, convertantur, spiritualiterque salventur.
paras.en: [[11:4|Thus saith the Lord my God|Hæc dicit Dominus Deus meus]]: [[11:4|Feed the flock of the slaughter|Pasce pecora occisionis]]: that is, thou, Zacharias the prophet, instruct now this people, who are to be slaughtered like brute beasts in the time of Titus, by foretelling now their coming calamity, so that in their own time, weighing from thy prophecy that it is soon to come upon them, they may be converted and saved spiritually.

paras.t: Quæ pecora qui possederant, puta Romani, occidebant ea, et non dolebant eis compatiendo ; et venundabant ea, dicentes : Benedictus Dominus, divites facti sumus. Romani quippe innumerabiles Judæos vendiderunt, et de eorum pretio gloriantes, benedicebant Domino, cujus nutu et potestate putabant se prævaluisse. Et forte quemadmodum Nabuchodonosor ad Sedeciam, ac Nabuzardan ad Jeremiam dixerunt ac fassi sunt, quod Judæi propter peccata in Deum ipsorum commissa, traditi essent in manus hostiles, ita Romani saltem nonnulli judicabant Judæos propter iniquitates suas traditos sibi. Et pastores eorum, id est sacerdotes et majores Judæorum, non parcebant eis. Nam ante adventum Romanorum subditos aggravaverant, suaque infidelitate ac vitiis ad tantam vastitatem eos duxerunt.
paras.en: [[11:5|Which they that possessed|Quæ pecora qui possederant]], namely the Romans, [[11:5|slew|occidebant ea]], [[11:5|and repented not|et non dolebant]] over them with any compassion; [[11:5|and they sold them, saying: Blessed be the Lord, we are become rich|et venundabant ea, dicentes : Benedictus Dominus, divites facti sumus]]. For the Romans sold countless Jews, and glorying in the price they fetched, blessed the Lord, by whose will and power they thought they had prevailed. And perhaps, just as Nabuchodonosor to Sedecias, and Nabuzardan to Jeremias, said and confessed that the Jews had been delivered into the hands of their enemies for the sins committed against their God[[Jer 40:2||]][[Jer 40:3||]] [the margin gives Jer. xi, 2, 3; Nabuzardan's words to Jeremias are at Jer 40:2–3], so at least some of the Romans judged that the Jews had been delivered to them for their iniquities. [[11:5|and their shepherds|Et pastores eorum]], that is, the priests and chief men of the Jews, [[11:5|spared them not|non parcebant eis]]. For before the coming of the Romans they had oppressed their subjects, and by their unbelief and vices they led them to so great a devastation.

paras.t: Et ego non parcam ultra super habitantes terram, id est, Judæorum terræ ac plebi non parcam diutius, dicit Dominus. De hac siquidem terra Judææ fit sermo. Ecce ego tradam homines Judæos, unumquemque in manu proximi sui : quia ut Josephus scribit, instante Judæorum dejectione a Tito, maxima fuit inter eos discordia, ita ut in tres partes dividerentur, et se mutuo impugnarent atque opprimerent ; et in manu regis sui, videlicet principis Romanorum, seu imperatoris, qui contra Judæos per Titum prævaluit. Et concident terram, id est, urbes et habitacula Judæorum demolientur Romani. Universas siquidem Judæorum urbes, secundum Hieronymum, destruxerunt. Et non eruam de manu eorum, id est, Judæos de manu Romanorum usque in finem mundi non eripiam. Pervenit enim ira Dei super eos usque in finem, sicut a Daniele fuit prædictum : Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio. De hac Judæorum vastatione apertissime scriptum est in Isaia : Facti sunt (inquit) in rapinam, nec est qui eruat ; in direptionem, nec est qui dicat, Redde. Dominus combussit eos in circuitu, et non cognoverunt. Ideo hoc loco ait Hieronymus : Audi, Judæe, qui tibi spes vanissimas repromittis, et non audis dicentem affirmantemque Dominum, Non eruam de manibus eorum, quod æterna sit apud Romanos tua futura captivitas.
paras.en: [[11:6|And I will no more spare the inhabitants of the land|Et ego non parcam ultra super habitantes terram]], that is, I will no longer spare the land and the people of the Jews, [[11:6|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. For the word here is of this land of Judea. [[11:6|behold I will deliver the men|Ecce ego tradam homines]], the Jews, [[11:6|every one into his neighbour's hand|unumquemque in manu proximi sui]]: for, as Josephus writes, when the overthrow of the Jews by Titus was at hand, there was very great discord among them, so that they were divided into three parties, and attacked and oppressed one another; [[11:6|and into the hand of his king|et in manu regis sui]], namely of the prince of the Romans, or the emperor, who prevailed against the Jews through Titus. [[11:6|and they shall destroy the land|Et concident terram]], that is, the Romans shall pull down the cities and dwellings of the Jews. For, according to Jerome, they destroyed all the cities of the Jews. [[11:6|and I will not deliver it out of their hand|Et non eruam de manu eorum]], that is, I will not rescue the Jews from the hand of the Romans until the end of the world: [[1 Thess 2:16|for the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|Pervenit enim ira Dei super eos usque in finem]], as was foretold by Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary: and the end thereof shall be waste|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, et finis ejus vastitas]], [[Dan 9:27|and the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end|et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio]]. Of this devastation of the Jews it is written most plainly in Isaias: [[Is 42:22|they are made|Facti sunt]] (he says) [[Is 42:22|a prey, and there is none to deliver them: a spoil, and there is none that saith: Restore|in rapinam, nec est qui eruat ; in direptionem, nec est qui dicat, Redde]]. The Lord [[Is 42:25|hath burnt him round about, and he knew not|combussit eos in circuitu, et non cognoverunt]]. Therefore Jerome says on this place: Hear, O Jew, who promisest thyself the vainest hopes, and dost not hear the Lord saying and affirming, [[11:6|I will not deliver it out of their hand|Non eruam de manibus eorum]], that thy captivity among the Romans is to be everlasting.

paras.t: Et pascam pecus occisionis, id est, Judæos morti destinatos interim alam, donec eorum tempus adveniat. Propter hoc, o pauperes gregis, id est, o vos fideles Judæi in Christum credentes, ex populo gregis præfati, seu Synagogæ, qui in primitiva Ecclesia cuncta terrena sprevistis, vitamque pauperrimam deduxistis : audite quæ sequenter dicturus sum.
paras.en: [[11:7|And I will feed the flock of slaughter|Et pascam pecus occisionis]], that is, I will meanwhile nourish the Jews destined for death, until their time comes. [[11:7|for this, O ye poor of the flock|Propter hoc, o pauperes gregis]], that is, O you faithful Jews who believe in Christ, from the people of the aforesaid flock, or Synagogue, who in the primitive Church despised all earthly things and led a life of the greatest poverty: hear what I am about to say next.

paras.t: Et assumpsi mihi duas virgas, id est, duos populos ad cultum meum ego Deus omnipotens vocavi : eos videlicet qui erant et mihi servierunt sub lege naturæ, quando post diluvium tempore Noe omnibus gentibus benedixi et modum vivendi præscripsi ; et alios qui a tempore Moysis, vel potius Abrahæ, specialiter ad cultum Dei vocati sunt, puta Judæos. Unam vocavi decoram, id est, primum populum appellavi pulchrum, vel propter naturæ puritatem, vel quoniam nondum ad idololatriam declinavit, et quia pulcherrimum fuit ut universitatis creator et pater omnes indifferenter ad se colendum vocaret; et alteram vocavi funiculum, scilicet populum Judæorum, quem a ceteris mihi abscidi, meoque cultui singulariter, aliis ad idololatriam labentibus, mancipavi : quemadmodum in Deuteronomio habetur, Pars autem Domini populus ejus, Jacob funiculus hereditatis ejus. Et pavi gregem : quia utrumque populum sustentavi, et specialiter populum Israel spiritualiter enutrivi : juxta illud Isaiæ, Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me.
paras.en: [[11:7|And I took unto me two rods|Et assumpsi mihi duas virgas]], that is, I, God almighty, called two peoples to my worship: namely those who were, and served me, under the law of nature, when after the flood, in the time of Noe, I blessed all nations and prescribed them a manner of life[[Gen 9:1||]]; and the others, who from the time of Moses, or rather of Abraham, were called in a special way to the worship of God, namely the Jews. [[11:7|one I called Beauty|Unam vocavi decoram]] [Denis's text reads *decoram*, "beautiful"; a note in the edition gives the reading *decorem*, "Beauty", as in the Vulgate], that is, I called the first people beautiful, whether because of the purity of nature, or because it had not yet turned aside to idolatry, and because it was most fitting that the creator and father of the universe should call all without distinction to worship him; [[11:7|and the other I called a Cord|et alteram vocavi funiculum]], namely the people of the Jews, which I cut off from the rest for myself and bound over to my worship alone, while the others were slipping into idolatry: as is found in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:9|But the Lord's portion is his people: Jacob the lot of his inheritance.|Pars autem Domini populus ejus, Jacob funiculus hereditatis ejus]] [the Latin word for "lot" is *funiculus*, "cord", the same as in this verse]. [[11:7|and I fed the flock|Et pavi gregem]]: because I sustained both peoples, and in particular nourished the people of Israel spiritually: according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me]].

paras.t: Et succidi tres pastores in mense uno. Hos tres pastores intelligit Hieronymus, fuisse Moysen, Aaron, et Mariam : qui Deum offenderunt, atque eodem mense deleti sunt aliquo modo. Siquidem illo mense quo Maria soror Moysis Aaronque defuncta est, Moyses et Aaron Deum ad aquas Contradictionis offenderunt, moxque divinitus adjudicati sunt non ingredi terram promissam, sed mori in solitudine. De quibus et per Isaiam Dominus ait : Interpretes tui prævaricati sunt ; itemque in Psalmo, Absorpti sunt juncti petræ judices eorum. Alii, tres pastores accipiunt sacerdotes, et prophetas falsos, ac principes Judæorum : qui omnes pariter post Christi passionem a Romanis occisi sunt.
paras.en: [[11:8|And I cut off three shepherds in one month|Et succidi tres pastores in mense uno]]. These three shepherds Jerome understands to have been Moses, Aaron and Mary, who offended God and in the same month were in some way destroyed. For in the month in which Mary, the sister of Moses and Aaron, died[[Num 20:1||]], Moses and Aaron offended God at the waters of Contradiction, and soon were sentenced by God not to enter the promised land but to die in the wilderness[[Num 20:12||]]. Of whom the Lord says also by Isaias: [[Is 43:27|thy teachers have transgressed|Interpretes tui prævaricati sunt]]; and likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 140:6|Their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed up|Absorpti sunt juncti petræ judices eorum]]. Others take the three shepherds to be the priests, the false prophets and the princes of the Jews, all of whom alike were slain by the Romans after the passion of Christ.

paras.t: Et contracta est anima mea in eis, id est, peccatis eorum indignatus sum, et quantum ad hæc, mihi displicuerunt. Unde de eis cantamus in Psalmo : Deus, tu propitius fuisti eis, et ulciscens in omnes adinventiones eorum. Siquidem et anima eorum variavit in me, id est, mihi uniformiter atque stabiliter non adhæsit, nec credidit, sed sæpe male agentes variaverunt cor suum a me.
paras.en: [[11:8|and my soul was straitened in their regard|Et contracta est anima mea in eis]], that is, I was indignant at their sins, and as to these, they displeased me. Hence we sing of them in the Psalm: [[Ps 98:8|thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions|Deus, tu propitius fuisti eis, et ulciscens in omnes adinventiones eorum]]. [[11:8|for their soul also varied in my regard|Siquidem et anima eorum variavit in me]], that is, it did not cleave to me steadily and constantly, nor believe, but often, doing evil, they turned their heart away from me.

paras.t: Et dixi : Non pascam vos. Deus enim comminabatur frequenter se populum Israel occisurum propter eorum peccata, sed Moyse exorante, placatus est. Vel, Non pascam vos, ad terram promissionis introducendo. Quod moritur, moriatur ; et quod succiditur, succidatur : id est, universi Judæi, qui contra me toties murmuraverunt in solitudine, cadant et deleantur. Nempe de tot millibus numeratis, soli Josue et Caleb terram sanctam ingressi sunt, ceteris in eremo mortuis. Et reliqui vorent unusquisque carnem proximi sui, id est, mutuo se occidant : sicut et factum fuit post aurei vituli adorationem ; quando tot millibus occisis, Moyses dixit : Consecrastis manus vestras Domino, unusquisque in fratre suo et proximo suo.
paras.en: [[11:9|And I said: I will not feed you|Et dixi : Non pascam vos]]. For God often threatened that he would slay the people of Israel for their sins[[Ex 32:10||]][[Num 14:12||]], but at the entreaty of Moses he was appeased[[Ex 32:14||]][[Num 14:20||]]. Or, [[11:9|I will not feed you|Non pascam vos]], by bringing you into the land of promise. [[11:9|that which dieth, let it die: and that which is cut off, let it be cut off|Quod moritur, moriatur ; et quod succiditur, succidatur]]: that is, let all the Jews who so often murmured against me in the wilderness fall and be destroyed. For of so many thousands that were numbered, only Josue and Caleb entered the holy land, the rest having died in the desert[[Num 26:64||]][[Num 26:65||]]. [[11:9|and let the rest devour every one the flesh of his neighbour|Et reliqui vorent unusquisque carnem proximi sui]], that is, let them slay one another: as was also done after the adoration of the golden calf, when, after so many thousands had been slain, Moses said: [[Ex 32:29|You have consecrated your hands this day to the Lord|Consecrastis manus vestras Domino]], [[Ex 32:29|every man in his son and in his brother|unusquisque in fratre suo et proximo suo]] [Denis reads "in his brother and his neighbour"; the Vulgate has "in his son and in his brother"].

paras.t: Et tuli, id est, a me projeci seu abstuli, virgam meam quæ vocabatur decus, id est populum nationum, et abscidi eam a collegio electorum, atque a meo obsequio, quando ad idololatriam declinaverunt. Omnes enim declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt. Ista abscisio facta est quando Judæorum populus ad Dei cultum specialiter vocabatur, secundum Hieronymum. Ut irritum facerem fœdus meum, quod percussi cum omnibus populis, id est, pactum illud dirumperem, per quod tempore Noe omnes nationes ad cultum meum vocandas institui, quando et omnibus benedixi, formamque vivendi præfixi : secundum quod in Genesi describitur. Hæc dictio, Ut, tenetur hic concomitanter, non causaliter, sicut in Psalmo : Tibi soli peccavi, ut justificeris.
paras.en: [[11:10|And I took|Et tuli]], that is, I cast away or took away from me, [[11:10|my rod that was called Beauty|virgam meam quæ vocabatur decus]], that is, the people of the nations, [[11:10|and I cut it asunder|et abscidi eam]] from the company of the elect and from my service, when they turned aside to idolatry. For [[Ps 13:3|They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together|Omnes enim declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt]]. This cutting off took place when the people of the Jews was called in a special way to the worship of God, according to Jerome. [[11:10|to make void my covenant, which I had made with all people|Ut irritum facerem fœdus meum, quod percussi cum omnibus populis]], that is, that I might break that pact by which in the time of Noe I appointed that all nations should be called to my worship, when I also blessed them all and laid down a form of life for them: according to what is described in Genesis[[Gen 9:1||]][[Gen 9:9||]]. This word *ut* ["to", "that"] is taken here concomitantly, not causally [that is, it marks what follows upon the act, not its purpose], as in the Psalm: [[Ps 50:6|To thee only have I sinned|Tibi soli peccavi]], [[Ps 50:6|that thou mayst be justified|ut justificeris]].

paras.t: Et in irritum deductum est in die illa, id est, tempore jam præfato diruptum est : quia ut ait Hieronymus, statim ut Israel assumptus est, gentium turba projecta est. Et cognoverunt sic pauperes gregis, id est humilis atque fidelis populus Judæorum, vel etiam alii ad gregem dominicum pertinentes, divinitus illustrati, puta electi gentiles, qui de Christi adventu fidem habuerunt, ut Job, qui custodiunt mihi, id est, ad honorem nominis mei præcepta mea observant, quia verbum Domini est, id est, quod ista gentium abjectio sit a Deo prævisa, prædicta, inflicta. Unde ad Abraham Dominus dixit : Pactum meum statuam inter me et te et semen tuum. Moyses quoque populo Judæorum perhibuit : Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram.
paras.en: [[11:11|And it was made void in that day|Et in irritum deductum est in die illa]], that is, it was broken at the time already mentioned: because, as Jerome says, as soon as Israel was taken up, the multitude of the nations was cast off. [[11:11|and so the poor of the flock|Et cognoverunt sic pauperes gregis]], that is, the humble and faithful people of the Jews, or also others belonging to the Lord's flock, enlightened by God, namely the elect gentiles who had faith in the coming of Christ, like Job, [[11:11|that keep for me|qui custodiunt mihi]], that is, keep my commandments to the honour of my name, [[11:11|understood that it is the word of the Lord|quia verbum Domini est]], that is, that this casting off of the nations was foreseen, foretold and inflicted by God. Hence the Lord said to Abraham: [[Gen 17:7|I will establish my covenant between me and thee|Pactum meum statuam inter me et te]], [[Gen 17:7|and between thy seed|et semen tuum]]. Moses also declared to the people of the Jews: [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]][[Deut 14:2||]][[Deut 26:18||]].

paras.t: Et dixi ego Deus ad eos, puta ad Judæos mihi deservientes : Si bonum est in oculis vestris, id est, si rationabile vobis apparet, afferte mercedem meam, id est, vicem mihi rependite, et aliquid pro me donate, mihi servite ac obedite pro beneficiis tantis, quod scilicet præ cunctis nationibus vos in populum hereditarium funiculumque assumpsi ; et si non, id est, si istud vobis non placet, nec justum videtur, quiescite, id est, a cultu meo cessate. Hoc Dominus ait, non licentiando ad malum, sed insinuando quod nullum cogit ad bonum, sed quemlibet in libertate arbitrii sui relinquit. Sic namque et Christus dixit ad Judam : Quod facis, fac citius, scilicet me tradendo. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Deus creavit hominem, et reliquit eum in manu consilii sui.
paras.en: [[11:12|And I said|Et dixi]], I God, [[11:12|to them|ad eos]], namely to the Jews who served me: [[11:12|If it be good in your eyes|Si bonum est in oculis vestris]], that is, if it seems reasonable to you, [[11:12|bring hither my wages|afferte mercedem meam]], that is, repay me in return, and give something for me, serve and obey me for such great benefits, namely that before all nations I took you to be a people of inheritance and a cord; [[11:12|and if not|et si non]], that is, if this does not please you nor seem just, [[11:12|be quiet|quiescite]], that is, cease from my worship. This the Lord says not by giving licence for evil, but by intimating that he forces no one to good, but leaves each one in the freedom of his own will. For so Christ also said to Judas: [[John 13:27|That which thou dost, do quickly|Quod facis, fac citius]], namely by betraying me. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 15:14|God made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his own counsel|Deus creavit hominem, et reliquit eum in manu consilii sui]].

paras.t: Et appenderunt mercedem meam triginta argenteos : id est, pro tantis bonis quæ eis exhibui, tandem pro me jam incarnato, ut traderer eis ad occidendum, exposuerunt triginta denarios, juxta illud Matthæi : Abiit Judas ad principes sacerdotum, et ait eis : Quid vultis mihi dare, et ego eum vobis tradam ? At illi constituerunt ei triginta argenteos. Hæc ergo dicuntur ex persona Filii, non Patris, aut Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[11:12|And they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver|Et appenderunt mercedem meam triginta argenteos]]: that is, for such great goods as I showed them, at last, for me now incarnate, that I might be delivered to them to be slain, they laid out thirty pence, according to that saying of Matthew: [[Matt 26:14|went one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, to the chief priests|Abiit Judas ad principes sacerdotum]], [[Matt 26:15|And said to them: What will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? But they appointed him thirty pieces of silver|et ait eis : Quid vultis mihi dare, et ego eum vobis tradam ? At illi constituerunt ei triginta argenteos]]. These things therefore are said in the person of the Son, not of the Father or of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad me Zachariam : Projice illos ad statuarium, id est, ante Deum omnium judicem, fictorem, fusorem, seu figulum, projice istos argenteos, vel projiciendos pronuntia, ut Deus factum istud decernat, et pretium istud dijudicet. Statuarius autem, fictor seu fusor statuarum vocatur. Denique aliqui dicunt, in Hebræo tale verbum haberi, quo non solum statuarius, sed et thesaurarius possit intelligi : ut denarii isti designentur projecti coram sacerdotibus in templum, qui erant thesaurorum templi custodes. Decorum pretium quo appretiatus sum ab eis. Hoc Christus ironice seu cum irrisione subsannationeque dicit, tanquam dicat : Quam vilis ab eis sum reputatus, qui me tam modico pretio vendendum atque emendum judicaverunt! Et tuli, id est, accepi ego Zacharias, triginta argenteos, pretium Christi, et projeci illos in domum Domini ad statuarium. Hoc Zacharias in imaginaria quadam repræsentatione, et prophetica futuri significatione fecisse credendus est, ad innuendum quod proditor Christi realiter faceret quod Propheta sibi facere in visione imaginaria videbatur.
paras.en: [[11:13|And the Lord said to me|Et dixit Dominus ad me]], to Zacharias: [[11:13|Cast it to the statuary|Projice illos ad statuarium]] [Denis reads *illos*, "them", where the Vulgate has *illud*, "it"], that is, before God, the judge, fashioner, founder or potter of all, cast these pieces of silver, or declare that they are to be cast, so that God may judge this deed and give sentence on this price. Now a statuary is the name for a fashioner or founder of statues. Again, some say that in the Hebrew there is a word by which not only a statuary but also a treasurer can be understood: so that these pence are signified as cast into the temple before the priests, who were the keepers of the temple's treasures. [[11:13|a handsome price, that I was prized at by them|Decorum pretium quo appretiatus sum ab eis]]. This Christ says ironically, or with derision and scorn, as if to say: How cheaply have I been reckoned by them, who judged that I should be sold and bought at so small a price! [[11:13|And I took|Et tuli]], that is, I Zacharias received, [[11:13|the thirty pieces of silver|triginta argenteos]], the price of Christ, [[11:13|and I cast them into the house of the Lord to the statuary|et projeci illos in domum Domini ad statuarium]]. Zacharias is to be believed to have done this in a kind of imaginary representation [that is, in a vision formed in the imagination], and as a prophetic sign of what was to come, to intimate that the betrayer of Christ would really do what the Prophet seemed to himself to do in an imaginary vision.

paras.t: Hanc autem scripturam allegat beatissimus Evangelista in Christi passione impletam. Sensum tamen magis quam verba commemorat, et aliqua interponit, secundum quod Spiritus Sanctus eum instruxit.
paras.en: Now the most blessed Evangelist alleges this scripture as fulfilled in the passion of Christ [in Matthew 27:9–10, where it is given under the name of Jeremias]. Yet he records the sense rather than the words, and inserts some things, according as the Holy Ghost instructed him.

paras.t: Præterea, sicut in aliis locis, ita et hic sacra Scriptura quasi de eisdem loquens, loquitur de diversis, ad eumdem tamen pertinentibus populum. Solet quippe sub nomine populi de diversis quasi de eisdem loqui.
paras.en: Moreover, as in other places, so here too holy Scripture, speaking as though of the same things, speaks of different ones, which yet belong to the same people. For it is wont, under the name of a people, to speak of different things as though of the same.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus ait : Et præcidi virgam meam secundam, quæ appellabatur funiculus : id est, statim quum tam vili pretio Judæi Christum emissent, tamque atrociter occidissent, abjeci virgam meam secundam, videlicet populum Judæorum, tradens eos usque in finem manibus Romanorum ; ut dissolverem germanitatem, id est propinquitatem atque concordiam, inter Judam et Israel, id est, fratres ab invicem separarem : eos videlicet qui ex Judaismo crediderunt in Christum, qui nomine Judæ signantur, et eos qui credere renuerunt, et nomine Israel exprimuntur, eo quod decem tribus quæ in infidelitate sua a tempore Jeroboam permanserunt, nomine Israel et Ephraim sæpius denotentur. Unde Christus in Evangelio ait : Non veni pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium : veni enim separare filium adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam, etc.
paras.en: Next the Lord says: [[11:14|And I cut off my second rod that was called a Cord|Et præcidi virgam meam secundam, quæ appellabatur funiculus]]: that is, as soon as the Jews had bought Christ at so vile a price and slain him so cruelly, I cast away my second rod, namely the people of the Jews, delivering them into the hands of the Romans until the end; [[11:14|that I might break the brotherhood|ut dissolverem germanitatem]], that is, the kinship and concord, [[11:14|between Juda and Israel|inter Judam et Israel]], that is, that I might separate brothers from one another: namely those who from Judaism believed in Christ, who are signified by the name of Juda, and those who refused to believe, who are expressed by the name of Israel, because the ten tribes, which persisted in their unbelief from the time of Jeroboam, are very often denoted by the name of Israel and of Ephraim. Hence Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:34|I came not to send peace, but the sword|Non veni pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium]]: [[Matt 10:35|For I came to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother|veni enim separare filium adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam]], etc.

paras.t: Jam per Zachariam Deus prædixit se relicturum populum Judæorum, eo quod Christum suscipere despexerunt ; nunc de eorum seductione ab Antichristo, et de adventu atque operibus Antichristi, prophetia inducitur. Et dixit Dominus ad me : Adhuc sume tibi vasa pastoris stulti, id est, insignia et vestimenta seu habitum pastoris hujusmodi indue, vel applica tibi, videlicet peram pastoralem, baculum, fistulam, sibilum : hoc est, ista assumendo, non solum verbis, sed rebus et factis denuntia esse futurum quod dicam : quemadmodum Isaias, nudus eundo, populi captivitatem monstravit ; Ezechiel quoque parietem perfodiendo, et vasa sua transferendo, quid futurum eis esset, rebus ostendit. Prophetæ namque non verbis dumtaxat, sed operibus etiam frequenter aliqua nuntiant. Insuper juxta Hebræos, cujuslibet artis instrumenta, vasa artificis nuncupantur.
paras.en: God has now foretold by Zacharias that he would abandon the people of the Jews because they disdained to receive Christ; now a prophecy is brought in of their seduction by Antichrist, and of the coming and works of Antichrist. [[11:15|And the Lord said to me|Et dixit Dominus ad me]]: [[11:15|Take to thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd|Adhuc sume tibi vasa pastoris stulti]], that is, put on, or take to thee, the marks and garments or dress of such a shepherd, namely a shepherd's scrip, staff, pipe and whistle: that is, by taking up these things, declare not only by words but by things and deeds that what I shall say is to come: as Isaias, by going naked, showed forth the captivity of the people[[Is 20:2||]][[Is 20:4||]]; and Ezechiel, by digging through the wall and carrying out his goods, showed by things what was to befall them[[Ezech 12:7||]]. For the prophets frequently announce things not by words only but also by deeds. Moreover, according to the Hebrews, the instruments of any craft are called the craftsman's vessels [*vasa*, "vessels", which the Douay-Rheims renders "instruments"].

paras.t: Quia ecce ego suscitabo permissive pastorem in terra, utpote Antichristum, de quo ait Salvator : Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non accepistis me ; si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum accipietis. Quoniam enim Christum summam veritatem suscipere noluerunt, justo Dei judicio ab Antichristo decipi merebuntur Judæi, sicut ait Apostolus ad Thessalonicenses : Quia non crediderunt veritati, consenserunt autem iniquitati, ideo mittet illis Deus spiritum erroris, ut credant mendacio. Istis enim dixerat Deus : Non pascam vos ; quod moritur, moriatur.
paras.en: [[11:16|For behold I will raise up|Quia ecce ego suscitabo]], permissively, [[11:16|a shepherd in the land|pastorem in terra]], namely Antichrist, of whom the Saviour says: [[John 5:43|I am come in the name of my Father, and you receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him you will receive.|Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non accepistis me ; si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum accipietis]] For since they would not receive Christ, the highest truth, the Jews will deserve by the just judgment of God to be deceived by Antichrist, as the Apostle says to the Thessalonians: Because they [[2 Thess 2:11|have not believed the truth but have consented to iniquity|non crediderunt veritati, consenserunt autem iniquitati]], [[2 Thess 2:10|Therefore God shall send them the operation of error, to believe lying|ideo mittet illis Deus spiritum erroris, ut credant mendacio]] [Denis has *spiritum erroris*, "the spirit of error", for the Vulgate's *operationem erroris*]. For to these God had said: [[11:9|I will not feed you|Non pascam vos]]: [[11:9|that which dieth, let it die|quod moritur, moriatur]].

paras.t: Qui derelicta non visitabit, id est, impios a Deo relictos, ad viam justitiæ non reducet, dispersa non quæret, id est, a Deo per errores vitiaque divisos spiritualiter non adunabit, et contritum non sanabit, id est, vitiis saucium non curabit, et id quod stat, non enutriet, id est, exsistentes in gratia non corroborabit, et carnes pinguium comedet, id est, divitum bona consumet, et ungulas eorum dissolvet, non consentientes sibi crudeliter persequendo, vel consentientes sibi spiritualiter occidendo. Itaque pastor iste nefarius, nullum veræ pietatis opus ad bonum spectans prælatum habebit, sed omnia prorsus contraria. Ideo contra eum exclamat Propheta :
paras.en: [[11:16|who shall not visit what is forsaken|Qui derelicta non visitabit]], that is, he will not bring back to the way of justice the wicked who have been forsaken by God; [[11:16|nor seek what is scattered|dispersa non quæret]], that is, he will not gather together spiritually those divided from God by errors and vices; [[11:16|nor heal what is broken|et contritum non sanabit]], that is, he will not cure one wounded by vices; [[11:16|nor nourish that which standeth|et id quod stat, non enutriet]], that is, he will not strengthen those who are in grace; [[11:16|and he shall eat the flesh of the fat ones|et carnes pinguium comedet]], that is, he will consume the goods of the rich; [[11:16|and break their hoofs|et ungulas eorum dissolvet]], cruelly persecuting those who do not consent to him, or spiritually slaying those who do. So this wicked shepherd will set before himself no work of true piety that tends to good, but everything quite the contrary. Therefore the Prophet cries out against him:

paras.t: O pastor, simulatione ac nomine, et idolum, id est, falsum et vanum simulacrum, quod appares non existendo, et qui te pro Deo facies adorari (extolletur enim supra omne quod est aut colitur Deus, ita ut in templo Dei sedeat, ostendens se tanquam sit Deus), derelinquens gregem, id est, tibi adhærentes subvertens ! Gladius super brachium ejus : id est, supra et contra potestatem Antichristi erit virtus, ultio atque sententia Christi, qui spiritu oris sui interficiet eum ; et super oculum dextrum ejus, id est super sapientiam illam eximiam, quam sibi inesse confinget. Asseret enim se omnibus sapientiorem. Sed Christus illustratione adventus sui destruet eum, ejusque figmenta nudabit. De qua re in Daniele, et in Apocalypsi per diversa capitula plenius scribitur. Brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur, id est, omnis potestas ejus dejicietur ; et oculus dexter ejus, id est sapientia divinorum, quam sibi inesse testabitur, tenebrescens, obscurabitur : quia et ipse in exteriores tartareas impelletur tenebras. Ipse enim est pseudopropheta et bestia, de quibus tanta in Apocalypsi leguntur.
paras.en: [[11:17|O shepherd|O pastor]], in pretence and in name, [[11:17|and idol|et idolum]], that is, a false and empty image, since thou appearest without truly being, and who wilt cause thyself to be adored as God (for he [[2 Thess 2:4|is lifted up above all that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself as if he were God|extolletur enim supra omne quod est aut colitur Deus, ita ut in templo Dei sedeat, ostendens se tanquam sit Deus]]), [[11:17|that forsaketh the flock|derelinquens gregem]], that is, overthrowing those who cleave to thee! [[11:17|the sword upon his arm|Gladius super brachium ejus]]: that is, over and against the power of Antichrist shall be the might, vengeance and sentence of Christ, who [[2 Thess 2:8|shall kill with the spirit of his mouth|spiritu oris sui interficiet eum]]; [[11:17|and upon his right eye|et super oculum dextrum ejus]], that is, upon that surpassing wisdom which he will pretend to have in himself. For he will assert that he is wiser than all. But Christ [[2 Thess 2:8|shall destroy with the brightness of his coming|illustratione adventus sui destruet eum]], and will lay bare his fictions. Of this it is written more fully in Daniel[[Dan 7:21||]], and in the Apocalypse in various chapters[[Apoc 13:1||]] [the margin gives Dan. vii, 21–27, and Apoc. xiii–xxii]. [[11:17|his arm shall quite wither away|Brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur]], that is, all his power shall be cast down; [[11:17|and his right eye|et oculus dexter ejus]], that is, the wisdom of divine things which he will claim to have in himself, [[11:17|shall be utterly darkened|tenebrescens, obscurabitur]]: because he himself too shall be driven into the outer darkness of hell. For he is the false prophet and the beast of whom so much is read in the Apocalypse.

paras.t: Præterea ista de Antichristo prolata, de negligentibus et superbis, imperitis carnalibusque pastoribus accipi possunt : qui sibi commissos spiritualiter non pascunt, non docent, non arguunt, non emendant, neque sustentant, neque perficiunt, imo negligunt et seducunt, sed de eorum bonis delicate se nutriunt. Horum cuilibet Dominus clamat : O pastor et idolum, derelinquens gregem ! Cujus potestatem et intellectum Christus dure tractabit. Unde boni pastoris est, gratia auxiliante, implere quod Dominus ait per Ezechielem : Quod perierat requiram, et quod abjectum erat reducam, et quod confractum fuerat alligabo, et quod infirmum fuerat consolidabo, et quod pingue et forte custodiam ; et pascam illas in judicio.
paras.en: Moreover, these things said of Antichrist can be taken of negligent and proud, unskilled and carnal shepherds, who do not feed spiritually those committed to them, do not teach, do not reprove, do not correct, neither sustain nor perfect them, but rather neglect and lead them astray, while they feed themselves daintily on their goods. To any one of these the Lord cries: [[11:17|O shepherd, and idol, that forsaketh the flock|O pastor et idolum, derelinquens gregem]]! His power and understanding Christ will handle harshly. Hence it belongs to a good shepherd, with the help of grace, to fulfil what the Lord says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:16|I will seek that which was lost: and that which was driven away, I will bring again: and I will bind up that which was broken, and I will strengthen that which was weak, and that which was fat and strong I will preserve, and I will feed them in judgment.|Quod perierat requiram, et quod abjectum erat reducam, et quod confractum fuerat alligabo, et quod infirmum fuerat consolidabo, et quod pingue et forte custodiam ; et pascam illas in judicio]]

paras.t: Postremo, per duas virgas de quibus nunc factus est sermo, quidam intelligunt duos reges, vel duo regna, videlicet duarum tribuum ac decem, hoc est : Jeroboam, qui pulcherrime locutus est decem tribubus, propter quod dicitur virga decora; et Roboam, qui dixit ad populum, Ego cædam vos scorpionibus, ideo appellatur funiculus. Primo autem abscidit Deus regnum decem tribuum per Salmanasar regem Assyriorum, deinde duarum tribuum regnum per Titum atque exercitum Romanorum. Siquidem per Chaldæos non erat omnino præcisum, sed post certum tempus reductum.
paras.en: Lastly, by the two rods of which we have now been speaking, some understand two kings, or two kingdoms, namely those of the two tribes and of the ten: that is, Jeroboam, who spoke most fairly to the ten tribes[[3 Kings 12:1||]], for which reason he is called the beautiful rod; and Roboam, who said to the people, [[3 Kings 12:11|I will beat you with scorpions|Ego cædam vos scorpionibus]], and is therefore called a cord [that is, a cord such as a scourge is made of]. Now God first cut off the kingdom of the ten tribes through Salmanasar king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]], and afterwards the kingdom of the two tribes through Titus and the army of the Romans. For by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:1||]] it had not been entirely cut off, but was brought back after a certain time[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 2:1||]][[1 Esd 7:1||]].

paras.t: Per tres autem pastores, uno mense succisos, intelligunt Ochoziam regem Juda, et Joram regem Israel, ejusque matrem Jezabel, quæ simul cum ipso populum rexit : quos Jehu filius Namsi simul occidit, ut legitur quarto Regum.
paras.en: And by the three shepherds cut off in one month they understand Ochozias king of Juda[[4 Kings 9:27||]], and Joram king of Israel[[4 Kings 9:24||]], and his mother Jezabel[[4 Kings 9:33||]], who ruled the people together with him: all of whom Jehu the son of Namsi slew at one time, as is read in the fourth book of Kings.

12.title: Elucidatio capituli duodecimi: Onus verbi Domini super Israel.
12.title_en: Explanation of the twelfth chapter: The burden of the word of the Lord upon Israel.

paras.t: Præsens capitulum et omnia quæ sequuntur, maximis obscuritatibus plena sunt, et a diversis expositoribus multiformiter exponuntur. Intendo autem sequi Hieronymum, quanquam et ipse recitative potius quam assertive in hoc loco loquatur.
paras.en: This chapter and all that follow are full of the greatest obscurities, and are expounded in many ways by different expositors. I intend, however, to follow Jerome, although he too speaks in this place by way of reporting rather than of asserting [that is, he relates the opinions of others rather than giving his own as certain].

paras.t: Onus verbi Domini, id est vastitas divino sermone prænuntiata, super Israel, id est contra plebem Judaicam. Et dixit Dominus extendens cœlum, id est, orbes cœlestes in latissima figura constituens, vel in maxima quantitate molitus: sphærica namque figura capacissima est. Unde in Isaia dicitur: Qui extendit velut nihilum cœlos, et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum; itemque in Psalmo, Extendens cœlum sicut pellem. Et fundans terram, id est, sua virtute eam in medio universi tanquam centrum fulciens et conservans, sine omni sustentaculo ei supposito, quum sit infimum elementum. Hinc in Job habetur: Super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt? Et alio loco: Deus appendit terram super nihilum. Non quod nihil sub ea sit, sed quia id ad ejus sustentationem non facit. Propter quod in Proverbiis legitur: Dominus sapientia fundavit terram. Verumtamen, secundum Philosophum, omnia tendunt ad centrum, sicque universæ partes terræ ad medium ejus naturaliter inclinantur. Et hoc unde? nisi ex institutione et impressione omnipotentis sapientiæ supergloriosissimi, supersanctissimi, supervoluptuosissimi Creatoris. Et fingens spiritum hominis in eo, id est, animam corpori organizato per creationem infundens, juxta illud Isaiæ: Ego Dominus, dans flatum hominibus super terram. Ex hoc demonstratur, quod anima rationalis in corpore esse incipiat, seu suæ exsistentiæ exordium sumat: ita quod nec omnes simul creatæ sunt, nec suis corporibus præexsistunt, sed quælibet dum corpori suo infunditur, simul creatur, juxta illud in Psalmo: Qui finxit sigillatim corda eorum.
paras.en: [[12:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the devastation foretold by the divine word, [[12:1|upon Israel|super Israel]], that is, against the Jewish people. [[12:1|Thus saith the Lord, who stretcheth forth the heavens|Et dixit Dominus extendens cœlum]], that is, setting the heavenly spheres in the widest figure, or building them in the greatest size: for the spherical figure is the most capacious. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 40:22|he that stretcheth out the heavens as nothing, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in|Qui extendit velut nihilum cœlos, et expandit illos sicut tabernaculum ad inhabitandum]]; and likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 103:2|Who stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion|Extendens cœlum sicut pellem]] [the margin gives Ps. cii, 2; the verse is Ps 103:2. The Latin *pellis* is "skin", where the Douay-Rheims has "pavilion"]. [[12:1|and layeth the foundations of the earth|Et fundans terram]], that is, by his power upholding and preserving it in the middle of the universe as its centre, with no support set beneath it, since it is the lowest element. Hence it is said in Job: [[Job 38:6|Upon what are its bases grounded?|Super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt?]] And in another place: God [[Job 26:7|hangeth the earth upon nothing|appendit terram super nihilum]]. Not that there is nothing beneath it, but because what is beneath does nothing to hold it up. Therefore we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:19|The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth|Dominus sapientia fundavit terram]]. Nevertheless, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle], all things tend towards the centre, and so all the parts of the earth naturally incline towards its middle. And whence is this, if not from the ordering and impress of the almighty wisdom of the supremely glorious, supremely holy, supremely delightful Creator? [[12:1|and formeth the spirit of man in him|Et fingens spiritum hominis in eo]], that is, pouring the soul into the organized body by creation, according to that word of Isaias: I the Lord, [[Is 42:5|that giveth breath to the people upon it|dans flatum hominibus super terram]] [Denis's wording, "I the Lord, giving breath to men upon the earth", is freer than the Vulgate]. From this it is shown that the rational soul begins to be in the body, that is, takes the beginning of its existence there: so that souls were not all created together, nor do they exist before their bodies, but each is created at the moment it is poured into its body, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 32:15|He who hath made the hearts of every one of them|Qui finxit sigillatim corda eorum]].

paras.t: Ecce ego ponam Jerusalem superliminare crapulæ, id est, hujusmodi superliminari eam assimilo, ita quod omnis qui eam invaserit, quasi crapula victus impingat et corruat. Sic itaque pono eam omnibus populis in circuitu ejus manentibus, qui eam impugnant. Istud creditur tempore Pompeii adimpletum: qui (ut Josephus scribit) Jerusalem cepit, et templum irreverenter ingressus est; cui et gentes in circuitu Judæorum manentes adhærebant, imo et quidam Judæorum capti ab eo, qui licet invite, tamen eidem videbantur ferre auxilium, de quibus subjungitur: Sed et Juda erit in obsidione contra Jerusalem. Sic quippe secundo Machabæorum quidam Judæi leguntur Nicanorem per necessitatem secuti contra Machabæum.
paras.en: [[12:2|Behold I will make Jerusalem a lintel of surfeiting|Ecce ego ponam Jerusalem superliminare crapulæ]], that is, I liken her to such a lintel, so that everyone who attacks her shall strike against it and fall, as one overcome with drunkenness [the Latin *crapula* is drunkenness or surfeit]. So then I make her such [[12:2|to all the people round about|omnibus populis in circuitu]] her, who dwell there and assail her. This is believed to have been fulfilled in the time of Pompey, who (as Josephus writes) took Jerusalem and irreverently entered the temple; and the nations dwelling round about the Jews sided with him, and indeed so did some of the Jews whom he had captured, who, though against their will, were seen to give him help; of these is added: [[12:2|and Juda also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem|Sed et Juda erit in obsidione contra Jerusalem]]. So too in the second book of Machabees we read that certain Jews followed Nicanor by necessity against Machabeus[[2 Mach 15:2||]].

paras.t: Et erit: In die illa, id est tempore illo, ponam Jerusalem lapidem oneris, id est, gravissimo oneri eam assimilabo, cunctis populis impugnantibus eam: ita quod sicut sine labore et pœna lapis gravis levari non valet, sic et Jerusalem non sine impugnatorum suorum ruina atque periculo dejicietur sive vincetur. Omnes qui levabunt eam, concisione lacerabuntur: id est, sicut rupturam incurrunt, qui saxum gravissimum ultra vires levare conantur, sic et vastantibus Jerusalem fiet. Et colligentur adversus eam omnia regna terræ: id est, aliqui de regionibus singulis principi Romanorum contra Jerusalem se adunabunt. Distributiones quippe in libris propheticis non sunt stricte intelligendæ in pluribus locis.
paras.en: [[12:3|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit: In die illa]], that is, at that time, [[12:3|that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone|ponam Jerusalem lapidem oneris]], that is, I will liken her to a very heavy burden, [[12:3|to all people|cunctis populis]] that assail her: so that, as a heavy stone cannot be lifted without toil and pain, so Jerusalem shall not be cast down or conquered without the ruin and peril of her assailants. [[12:3|all that shall lift it up shall be rent and torn|Omnes qui levabunt eam, concisione lacerabuntur]]: that is, as those who try to lift a very heavy rock beyond their strength suffer a rupture, so shall it be with those who lay Jerusalem waste. [[12:3|and all the kingdoms of the earth shall be gathered together against her|Et colligentur adversus eam omnia regna terræ]]: that is, some from each of the regions shall join the Roman prince against Jerusalem. For in many places of the prophetic books distributive words [that is, words such as "all" and "every"] are not to be understood strictly.

paras.t: In die illa, dicit Dominus, percutiam omnem equum in stuporem, et ascensorem ejus in amentiam, id est, equos et equites præinductos conteram et vastabo. Ut enim in chronicis atque historiis scriptum est, ab eo tempore quo Pompeius templum ingressus est, ipse cum suis deficere et perire incipit, nec amplius ut ante est prosperatus, tandemque decollatus occubuit. Et super domum Juda aperiam oculos meos, id est, Judæos qui necessitate compulsi contra Jerusalem pugnaverunt, clementer adspiciam, nec ut ceteros puniam eos. Et omnem equum populorum percutiam cæcitate, vita et visu eos privando, ne ultra subserviant his qui contra Jerusalem intumescunt et pugnant.
paras.en: [[12:4|In that day, saith the Lord, I will strike every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness|In die illa, dicit Dominus, percutiam omnem equum in stuporem, et ascensorem ejus in amentiam]], that is, I will crush and lay waste the horses and horsemen spoken of before. For, as is written in the chronicles and histories, from the time when Pompey entered the temple he and his men began to fail and perish, nor did he prosper any more as before, and at last he fell beheaded. [[12:4|and I will open my eyes upon the house of Juda|Et super domum Juda aperiam oculos meos]], that is, I will look with mercy on the Jews who, compelled by necessity, fought against Jerusalem, and will not punish them as the others. [[12:4|and will strike every horse of the nations with blindness|Et omnem equum populorum percutiam cæcitate]], depriving them of life and sight, so that they may no longer serve those who swell with pride and fight against Jerusalem.

paras.t: Et dicent duces Juda in corde suo, id est principales Judæorum contra Jerusalem necessitate quadam pugnantium: Confortentur mihi, id est ad gaudium meum et commodum, habitatores Jerusalem in Domino exercituum Deo eorum. Cordialiter namque optabant ipsam Jerusalem prævalere.
paras.en: [[12:5|And the governors of Juda shall say in their heart|Et dicent duces Juda in corde suo]], that is, the leaders of the Jews who by a certain necessity were fighting against Jerusalem: [[12:5|Let the inhabitants of Jerusalem be strengthened for me|Confortentur mihi]], that is, for my joy and advantage, [[12:5|in the Lord of hosts, their God|habitatores Jerusalem in Domino exercituum Deo eorum]]. For they wished with all their heart that Jerusalem herself should prevail.

paras.t: In die illa ponam duces Juda jam dictos, sicut caminum ignis in lignis, et sicut faciem ignis in fœno. Cur autem comparatio ista detur, subjungitur: Et devorabunt, id est, occident vel superabunt, ad dexteram et ad sinistram, et pari ratione ad alios situs terræ, omnes populos in circuitu, id est quosdam de omnibus, et inopinabiliter multos circa se et in suo gyro manentes. Et habitabitur Jerusalem rursus in loco suo, id est, a civibus suis pacifice iterum incoletur, in Jerusalem, id est in loco et spatio solito. Judæi namque post abscessum mortemque Pompeii, in magna potestate fuerunt ac pace. Nam et Octavianus favebat eisdem.
paras.en: [[12:6|In that day I will make the governors of Juda|In die illa ponam duces Juda]] just mentioned [[12:6|like a furnace of fire amongst wood|sicut caminum ignis in lignis]], [[12:6|and as a firebrand amongst hay|et sicut faciem ignis in fœno]] [Denis reads *faciem*, "the face of fire", where the Vulgate has *facem*, "a torch"]. Why this comparison is made is then added: [[12:6|and they shall devour|Et devorabunt]], that is, shall slay or overcome, [[12:6|to the right hand, and to the left|ad dexteram et ad sinistram]], and by the same token towards the other quarters of the earth, [[12:6|all the people round about|omnes populos in circuitu]], that is, some of all of them, and beyond expectation many of those dwelling near them and around them. [[12:6|and Jerusalem shall be inhabited again in her own place|Et habitabitur Jerusalem rursus in loco suo]], that is, shall again be peacefully inhabited by her citizens, [[12:6|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], that is, in its usual place and extent. For after the departure and death of Pompey the Jews were in great power and at peace; for Octavian too favoured them.

paras.t: Et salvabit Dominus tabernacula Juda, id est urbes, castella, villas, et viculos eorum qui necessitate quadam sequebantur Pompeianos, illis a Judæa abscisis, sicut in principio: ut non magnifice, id est immoderanter et vane, glorietur domus David, et gloria habitantium Jerusalem, id est famosi et inclyti cives Jerusalem, qui tempore persecutionis manserunt constantes, quorum nonnulli de David progenie fuerant, contra Judam, id est eos qui formidine victi, adversariis se junxerunt, sed considerando se divina potestate protectos, ad suos reversi sunt.
paras.en: [[12:7|And the Lord shall save the tabernacles of Juda|Et salvabit Dominus tabernacula Juda]], that is, the cities, forts, farms and hamlets of those who by a certain necessity followed Pompey's men, these being cut off from Judea, [[12:7|as in the beginning|sicut in principio]]: that [[12:7|the house of David|glorietur domus David]], [[12:7|and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem|et gloria habitantium Jerusalem]] (that is, the famous and renowned citizens of Jerusalem, who stayed constant in the time of persecution, some of whom were of the line of David), [[12:7|may not boast and magnify themselves|ut non magnifice]], that is, immoderately and vainly, [[12:7|against Juda|contra Judam]], that is, against those who, overcome by fear, joined the enemy, but, seeing themselves protected by divine power, returned to their own.

paras.t: In die illa proteget Dominus habitatores Jerusalem, ne ab adversariis eos obsidentibus penitus conterantur. Et erit qui offenderit ex eis in die illa, id est, qui peccaverit, quasi David, id est, misericordiam a Deo cito et largiter consequetur, sicut et David frequenter: de quo dixerat Deus, Misericordiam meam non auferam ab eo; et domus David, id est filii ejus carne et fidei atque constantiæ imitatione, erunt quasi Dei, id est sicut præelectissimi gratiæ filii, qui mentem suam nusquam mutaverunt a Deo. Ideo subditur: sicut angelus Domini in conspectu eorum qui gratiam istam eis donandam præsentialiter viderint, apparebunt: sicut solemus de homine plurimum gratioso asserere, quod sit angelicus homo. Ad ipsumque David mulier Thecuites loquitur: Tu, Domine mi rex, quasi angelus Dei es super terram.
paras.en: [[12:8|In that day shall the Lord protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem|In die illa proteget Dominus habitatores Jerusalem]], that they may not be utterly crushed by the enemies besieging them. [[12:8|and he that hath offended among them in that day|Et erit qui offenderit ex eis in die illa]], that is, he that hath sinned, [[12:8|shall be as David|quasi David]], that is, shall obtain mercy from God quickly and abundantly, as David also often did, of whom God had said: [[2 Kings 7:15|my mercy I will not take away from him|Misericordiam meam non auferam ab eo]]; [[12:8|and the house of David|et domus David]], that is, his sons by flesh and by imitation of his faith and constancy, shall be [[12:8|as that of God|quasi Dei]], that is, as most chosen sons of grace, who never turned their mind away from God. Therefore it is added: they shall appear [[12:8|as an angel of the Lord in their sight|sicut angelus Domini in conspectu eorum]], that is, in the sight of those who shall see with their own eyes this grace that is to be given them: as we are wont to say of a man full of grace that he is an angelic man. And the woman of Thecua says to David himself: Thou, my lord the king, art [[2 Kings 14:17|as an angel of God|quasi angelus Dei]] upon earth [Denis gives the sense of the verse in his own words].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa: Quæram conterere omnes gentes, de quibus nunc dictum est, quæ veniunt contra Jerusalem animo disperdendi quæ perierunt.
paras.en: [[12:9|And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations|Et erit in die illa: Quæram conterere omnes gentes]] of which mention has just been made, [[12:9|that come against Jerusalem|quæ veniunt contra Jerusalem]] with intent to destroy it; and they perished.

paras.t: Et effundam super domum David et super habitatores Jerusalem: de quibus jam facta est mentio, scilicet super posteros David et cives Jerusalem, super nobiles et vulgares; spiritum gratiæ et precum, id est Spiritum Sanctum totius gratiæ fontem, devotarumque orationum datorem. Quid enim oremus sicut oportet, ignoramus, sed ipse Spiritus orantes nos facit. Istud potissimum fuit impletum modico tempore post prædicta. Siquidem post mortem Pompeii, Julius ei contemporaneus usurpavit sibi imperium: cui successit Octavianus, sub quo natus est Christus. Post cujus nativitatem mox cœpit gratia Dei abundare in populo Judæorum: propter quod, tempus Christi appellatum est per antonomasiam tempus gratiæ. Hinc in Isaia Deus hortatur: Noli timere, serve meus Jacob; effundam spiritum meum super semen tuum, et benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam. Hoc est quod Christus ait: Venit tempus, quando veri adoratores adorabunt Patrem in spiritu et veritate.
paras.en: [[12:10|And I will pour out upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem|Et effundam super domum David et super habitatores Jerusalem]], of whom mention has already been made, that is, upon the descendants of David and the citizens of Jerusalem, upon nobles and common people, [[12:10|the spirit of grace, and of prayers|spiritum gratiæ et precum]], that is, the Holy Ghost, the fount of all grace and the giver of devout prayers. For [[Rom 8:26|we know not what we should pray for as we ought|Quid enim oremus sicut oportet, ignoramus]], but the Spirit himself makes us pray. This was fulfilled above all a short time after the events foretold above. For after the death of Pompey, Julius, his contemporary, usurped the empire for himself; and Octavian succeeded him, under whom Christ was born. Soon after his birth the grace of God began to abound among the Jewish people: wherefore the time of Christ is called by antonomasia [that is, by a name given to it above all others] the time of grace. Hence God exhorts in Isaias: [[Is 44:2|Fear not, O my servant Jacob|Noli timere, serve meus Jacob]]; [[Is 44:3|I will pour out my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thy stock|effundam spiritum meum super semen tuum, et benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam]]. This is what Christ says: [[John 4:23|the hour cometh|Venit tempus]] [Denis has *tempus*, "the time", for the Vulgate's *hora*], [[John 4:23|when the true adorers shall adore the Father in spirit and in truth|quando veri adoratores adorabunt Patrem in spiritu et veritate]].

paras.t: Et adspicient ad me, quem confixerunt. Istam scripturam ad Christi passionem pertinere, et in ea impletam esse, docet discipulus quem diligebat Jesus: Facta, inquit, sunt hæc, ut scriptura impleretur: Videbunt in quem transfixerunt. Adspexerunt autem Judæi ad Christum quem occiderunt, quando post passionem et resurrectionem atque Paracleti missionem, ad prædicationem Apostolorum conversi sunt, in tantum quoque, ut multa sacerdotum turba Evangelio obediret, ut scribitur in Actibus. De illis quippe Christus, passione sua instante, in Joanne scribitur prædixisse: Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
paras.en: [[12:10|and they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced|Et adspicient ad me, quem confixerunt]]. That this scripture belongs to the passion of Christ and was fulfilled in it, the disciple whom Jesus loved teaches: [[John 19:36|these things were done|Facta]], he says, [[John 19:36|that the scripture might be fulfilled|sunt hæc, ut scriptura impleretur]]: [[John 19:37|They shall look on him whom they pierced|Videbunt in quem transfixerunt]]. Now the Jews looked upon Christ, whom they had slain, when, after the passion and resurrection and the sending of the Paraclete, they were converted at the preaching of the Apostles, so much so that a great multitude of the priests obeyed the Gospel, as is written in the Acts[[Acts 6:7||]]. For it is written in John that Christ, when his passion was at hand, foretold of them: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]].

paras.t: Tunc insuper impleta sunt quæ subjunguntur: Et plangent eum, videlicet Christum a se occisum Judæi isti conversi, planctu quasi super unigenitum, id est tali deploratione, qua decuit unigenitum Dei Filium a suis interfectoribus lamentari. Vel sensus est, quod plangerent eum cordialiter et amare, sicut unigenitus defunctus solet a suis defleri parentibus. Propter quod subditur: et dolebunt super eum, quod eum tam crudeliter fuerant persecuti, sicut doleri solet in morte primogeniti, id est valde vehementer. Dubium enim non est, quin inæstimabiliter eum, imo et propria sua peccata, deplanxerint, prout mox clarius subditur.
paras.en: Then too were fulfilled the words that follow: [[12:10|and they shall mourn for him|Et plangent eum]], that is, these converted Jews shall mourn for Christ, slain by them, [[12:10|as one mourneth for an only son|planctu quasi super unigenitum]], that is, with such weeping as was fitting for the only-begotten Son of God to be lamented by those who killed him. Or the sense is that they would mourn for him from the heart and bitterly, as a dead only son is wont to be wept for by his parents. Therefore it is added: [[12:10|and they shall grieve over him|et dolebunt super eum]], because they had persecuted him so cruelly, [[12:10|as the manner is to grieve for the death of the firstborn|sicut doleri solet in morte primogeniti]], that is, most vehemently. For there is no doubt that they lamented him beyond reckoning, and their own sins as well, as is added more clearly just after.

paras.t: In die illa magnus erit planctus in Jerusalem, sicut planctus Adadremmon in campo Mageddo, id est, sicut Judæi vehementissime deplanxerunt Josiam regem a Pharaone Nechao rege Ægypti occisum: qui planctus fuit Adadremmon, id est civitatis sic dictæ, ac sitæ in campo Mageddo, in quo campo Josias fuit occisus, propter quod planctus iste incepit in urbe et campo præfatis. De qua re scriptum est plenius secundo libro Paralipomenon, quo inter cetera legitur, quod Jeremias luxerit eum maxime: cujus cantores et cantatrices usque in præsentem diem lamentationem super Josiam replicant.
paras.en: [[12:11|In that day there shall be a great lamentation in Jerusalem like the lamentation of Adadremmon in the plain of Mageddon|In die illa magnus erit planctus in Jerusalem, sicut planctus Adadremmon in campo Mageddo]], that is, as the Jews most vehemently lamented King Josias, slain by Pharao Nechao king of Egypt: which was the lamentation of Adadremmon, that is, of the city so called, which lies in the plain of Mageddo, the plain in which Josias was slain[[2 Par 35:22||]]; for which reason this lamentation began in the city and plain just named[[2 Par 35:24||]]. Of this it is written more fully in the second book of Paralipomenon, where among other things we read that Jeremias mourned for him most of all, whose singing men and singing women repeat the lamentation over Josias unto this day[[2 Par 35:25||]].

paras.t: Et planget Christum terra Juda, id est habitatores terræ, de quibus mox additur: familiæ et familiæ seorsum, id est quælibet per se; familiæ domus David seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum. Tempore enim tribulationis et orationis decet viros ab uxoribus separari, ut devotius atque honestius invocent Deum. Propter quod dictum est a Joele: Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo. Hoc apud Judæos observabatur, quemadmodum nunc in Ecclesia viri et feminæ resident segregatim.
paras.en: [[12:12|And the land shall mourn|Et planget]] for Christ, the land of Juda [Denis's text reads *terra Juda*, "the land of Juda", where the Vulgate has *terra* alone], that is, the dwellers in the land, of whom it is added at once: [[12:12|families and families apart|familiæ et familiæ seorsum]], that is, each by itself; [[12:12|the families of the house of David apart, and their women apart|familiæ domus David seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum]]. For in time of tribulation and prayer it is fitting that husbands be separated from their wives, that they may call upon God more devoutly and more becomingly. Therefore it was said by Joel: [[Joel 2:16|let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bridal chamber|Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo]]. This was observed among the Jews, as now in the Church men and women sit apart.

paras.t: Familiæ domus Nathan seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum; familiæ domus Levi seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum; familiæ Semei seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum. Secundum Hieronymum, per familiam David intelligitur regia tribus, videlicet Juda; per familiam Nathan, prophetalis ordo signatur; per familiam Levi, sacerdotalis progenies; per tribum Semei, doctores expressi sunt, quia ex hac tribu magistrorum agmina pullulaverunt.
paras.en: [[12:13|The families of the house of Nathan apart, and their women apart: the families of the house of Levi apart, and their women apart: the families of Semei apart, and their women apart|Familiæ domus Nathan seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum; familiæ domus Levi seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum; familiæ Semei seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum]]. According to Jerome, by the family of David is understood the royal tribe, that is, Juda; by the family of Nathan the prophetic order is signified; by the family of Levi the priestly line; by the tribe of Semei the teachers are expressed, because from this tribe hosts of masters sprang up.

paras.t: Omnes familiæ reliquæ, familiæ et familiæ seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum. Hæ familiæ generaliter exprimuntur, non particulariter distinguuntur, quoniam speciale dignitatis privilegium non habuerunt. Secundum Hieronymum, si consideremus quam multa millia Judæorum in Jerusalem ab Apostolis mox misso Spiritu Sancto conversa fuerunt, facile est pensare quam vere tunc ista impleta sunt, præsertim quum in Actibus dicatur: Erant autem in Jerusalem habitantes Judæi viri religiosi ex omni natione quæ sub cælo est: et ex illis multi tunc convertebantur.
paras.en: [[12:14|All the rest of the families, families and families apart, and their women apart|Omnes familiæ reliquæ, familiæ et familiæ seorsum, et mulieres eorum seorsum]]. These families are named in general and not distinguished one by one, since they had no special privilege of rank. According to Jerome, if we consider how many thousands of Jews in Jerusalem were converted by the Apostles soon after the Holy Ghost was sent, it is easy to weigh how truly these things were then fulfilled, especially since it is said in the Acts: [[Acts 2:5|Now there were dwelling at Jerusalem, Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven|Erant autem in Jerusalem habitantes Judæi viri religiosi ex omni natione quæ sub cælo est]]: and of these many were then converted[[Acts 2:41||]].

paras.t: Denique vehemens planctus iste statim in hora mortis Christi sumpsit exordium, juxta illud: Omnis turba eorum qui simul aderant ad spectaculum istud, et videbant quæ fiebant, percutientes pectora sua, revertebantur.
paras.en: Finally, this vehement lamentation began at once in the hour of Christ's death, according to that word: [[Luke 23:48|And all the multitude of them that were come together to that sight and saw the things that were done returned, striking their breasts|Omnis turba eorum qui simul aderant ad spectaculum istud, et videbant quæ fiebant, percutientes pectora sua, revertebantur]].

12.title: De alia ejusdem capituli duodecimi explanatione.
12.title_en: Of another explanation of the same twelfth chapter.

paras.t: Denique intuendum, quod quidam expositores præinductum capitulum ad litteram exponunt de Ecclesia Christi, et persecutione ipsius : quorum nonnulli exponunt de persecutione Ecclesiæ primitivæ a Judæis incredulis principibusque Romanis, alii vero de persecutione Ecclesiæ tempore Antichristi. Ceteri autem, quos jam assecutus sum, exponunt ad litteram de Synagoga; mystice vero, de Ecclesia secundum ejus decursum a principio usque ad finem. Nunc ergo præsens capitulum taliter exponetur, ut ad omnia ista faciliter valeat ejus expositio applicari.
paras.en: Finally, it should be observed that some expositors explain the foregoing chapter literally of the Church of Christ and of her persecution: some of them explain it of the persecution of the primitive Church by the unbelieving Jews and the Roman rulers, others of the persecution of the Church in the time of Antichrist. But the others, whom I have followed so far, explain it literally of the Synagogue, and mystically of the Church according to her course from the beginning to the end. Now therefore the present chapter will be expounded in such a way that its exposition may easily be applied to all of these.
