paras.t: Onus verbi Domini, id est tribulatio divinitus denuntiata, super Israel, id est Ecclesiam, quæ vere ac spiritualiter Israel, id est Deum videns, vocatur. Et dixit Dominus extendens cœlum, id est, homines contemplativos puræ cœliformisque conversationis, ad amorem divinorum sustollens, ad supernaque elevans, atque per caritatis latitudinem ad benefaciendum omnibus ducens; et fundans terram, id est activos et conjugatos, quorum pedes terram jugiter calcant, dum in temporalibus quotidie occupantur. Hos Deus fundat in humilitate, timore, et præceptorum custodia, ne per multa diffusi ac vagi, mente separentur a Deo, caducis magis quam summo ac invariabili bono affectualiter adhærendo. Et fingens spiritum hominis in eo, id est, gratiam devotionis, contritum ac humilem spiritum præstans hominibus, sicut oramus in Psalmo : Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis. Ad Timotheum quoque ait Apostolus : Dedit nobis Deus spiritum virtutis, et dilectionis, et sobrietatis.
paras.en: [[12:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the tribulation foretold by God, [[12:1|upon Israel|super Israel]], that is, upon the Church, which is truly and spiritually called Israel, that is, *seeing God*. [[12:1|Thus saith the Lord, who stretcheth forth the heavens|Et dixit Dominus extendens cœlum]]: that is, raising contemplative men, of a pure and heavenly manner of life, to the love of divine things, lifting them up to the things above, and leading them through the breadth of charity to do good to all; [[12:1|and layeth the foundations of the earth|et fundans terram]], that is, the active and the married, whose feet continually tread the earth, since they are busied every day with temporal things. These God grounds in humility, in fear, and in the keeping of the commandments, lest, scattered and wandering among many things, they be separated in mind from God, clinging in their affections to perishable things rather than to the highest and unchangeable good. And [[12:1|formeth the spirit of man in him|fingens spiritum hominis in eo]], that is, granting men the grace of devotion, a contrite and humble spirit, as we pray in the Psalm: [[Ps 50:12|Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels|Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis]]. And the Apostle also says to Timothy: God hath [[2 Tim 1:7|given us the spirit|Dedit nobis Deus spiritum]] [[2 Tim 1:7|of power and of love and of sobriety|virtutis, et dilectionis, et sobrietatis]] [Denis gives only the second half of the verse, leaving out "not the spirit of fear"].

paras.t: Ecce ego ponam Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam : de qua ab Isaia dicitur, Surge, illuminare, Jerusalem; et in Apocalypsi, Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem, descendentem de cœlo; superliminare crapulæ : ita ut omnis qui limen ejus, seu eam malignanter invaserit, cadat et pereat. Sic enim perierunt persecutores primitivæ Ecclesiæ, saltem in anima, et multi etiam corporaliter fuerunt plagati. Sic etiam Antichristus cum suis peribit; sic et tyranni et hæretici, itemque schismatici, omnesque persecutores justorum perierunt, pereunt, et peribunt.
paras.en: [[12:2|Behold I will make Jerusalem|Ecce ego ponam Jerusalem]], that is, the Church, of which it is said by Isaias: [[Is 60:1|Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem|Surge, illuminare, Jerusalem]]; and in the Apocalypse: I [[Apoc 21:2|saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven|Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem, descendentem de cœlo]]; [[12:2|a lintel of surfeiting|superliminare crapulæ]] [*superliminare*, the lintel or upper threshold of a door: Denis takes it as a threshold over which the attacker stumbles, as one stupefied with drink, *crapula*], so that everyone who maliciously assails its threshold, or rather the Church herself, falls and perishes. For so the persecutors of the primitive Church perished, at least in soul, and many of them were also stricken in body. So too Antichrist will perish with his followers; so too tyrants and heretics, and schismatics likewise, and all the persecutors of the just, have perished, are perishing, and will perish.

paras.t: Sed et Juda erit in obsidione contra Jerusalem. Hoc fuit in primitiva Ecclesia adimpletum, quando aliqui corde christiani, qui nomine Judæ, qui interpretatur confessio, designantur, ex timore junxerunt se persecutoribus Ecclesiæ, quæ per Jerusalem significatur. Sic demum erit et tempore Antichristi, in cujus exercitu erunt aliqui fideles timore compulsi. Sed et persecutionis tempore id sæpius accidit. Præterea, Juda est in obsidione contra Jerusalem, dum clerici, et qui alios a peccatis revocare deberent, vulgum et simplices vel subjectos ad vitia pertrahunt, a bono impediunt, vel propter justitiam tribulant.
paras.en: [[12:2|and Juda also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem|Sed et Juda erit in obsidione contra Jerusalem]]. This was fulfilled in the primitive Church, when some who were Christians at heart, who are signified by the name of Juda, which is interpreted *confession*, joined themselves out of fear to the persecutors of the Church, which is signified by Jerusalem. So too it will be in the time of Antichrist, in whose army there will be some of the faithful, driven by fear. And indeed this has often happened in time of persecution. Moreover, Juda is in the siege against Jerusalem when clerics, and those who ought to call others back from sin, draw the common people and the simple or their subjects into vice, hinder them from good, or afflict them for justice' sake.

paras.t: In die illa ponam Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam, lapidem oneris cunctis populis : ita quod omnes qui eam tollere moliuntur, succumbent, sicut succumbit qui saxum gravissimum levare conatur. Non enim deficit, sed augetur persecutionibus Ecclesia Christi. Et quamvis tempore Antichristi ad tempus aliquantulum valde minorari videbitur persecutione dirissima, finaliter tamen, imo et cito, penitus prævalebit. Et colligentur adversus eam omnia regna terræ, id est multi de regionibus universis : quemadmodum tempore imperatorum Ecclesiam vastantium constat impletum, et in Antichristi diebus implebitur. Propter quod Christus dixit discipulis : Odio eritis omnibus hominibus propter me.
paras.en: [[12:3|In that day|In die illa]] [[12:3|I will make Jerusalem|ponam Jerusalem]], that is, the Church, [[12:3|a burdensome stone to all people|lapidem oneris cunctis populis]]: so that all who strive to lift her will sink beneath her, as he sinks who tries to raise a very heavy rock. For the Church of Christ does not fail, but grows through persecutions. And although in the time of Antichrist she will seem for a while to be very greatly diminished by a most cruel persecution, yet in the end, and indeed soon, she will wholly prevail. And [[12:3|all the kingdoms of the earth shall be gathered together against her|colligentur adversus eam omnia regna terræ]], that is, many from all regions: as is known to have been fulfilled in the time of the emperors who laid waste the Church, and will be fulfilled in the days of Antichrist. Wherefore Christ said to the disciples: [[Matt 24:9|you shall be hated by all|Odio eritis omnibus]] men for my sake [the margin gives Matt. xxiv, 9; Denis's wording, "by all men", is closer to Matt 10:22].

paras.t: In die illa, percutiam omnem equum in stuporem, et ascensorem ejus in amentiam, id est, universa præsidia prædictorum Ecclesiæ adversariorum dejiciam. Denique dæmonum equi sunt omnes perversi, præsertim qui opprimunt bonos. Hæreticorum quoque et schismaticorum equi sunt, qui eis consentiunt, eosque portant atque circumferunt : imo omnes qui aliorum impietatibus subministrant, eorum equi censentur. Et super domum Juda aperiam oculos meos, id est, eos qui solo timore et non ex animo adhæserunt persecutoribus Ecclesiæ, clementer adspiciam, ne æternaliter pereant. Talibus quoque miserebitur Deus tempore Antichristi, quia cum ipso non peribunt, imo eo occiso ad fideles redibunt, et suam imperfectionem deflebunt.
paras.en: [[12:4|In that day|In die illa]], [[12:4|I will strike every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness|percutiam omnem equum in stuporem, et ascensorem ejus in amentiam]], that is, I will cast down all the defences of the aforesaid adversaries of the Church. Further, all the wicked are horses of the demons, especially those who oppress the good. The horses of heretics and schismatics, too, are those who consent to them, and carry them and bear them about: indeed, all who minister to the impieties of others are reckoned their horses. [[12:4|and I will open my eyes upon the house of Juda|Et super domum Juda aperiam oculos meos]], that is, I will look mercifully upon those who clung to the persecutors of the Church out of fear alone and not from the heart, lest they perish eternally. On such God will have mercy in the time of Antichrist as well, for they will not perish with him; rather, when he is slain they will return to the faithful and will bewail their own imperfection.

paras.t: Et dicent duces Juda in corde suo, id est principales inter hos : Confortentur mihi habitatores Jerusalem, id est, filii Ecclesiæ prævaleant. Hoc quippe toto corde concupient. Potestque hoc etiam ad primitivam Ecclesiam applicari (quamvis quidam dicat oppositum) : eo quod tunc multi Judæi fuerint occulte christiani, sicut fuit ad tempus magnus ille Gamaliel ; imo et ante passionem non pauci crediderunt in Christum, juxta illud Joannis : Ex principibus multi crediderunt in eum ; sed propter Judæos non confitebantur. Tales ergo prosperitatem Ecclesiæ affectabant.
paras.en: [[12:5|And the governors of Juda shall say in their heart|Et dicent duces Juda in corde suo]], that is, the chief among these: [[12:5|Let the inhabitants of Jerusalem be strengthened for me|Confortentur mihi habitatores Jerusalem]], that is, let the sons of the Church prevail. For this they will desire with all their heart. And this can also be applied to the primitive Church (though a certain writer says the opposite), because at that time many Jews were secretly Christians, as for a time was that great Gamaliel[[Acts 5:34||]]; indeed, even before the Passion not a few believed in Christ, according to that word of John: [[John 12:42|many of the chief men also believed in him|Ex principibus multi crediderunt in eum]]; but because of the Jews [[John 12:42|they did not confess him|non confitebantur]] [the Douay-Rheims, with the Vulgate, has "because of the Pharisees"]. Such men, then, longed for the prosperity of the Church.

paras.t: In die illa ponam duces Juda, de quibus jam dictum est, sicut caminum ignis, id est, virtutem constantiæ roburque animi tribuam eis, ut adversariis suis prævaleant, vel spiritualiter tantum, vel etiam corporaliter. Nam Antichristo sublato, qui ei ex timore adhærebunt, Christianis conjuncti, contra perfidos victoriose resistent. Insuper Salvator suis ait : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit. Spiritualiter vero devoraverunt fideles primitivæ Ecclesiæ, et devorabunt post mortem Antichristi tunc Christifideles, ad dexteram et sinistram omnes populos in circuitu, quosdam, imo plurimos valde, de omni natione et regnis convertendo, et Domino Salvatori eosdem salubriter incorporando.
paras.en: [[12:6|In that day I will make the governors of Juda|In die illa ponam duces Juda]], of whom we have just spoken, [[12:6|like a furnace of fire|sicut caminum ignis]], that is, I will give them the strength of constancy and firmness of mind, so that they may prevail over their adversaries, either only spiritually, or bodily as well. For when Antichrist has been taken away, those who clung to him out of fear, joined to the Christians, will victoriously withstand the faithless. Moreover, the Saviour says to his own: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi]] [[Luke 10:19|upon all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit]]. And spiritually the faithful of the primitive Church devoured, and after the death of Antichrist the faithful of Christ of that day [[12:6|shall devour|devorabunt]], [[12:6|to the right hand, and to the left|ad dexteram et sinistram]], [[12:6|all the people round about|omnes populos in circuitu]], by converting some, indeed very many, of every nation and kingdom, and incorporating them unto salvation into the Lord the Saviour.

paras.t: Et salvabit Dominus tabernacula Juda, id est præfatos, qui ad tempus timore inordinato a fidelibus recesserunt : ut non magnifice glorietur domus David, et gloria habitantium Jerusalem contra Judam, id est, ne inconcussi atque perfecti, qui in omni eventu constantes in Ecclesia perstiterunt, eos qui perterriti fuerant prorsus contemnant, sed eis redeuntibus, caritative condoleant et succurrant.
paras.en: [[12:7|And the Lord shall save the tabernacles of Juda|Et salvabit Dominus tabernacula Juda]], that is, those spoken of above, who for a time withdrew from the faithful through inordinate fear: [[12:7|that the house of David, and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, may not boast and magnify themselves against Juda|ut non magnifice glorietur domus David, et gloria habitantium Jerusalem contra Judam]], that is, lest the unshaken and perfect, who in every event stood constant in the Church, should utterly despise those who had been terrified; but rather, when these return, they should in charity feel for them and succour them.

paras.t: In die illa protegat Dominus habitatores Jerusalem, id est electos Ecclesiæ filios : quos et in primitiva Ecclesia protexit, nunc quoque protegit, et tempore Antichristi defendet. Nam etsi corporaliter eos occidi permittat, animas tamen ab omni periculo eripit, ipsamque quam sustinent passionem, ad ineffabilem eis felicitatem convertet, juxta illud Sapientiæ : Etsi coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes electorum immortalitate plena est; in paucis vexati, in multis bene disponentur, quoniam Deus dextera sua teget eos, et brachio suo defendet eos. Et erit qui offenderit ex eis, quasi David, ita quod cito per pœnitentiam surget, et cautior erit post lapsum, quam fuit : et domus David, id est Ecclesia fortium mente atque constantium in æquitate, erit quasi Dei, sicut angelus Domini, id est, magna gratia decorabitur : per quod magnitudo excellentiæ gratiæ Dei tempore legis evangelicæ insinuatur.
paras.en: [[12:8|In that day shall the Lord protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem|In die illa protegat Dominus habitatores Jerusalem]], that is, the chosen sons of the Church, whom he protected in the primitive Church, protects now also, and will defend in the time of Antichrist. For though he permit them to be slain in body, yet he rescues their souls from every danger, and will turn the very passion they endure into unspeakable happiness for them, according to that word of Wisdom: [[Wis 3:4|though in the sight of men they suffered torments|Etsi coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt]], the hope of the elect [[Wis 3:4|is full of immortality|immortalitate plena est]] [Denis has "the hope of the elect" for "their hope"]; [[Wis 3:5|Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded|in paucis vexati, in multis bene disponentur]], [[Wis 5:17|for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them|quoniam Deus dextera sua teget eos, et brachio suo defendet eos]]. And [[12:8|he that hath offended among them|qui offenderit ex eis]] [[12:8|shall be as David|quasi David]], in that he will soon rise again by penance, and will be more cautious after his fall than he was before; [[12:8|and the house of David|et domus David]], that is, the Church of those who are strong in mind and constant in equity, shall be [[12:8|as that of God, as an angel of the Lord|quasi Dei, sicut angelus Domini]], that is, it will be adorned with great grace: by which is intimated the great excellence of the grace of God in the time of the law of the Gospel.

paras.t: Et effundam super domum David et super habitatores Jerusalem spiritum gratiæ et precum. Hoc in fine mundi copiose implebitur, quando ad prædicationem Eliæ Judæi convertentur, sicut in Evangelio Christus testatur : Elias quum venerit, restituet omnia. Quum enim plenitudo gentium intraverit, omnis Israel salvus fiet, secundum Apostolum ad Romanos. Præterea omni die effundit Deus spiritum gratiæ et precum super domum Juda, videlicet eos qui fide et opere Dominum confitentur ac laudant, et super habitatores Jerusalem, eos videlicet qui in pace cum Deo deambulant.
paras.en: [[12:10|And I will pour out upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace, and of prayers|Et effundam super domum David et super habitatores Jerusalem spiritum gratiæ et precum]]. This will be abundantly fulfilled at the end of the world, when the Jews will be converted at the preaching of Elias, as Christ testifies in the Gospel: [[Matt 17:11|Elias indeed shall come, and restore all things|Elias quum venerit, restituet omnia]]. For when [[Rom 11:25|the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|plenitudo gentium intraverit]], [[Rom 11:26|all Israel should be saved|omnis Israel salvus fiet]], according to the Apostle to the Romans. Moreover, every day God pours out the spirit of grace and of prayers upon the house of Juda [so the print; the verse has "the house of David"], namely, upon those who confess and praise the Lord in faith and in deed, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, namely, those who walk in peace with God.

paras.t: Et adspicient ad me, quem confixerunt, etc. Antichristo quippe sublato, Judæi fide suscepta cum ingenti dolore ac lacrimis fatebuntur se Christum crucifixisse : vel quia ab eorum populo occisus est, vel quia occisoribus Christi usque ad fidei susceptionem faverunt, putantes illos bene fecisse. Præterea ingrati et impii quotidie Christum, quantum in eis est, configunt. De quibus ad Hebræos ait Apostolus : Rursum crucifigentes sibimet Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes. Et super hos Christus nonnunquam ex sua pietate immensa, spiritum gratiæ precumque effundit, ita ut mox compuncti, cum interno cordis doloroso ac lacrimoso affectu adspiciant Christum, ejus passioni compatientes, propriasque impietates deflentes. Cetera patent ex præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: And [[12:10|they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced|adspicient ad me, quem confixerunt]], etc. For when Antichrist has been taken away, the Jews, having received the faith, will confess with immense sorrow and tears that they crucified Christ: either because he was slain by their people, or because until they received the faith they favoured the slayers of Christ, thinking that they had done well. Moreover, the ungrateful and the wicked pierce Christ every day, as far as in them lies. Of these the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 6:6|crucifying again to themselves the Son of God and making him a mockery|Rursum crucifigentes sibimet Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes]]. And upon these Christ sometimes, of his immense goodness, pours out the spirit of grace and of prayers, so that, soon pierced with compunction, they look upon Christ with an inward, sorrowful and tearful affection of heart, compassionating his Passion and bewailing their own impieties. The rest is plain from the preceding article.

13.title: Elucidatio capituli tertiidecimi: In die illa erit fons patens domui David.
13.title_en: Explanation of the thirteenth chapter: In that day there shall be a fountain open to the house of David.

paras.t: Quum in principio hujus capituli dicatur, In die illa, certum est ista quæ nunc dicentur, ad idem tempus pertinere referendaque esse, de quo in fine præcedentis capituli dictum est. Itaque, In die illa, id est tempore illo quo omnes Judæorum familiæ præmemoratæ Christum a se confixum adspicient atque deplangent : quod et post Christi passionem mox factum est, et in fine mundi Judæis conversis fiet. Imo, ut sanctus ait Methodius martyr, detecta per Eliam et Enoch falsitate Antichristi, tot Judæi convertentur ad Christum, ita quod de qualibet tribu eorum quadraginta quatuor millia martyrio coronabuntur. Tunc ergo erit fons, id est Christi Baptismus, seu aqua Baptismatis, patens, id est apertus, manifestus atque paratus, domui David et habitantibus Jerusalem, id est cunctis Judæis sancti David fidem sequentibus, atque in Christum credentibus, in ablutionem peccatoris et menstruatæ, id est ad emendationem peccatorum virorum ac mulierum quantumcumque immundorum. De quo fonte multa prædicta sunt ab Ezechiele, quod scilicet erumpet fons de domo Domini, et pergat ad solitudinem, et omnis anima ad quam devenerit, vivat. Item a Joele : Fons de domo Domini egredietur, et irrigabit torrentem spinarum. De hoc fonte dixit Petrus Judæis corde compunctis veniamque petentibus : Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi in remissionem peccatorum.
paras.en: Since at the beginning of this chapter it is said, [[13:1|In that day|In die illa]], it is certain that the things now to be said belong and are to be referred to the same time of which it was spoken at the end of the preceding chapter. And so, [[13:1|In that day|In die illa]], that is, in that time when all the families of the Jews named above shall look upon Christ whom they pierced, and shall mourn for him: which both came to pass soon after Christ's passion, and will come to pass at the end of the world, when the Jews are converted. Nay more, as the holy martyr Methodius says [the *Revelations* that went under the name of St. Methodius], once the falsehood of Antichrist has been laid bare by Elias and Enoch, so many Jews will be converted to Christ that out of each of their tribes forty-four thousand will be crowned with martyrdom. Then therefore [[13:1|there shall be a fountain|erit fons]], that is, the Baptism of Christ, or the water of Baptism, [[13:1|open|patens]], that is, opened, manifest and ready, [[13:1|to the house of David, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem|domui David et habitantibus Jerusalem]], that is, to all the Jews who follow the faith of holy David and believe in Christ, [[13:1|for the washing of the sinner, and of the unclean woman|in ablutionem peccatoris et menstruatæ]], that is, for the amendment of sinful men and women, however unclean. Of this fountain many things were foretold by Ezechiel: namely, that a fountain shall burst forth from the house of the Lord and go on into the wilderness, and every soul to which it comes shall live[[Ezech 47:8||]][[Ezech 47:9||]] [Denis gives the sense of Ezechiel's vision of the waters, not its words]. Likewise by Joel: [[Joel 3:18|a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord, and shall water the torrent of thorns|Fons de domo Domini egredietur, et irrigabit torrentem spinarum]]. Of this fountain Peter spoke to the Jews, when they were pricked in heart and asked for pardon: [[Acts 2:38|be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of your sins|Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi in remissionem peccatorum]].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, scilicet tempore promulgationis evangelicæ legis, dicit Dominus exercituum : Disperdam nomina idolorum de terra, id est, idololatriam ubilibet destruam, in omnibus locis ubi gentes fidem Christi suscipient, et non memorabuntur ultra, id est, oblivioni tradentur a suis cultoribus, quantum ad cultum, non quantum ad nudam memoriam. Sic enim et nunc usque fideles reminiscuntur qualiter olim gentes idola coluerunt. Innumerabiles quoque Christiani de idolis gentium loqui nil sciunt.
paras.en: [[13:2|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit in die illa]], namely in the time of the promulgation of the law of the Gospel, [[13:2|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]: [[13:2|that I will destroy the names of idols out of the earth|Disperdam nomina idolorum de terra]], that is, I will destroy idolatry everywhere, in all the places where the nations shall receive the faith of Christ, [[13:2|and they shall be remembered no more|et non memorabuntur ultra]], that is, they shall be given over to forgetfulness by their worshippers as regards worship, not as regards the bare memory of them. For even to this day the faithful remember how the nations once worshipped idols. And countless Christians know nothing to say of the idols of the nations.

paras.t: Istud videtur quibusdam non esse impletum tempore Apostolorum et interim, sed in fine mundi : quia ut dicunt, tunc Antichristo occiso, omnes concorditer gentiles atque Judæi unientur in fide Christi. Sed istud infirmiter dictum est. Constat enim, quod eo modo ac sensu tempore Apostolorum et interim impletum est illud Psalmi : In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, etc. ; et item, Et benedicentur in ipso omnes tribus terræ, omnes gentes magnificabunt eum ; itemque, Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ ; et quod Christus dixit Apostolis, Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ ; multaque alia ad idem spectantia. Etiam tunc impletum est quod nunc de idololatriæ ablatione asseritur. Nec verum quod circa finem sæculi, vel post mortem Antichristi, omnes penitus convertentur ad Christum : imo multi in malo obstinati manebunt. De quibus ait Apostolus : Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus sicut dolor in utero habentis, et non effugient. Christus quoque : Tanquam laqueus superveniet dies illa, puta judicii, in omnes qui sedent super faciem omnis terræ ; et iterum, Sicut fuit, inquit, in diebus Noe, etc.
paras.en: To some it seems that this was not fulfilled in the time of the Apostles and the time since, but will be at the end of the world: because, as they say, then, when Antichrist has been slain, all Gentiles and Jews alike will be united with one accord in the faith of Christ. But this is weakly said. For it is certain that in the time of the Apostles and the time since, that saying of the Psalm has been fulfilled in the same manner and sense: [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]], etc.; and again, [[Ps 71:17|And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: all nations shall magnify him|Et benedicentur in ipso omnes tribus terræ, omnes gentes magnificabunt eum]]; and again, [[Ps 21:28|All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord|Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ]]; and what Christ said to the Apostles, [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and many other things to the same effect. Then too was fulfilled what is now asserted about the taking away of idolatry. Nor is it true that about the end of the world, or after the death of Antichrist, absolutely all will be converted to Christ: nay, many will remain obstinate in evil. Of whom the Apostle says: [[1 Thess 5:3|when they shall say: Peace and security; then shall sudden destruction come upon them, as the pains upon her that is with child, and they shall not escape|Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus sicut dolor in utero habentis, et non effugient]]. Christ too: [[Luke 21:35|as a snare shall it come|Tanquam laqueus superveniet]], that day, namely of judgment, [[Luke 21:35|upon all that sit upon the face of the whole earth|in omnes qui sedent super faciem omnis terræ]]; and again, [[Luke 17:26|as it came to pass|Sicut fuit]], he says, [[Luke 17:26|in the days of Noe|in diebus Noe]], etc.

paras.t: Et pseudoprophetas et spiritum immundum auferam de terra, id est, prophetas falsos tam gentilium quam Judæorum fidem Christi sumentium, spiritusque malignos de infidelium cordibus auferam : secundum quod Christus dixit, Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras.
paras.en: [[13:2|and I will take away the false prophets, and the unclean spirit out of the earth|Et pseudoprophetas et spiritum immundum auferam de terra]], that is, I will take away the false prophets both of the Gentiles and of the Jews who take up the faith of Christ, and the wicked spirits out of the hearts of unbelievers: according to what Christ said, [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]].

paras.t: Et erit : Quum prophetaverit quispiam ultra, id est, quum aliquis inter conversos et Christianos vaticinari non ex Spiritu Sancto, sed spiritu proprio vel maligno, præsumpserit, dicent ei pater ejus et mater ejus qui genuerunt eum : Non vives, quia mendacium locutus es in Domino, id est, dixisti te ex Deo locutum, quod Domini effectum non habuit, ideo morte es dignus. Tales enim et Moyses jussit occidi. Et configent eum pater ejus et mater ejus quum prophetaverit : id est, tantæ justitiæ erunt parentes et cognati, quod contra ordinem legis divinæ et æquitatis christianæ nemini parcent, quantumcumque propinquo, inaniter prophetanti, aut mala similia perpetranti.
paras.en: [[13:3|And it shall come to pass, that when any man shall prophesy any more|Et erit : Quum prophetaverit quispiam ultra]], that is, when anyone among the converted and the Christians shall presume to prophesy, not from the Holy Ghost but from his own spirit or an evil one, [[13:3|his father and his mother that brought him into the world, shall say to him: Thou shalt not live: because thou hast spoken a lie in the name of the Lord|dicent ei pater ejus et mater ejus qui genuerunt eum : Non vives, quia mendacium locutus es in Domino]] [the print reads *in Domino*, "in the Lord", with *nomine* noted beside it, as in the Vulgate's *in nomine Domini*], that is, thou hast said that thou spokest from God what had not the Lord's effect [that is, what the Lord did not bring to pass]; therefore thou art worthy of death. For Moses too commanded that such men be slain[[Deut 13:5||]]. [[13:3|And his father, and his mother, his parents, shall thrust him through, when he shall prophesy|Et configent eum pater ejus et mater ejus quum prophetaverit]]: that is, the parents and kinsfolk shall be of such justice that they will spare no one against the order of the divine law and of Christian equity, however near to them, who prophesies falsely or commits like evils.

paras.t: Et erit in die illa : Confundentur prophetæ fallaces, unusquisque ex visione sua quum prophetaverit : quia Deo revelante, scient fideles quod divinitus missi non sint ; nec operientur pallio saccino, id est, veste cilicina et aspera seu sacco et vili indumento non induent se : quemadmodum moris fuit Prophetis, quando futura prænuntiando, populum ad pœnitentiam provocabant, ut legitur quarto Regum de Elia ; Isaiæ quoque Dominus dixit, Tolle saccum de lumbis tuis ; ut mentiantur, id est, quatenus sub aliena et humili veste prophetalique indumento simplices fallant. Hoc igitur timore pœnæ facere non audebunt.
paras.en: [[13:4|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit in die illa]]: the false prophets [[13:4|shall be confounded, every one by his own vision, when he shall prophesy|Confundentur prophetæ fallaces, unusquisque ex visione sua quum prophetaverit]]: because, God revealing it, the faithful will know that they are not sent from God; [[13:4|neither shall they be clad with a garment of sackcloth|nec operientur pallio saccino]], that is, they will not put on a garment of haircloth and rough, or sackcloth and mean clothing: as was the custom of the Prophets when, foretelling things to come, they called the people to penance, as we read in the fourth book of Kings of Elias[[4 Kings 1:8||]]; and the Lord also said to Isaias, Take [[Is 20:2|the sackcloth from off thy loins|saccum de lumbis tuis]] [the Vulgate has *solve*, loose, where Denis has *tolle*, take]; [[13:4|to deceive|ut mentiantur]], that is, so as to deceive the simple under a garment not their own, humble and prophetic. This, then, for fear of punishment they will not dare to do.

paras.t: Sed dicet, id est, quilibet talium dicet : Non sum propheta, homo agricola ego sum, id est, non officio prophetandi, sed agriculturæ intendo, quoniam Adam exemplum meum, id est, Adam factus est mihi forma vivendi, et ejus vitam quasi exemplum sectatus sum, ab adolescentia mea, observando quod in Genesi Dominus loquitur ei : In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo. Et de ipso scribitur in Genesi : Emisit eum Dominus de paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur terram de qua sumptus est.
paras.en: [[13:5|But he shall say|Sed dicet]], that is, each of these shall say: [[13:5|I am no prophet, I am a husbandman|Non sum propheta, homo agricola ego sum]], that is, I give myself not to the office of prophesying but to husbandry, [[13:5|for Adam is my example|quoniam Adam exemplum meum]], that is, Adam has become for me the pattern of living, and I have followed his life as an example, [[13:5|from my youth|ab adolescentia mea]], keeping what the Lord says to him in Genesis: [[Gen 3:19|In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread|In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo]]. And of him it is written in Genesis: The Lord [[Gen 3:23|sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken|Emisit eum Dominus de paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur terram de qua sumptus est]].

paras.t: Et dicetur ei : Quid sunt plagæ istæ in medio manuum tuarum ? id est, cur ita confixus es, vel affixus patibulo ? quid criminis commisisti, ut sic vulneratus appareas ? Et dicet : His plagatus sum in domo eorum qui diligebant me, id est, vulnera ista a propinquis atque amicis meis accepi, non ex eorum rancore ad me, sed zelo justitiæ et pro mea correctione.
paras.en: [[13:6|And they shall say to him: What are these wounds in the midst of thy hands?|Et dicetur ei : Quid sunt plagæ istæ in medio manuum tuarum]] that is, why art thou thus pierced, or fastened to the gibbet? What crime hast thou committed, that thou appearest wounded thus? [[13:6|And he shall say: With these I was wounded in the house of them that loved me|Et dicet : His plagatus sum in domo eorum qui diligebant me]], that is, I received these wounds from my kinsfolk and friends, not out of their rancour towards me, but out of zeal for justice and for my correction.

paras.t: Denique, quia nunc de fonte Baptismatis locutus fuit Propheta, interserit et aliud de Christi passione, a qua Baptismus et cetera sacramenta efficaciam suam sortita sunt. Loquitur itaque Deus Pater : Framea mea, id est, rhomphæa passionis, suscitare super pastorem meum, id est, consurge et irrue super Christum summum pastorem : qui ait in Joanne, Ego sum pastor bonus ; de quo in Ezechiele Dominus contestatur : Salvabo gregem meum, et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum, id est Christum, ut Judæi quoque exponunt. Framea ergo non sumitur hic determinate pro gladio, sed pro acerba afflictione : de qua Christus in Psalmo precatur, Erue a framea, Deus, animam meam. Et per Amos Dominus asserit : In gladio morientur omnes peccatores terræ. Et super virum cohærentem mihi, id est Christum mihi inseparabiliter adhærentem : qui ait, Qui me misit, mecum est ; et, Pater non reliquit me solum, quia ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper.
paras.en: Next, since the Prophet has just spoken of the fountain of Baptism, he inserts something else besides, about the passion of Christ, from which Baptism and the other sacraments have received their efficacy. So God the Father speaks: [[13:7|O sword|Framea mea]] [Denis reads *Framea mea*, my sword], that is, the sword [*rhomphæa*, a long two-edged sword] of the passion, [[13:7|Awake|suscitare]] [[13:7|against my shepherd|super pastorem meum]], that is, rise up and rush upon Christ, the chief shepherd: who says in John, [[John 10:11|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]][[John 10:14||]]; of whom the Lord bears witness in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]], [[Ezech 34:23|And I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum]], that is, Christ, as the Jews too expound it. So *framea* [a kind of spear or sword] is not taken here strictly for a sword, but for bitter affliction: from which Christ prays in the Psalm, [[Ps 21:21|Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword|Erue a framea, Deus, animam meam]]. And by Amos the Lord declares: [[Amos 9:10|All the sinners of my people shall fall by the sword|In gladio morientur omnes peccatores terræ]] [Amos has *of my people*, Denis *of the earth*]. [[13:7|and against the man that cleaveth to me|Et super virum cohærentem mihi]], that is, Christ, who cleaves to me inseparably: who says, [[John 8:29|he that sent me is with me|Qui me misit, mecum est]]; and, The Father [[John 8:29|hath not left me alone. For I do always the things that please him|non reliquit me solum, quia ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]].

paras.t: Præterea Christus secundum divinam naturam adhæret Patri per amorem immensum, voluntatis indivisibilem identitatem, atque essentiæ unitatem ; sed secundum naturam assumptam adhæret per creatæ voluntatis conformationem et subjectionem ad voluntatem divinam. Propter quod dixit : Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me ; et rursus, Pater, non quod ego volo, sed quod tu. Dicit Dominus exercituum.
paras.en: Moreover, Christ according to his divine nature cleaves to the Father by boundless love, by an indivisible identity of will, and by unity of essence; but according to the nature he assumed he cleaves by the conformity and subjection of a created will to the divine will. For which reason he said: [[John 6:38|I came down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed ejus qui misit me]]; and again, Father, [[Matt 26:39|not as I will but as thou wilt|non quod ego volo, sed quod tu]]. [[13:7|saith the Lord of hosts|Dicit Dominus exercituum]].

paras.t: Percute, o framea, pastorem, videlicet Christum, et dispergentur oves gregis, id est, discipuli sui electi gregis cui dicebat, Nolite timere, pusillus grex, ab ipso diffugient. Porro hanc scripturam ad se suamque passionem respicere ipsemet Christus docet, quum ait Apostolis : Omnes vos scandalum patiemini in me in ista nocte : scriptum est enim, Percutiam pastorem, et dispergentur oves gregis. Nec obstat, quod hic dicitur, Percute ; ibi, Percutiam pastorem : nam sensus redit in idem, quoniam Deo volente et præordinante, framea passionis irruit super Christum, qui in Psalmo ait ad Patrem : Quoniam quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt. Et per Isaiam Pater testatur : Propter peccata populi mei percussi eum. Unde in Actibus Petrus fatetur : Deus qui prænuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic. Postremo, ipse Christus tradidit semetipsum, oblatusque est quia voluit.
paras.en: [[13:7|strike|Percute]], O sword, [[13:7|the shepherd|pastorem]], namely Christ, [[13:7|and the sheep shall be scattered|et dispergentur oves gregis]], that is, his disciples, of the chosen flock to which he said, [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock|Nolite timere, pusillus grex]], shall flee away from him. Further, that this scripture looks to himself and his passion Christ himself teaches, when he says to the Apostles: [[Matt 26:31|All you shall be scandalized in me this night. For it is written: I will strike the shepherd: and the sheep of the flock shall be dispersed|Omnes vos scandalum patiemini in me in ista nocte : scriptum est enim, Percutiam pastorem, et dispergentur oves gregis]]. Nor is it an objection that here it says [[13:7|strike|Percute]], and there [[Matt 26:31|I will strike the shepherd|Percutiam pastorem]]: for the sense comes to the same, since by God's will and foreordaining the sword of the passion rushed upon Christ, who says to the Father in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:27|Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten|Quoniam quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt]]. And by Isaias the Father testifies: [[Is 53:8|for the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter peccata populi mei percussi eum]]. Hence Peter confesses in the Acts: [[Acts 3:18|God before had shewed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled|Deus qui prænuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic]]. Lastly, Christ himself [[Gal 2:20|delivered himself|tradidit semetipsum]], and [[Is 53:7|was offered because it was his own will|oblatusque est quia voluit]].

paras.t: Et convertam manum meam ad parvulos, id est, potestatem gratiæ meæ ostendam et exercebo circa humiles Christi discipulos : qui tempore passionis ex propria infirmitate fugerunt, sed post passionem per virtutem gratiæ Spiritus Sancti invincibiles constantissimique fuerunt. De quibus per Isaiam loquitur Christus : Ecce ego et pueri mei, quos dedit mihi Dominus ; itemque in Evangelio, Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Impleverunt enim quod dixit Salvator : Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum.
paras.en: [[13:7|and I will turn my hand to the little ones|Et convertam manum meam ad parvulos]], that is, I will show and exercise the power of my grace towards the humble disciples of Christ: who at the time of the passion fled out of their own weakness, but after the passion, by the power of the grace of the Holy Ghost, were invincible and most steadfast. Of them Christ speaks by Isaias: [[Is 8:18|Behold I and my children, whom the Lord hath given me|Ecce ego et pueri mei, quos dedit mihi Dominus]]; and likewise in the Gospel, [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. For they fulfilled what the Saviour said: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]].

paras.t: Et erunt in omni terra, dicit Dominus, partes, id est, in toto mundo genus hominum seu populus terræ erit divisus in partes tres, puta Judæorum, et gentilium, ac Christianorum. Duæ in ea, id est duæ partes hominum, scilicet gentiles et Judæi increduli, dispergentur ac deficient, id est, a Deo reprobabuntur, et a gratia cadent. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Duæ partes peribunt. Et tertia pars relinquetur in ea, id est, Christiani sequentur salutem, et habitatione terræ digni consistent. In fine etiam sæculi, Judæi atque gentiles pro maxima parte convertentur ad Christum, ita quod tunc duæ primæ sectæ quasi deficient : tamen, ut dictum est, aliqui in obstinatione sua persistent usque in diem judicii.
paras.en: [[13:8|And there shall be in all the earth, saith the Lord|Et erunt in omni terra, dicit Dominus]], [[13:8|parts|partes]], that is, in the whole world the race of men, or the people of the earth, shall be divided into three parts, namely of the Jews, of the Gentiles and of the Christians. [[13:8|two parts in it|Duæ in ea]], that is, two parts of men, namely the Gentiles and the unbelieving Jews, [[13:8|shall be scattered, and shall perish|dispergentur ac deficient]], that is, shall be rejected by God and shall fall from grace. Hence the Septuagint translated: Two parts shall perish. [[13:8|but the third part shall be left therein|Et tertia pars relinquetur in ea]], that is, the Christians shall attain salvation and shall remain worthy to dwell on the earth. At the end of the world too, the Jews and the Gentiles will for the most part be converted to Christ, so that then the first two sects will as it were fail: yet, as has been said, some will persist in their obstinacy until the day of judgment.

paras.t: Et ducam tertiam partem per ignem, id est, multiplici et pœnosa tribulatione, persecutione, tentatione, adversitate exercebo electos, fideles seu Christianos : quibus ait Salvator, Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur ; et rursus, Non est servus major domino suo. Ideo Paulus : Per multas, inquit, tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum. In Psalmo quoque clamant electi : Transivimus per ignem et aquam. Et uram eos, sicut uritur argentum, id est, omnem peccati impuritatem per tribulationes has tollam ab eis ; et probabo eos, non ut ego agnoscam, sed ad aliorum ædificationem, et sic eos probatos ostendam per ignem adversitatum, sicut probatur aurum in conflatorio artificis. In adversis enim potissimum virtus probatur, et quid homo profecerit, demonstratur. Propter quod patientia opus perfectum habet, ut dicitur in Jacobo : et ipsa ceterarum virtutum probatio nuncupatur. Hinc scriptum est : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos ; et alibi, Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Non ergo in adversis tristemur, sed quod ea quæ electis Dei conceduntur, patimur, cordialiter gloriemur, præsertim quum Tobiæ angelus Raphael dicat eidem : Quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te.
paras.en: [[13:9|And I will bring the third part through the fire|Et ducam tertiam partem per ignem]], that is, I will exercise the elect, the faithful or Christians, with manifold and painful tribulation, persecution, temptation and adversity: to whom the Saviour says, [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]]; and again, [[John 13:16|The servant is not greater than his lord|Non est servus major domino suo]][[John 15:20||]]. Therefore Paul says: [[Acts 14:21|through many|Per multas]], he says, [[Acts 14:21|tribulations we must enter into the kingdom|tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum]] of heaven [Acts has *of God*]. In the Psalm too the elect cry out: [[Ps 65:12|We have passed through fire and water|Transivimus per ignem et aquam]]. [[13:9|and will refine them as silver is refined|Et uram eos, sicut uritur argentum]], that is, by these tribulations I will take away from them every impurity of sin; [[13:9|and I will try them|et probabo eos]], not so that I may come to know them, but for the edification of others, and so I will show them proved by the fire of adversities, [[13:9|as gold is tried|sicut probatur aurum]] in the craftsman's crucible. For it is in adversity above all that virtue is proved, and what progress a man has made is shown. For which reason [[Jas 1:4|patience hath a perfect work|patientia opus perfectum habet]], as is said in James: and it is called the proof of the other virtues. Hence it is written: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace|Tanquam aurum in fornace]] the Lord hath proved his elect, [[Wis 3:6|and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos]]; and elsewhere, [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. Let us not then be sad in adversity, but let us glory from the heart that we suffer the things that are granted to the elect of God, above all since the angel Raphael says to Tobias: [[Tob 12:13|because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee|Quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te]].

paras.t: Ipse vocabit nomen meum, id est, plebs ista electa me devote invocabit, et ego exaudiam eum. Et dicam : Populus meus es, non solum per creationem ut ceteri, sed per devotionem et cultum, et per prædestinationem et gratiæ infusionem, per providentiam singularem, per mutuam caritatem. Et ipse dicet : Dominus Deus meus es tu, quem solum summe desidero, diligo, colo.
paras.en: [[13:9|They shall call on my name|Ipse vocabit nomen meum]], that is, this chosen people shall call upon me devoutly, [[13:9|and I will hear them|et ego exaudiam eum]]. [[13:9|I will say: Thou art my people|Et dicam : Populus meus es]], not only by creation, as the rest are, but by devotion and worship, by predestination and the infusion of grace, by a singular providence, by mutual charity. [[13:9|and they shall say: The Lord is my God|Et ipse dicet : Dominus Deus meus es tu]], whom alone I supremely desire, love and worship.

paras.t: Postremo, frequenter contingit, quod sicut discipuli Christo capto et cæso dispersi sunt, ita dum pastores boni per mortem vel alias auferuntur, subditi per errores et vitia dispergantur. Ideo Deum semper invocare debemus, pro bono prælato et efficaci pastore : quod est præcipuum Dei donum, sicut insufficientem et negligentem habere periculosissimum est. — Convertit quoque Dominus manum suam ad parvulos, ad egenos, abjectos et humiles, sicut per Isaiam testatur : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad quietum et humilem ? Nempe, ut ait Apostolus, quæ infirma et stulta sunt mundi, elegit Deus, et ignobilia et contemptibilia. Hos ergo adspicit Deus, quos despicit mundus.
paras.en: Lastly, it often happens that, as the disciples were scattered when Christ was taken and beaten, so when good shepherds are taken away, by death or otherwise, those under them are scattered through errors and vices. Therefore we ought always to call upon God for a good prelate and an effective shepherd: which is a chief gift of God, just as to have one who is inadequate and negligent is most perilous. — The Lord also turns his hand to the little ones, to the needy, the outcast and the humble, as he testifies by Isaias: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect|Ad quem respiciam]], but to the quiet and the humble? [Denis reads *quietum et humilem*; the Vulgate has *pauperculum*, the poor and little]. For indeed, as the Apostle says, the weak and [[1 Cor 1:27|foolish things of the world hath God chosen|stulta sunt mundi, elegit Deus]], [[1 Cor 1:28|And the base things of the world and the things that are contemptible|et ignobilia et contemptibilia]]. These, then, God looks upon, whom the world looks down upon [Latin *adspicit … despicit*, a play on words].

14.title: Declaratio capituli quartidecimi: Ecce dies Domini veniunt.
14.title_en: Exposition of the fourteenth chapter: Behold the days of the Lord shall come.

paras.t: Præsens capitulum maximis difficultatibus et obscurationibus plenum est: propter quod a diversis variis modis exponitur. Intendo autem expositionem sequi, quæ textui amplius consonat.
paras.en: The present chapter is full of the greatest difficulties and obscurities, and for that reason it is expounded in various ways by various writers. I intend, however, to follow the exposition that agrees best with the text.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta de persecutione circa finem mundi per Antichristum ventura, ait: Ecce dies Domini veniunt, id est, tempus a Deo dispositum appropinquat, quo quæ subjuncta sunt fient; et dividentur spolia tua, o Jerusalem, id est bona tibi per spoliationem ablata ab Antichristo et ejus ministris, in medio tui, ita quod juxta voluntatem suam sine timore bona tua prædabitur. Et congregabo omnes gentes ad Jerusalem in prælium contra eam: siquidem de omni natione quamplurimi adhæserunt Antichristo; et capietur civitas et vastabuntur domus, et mulieres violabuntur a satellitibus Antichristi, quibus ipse, ut dicitur, concupiscentiarum frena laxabit. Aliqui referunt hoc ad Jerusalem, a Romanis (eo quod Christum occiderit) captam; sed sequentia non concordant. Judæi autem, ut refert Hieronymus, sub Gog et Magog hæc dicunt implenda. Et egredietur media pars civitatis in captivitatem, ita quod multi de habitatoribus ejus ab Antichristo captivi ducentur, et reliquum populi non auferetur ex urbe, illi videlicet qui Antichristo adhærere voluerint.
paras.en: Speaking, then, of the persecution that is to come through Antichrist about the end of the world, the Prophet says: [[14:1|Behold the days of the Lord shall come|Ecce dies Domini veniunt]], that is, the time appointed by God draws near in which the things added here shall come to pass; [[14:1|and thy spoils shall be divided|et dividentur spolia tua]], O Jerusalem, that is, the goods taken from thee by plunder by Antichrist and his ministers, [[14:1|in the midst of thee|in medio tui]], so that he shall prey upon thy goods at his will and without fear. [[14:2|And I will gather all nations to Jerusalem to battle|Et congregabo omnes gentes ad Jerusalem in prælium]] against her: for a great many of every nation will cleave to Antichrist; [[14:2|and the city shall be taken, and the houses shall be rifled, and the women shall be defiled|et capietur civitas et vastabuntur domus, et mulieres violabuntur]] by the henchmen of Antichrist, for whom, as is said, he will slacken the reins of their lusts. Some refer this to Jerusalem taken by the Romans (because she had slain Christ); but what follows does not agree with that. The Jews, however, as Jerome relates, say that these things are to be fulfilled under Gog and Magog. [[14:2|and half of the city shall go forth into captivity|Et egredietur media pars civitatis in captivitatem]], so that many of its inhabitants shall be led away captive by Antichrist, [[14:2|and the rest of the people shall not be taken away out of the city|et reliquum populi non auferetur ex urbe]], namely those who are willing to cleave to Antichrist.

paras.t: Et egredietur Dominus: non locum mutando, sed novum atque insolitum suæ effectum potentiæ ostendendo; vel de lenitate suæ clementiæ ad rigorem justitiæ, juxta illud in Psalmo, Exsurge, Domine, in ira tua; et, Propter hanc in altum regredere; et in Habacuc, Egressus es in salutem populi tui. Moyses quoque dixit ad Dominum: Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto. Et præliabitur contra gentes illas, id est, divina sua virtute Antichristum cum reprobis sui exercitus opprimet et occidet, juxta illud Danielis: Judicium sedebit, ut auferatur potentia ejus et conteratur, et dispereat usque in finem; sicut præliatus est in die certaminis, id est die qua Pharaonem cum suo exercitu submersit in mari Rubro.
paras.en: [[14:3|Then the Lord shall go forth|Et egredietur Dominus]]: not by changing place, but by showing a new and unwonted effect of his power; or by going forth from the mildness of his clemency to the rigour of justice, according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 7:7|Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger|Exsurge, Domine, in ira tua]]; and, [[Ps 7:8|for their sakes return thou on high|Propter hanc in altum regredere]]; and in Habacuc, [[Hab 3:13|Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people|Egressus es in salutem populi tui]]. Moses too said to the Lord: [[Ex 33:15|If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place|Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto]]. [[14:3|and shall fight against those nations|Et præliabitur contra gentes illas]], that is, by his divine power he shall crush and slay Antichrist with the reprobate of his army, according to that of Daniel: [[Dan 7:26|a judgment shall sit, that his power may be taken away, and be broken in pieces, and perish even to the end|Judicium sedebit, ut auferatur potentia ejus et conteratur, et dispereat usque in finem]]; [[14:3|as when he fought in the day of battle|sicut præliatus est in die certaminis]], that is, on the day when he drowned Pharao with his army in the Red Sea.

paras.t: Et stabunt pedes ejus in die illa super montem Olivarum, qui est contra Jerusalem ad orientem: id est, in monte illo divinæ potestatis efficacia apparebit, eo quod ibi vel circa, occidendus sit Antichristus. Porro pedes incircumscriptibilis ac simplicissimi Dei, non sunt materialiter intelligendi; sed virtutis ejus pia ac fixa adsistentia, nomine pedum exprimitur. Unde et per Isaiam fatetur: Cælum mihi sedes est, terra autem scabellum pedum meorum. Et tamen Salomon loquitur: Cœlum et cœli cœlorum te capere non possunt. Nempe, ut canit Psalmista, Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis, et magnitudinis ejus non est finis.
paras.en: [[14:4|And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is over against Jerusalem towards the east|Et stabunt pedes ejus in die illa super montem Olivarum, qui est contra Jerusalem ad orientem]]: that is, on that mount the efficacy of the divine power shall appear, because Antichrist is to be slain there or thereabouts. Now the feet of God, who is uncircumscribable [that is, not contained or bounded by any place] and most simple, are not to be understood materially; but the loving and abiding presence of his power is expressed by the name of feet. Hence he declares through Isaias also: [[Is 66:1|Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool|Cælum mihi sedes est, terra autem scabellum pedum meorum]]. And yet Solomon says: [[3 Kings 8:27|heaven, and the heavens of heavens, cannot contain thee|Cœlum et cœli cœlorum te capere non possunt]]. For indeed, as the Psalmist sings, [[Ps 144:3|Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised: and of his greatness there is no end|Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis, et magnitudinis ejus non est finis]][[Ps 47:2||]].

paras.t: Et scindetur mons Olivarum ex media parte sui ad orientem et ad occidentem prærupto grandi valde. Et separabitur medium montis ejus ad aquilonem, et medium ejus ad meridiem. Secundum Hieronymum, sensus est, quod mons Oliveti grandi voragine dirumpetur, ita quod una pars ad orientem, altera ad occidentem respiciet: quo facto, repente in ipsa voragine alia scissio fiet, ita quod una pars scissi montis verget ad aquilonem, alia ad meridiem, sicut præruptum quadrangulum fiet. Alii asserunt quod scissio ista non erit nisi in duas partes, ita quod una pars montis inclinabitur versus aquilonem, alia versus meridiem, et scissura intermedia erit, sic quod longitudo ejus erit ab oriente ad occidentem.
paras.en: [[14:4|and the mount of Olives shall be divided in the midst thereof to the east, and to the west with a very great opening|Et scindetur mons Olivarum ex media parte sui ad orientem et ad occidentem prærupto grandi valde]]. [[14:4|and half of the mountain shall be separated to the north, and half thereof to the south|Et separabitur medium montis ejus ad aquilonem, et medium ejus ad meridiem]]. According to Jerome the sense is that the Mount of Olivet shall be burst asunder by a great chasm, so that one part shall face the east, the other the west; and when this is done, suddenly in that very chasm another cleft shall be made, so that one part of the cleft mountain shall slope towards the north, the other towards the south, so that a four-sided chasm is formed. Others assert that this cleaving will be into two parts only, so that one part of the mountain shall lean towards the north, the other towards the south, and the cleft will lie between them, in such a way that its length will run from east to west.

paras.t: Et fugietis, qui tunc ista videbitis, ad vallem montium eorum, quoniam conjungetur vallis montium, id est, vallis Josaphat, sita inter montem Sion et Oliveti, jungetur usque ad proximum, scilicet locum scissuræ jam dictæ. Et fugietis, istam voraginem horrendam conspicientes, sicut fugistis a facie terræ motus, qui factus est in diebus Oziæ regis Juda: qui quum officium sacerdotale in thurificando usurpasset, percussus est lepra, ut scribitur libro secundo Paralipomenon; et tunc ad divinæ indignationis indicium factus est terræ motus, sicut et apud Amos habetur. Unde et de præinducta scissione montis Olivarum aliqui arbitrantur, quod erit ex terræ motu ingenti, quem dicunt futurum in Antichristi fulminatione seu simili percussione, ad demonstrationem potestatis divinæ et iræ Dei contra superbissimum Antichristum adorari se facientem.
paras.en: [[14:5|And you shall flee|Et fugietis]], you who shall then see these things, [[14:5|to the valley of those mountains|ad vallem montium eorum]], [[14:5|for the valley of the mountains shall be joined|quoniam conjungetur vallis montium]], that is, the valley of Josaphat, which lies between Mount Sion and Olivet, shall be joined [[14:5|even to the next|usque ad proximum]], namely to the place of the cleft just spoken of. [[14:5|and you shall flee|Et fugietis]], as you behold this horrible chasm, [[14:5|as you fled from the face of the earthquake|sicut fugistis a facie terræ motus]], which happened [[14:5|in the days of Ozias king of Juda|in diebus Oziæ regis Juda]]: who, having usurped the priestly office by burning incense, was struck with leprosy, as is written in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 26:16||]][[2 Par 26:19||]]; and then the earthquake took place as a sign of the divine indignation, as is also found in Amos[[Amos 1:1||]]. Hence some think too that the cleaving of the Mount of Olives spoken of above will come from a mighty earthquake, which they say will happen when Antichrist is struck down by a thunderbolt or some like blow, to show the divine power and the wrath of God against Antichrist in his utmost pride, who makes himself be adored.

paras.t: Quidam Sanctorum per montem Olivarum intelligunt Ecclesiam, cujus filii sunt sicut novellæ olivarum: cujus media pars scinditur ad orientem, in qua sunt arbores fructuosæ et bonæ, puta electi; et alia ad occidentem, in qua sunt arbores steriles.
paras.en: Some of the Saints understand by the mount of Olives the Church, whose children are [[Ps 127:3|as olive plants|sicut novellæ olivarum]] [the margin gives Ps. cxxxvii, 3; the words are Ps 127:3]: half of which is cleft towards the east, and in it are fruitful and good trees, that is, the elect; and the other half towards the west, in which are barren trees.

paras.t: Et veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo. Istud, secundum Hieronymum, manifeste dicitur de secundo Christi adventu, quando post mortem Antichristi, aliquanto tempore interjecto, veniet generale atque finale judicium exercere, comitatus omnium agmine Beatorum: sicut et Christus in Evangelio de se ipso testatur, quod videbitur advenire cum potestate magna et gloria. Judas quoque apostolus inducit: Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis facere judicium. Isaias quoque: Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus. Ex his innotescit, quod hoc loco loquatur Propheta de his quæ circa finem mundi contingent.
paras.en: [[14:5|and the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him|Et veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo]]. This, according to Jerome, is plainly said of the second coming of Christ, when, after the death of Antichrist and after some time has passed, he shall come to hold the general and final judgment, attended by the host of all the Blessed: as Christ too testifies of himself in the Gospel, that he shall be seen coming [[Luke 21:27|with great power and majesty|cum potestate magna et gloria]]. Jude the apostle also brings in: [[Jude 1:14|Behold, the Lord cometh with thousands of his saints|Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis]] [[Jude 1:15|To execute judgment|facere judicium]]. And Isaias: [[Is 3:14|The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus]]. From these it is made known that in this place the Prophet is speaking of the things that shall happen about the end of the world.

paras.t: Et erit in die illa: Non erit lux, sed frigus et gelu: id est, tanta tunc erit impiorum pressura, carentia gratiæ, tribulatio et angustia, quod lux prosperitatis non erit eis, sed frigus et gelu, quia præ timore arescent, eruntque horrore ac timore repleti. Timor autem corporalis infrigidat, faciendo sanguinem ad cor ipsum refugere: quo sic a membris recedente, tremor causatur. Hinc ait Psalmista: Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus; et, In circuitu ejus tempestas valida.
paras.en: [[14:6|And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall be no light, but cold and frost|Et erit in die illa: Non erit lux, sed frigus et gelu]]: that is, so great shall then be the affliction of the wicked, their want of grace, their tribulation and anguish, that the light of prosperity shall not be theirs, but cold and frost, because they shall wither away for fear, and be filled with dread and fear[[Luke 21:26||]]. For bodily fear chills, by making the blood flee back to the heart itself; and as it thus withdraws from the limbs, trembling is caused. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him|Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus]]; and, [[Ps 49:3|a mighty tempest shall be round about him|In circuitu ejus tempestas valida]].

paras.t: Et erit dies una, quæ nota est Domino, id est dies æternitatis, vel hora glorificationis electorum: quæ dies æternaliter stabit, nec defluet. Vel loquitur de die judicii, de qua ait Salvator: De die illa et hora nemo scit, neque angeli in cœlo, sed solus Pater: cujus quum sit cum Filio et Spiritu Sancto una essentia, una est cum eis notitia. Non dies neque nox: id est, dies illa æternitatis seu retributionis atque judicii, non est proprie atque univoce dies cum die naturali qui noctem includit, vel artificiali qui est latio solis supra nostrum horizontem: siquidem dies illa non causabitur ex motu solis, nec temporali extensione decurret, nec terminabitur nocte. De qua die cantamus in Psalmo: Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis super millia. In generali vero resurrectione motus cœli cessabit, ideo solitus diei fluxus non erit. Propter quod in Apocalypsi prædictum est: Quia tempus ultra non erit. Et in tempore vesperi, id est in fine sæculi seu termino temporalis diei, erit lux, id est claritas beatificæ visionis, et lumen gloriæ consummatum in omnibus prædestinatis. De quo scriptum est in Apocalypsi: Civitas non eget sole neque luna, sed claritas Dei illuminabit eam. Quod et in Isaia scribitur. Paulo ante dixit Propheta, quod in die illa non erit lux; nunc ait, quod in tempore vesperi erit lux. Illud ergo ad reprobos, istud ad electos refertur. Consonat quoque huic prophetico verbo, quod Christus in Evangelio loquitur: Quum sero factum esset, præcepit Dominus operariis reddi mercedem.
paras.en: [[14:7|And there shall be one day, which is known to the Lord|Et erit dies una, quæ nota est Domino]], that is, the day of eternity, or the hour of the glorification of the elect: which day shall stand eternally and shall not slip away. Or he is speaking of the day of judgment, of which the Saviour says: [[Mark 13:32|of that day or hour no man knoweth, neither the angels in heaven|De die illa et hora nemo scit, neque angeli in cœlo]], [[Mark 13:32|but the Father|sed solus Pater]] [the Gospel also has "nor the Son", which Denis leaves out, though what he says next answers it]: and since the Father has one essence with the Son and the Holy Ghost, he has one knowledge with them. [[14:7|not day nor night|Non dies neque nox]]: that is, that day of eternity, or of retribution and judgment, is not properly and univocally a day [that is, a day in the same sense of the word] as is the natural day, which includes the night, or the artificial day, which is the course of the sun above our horizon: for that day shall not be caused by the motion of the sun, nor run its course by stretching out in time, nor be ended by night. Of this day we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 83:11|For better is one day in thy courts above thousands|Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis super millia]]. In the general resurrection, moreover, the motion of the heavens shall cease, and therefore the accustomed passing of the day shall be no more. For this reason it is foretold in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 10:6|That time shall be no longer|Quia tempus ultra non erit]]. [[14:7|and in the time of the evening|Et in tempore vesperi]], that is, at the end of the world, or the close of the temporal day, [[14:7|there shall be light|erit lux]], that is, the brightness of the beatific vision, and the light of glory brought to its fullness in all the predestined. Of which it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:23|the city hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon|Civitas non eget sole neque luna]], but [[Apoc 21:23|the glory of God hath enlightened it|claritas Dei illuminabit eam]]. This is written in Isaias too [Is 60:19–20, quoted further on]. A little before, the Prophet said that in that day there shall be no light; now he says that in the time of the evening there shall be light. The former, then, refers to the reprobate, the latter to the elect. With this prophetic word there also agrees what Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 20:8|when evening was come|Quum sero factum esset]], the lord bade the labourers be paid their hire.

paras.t: Et erit in die illa æternitatis sive judicii: Exibunt aquæ vivæ, id est plenissima effusio et gloriosa communio beatificæ agnitionis, felicitatis et gloriæ. De quibus habetur in Psalmo: Apud te est fons vitæ, et torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos; et, Fluminis impetus lætificat civitatem Dei. Isaias quoque ait: Ad fontes aquarum potabit eos. De Jerusalem illa cœlesti, de qua dicit Apostolus ad Hebræos: Accessistis ad Jerusalem civitatem et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam. Itemque Psalmista: Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio in te; et, Lauda, Jerusalem, Dominum. De qua Isaias multa dicit, quæ de terrena Jerusalem nequaquam verificantur, quum inter cetera ibi dicatur: Non erit tibi sol amplius ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te. Itaque aquæ istæ egredientur de Jerusalem, quia a Deo sublimi et benedicto in superna Jerusalem præsidenti, descendunt in Sanctos, juxta illud Apocalypsis: Agnus ducet eos ad vitæ fontes aquarum. Medium earum ad mare orientale, et medium earum ad mare novissimum: id est, una pars beatitudinis sempiternæ derivatur a Deo in eos qui prioribus fuerunt temporibus; alia, ad eos electos qui tempore posteriori fuerunt: non quod aliquorum beatitudo sit imperfecta atque divisa; sed his verbis insinuatur, quod beatitudo descendit ad omnes æqualiter ex parte objecti et æquali existente merito. Unde denarius, qui omnibus vineæ laboratoribus datur, unus et idem est. Ipse paterfamilias: Volo, inquit, huic novissimo dare sicut et tibi priori. Nomine autem maris et aquæ, populi designantur, secundum quod in Apocalypsi legitur: Aquæ multæ, populi multi; et in Ecclesiaste, Mitte panem tuum super transeuntes aquas. In æstate et in hieme erunt: id est, aquæ istæ seu præmia Beatorum jugiter permanebunt, quum perpetuitas atque securitas sint de ratione perfectæ ac veræ felicitatis. Quamvis autem tunc æstas et hiems non erunt, tamen per has temporis differentias æternitas denotatur, quam per partes temporis significare solemus. Sic enim in Isaia legitur, Erit mensis ex mense, et sabbatum ex sabbato: per quod perpetua Sanctorum in gloria mansio explicatur.
paras.en: [[14:8|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit in die illa]] of eternity or of judgment, [[14:8|that living waters shall go out|Exibunt aquæ vivæ]], that is, the fullest outpouring and glorious sharing of the beatific knowledge, happiness and glory. Of these we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 35:10|with thee is the fountain of life|Apud te est fons vitæ]], [[Ps 35:9|and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure|et torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos]]; and, [[Ps 45:5|The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful|Fluminis impetus lætificat civitatem Dei]]. Isaias too says: [[Is 49:10|at the fountains of waters he shall give them drink|Ad fontes aquarum potabit eos]] [the margin gives Is. xliv, 10; the words are Is 49:10]. [[14:8|from Jerusalem|De Jerusalem]], that heavenly Jerusalem of which the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come|Accessistis]] to Jerusalem the city, and to [[Heb 12:22|the company of many thousands of angels|multorum millium angelorum frequentiam]] [the margin gives Hebr. vii, 22; the words are Heb 12:22]. And likewise the Psalmist: [[Ps 86:7|The dwelling in thee is as it were of all rejoicing|Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio in te]]; and, [[Ps 147:1|Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem|Lauda, Jerusalem, Dominum]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 12, the Hebrew numbering]. Of her Isaias says many things that are by no means verified of the earthly Jerusalem, since among other things it is said there: [[Is 60:19|Thou shalt no more have the sun for thy light by day, neither shall the brightness of the moon enlighten thee|Non erit tibi sol amplius ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te]]. And so these waters shall go out from Jerusalem, because they come down upon the Saints from God, sublime and blessed, who presides in the Jerusalem above, according to that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 7:17|the Lamb|Agnus]] [[Apoc 7:17|shall lead them to the fountains of the waters of life|ducet eos ad vitæ fontes aquarum]]. [[14:8|half of them to the east sea, and half of them to the last sea|Medium earum ad mare orientale, et medium earum ad mare novissimum]]: that is, one part of everlasting beatitude flows down from God upon those who lived in earlier times; the other upon those elect who lived in later time: not that the beatitude of any is imperfect and divided; but by these words it is hinted that beatitude comes down upon all equally on the side of the object [that is, God himself, whom all the Blessed see and enjoy], and equally where merit is equal. Hence the penny that is given to all the labourers of the vineyard is one and the same. The householder himself says: [[Matt 20:14|I will|Volo]], he says, [[Matt 20:14|also give to this last even as to thee|huic novissimo dare sicut et tibi]] who came first. By the name of sea and water peoples are signified, as we read in the Apocalypse: Many waters, many peoples[[Apoc 17:1||]][[Apoc 17:15||]]; and in Ecclesiastes, [[Eccles 11:1|Cast thy bread upon the running waters|Mitte panem tuum super transeuntes aquas]]. [[14:8|they shall be in summer and in winter|In æstate et in hieme erunt]]: that is, these waters, or the rewards of the Blessed, shall abide for ever, since perpetuity and security belong to the very nature of perfect and true happiness. And though there shall then be no summer and winter, yet eternity is denoted by these differences of time, as we are wont to signify it by the parts of time. For so it is read in Isaias: [[Is 66:23|there shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath|Erit mensis ex mense, et sabbatum ex sabbato]]: by which the everlasting dwelling of the Saints in glory is set forth.

paras.t: Et erit Dominus rex super omnem terram: quia tunc Christo perfectissime erit subjecta non solum Ecclesia, sed omnis insuper creatura. Tunc quoque in hominibus et angelis cessabit prælatio, quantum ad officium administrationis sæculi pertinet. Propter quod ad Corinthios scriptum est: Quum tradiderit Christus regnum Deo et Patri, quum evacuaverit omnem principatum et potestatem et virtutem, ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus. In die illa æternitatis, erit Dominus unus omnium Beatorum: qui sicut est trinus in Personis, ita est unus in natura; et erit nomen ejus unum, id est, una appellatione designabitur, sicut et una cognitione, et una quasi intelligibili specie cognoscetur. Sicut enim rem cognoscimus, sic eam significamus atque exprimimus. Et quoniam in hac vita Deum in suis effectibus speculamur, in quibus tota ejus perfectio non relucet; ideo nunc eum obscure et imperfecte cognoscimus, pluribusque nominibus explicamus, sic quod ejus perfectio in diversis diversimode repræsentatur. Porro, in patria videbimus eum sicuti est, facie ad faciem, per ejus essentiam, quasi per intelligibilem formam. Idcirco tunc uno nomine exprimetur, sicut et uno intuitu conspicietur.
paras.en: [[14:9|And the Lord shall be king over all the earth|Et erit Dominus rex super omnem terram]]: because then not only the Church but every creature besides shall be most perfectly subject to Christ. Then too all prelacy among men and angels shall cease, so far as it belongs to the office of governing the world. For which reason it is written to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:24|when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father: when he shall have brought to nought all principality and power and virtue|Quum tradiderit Christus regnum Deo et Patri, quum evacuaverit omnem principatum et potestatem et virtutem]], [[1 Cor 15:28|that God may be all in all|ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus]]. [[14:9|in that day|In die illa]] of eternity [[14:9|there shall be one Lord|erit Dominus unus]] of all the Blessed: who, as he is three in Persons, so is one in nature; [[14:9|and his name shall be one|et erit nomen ejus unum]], that is, he shall be designated by one name, as he shall also be known by one knowledge and, as it were, by one intelligible species [that is, the likeness through which the mind knows a thing]. For as we know a thing, so we signify and express it. And since in this life we behold God in his effects, in which his whole perfection does not shine forth, we therefore know him now darkly and imperfectly and express him by many names, so that his perfection is represented in different ways in different things. But in our homeland [[1 John 3:2|we shall see him as he is|videbimus eum sicuti est]], [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]], through his essence, as through an intelligible form. Therefore he shall then be expressed by one name, as he shall also be beheld in one gaze.

paras.t: Deinceps redit Propheta, et loquitur de statu Ecclesiæ post Antichristi interitum supra descriptum. Jam enim non ait, In illa die, vel aliquid tale, ut cogamur ista præcedentibus continuare. Et revertetur omnis terra ad fidem atque obsequium Christi, Antichristo deleto, id est multi de omni natione ac populo, usque ad desertum inclusive, id est etiam a locis desertis, et habitantibus juxta ea, sive in eis, de colle Remmon ad austrum Jerusalem. Et exaltabitur Ecclesia Christi, vel civitas Jerusalem, et habitabitur a Christianis, in loco suo, a porta Benjamin usque ad locum portæ prioris, et usque ad portam angulorum; et a turre Hananeel usque ad torcularia regis.
paras.en: From here the Prophet turns back and speaks of the state of the Church after the destruction of Antichrist described above. For he no longer says, In that day, or anything of the kind, so that we should be forced to join these things on to what goes before. [[14:10|And all the land shall return|Et revertetur omnis terra]] to the faith and service of Christ, once Antichrist is destroyed, that is, many of every nation and people, [[14:10|even to the desert|usque ad desertum]] inclusively, that is, even from desert places, and from those dwelling near them or in them, [[14:10|from the hill to Remmon to the south of Jerusalem|de colle Remmon ad austrum Jerusalem]]. [[14:10|and she shall be exalted|Et exaltabitur]], namely the Church of Christ, or the city of Jerusalem, [[14:10|and shall dwell|et habitabitur]], being inhabited by Christians [Denis reads *habitabitur*, "shall be inhabited", for the Vulgate's *habitabit*, "shall dwell"], [[14:10|in her own place, from the gate of Benjamin even to the place of the former gate, and even to the gate of the corners: and from the tower of Hananeel even to the king's winepresses|in loco suo, a porta Benjamin usque ad locum portæ prioris, et usque ad portam angulorum; et a turre Hananeel usque ad torcularia regis]].

paras.t: Et habitabunt in ea. Antichristus quippe civitatem Jerusalem auferet Christianis: quo occiso, reddetur eisdem, et plene incolent eam. Et anathema, id est maledictio, non erit amplius populo christiano, et urbi Jerusalem, quum persecutio Antichristi futura sit ultima, sed sedebit Jerusalem secura.
