paras.en: [[14:11|And people shall dwell in it|Et habitabunt in ea]]. For Antichrist will take the city of Jerusalem from the Christians: when he is slain, it shall be given back to them, and they shall inhabit it fully. And [[14:11|anathema|anathema]], that is, a curse, [[14:11|shall be no more|non erit amplius]] for the Christian people and for the city of Jerusalem, since the persecution of Antichrist is to be the last, [[14:11|but Jerusalem shall sit secure|sed sedebit Jerusalem secura]].

paras.t: Et hæc, quæ subditur, erit plaga qua percutiet Dominus omnes gentes quæ pugnaverunt adversus Jerusalem, id est Antichristum et ejus fautores: in cujus exercitu plurimi erunt de omni hominum genere, qui et Ecclesiam et urbem Jerusalem impugnabunt, et prævalebunt. Jam plaga exprimitur: Tabescet caro uniuscujusque eorum stantis super pedes suos, id est, præ dolore deficiet, et oculi ejus contabescent in foraminibus suis, id est, vim visivam in organis suis amittent, et lingua eorum contabescet in ore suo. Hoc totum et spiritualiter et corporaliter tyranni et persecutores Ecclesiæ frequenter perpessi sunt: qui et dire plagati subito obierunt, et interiores eorum oculi excæcabantur; corpora quoque vitiis servierunt, dæmonumque obsequio contabuerunt.
paras.en: [[14:12|And this|Et hæc]], namely what is added next, [[14:12|shall be the plague wherewith the Lord shall strike all nations that have fought against Jerusalem|erit plaga qua percutiet Dominus omnes gentes quæ pugnaverunt adversus Jerusalem]], that is, Antichrist and his abettors: in whose army there shall be very many of every race of men, who shall attack both the Church and the city of Jerusalem, and shall prevail. Now the plague is described: [[14:12|the flesh of every one shall consume away while they stand upon their feet|Tabescet caro uniuscujusque eorum stantis super pedes suos]], that is, shall fail for pain, [[14:12|and their eyes shall consume away in their holes|et oculi ejus contabescent in foraminibus suis]], that is, they shall lose the power of sight in their organs, [[14:12|and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth|et lingua eorum contabescet in ore suo]]. All this the tyrants and persecutors of the Church have often suffered, both spiritually and bodily: they were grievously stricken and died suddenly, and their inner eyes were blinded; their bodies too were slaves to vices, and wasted away in the service of devils.

paras.t: In illa die erit tumultus Domini magnus in eis, id est, magnam, Deo agente aut permittente, turbationem inquietudinemque habebunt ex abundantia malorum culpæ ac pœnæ. Et apprehendet vir manum proximi sui, et conseretur manus ejus super manum proximi sui, id est, præ timore atque angustia capiet unus manum alterius causa auxilii. Quidam exponunt hoc, quod quidam eorum se invicem interficient; sed hoc littera ista non videtur prætendere.
paras.en: [[14:13|In that day there shall be a great tumult from the Lord among them|In illa die erit tumultus Domini magnus in eis]], that is, by God's doing or permission they shall have great disturbance and unrest from the abundance of evils, of guilt and of punishment. [[14:13|and a man shall take the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall be clasped upon his neighbour's hand|Et apprehendet vir manum proximi sui, et conseretur manus ejus super manum proximi sui]], that is, for fear and anguish one shall seize the hand of another to get help. Some expound this to mean that some of them shall kill one another; but the letter does not seem to bear this.

paras.t: Sed et Judas pugnabit adversus Jerusalem. Hoc supra diligenter expositum est. Et congregabuntur divitiæ omnium gentium in circuitu, id est, ad Jerusalem apportabuntur ab Antichristo ejusque populo, utpote aurum et argentum, et vestes multæ satis. Potest autem et spiritualiter exponi in bono, ita ut quidquid naturalis perfectionis in gentibus fuerit, scilicet ingenii, virtuositatis, scientiæ, eloquentiæ, ad ipsam Ecclesiam colligatur, dum gentes talibus donis ornatæ convertuntur ad fidem: quia tunc dona naturæ perficiuntur muneribus gratiæ, et defendunt Ecclesiam qui eam aliquando impugnabant.
paras.en: [[14:14|And even Juda shall fight against Jerusalem|Sed et Judas pugnabit adversus Jerusalem]]. This has been carefully expounded above [apparently at 12:2, "Juda also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem"]. [[14:14|and the riches of all nations round about shall be gathered together|Et congregabuntur divitiæ omnium gentium in circuitu]], that is, they shall be brought to Jerusalem by Antichrist and his people, such as [[14:14|gold, and silver, and garments in great abundance|aurum et argentum, et vestes multæ satis]]. It can also be expounded spiritually in a good sense, so that whatever natural perfection there has been among the nations, namely of talent, of virtue, of knowledge, of eloquence, is gathered into the Church herself, when nations adorned with such gifts are converted to the faith: for then the gifts of nature are perfected by the gifts of grace, and those who once attacked the Church defend her.

paras.t: Et sic erit ruina equi, et muli, et cameli, et asini, et omnium jumentorum quæ fuerint in castris Antichristi, id est, ita Deo plagante, peribunt universa animalia irrationabilia Antichristi atque satellitum ejus, sicut ruina hæc, id est, quemadmodum homines præinducti eis utentes peribunt. Deus enim propter hominum peccata, ad majorem eorum confusionem, interdum bruta eorum occidit, imo quandoque hoc fit ad eorum piam correctionem. Præterea, homines qui propter passiones certas et vitia quædam præfatis jumentis comparantur, atque eorum nominibus exprimuntur, spiritualiter salubriterque labuntur, dum ad virtutes contrarias, Deo clementer suffragante, pertingunt. Per equos enim designantur lascivi; per mulos, infructuosi (muli enim non generant); per camelum, qui delictorum onere aggravantur; per asinos, male simplices et indocti. Dum itaque lascivi fiunt casti; infructuosi, bonis operibus abundantes; peccatis gravati, virtutibus pleni, ut ubi abundavit peccatum, abundet et gratia; maleque simplices et indocti, efficiuntur a Spiritu Sancto uncti et illustrati: tunc præfata jumenta salubriter ruunt.
paras.en: [[14:15|And the destruction of the horse, and of the mule, and of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts|Et sic erit ruina equi, et muli, et cameli, et asini, et omnium jumentorum]] [[14:15|that shall be|quæ fuerint]] in the camp of Antichrist, that is, as God thus strikes them, all the irrational animals of Antichrist and of his henchmen shall perish, [[14:15|like this destruction|sicut ruina hæc]], that is, just as the men spoken of before, who use them, shall perish. For God, on account of men's sins and to their greater confusion, sometimes kills their beasts; indeed sometimes this is done for their loving correction. Moreover, men who on account of certain passions and vices are compared to the beasts just named, and are expressed by their names, fall spiritually and to their salvation when, by God's merciful help, they attain to the contrary virtues [Latin *ruina*, "destruction", is also a "fall", hence Denis's play]. For by horses are signified the wanton; by mules, the unfruitful (for mules do not breed); by the camel, those weighed down by the burden of sins; by asses, the wrongly simple and the untaught. So when the wanton become chaste; the unfruitful, abounding in good works; those weighed down by sins, full of virtues, so that, [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded|ubi abundavit peccatum]], grace too may abound; and the wrongly simple and untaught are anointed and enlightened by the Holy Ghost: then the beasts just named fall to their salvation.

paras.t: Et omnes qui reliqui fuerint de universis gentibus quæ venerint contra Jerusalem, id est, gentes illæ quæ cum Antichristo non perierunt, eo quod timore vel excusabili deceptione eum secutæ sint contra Jerusalem atque Ecclesiam, ascendent ab anno in annum, id est singulis annis diebus debitis, ut adorent regem Dominum exercituum, id est Christum principem universorum, in Jerusalem vel Ecclesia. Ista expositio videtur supponere quod post Antichristi interitum durabit cursus novi Testamenti in sæculo isto per annos. Quid autem de hoc sentiendum sit, sapientioribus derelinquo. Et celebrent festivitatem Tabernaculorum: non eo modo quo fiebat in veteri Testamento, sed quantum ad figuratum, videlicet quoad id quod per festum illud significabatur. Fiebat quippe festivitas illa in lege, in memoriam quod filii Israel de Ægypti servitute liberati, in deserto in tabernaculis morabantur, ut terram promissionis intrarent. Per quod figurabatur, quod in novo Testamento Christiani de peccati atque diaboli servitute per Christum erepti, et in hac valle miseriæ commorantes, ad patriam paradisi cœlestis in virtutibus proficiendo ascenderent, janua gloriæ merito dominicæ passionis patefacta: sicque Christifideles festum tabernaculi celebrant; et tanto post Antichristi interitum devotius celebrabunt, quanto tunc in eis amplior fidei fervor consistet.
paras.en: [[14:16|And all they that shall be left of all nations that came against Jerusalem|Et omnes qui reliqui fuerint de universis gentibus quæ venerint contra Jerusalem]], that is, those nations that did not perish with Antichrist, because they followed him against Jerusalem and the Church out of fear or excusable deception, [[14:16|shall go up from year to year|ascendent ab anno in annum]], that is, every year on the appointed days, [[14:16|to adore the King, the Lord of hosts|ut adorent regem Dominum exercituum]], that is, Christ the prince of all things, in Jerusalem or in the Church. This exposition seems to suppose that after the destruction of Antichrist the course of the New Testament will last in this world for years. What is to be thought of this I leave to wiser men. [[14:16|and to keep the feast of tabernacles|Et celebrent festivitatem Tabernaculorum]]: not in the way it was kept in the Old Testament, but as to what it figured, namely as to what was signified by that feast. For that feast was kept under the Law in memory that the children of Israel, freed from the bondage of Egypt, dwelt in tents [*tabernacula*, the word rendered "tabernacles"] in the desert, so that they might enter the land of promise. By this it was figured that in the New Testament Christians, delivered by Christ from the bondage of sin and of the devil, and dwelling in this valley of misery, would go up to the homeland of the heavenly paradise by advancing in virtues, the gate of glory having been opened by the merit of the Lord's passion: and so the faithful of Christ keep the feast of tabernacles; and after the destruction of Antichrist they will keep it the more devoutly, the greater the fervour of faith that shall then be in them.

paras.t: Et erit: Qui non ascenderint de familiis terræ ad Jerusalem, id est Christi Ecclesiam: in civitatem namque illam particularem omnes gentes annuatim venire non possent, nec capi ibidem; et nunc satis ostensum est, in Prophetis per Jerusalem litteraliter exprimi Christi Ecclesiam; ut adorent regem Dominum exercituum; non erit super eos imber, id est perfusio gratiæ Dei, sed in mortalibus vitiis disperibunt.
paras.en: [[14:17|And it shall come to pass|Et erit]]: [[14:17|that he that shall not go up of the families of the land to Jerusalem|Qui non ascenderint de familiis terræ ad Jerusalem]], that is, to the Church of Christ: for all nations could not come every year into that particular city, nor find room there; and it has by now been sufficiently shown that in the Prophets the Church of Christ is expressed literally by Jerusalem; [[14:17|to adore the King, the Lord of hosts|ut adorent regem Dominum exercituum]], [[14:17|there shall be no rain upon them|non erit super eos imber]], that is, the outpouring of God's grace, but they shall perish in deadly vices.

paras.t: Quod et si familia Ægypti, id est populus regni illius antiqui atque famosi, non ascenderit, et non venerit, ad adorandum modo jam dicto; nec super eos erit imber gratiæ et doctrinæ divinæ; sed erit ruina, id est, hujus imbris carentia erit pœna una, qua percutiet Dominus omnes gentes quæ non ascenderint ab imo vitiorum ad arcem virtutum, ad celebrandum festivitatem Tabernaculorum, spiritualiter, non litteraliter. Littera nempe occidit, spiritus autem vivificat. Et certum est, a publicatione evangelicæ legis, observantiam legalium, quantum ad cærimonialia, fuisse prohibitam et letalem, quoniam veritate revelata, cessare debet figura. Hoc erit peccatum, id est transgressio divini præcepti, Ægypti, et hoc peccatum omnium gentium quæ non ascenderint ad celebrandum festivitatem Tabernaculorum: secundum sensum prætactum.
paras.en: [[14:18|And if the family of Egypt|Quod et si familia Ægypti]], that is, the people of that ancient and famous kingdom, [[14:18|go not up nor come|non ascenderit, et non venerit]] to adore in the way just spoken of, [[14:18|neither shall it be upon them|nec super eos erit]], the rain of divine grace and teaching; [[14:18|but there shall be destruction|sed erit ruina]], that is, the want of this rain shall be one punishment, [[14:18|wherewith the Lord will strike all nations that will not go up|qua percutiet Dominus omnes gentes quæ non ascenderint]] from the depth of vices to the citadel of virtues, [[14:18|to keep the feast of tabernacles|ad celebrandum festivitatem Tabernaculorum]], spiritually, not literally. For [[2 Cor 3:6|the letter killeth: but the spirit quickeneth|Littera nempe occidit, spiritus autem vivificat]]. And it is certain that from the promulgation of the law of the Gospel the observance of the legal precepts [that is, those of the Law of Moses], as regards the ceremonial ones, has been forbidden and deadly, since once the truth is revealed the figure must cease. [[14:19|This shall be the sin|Hoc erit peccatum]], that is, the transgression of a divine precept, [[14:19|of Egypt, and this the sin of all nations, that will not go up to keep the feast of tabernacles|Ægypti, et hoc peccatum omnium gentium quæ non ascenderint ad celebrandum festivitatem Tabernaculorum]]: in the sense touched on above.

paras.t: In die illa erit, quod super frenum equi est, sanctum Domino: id est, ornamenta aurea atque argentea, quæ in equorum frenis poni solebant, Domino offerentur, quoniam usus equorum et armorum necessarius non exsistet, Antichristo occiso, sed pax erit præcipua. Sic Glossa exponit. Et erunt lebetes, id est vasa divini cultus, in domo Domini, id est in Ecclesia, in qua sunt calices, pyxides, aliaque divino cultui vasa aptata: quæ jam nomine lebetum signantur, quoniam Propheta per metaphoram exprimit ea quæ ad evangelicæ legis pertinent cultum, per ea quæ erant in Synagoga et veteri Testamento, quum fuerint figurativa horum quæ in nova sunt lege, et cultus Ecclesiæ; quasi phialæ coram altare: nam coram altari feruntur præcipue, sicut phialæ, quæ sunt vasa ad vinum potandum formata, ad mensam portantur. Spiritualiter lebetes sunt homines virtuosi, qui sciunt juxta apostolicum documentum vas suum seu corpus possidere in sanctificatione: qui quum sint bonus odor Christi in omni loco, phialis comparantur.
paras.en: [[14:20|In that day that which is upon the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord|In die illa erit, quod super frenum equi est, sanctum Domino]]: that is, the ornaments of gold and silver that used to be put on the bridles of horses shall be offered to the Lord, since, Antichrist being slain, there will be no need to use horses and arms, but peace shall prevail. So the Gloss expounds it. [[14:20|and the caldrons|Et erunt lebetes]], that is, the vessels of divine worship, [[14:20|in the house of the Lord|in domo Domini]], that is, in the Church, in which there are chalices, pyxes and other vessels fitted for divine worship: these are here signified by the name of caldrons, since the Prophet by metaphor expresses the things that belong to the worship of the law of the Gospel by the things that were in the Synagogue and the Old Testament, for those were figures of the things that are in the new law and of the worship of the Church; [[14:20|shall be as the phials before the altar|quasi phialæ coram altare]]: for they are carried chiefly before the altar, as phials, which are vessels shaped for drinking wine, are carried to the table. Spiritually, the caldrons are virtuous men, who know, according to the Apostle's teaching, how [[1 Thess 4:4|to possess his vessel|vas suum]], that is, the body, [[1 Thess 4:4|in sanctification|possidere in sanctificatione]]: and since they are [[2 Cor 2:15|the good odour of Christ|bonus odor Christi]] in every place, they are compared to phials.

paras.t: Et erit omnis lebes in Jerusalem, et in Juda, id est in Ecclesia et populo confitenti, vel etiam in civitate illa Judæ et conversis Judæis, sanctificatus Domino exercituum, id est divino cultui mancipatus, ut in aliis non liceat eis uti, quum sint vasa sacrata. Et venient omnes immolantes, id est sacerdotes sacramentum Eucharistiæ offerentes, aliique fideles, alia novæ legis sacrificia spiritualia seu corporalia in Ecclesia immolantes; et sument ex eis, id est ex vasis sanctis prædictis sacramenta christianæ religionis, et coquent in eis, id est, Sacramentum altaris in igne Sancti Spiritus, seu caritatis fervore, conficient, tractabunt, vel sument, ne crudas agni comedant carnes, nec sacramentaliter tantum communicent, sed in vasis congrua devotione animæ sibi præparent cibum salvificum. Loquitur autem Propheta metaphorice et obscure, sicut et supra frequenter, ut moris est in Prophetis. Et non erit mercator ultra, id est spiritualium venditor, vel simoniacus, aut generaliter emptor et venditor, in domo Domini exercituum, scilicet in Ecclesia: hæc enim vitia prohibentur a Christo, qui ejecit de templo ementes atque vendentes; in die illa, id est tempore illo post Antichristi dejectionem: quia ex tunc simonia inter fideles non erit, neque in Ecclesia negotiatio vitiosa, eo quod tunc imminente termino mundi, devotissime obsequuntur Christiani Creatori et Salvatori suo, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[14:21|And every caldron in Jerusalem and Juda|Et erit omnis lebes in Jerusalem, et in Juda]], that is, in the Church and the people that confesses [*Juda* is taken to mean "confession"], or also in that city of Juda and among the converted Jews, [[14:21|shall be sanctified to the Lord of hosts|sanctificatus Domino exercituum]], that is, given over to divine worship, so that it shall not be lawful for them to use them for other things, since they are consecrated vessels. [[14:21|and all that sacrifice shall come|Et venient omnes immolantes]], that is, the priests offering the sacrament of the Eucharist, and the other faithful, offering in the Church the other sacrifices of the new law, spiritual or bodily; [[14:21|and take of them|et sument ex eis]], that is, from the holy vessels just spoken of, the sacraments of the Christian religion, [[14:21|and shall seethe in them|et coquent in eis]], that is, they shall consecrate, handle or receive the Sacrament of the altar in the fire of the Holy Ghost, or in the fervour of charity, so that they may not eat the flesh of the lamb raw, nor communicate only sacramentally [that is, receiving the sacrament outwardly without its fruit in the soul], but may prepare the saving food for themselves in the vessels, with the fitting devotion of the soul. The Prophet speaks, however, metaphorically and obscurely, as he often has above, as is the custom of the Prophets. [[14:21|and the merchant shall be no more|Et non erit mercator ultra]], that is, the seller of spiritual things, or the simoniac, or in general the buyer and seller, [[14:21|in the house of the Lord of hosts|in domo Domini exercituum]], namely in the Church: for these vices are forbidden by Christ, who cast out of the temple those who bought and sold[[Matt 21:12||]]; [[14:21|in that day|in die illa]], that is, in that time after the overthrow of Antichrist: for from then on there shall be no simony among the faithful, nor sinful trading in the Church, because then, with the end of the world at hand, Christians will most devoutly serve their Creator and Saviour, who is God over all, sublime and blessed. Amen.
